Both feet are at the same voltage, so no current flows through the bird
The power line carries too little current to harm a small bird
Birds are naturally immune to electric shocks
explanation: Both of the bird's feet are at the same voltage on a single wire, so no current flows through its body.

q: How does the palm civet mark its territory?
options: By scratching deep claw marks into tree bark
By using scent glands beneath its tail
By making loud calls heard from far away
By leaving droppings in visible places
explanation: The palm civet uses scent glands beneath its tail to mark its territory and communicate with other civets.

q: How is sugarcane planted in the fields of Negros?
options: Seeds are scattered directly onto the soil
Stem cuttings are cut and buried in the soil
Young seedlings are grown in nurseries first
Roots from old plants are divided and replanted
explanation: Sugarcane is not planted from seeds — pieces of its stalk are cut and buried in the soil, and a new plant sprouts from each piece.

q: What does the body do for a child during sleep?
options: It stops all body processes to save energy
It repairs damaged cells, strengthens immunity, and releases growth hormones
It converts stored fat into extra energy for the next day
It slows the heartbeat to prevent wear on the heart
explanation: During sleep the body repairs damaged cells, strengthens the immune system, and releases hormones that help a child grow.

q: Why are vehicle tires made of vulcanized rubber?
options: Because it is the lightest material available for wheels
Because it is elastic and creates friction with the road for safe braking
Because it does not get hot when the vehicle moves fast
Because it is cheaper to produce than other tire materials
explanation: Vulcanized rubber is elastic and provides friction with the road, allowing safe braking and cushioning bumps.

q: Why are the brain and heart the first organs harmed when carbon monoxide blocks oxygen?
options: They are closest to the lungs where CO enters the body
They are the largest organs and use the most blood
They work all the time and need a constant supply of oxygen
They store very little oxygen compared to other organs
explanation: The brain and heart work all the time and need constant oxygen, so they are the first to be affected when carbon monoxide blocks oxygen from reaching them.

q: What makes bioplastic different from regular plastic?
options: Bioplastic is stronger and lasts longer than regular plastic
Bioplastic is made from plants and breaks down faster because bacteria can eat it
Bioplastic is made from recycled regular plastic melted at high heat
Bioplastic dissolves completely in water within a few days
explanation: Bioplastic is made from plants like corn and breaks down faster than regular plastic because bacteria can eat it, though it still needs the right conditions to fully rot.

q: How do bats figure out how far away an object is in the dark?
options: They sense heat given off by nearby warm objects
They feel changes in air pressure caused by objects nearby
They send out high-frequency sounds and measure how long it takes for the echo to return
They use their sharp eyesight to spot objects even in dim light
explanation: Bats send out high-frequency sounds and calculate the distance to objects from the time it takes for the echo to return.

q: What is special about Enhanced Geothermal Systems (EGS)?
options: They only work near active volcanoes where steam already rises naturally
They use hot underground rock even where there is no natural water present
They generate electricity by burning dried volcanic ash as fuel
They cool hot springs to a safe temperature before pumping water underground
explanation: EGS allows engineers to use hot underground rock with no natural water — they drill deep holes, pump water down, and collect the resulting steam.

q: How do we know that sound carries energy?
options: Sound travels faster in warmer air, showing it has heat energy
We can feel the vibrations from a nearby loud speaker or drum
Sound waves glow faintly when they pass through glass
A microphone converts sound into light, proving it has energy
explanation: Sound carries energy, which is why we can feel the vibration from a loud speaker or drum nearby.

q: What happens to collected recyclable materials at a recycling center?
options: They are buried in a lined pit and left to decompose safely
They are burned to produce electricity for the community
They are cleaned, sorted, crushed or melted, and turned into material for new products
They are shipped overseas where factories buy them for cheap
explanation: At a recycling center or factory, collected items are cleaned, sorted, crushed or melted, and turned into material for new products.

q: What two metals are combined to make bronze?
options: Iron and copper
Copper and tin
Silver and iron
Gold and copper
explanation: Bronze is an alloy made by combining copper and tin, and it is harder than pure copper.

q: Why do doctors give eye tests and hearing tests to patients?
options: To count how many senses a person has
To check if the senses are working well and give help if they are not
To measure how fast nerve signals travel to the brain
To make sure patients are not faking their symptoms
explanation: Doctors test our senses — like sight and hearing — to check if they are working well, and if a sense is weak they provide help such as eyeglasses.

q: What is true about a machine with a mechanical advantage less than 1?
options: It multiplies the input force so less effort is needed
It requires more input force than output force but moves the load faster or farther
It cannot do any useful work at all
It converts electrical energy into mechanical movement
explanation: Machines with mechanical advantage less than 1 require more input force than output force, but this tradeoff gives greater speed or distance of movement at the load end.

q: How do soldier termites protect their colony?
options: By sealing tunnel entrances with sticky secretions
By using their large jaws to fight off enemies like ants
By releasing a strong smell that drives away predators
By swarming and flying toward threats to scare them away
explanation: Soldier termites have large jaws they use to defend the colony from enemies like ants.

q: According to the 60-60 rule for safe listening, what should you do?
options: Listen to music for 60 seconds, then pause for 60 seconds repeatedly
Keep earphones at no more than 60% volume and listen for no more than 60 minutes before resting
Use earphones no more than 60 days a year and clean them every 60 days
Play audio at 60% speed and keep the volume below 60 decibels
explanation: The 60-60 rule says to keep earphones at no more than 60% volume and listen for no longer than 60 minutes before resting your ears.

q: How do you know a beam scale is showing the correct weight?
options: When the pointer moves as far to the right as possible
When the beam becomes level because the weights on both ends are equal
When the scale makes a clicking sound at the right measurement
When the heavier side touches the base of the scale
explanation: A beam scale becomes level when the weights on both ends are equal, and that is when you read the correct weight.

q: Where can children in the Philippines get free vaccines?
options: Only at private hospitals that accept PhilHealth
At health centers through the DOH's national vaccination program
Only from school nurses during special health days
At pharmacies when the child shows a prescription
explanation: In the Philippines, the DOH gives free vaccines for children at health centers as part of a national program.

q: The rhea is a large flightless bird that looks like an ostrich. Where does it come from?
options: Australia
Africa
South America
Southeast Asia
explanation: The rhea is a large flightless bird from South America that resembles an ostrich.

q: When you roll an object down a ramp, why does it move slower on a rough surface than on a smooth one?
options: The rough surface adds extra weight to the rolling object
Rough surfaces create more friction that slows the object down
The object bounces more on a rough surface, losing energy upward
Rough surfaces are always steeper, making the object move in a curve
explanation: A rough surface creates more friction, which slows down an object rolling down a ramp.

q: Why is a compass especially important for Filipino fishermen and sailors crossing the sea?
options: It measures wind speed so they can predict when storms will arrive
It works because of Earth's magnetic poles and shows north when no land or stars are in sight
It helps them track schools of fish moving under the water's surface
It measures the depth of the sea to find safe routes between islands
explanation: A compass works because of Earth's magnetic poles and shows where north is, which is vital for Filipino sailors when no land or stars are visible across thousands of islands.

q: How does trash from the Philippines end up creating garbage patches in the ocean?
options: Garbage trucks accidentally drop waste when crossing long bridges over the sea
A lot of trash passes through rivers like the Pasig River and flows out to the ocean
Strong typhoon winds blow plastic bags directly from land into the sea
Fishing boats dump their nets and old equipment into deep water
explanation: The Philippines is one of the countries that sends the most plastic into the ocean because a lot of trash passes through rivers like the Pasig.

q: Why do plants need sunlight to survive?
options: Sunlight warms the soil so roots can absorb more water
Plants use sunlight's energy in photosynthesis to make their own food
Sunlight kills harmful insects and fungi that attack plant leaves
Plants need sunlight to produce seeds but not to grow leaves
explanation: Plants use sunlight's energy in photosynthesis to make their own food, and without light most plants cannot make food and will weaken.

q: How is the cloud rat different from the pest rats found in Filipino homes?
options: The cloud rat is smaller and faster than house rats
The cloud rat is a wild forest animal, not a house pest
The cloud rat eats insects while house rats eat stored grain
The cloud rat lives underground while house rats climb walls
explanation: The cloud rat is a wild forest animal and is different from the pest rats found in houses.

q: How does a lightning rod protect a building during a thunderstorm?
options: It creates a magnetic field that repels lightning away from the building
It attracts lightning and safely carries its electricity into the ground
It absorbs the lightning's energy and converts it into usable electricity
It breaks the lightning bolt into smaller harmless sparks before it hits the roof
explanation: A lightning rod is a metal pole on a roof that attracts lightning and safely carries its electricity into the ground.

q: Which pen name did Marcelo H. del Pilar use during the Propaganda Movement?
options: Laong Laan
Dimasalang
Plaridel
Agapito Bagumbayan
explanation: Marcelo H. del Pilar used the pen name 'Plaridel' in the Propaganda Movement.

q: How does the Komodo dragon detect prey that is far away?
options: It uses large ears that can hear very faint sounds at a distance
It has heat-sensing pits around its mouth to detect warm-blooded animals
It uses its forked tongue to smell prey from far away
It watches for movement using its wide, forward-facing eyes
explanation: The Komodo dragon uses its forked tongue to smell prey from far away.

q: Where is the tallest waterfall in the world located, and how high is it?
options: Victoria Falls in Zimbabwe, about 108 meters high
Niagara Falls in Canada, about 57 meters high
Iguazu Falls in Argentina, about 269 meters high
Angel Falls in Venezuela, about 979 meters high
explanation: Angel Falls in Venezuela is the tallest waterfall in the world, about 979 meters high.

q: What powers the human voice when we speak or sing?
options: Muscles in the throat that squeeze together to produce sound
Air pushed out from our lungs flowing past the vocal cords
Vibrations from the jawbone that travel up to the mouth
Water stored in the throat that vibrates when we breathe out
explanation: Air pushed out from our lungs flows past the vocal cords to make our voice.

q: How do epiphytes spread to grow on new trees?
options: Animals eat their fruit and deposit seeds on tree branches
Their roots grow along the ground until they reach a new tree
Tiny seeds or spores are carried by the wind to other trees
They send out long runners that attach to nearby tree trunks
explanation: Epiphytes spread by very tiny seeds or spores that the wind carries to other trees, where they grow into new plants.

q: What does it mean that the cell membrane is selectively permeable?
options: The membrane completely blocks all substances from entering or leaving the cell
The membrane is made of a hard material that cannot be crossed by any molecule
The membrane lets in needed substances like nutrients and pushes out waste, choosing what passes through
The membrane allows anything to pass freely in and out of the cell without restriction
explanation: The cell membrane selectively chooses what to let in, such as nutrients, and what to push out, such as waste.

q: What type of glass is used for soft drink bottles and condiment jars in the Philippines?
options: Borosilicate glass, known for withstanding high heat
Tempered glass, which shatters into safe small pieces
Lead crystal glass, valued for its clarity and strength
Soda-lime glass, which can be melted down and reused by factories
explanation: In the Philippines, soda-lime glass is used for soft drink bottles and jars, and many of these bottles are returned and melted down again to be reused.

q: Which of the following does the nervous system control automatically, without you thinking about it?
options: Writing your name on a piece of paper
Kicking a ball during a game
Breathing, heartbeat, and digestion
Choosing what food to eat at lunch
explanation: The nervous system automatically manages breathing, heartbeat, and digestion even when we are not thinking about them.

q: What is the correct order of trophic levels in a food chain?
options: Animal-eaters at the first level, plants at the second, plant-eaters at the third
Plants at the first level, plant-eaters at the second, animal-eaters at the third
Plant-eaters at the first level, plants at the second, animal-eaters at the third
Animal-eaters at the first level, plant-eaters at the second, plants at the third
explanation: Each feeding level is a trophic level: plants are first, plant-eaters second, and animal-eaters third.

q: Why do different sources give different estimates — 100, 200, or 500 years — for how long plastic takes to break down?
options: Scientists disagree because plastic companies hide the true data
It depends on conditions like sunlight, heat, and air, and no one has watched plastic fully break down yet
The estimates differ because different plastics come in different colors and sizes
Older plastic breaks down much faster than newly manufactured plastic
explanation: The exact time depends on conditions such as sunlight, heat, and air, and because plastic is so new, no one has actually watched it fully break down.

q: Why is plastic in the ocean dangerous for sea animals like turtles and fish?
options: Plastic releases toxic chemicals that make the water too salty for sea life
Animals mistake plastic for food, swallow it, but cannot digest it, so their stomachs fill up
Plastic blocks sunlight from reaching coral reefs, killing the algae inside corals
Floating plastic traps sea animals and stops them from swimming to the surface
explanation: Many sea animals mistake plastic for food and swallow it, but since it cannot be digested their stomachs fill up and they can die.

q: What are fish pens in Laguna de Bay used for?
options: Storing fishing boats safely away from storms
Separating dangerous species from the rest of the lake
Raising fish like bangus and tilapia as an important food source and livelihood
Filtering pollution out of the lake water before it reaches Manila Bay
explanation: Fisherfolk use Laguna de Bay's large fish pens to raise bangus and tilapia, making it an important source of food and livelihood.

q: Approximately how tall is Maria Cristina Falls in Iligan?
options: About 45 meters high
About 98 meters high
About 150 meters high
About 200 meters high
explanation: Maria Cristina Falls in Iligan is about 98 meters high.

q: A typhoon in the Philippines and a hurricane in America are actually the same kind of storm. What is different about them?
options: Hurricanes are stronger because they form over warmer ocean water
Typhoons rotate clockwise while hurricanes rotate counter-clockwise
Only the name is different because of the region — they both have an eyewall and the same science
Typhoons have an eye but hurricanes do not form a clear eye
explanation: Typhoons and hurricanes are the same kind of storm — the name differs only because of the region, but they both have an eyewall and the same science behind them.

q: What is molasses and where does it come from?
options: A white powder left over when rice is milled and polished
The dark liquid remaining after sugar crystals are removed from sugarcane juice
A sweet syrup made by boiling coconut sap until it thickens
The foam that forms on top of fermenting fruit juice
explanation: Molasses is the dark liquid remaining after sugar crystals are removed from sugarcane juice; it is used as a food flavoring, animal feed, and can be fermented to make alcohol.

q: What shape are the columns that form when a thick lava flow cools slowly?
options: Round cylinders that stack on top of each other
Flat oval slabs that peel away in layers
Regular six-sided (hexagonal) columns
Triangular wedges that lean against each other
explanation: Columnar jointing forms when thick lava cools slowly and contracts, cracking into regular six-sided (hexagonal) columns.

q: Which pendulum swings more slowly?
options: A longer pendulum
A shorter pendulum
A heavier pendulum
A lighter pendulum
explanation: A longer pendulum swings more slowly, which is why a grandfather clock with a long pendulum ticks at a slower rate.

q: During the amihan season in the Philippines, which fishermen have calmer, safer waters for fishing?
options: Fishermen on the western side
Fishermen on the eastern side
Fishermen in the far south
Fishermen in mountain rivers
explanation: During amihan, the eastern seas are rough and dangerous, so fishermen on the western side enjoy calmer waters.

q: What causes ocean currents to move through the sea?
options: Wind, heat, and differences in saltiness and temperature
Only the Moon's gravity pulling on the water
Underwater volcanoes heating the ocean floor
Fish and whales swimming in large groups
explanation: Ocean currents move because of wind, heat, and differences in saltiness and temperature, and they carry heat around the world.

q: What can sometimes remain on the skin even after a deep wound has completely healed?
options: A scar
A bruise
A blister
A rash
explanation: Sometimes a deep wound leaves a scar even after it has fully healed.

q: Why are food cans coated with a thin layer of tin?
options: To prevent rust and keep the food's flavor
To make the can lighter and easier to carry
To help keep the food cold inside
To make the can easier to open
explanation: Tin cans are steel coated with tin to prevent rust and to avoid altering the flavor of the food stored inside.

q: Besides oxygen and nutrients, what else does blood carry to send instructions to parts of the body?
options: Hormones
Enzymes
Vitamins
Minerals
explanation: Blood also carries hormones, which are chemical messengers that tell different parts of the body what to do.

q: On the Mohs hardness scale, which mineral is rated the hardest at number 10?
options: Diamond
Talc
Quartz
Feldspar
explanation: The Mohs scale goes from 1 (softest, talc) to 10 (hardest, diamond), based on which mineral can scratch the other.

q: Which fishing methods are prohibited in the Philippines because they destroy coral reefs?
options: Dynamite and cyanide fishing
Net fishing and spearfishing
Fishing with lines and hooks
Using bamboo fish traps
explanation: Dynamite and cyanide fishing are prohibited in the Philippines because they destroy coral reefs and kill many sea creatures.

q: How is cellular respiration related to photosynthesis?
options: They are almost opposite processes: one uses glucose and oxygen, the other makes them
They are identical processes that happen in all cells
Cellular respiration only happens in plants, while photosynthesis happens in animals
Both processes release carbon dioxide and use sunlight
explanation: Cellular respiration is almost the opposite of photosynthesis: one uses glucose and oxygen, while the other makes them.

q: How does the seahorse survive even though it is one of the slowest fish?
options: It hides and clings quietly to seaweed so predators cannot easily spot it
It has a hard shell that protects it from being eaten
It releases a poison cloud to drive away predators
It swims in large groups so predators get confused
explanation: The seahorse survives by hiding and clinging quietly to seaweed, making it hard for predators to spot it.

q: What material makes up the tough walls of fungal hyphae?
options: Chitin
Cellulose
Lignin
Starch
explanation: Fungal hyphae have walls made of chitin, the same strong material found in insect shells — unlike plant walls, which are made of cellulose.

q: What is the main difference between a vaccine and medicine?
options: A vaccine is given before you get sick to prevent disease; medicine is taken when you are already sick
A vaccine cures the disease faster than medicine does
Medicine prevents disease, while a vaccine cures it
Both a vaccine and medicine are only taken when you feel sick
explanation: A vaccine prevents disease by being given before illness, while medicine is taken to treat someone who is already sick.

q: What special wing movement allows a hummingbird to hover in the air?
options: Moving its wings in a figure-eight pattern
Flapping its wings straight up and down very fast
Spreading its wings wide and gliding on air
Twisting each wing in opposite directions
explanation: A hummingbird moves its wings in a figure-eight pattern, which lets it hover in the air.

q: What do optical illusions reveal about how the brain works?
options: The brain does not always correctly interpret what the eyes see
The eyes are more powerful than the brain at judging images
Optical illusions only fool young children, not adults
The brain always sees things exactly as they really are
explanation: Optical illusions show that the brain makes predictions based on past experience and context, and does not always interpret what the eyes see correctly.

q: Which bones form a cage in the chest that protects the heart and lungs?
options: The ribs
The spine
The shoulder blades
The collar bones
explanation: The ribs form a cage in the chest that protects the heart and lungs while still letting you breathe.

q: Why does the anglerfish have its own light?
options: It lives in the very deep sea where sunlight cannot reach, so it uses its light to catch food in the dark
It uses its light to warn other fish to stay away from its territory
Its light helps it see colorful coral reefs in shallow water
It glows to attract a mate during the breeding season
explanation: The anglerfish lives in the pitch-black deep sea where sunlight cannot reach, so its own light helps it catch food in the dark.

q: Which of the following is true about arachnids compared to insects?
options: Arachnids have no antennae, but insects do
Arachnids have six legs, just like insects
Arachnids have antennae, but insects do not
Both arachnids and insects have antennae
explanation: Arachnids have no antennae, while insects do have them.

q: How does a new banana plant grow?
options: From small suckers that sprout beside the parent plant
From seeds found inside the banana fruit
From cuttings taken from the banana leaves
From spores released by the banana flower
explanation: A new banana plant grows from small suckers that sprout beside the parent plant, so no seed is needed.

q: How does a fluorescent light produce its glow?
options: From gas and a special coating that lights up
From a hot metal filament inside the bulb
From burning a small amount of oil
From a heated wire wrapped around a glass tube
explanation: A fluorescent light glows from gas and a coating that lights up, unlike an incandescent light which glows from a hot filament.

q: What type of lens do eyeglasses use to help a nearsighted person see things far away?
options: Concave lenses
Convex lenses
Flat lenses
Magnifying lenses
explanation: Concave lenses help nearsighted people see far away, while convex lenses help farsighted people see close up.

q: Where do female mosquitoes lay their eggs?
options: In stagnant (standing) water
In damp soil under leaves
On the surface of moving river water
Inside cracks in tree bark
explanation: Female mosquitoes lay eggs in stagnant water — even a spoonful is enough — so removing standing water is key to preventing dengue.

q: How is a young praying mantis different from an adult?
options: It looks like the adult but has no wings yet
It has wings but a completely different body shape
It looks nothing like an adult until its final molt
It hatches from a cocoon, unlike the adult
explanation: A young praying mantis looks like the adult but has no wings yet, and it grows by shedding its skin.

q: Why are many chrysalises colored like leaves or twigs?
options: To hide from birds and other predators
To attract bees that help keep them warm
To signal to other butterflies where to lay eggs
To soak up more sunlight and stay warm
explanation: Many chrysalises are colored like leaves or twigs to camouflage themselves and stay safe from birds and other predators.

q: After you recover from a fever, why might you not get sick from the same germ again?
options: Your body learned to recognize that germ and fights it faster the next time
The germ becomes too weak to infect anyone after it once causes a fever
Medicine you took destroyed all copies of the germ permanently
Your fever killed all germs in your body so they cannot return
explanation: After recovering from illness, your body remembers the germ and fights it faster the next time it enters, sometimes preventing you from getting sick at all.

q: What happens to a cell's DNA before the cell divides?
options: It copies all of its DNA so each new cell gets a complete set
It splits the DNA in half so each new cell gets a partial set
It destroys its DNA and rebuilds it from scratch
It transfers all its DNA to just one of the two new cells
explanation: Before a cell divides, it first copies all of its DNA so each new cell gets a complete set.

q: Which part of a plant makes food using sunlight?
options: The leaf
The root
The stem
The flower
explanation: The leaf is the plant part that makes food through photosynthesis using sunlight.

q: In what year was Jonas Salk's polio vaccine released?
explanation: Jonas Salk's polio vaccine was released in 1955.

q: Is it true that pythons grow forever without limit throughout their lives?
options: No — pythons keep growing but growth slows as they get old, so they do not become endlessly huge
Yes — pythons grow without any limit as long as they have enough food
No — pythons only grow for the first two years of their life, then stop
Yes — pythons can grow to any size, limited only by how much they eat
explanation: A python keeps growing throughout its life, but growth slows as it ages and it does not become endlessly huge.

q: What is a bulul in Ifugao culture?
options: A figure carved from hard wood and placed in the granary as a guardian of the rice harvest
A special tool made of bamboo used to plant rice on the terraces
A traditional song sung by Ifugao farmers during the harvest season
A type of rice variety grown only on the Ifugao mountain terraces
explanation: The bulul is a figure carved from hard wood by the Ifugao and placed in the granary as a guardian of the rice they grow on terraced fields.

q: Which type of cloud is high in the sky and appears thin and wispy?
options: Cirrus
Cumulus
Stratus
Nimbus
explanation: Cirrus clouds are high and wispy, while cumulus look like lumpy cotton and stratus form flat sheets spread across the sky.

q: When are carabao mangoes most plentiful and sweetest in the Philippines?
options: During the hot months of March to May
During the rainy months of July to September
During the cool months of December to February
All year round with no seasonal peak
explanation: The carabao mango is a summer fruit, most plentiful and sweetest during the hot months around March to May.

q: Where is the southern Luzon giant cloud rat (Phloeomys cumingi) found?
options: In southern Luzon
In northern Luzon
In the Visayas islands
In Mindanao
explanation: The southern Luzon giant cloud rat (Phloeomys cumingi) is darker in color and is found in southern Luzon.

q: What nickname is often given to the Banaue Rice Terraces?
options: The Eighth Wonder of the World
The Pride of Asia
The Green Crown of the Philippines
The Ancient Garden of Luzon
explanation: The Banaue Rice Terraces are often called the "Eighth Wonder of the World."

q: How do animals like bats, birds, and bees help rainforest trees grow and spread?
options: They pollinate flowers and spread seeds when they eat fruit
They carry water to trees during dry spells
They break down dead wood to fertilize the soil around tree roots
They scare away insects that would otherwise eat the tree leaves
explanation: In a rainforest, animals like bats, birds, and bees help pollinate flowers and spread seeds when they eat fruit, keeping the trees growing and spreading.

q: Why does boiling water stay at about 100 degrees Celsius even when you add more heat?
options: The extra heat goes into turning the water into steam instead of raising the temperature
Water cannot absorb heat once it reaches 100 degrees Celsius
The pot reflects the extra heat back into the stove
Adding more heat actually cools the water slightly back down
explanation: While water boils, it stays at about 100 degrees Celsius because the extra heat goes into turning the water into steam rather than raising the temperature.

q: What three things does corn need to grow?
options: Sunlight, water, and healthy soil
Only water and nutrients from fertilizer
Sunlight, cool temperatures, and lots of shade
Water, shade, and salty soil
explanation: To grow, corn needs sunlight, water, and healthy soil.

q: Which four ink colors does an inkjet printer use to reproduce all colors?
options: Cyan, magenta, yellow, and black
Red, blue, yellow, and white
Green, orange, purple, and black
Red, green, blue, and white
explanation: Inkjet printers use cyan, magenta, yellow, and black (CMYK) inks to reproduce all colors through subtractive color mixing.

q: How do fossils in deeper rock layers generally compare to fossils found higher up?
options: Fossils in deeper layers are often quite different from species alive today, while those in higher layers resemble living species more
Deeper layers always contain larger and more complete fossils than higher layers
Fossils in deeper layers are younger and better preserved than those near the surface
Fossils in higher layers are always older and harder to identify
explanation: Fossils in higher (more recently deposited) layers usually resemble species alive today, while fossils in deeper (older) layers are often quite different.

q: Is it true that only the tip of the tongue can taste sweetness?
options: No — almost all parts of the tongue can sense all the tastes; separate taste zones are a myth
Yes — the tip tastes sweet, the back tastes bitter, and the sides taste sour
Yes — each area of the tongue has special taste cells for just one flavor
No — the tongue cannot taste sweetness at all; only the nose detects sweet smells
explanation: The idea of separate taste zones on the tongue is a myth; science has shown that almost all parts of the tongue can sense all the tastes.

q: Why do complex carbohydrates like brown rice provide more steady energy than simple sugars like soft drinks?
options: Complex carbohydrates digest slowly and release energy steadily; simple sugars enter the blood quickly causing rapid spikes
Complex carbohydrates have more calories, so they last much longer in the body
Simple sugars are always unhealthy, while complex carbohydrates never raise blood sugar
Brown rice releases energy faster than soft drinks because it is solid, not liquid
explanation: Simple sugars enter the blood quickly causing rapid energy spikes, while complex carbohydrates digest slowly and provide steady energy.

q: What should you do if a pet shows signs of being scared when you approach it?
options: Stop coming closer and give it space
Move faster so it gets used to you quickly
Make a loud noise to distract it from its fear
Pick it up right away so it feels safe with you
explanation: We should be gentle and kind to pets, and stop coming closer when they show signs of being scared.

q: How does a fish use its swim bladder to control how deep it floats in the water?
options: By adding or releasing gas in the swim bladder
By flapping its fins faster or slower
By drinking more water to become heavier
By curling or straightening its body
explanation: By adding or releasing gas in the swim bladder, a fish adjusts how deep it floats in the water.

q: What is a 'supermoon'?
options: When the Moon is at its closest point to Earth in its elliptical orbit, appearing larger and brighter
When the Moon is at its farthest point from Earth and reflects the most sunlight
When the Moon passes directly between the Earth and the Sun
When the Moon rises earlier than usual during a full moon phase
explanation: A supermoon occurs when the Moon is at its closest point to Earth (perigee) in its elliptical orbit, making it appear larger and brighter in the sky.

q: What is true about vitamins and energy?
options: Vitamins do not give energy by themselves, but the body needs them to use food properly
Vitamins are the main source of energy in our diet
Vitamins give quick energy like sugar does
Vitamins only provide energy when combined with proteins
explanation: Vitamins do not give energy by themselves, but the body needs them to use food properly.

q: What determines the color of light an LED produces?
options: The semiconductor material it is made from
The amount of electric current flowing through it
The thickness of the glass cover over the LED
The temperature of the room where it is used
explanation: An LED's color depends on its semiconductor material — different materials like gallium arsenide, gallium phosphide, or gallium nitride produce different colors.

q: Which Philippine government agency manages the Philippine Science High School System?
options: DOST (Department of Science and Technology)
DepEd (Department of Education)
CHED (Commission on Higher Education)
NEDA (National Economic and Development Authority)
explanation: The Philippine Science High School System is managed by DOST and provides high-level science and mathematics education to talented students.

q: Which dating method is used to find the age of things less than 50,000 years old?
options: Carbon-14
Potassium-argon
Uranium-lead
Rubidium-strontium
explanation: Carbon-14 is used for radiometric dating of things less than 50,000 years old, while potassium-argon and uranium-lead are used for much older rocks.

q: Which type of radiation requires thick lead or concrete to stop it because it is so penetrating?
options: Gamma radiation
Alpha radiation
Beta radiation
Infrared radiation
explanation: Gamma radiation is the most penetrating of the three types of radiation and needs thick lead or concrete to stop it.

q: Whose face appeared on the Penny Black, the world's first postage stamp?
options: Queen Victoria of Britain
King George III of Britain
Napoleon Bonaparte of France
Abraham Lincoln of the United States
explanation: The face on the Penny Black, the first postage stamp, was that of Queen Victoria of Britain.

q: Because of Earth's rotation, in which direction do ocean currents curve in the northern hemisphere?
options: To the right
To the left
Straight downward
Straight toward the equator
explanation: Because Earth rotates, the Coriolis effect causes currents to curve to the right in the northern hemisphere and to the left in the southern hemisphere.

q: Which material has the highest density — meaning the most mass packed into the same space?
options: Gold
Iron
Lead
Silver
explanation: Gold has the highest density of common metals at 19.3 g/cm³, making it heavier than the same volume of iron, silver, or lead.

q: What does voltage do in an electric circuit?
options: It provides the push that drives electrons around the circuit
It stores electricity in a battery for later use
It measures how much current has already been used
It slows electrons down to prevent overheating
explanation: Voltage is the electrical "push" that drives electrons around a circuit, and it is measured in volts.

q: A car travels 60 km in one hour but stops at red lights along the way. What does 60 km/h describe?
options: The car's average speed for the whole trip
The car's speed at every single moment of the trip
The car's maximum speed reached during the trip
The car's speed while stopped at the red light
explanation: Average speed is total distance divided by total time for the whole trip, so 60 km/h is still the average even though the car was stopped at some moments.

q: A snake flicks its tongue in and out and then touches it to the roof of its mouth. What is the snake doing?
options: Reading scents it collected with its tongue
Feeling the temperature of the air around it
Tasting the ground to look for water
Communicating with other snakes nearby
explanation: A snake touches its tongue to the Jacobson's organ on the roof of its mouth to read the scents it caught in the air.

q: Your doctor says you have the flu. Why would taking antibiotics NOT help you get better?
options: Antibiotics can only kill bacteria, and the flu is caused by a virus
Antibiotics are too strong and would make the flu worse
The flu is caused by fungi, which antibiotics cannot reach
Antibiotics only work on infections outside the body
explanation: Antibiotics kill bacteria but have no effect on viruses, so they cannot cure colds or flu, which are caused by viruses.

q: Which sense organ covers the entire body and lets you feel touch or heat anywhere?
options: The skin
The nose
The tongue
The ears
explanation: The skin is our largest sense organ because it covers the whole body, allowing us to feel touch or heat on any part of us.

q: Which small brain region sends signals to control your body temperature and tell you when you are hungry?
options: The hypothalamus
The cerebellum
The medulla oblongata
The hippocampus
explanation: The hypothalamus is the small brain region that regulates body temperature, hunger, and thirst by sending signals to other body systems.

q: The musang (alamid) of the Philippines is active at night and looks a little like a cat. What kind of animal is it really?
options: A small furry mammal
A large reptile
A type of wild cat
A nocturnal bird
explanation: The palm civet (musang/alamid) is a small furry mammal, not a cat, even though the two look somewhat alike.

q: A wooden post looks perfectly solid on the outside, but it suddenly collapses. What insect most likely caused this damage?
options: Termites, which eat wood from the inside out
Ants, which carry pieces of wood away overnight
Beetles, which scratch the surface until it cracks
Wasps, which build nests that crush the wood
explanation: Termites eat wood from the inside, leaving it looking solid on the outside while it becomes hollow and weak inside.

q: Your classmate says she got astigmatism from reading in the dark. What do we actually know about astigmatism?
options: Most people are simply born with that eye shape, and it is not contagious
It spreads from person to person through shared eyeglasses
It is always caused by too much screen time as a child
It develops only in adults who never wore sunglasses
explanation: Astigmatism is not contagious and is usually not caused by habits like reading in the dark — most people are simply born with that eye shape.

q: Where does a leech place the eggs it lays?
options: Inside a pouch called a cocoon
Directly into the host animal's skin
In a nest built from mud and leaves
Attached to underwater rocks in a row
explanation: A leech lays eggs and places them inside a protective pouch called a cocoon.

q: Which bear holds the record as the largest type of brown bear on Earth?
options: The Kodiak bear of Alaska
The grizzly bear of Canada
The polar bear of the Arctic
The sun bear of Southeast Asia
explanation: The Kodiak bear of Alaska is the largest brown bear and can weigh up to about 720 kilograms.

q: What is a newly hatched baby echidna called?
options: A puggle
A joey
A kit
A cub
explanation: A newly hatched baby echidna is called a puggle, and it is very tiny when it hatches.

q: When you have a bad cold and a stuffy nose, why does your food seem to have less flavor?
options: Your nose is blocked, so smell cannot help your sense of taste
Your taste buds are covered by mucus and cannot work
Your body is too tired to send taste signals to the brain
Fever raises your body temperature and changes how food tastes
explanation: When your nose is stuffy, your sense of smell is blocked, and since smell helps you taste, food seems bland.

q: When you touch something very hot and pull your hand away instantly, where does the signal travel before reaching your muscles?
options: From your skin through nerves to the spinal cord, then back to the muscle
From your skin directly up to your brain, then down to your hand
From your muscles to your brain, then back down to your skin
From your spinal cord to your eyes first, then to the muscle
explanation: A reflex travels along the reflex arc: skin sensor to nerves to spinal cord and back to the muscle, which is why it happens so fast.

q: How does ultraviolet (UV) light kill bacteria and viruses in water?
options: UV damages the DNA of microbes so they cannot reproduce
UV heats the water until microbes boil and die
UV makes the water too acidic for microbes to survive
UV reflects off microbes and pushes them out of the water
explanation: The high energy of UV light damages the DNA of microbes, preventing them from reproducing and effectively killing them.

q: The binturong (bearcat) found in Palawan has a special ability. What does it use its tail for?
options: To grip tree branches while climbing
To communicate danger signals to other bearcats
To store fat for times when food is scarce
To splash water on prey below
explanation: The binturong uses its prehensile tail to grip tree branches, helping it move through the forest canopy.

q: Why does an ordinary plant wilt when it is planted in salty soil?
options: Salt in the soil pulls water back out of the plant's roots
Salt clogs the tiny holes on leaves so the plant cannot breathe
Salt makes the soil too hard for roots to grow deeper
Salt blocks sunlight from reaching the plant's leaves
explanation: Salt in the soil pulls water back out of a plant's roots by osmosis, causing the plant to lose water and wilt.

q: You can barely hear your neighbor talking through a thick concrete wall. Why?
options: Thick solid walls block most sound, making it much fainter
Sound waves travel only through air and stop completely at any wall
Concrete absorbs all sound and converts it into heat
Sound waves speed up inside the wall and arrive too fast to hear
explanation: Thick, solid walls block most sound, so it is heard much fainter on the other side.

q: About how wide is the calm eye at the center of a typhoon?
options: About 30 to 65 kilometers across
About 5 to 10 kilometers across
About 200 to 300 kilometers across
About 1 to 2 kilometers across
explanation: The eye of a typhoon is usually about 30 to 65 kilometers across.

q: What does the mechanical advantage of a machine tell you?
options: How much the machine multiplies your input force
How fast the machine can do a job compared to a person
How much electricity the machine uses per hour
How heavy the machine itself is compared to its load
explanation: Mechanical advantage tells how much a machine multiplies your force — for example, a lever can lift something much heavier than you could lift alone.

q: Iron is dropped into a copper sulfate solution and copper forms on the iron. What type of chemical reaction is this?
options: A single replacement reaction, where iron displaces copper
A double replacement reaction, where two compounds swap parts
A synthesis reaction, where two substances join to form one
A decomposition reaction, where one substance breaks into two
explanation: In a single replacement reaction, a more reactive element (iron) displaces another element (copper) from its compound.

q: The horseshoe crab has no jaws. How does it grind up its food?
options: Spiny parts at the bases of its legs grind food as it walks
It swallows food whole and digests it with strong stomach acid
It uses its hard shell edge like a blade to cut food apart
It squirts digestive fluid onto food before sucking it in
explanation: The horseshoe crab has spiny parts at the bases of its legs that grind up food and push it into the mouth located in the middle of its legs.

q: Why do Philippine cobras stay active all year and never need to hibernate?
options: The Philippines is warm all year, so snakes never need to sleep through a cold season
Philippine cobras have thicker scales that keep them warm even in winter
Cobras eat so much during summer that they have enough energy for the cold months
Philippine cobras migrate to warmer islands instead of hibernating
explanation: The Philippines has a warm climate all year, so snakes like the Philippine cobra never face a cold winter and have no need to hibernate.

q: Why is it much darker on the forest floor than at the top of a rainforest?
options: Leaves in the layers above block the sunlight before it reaches the bottom
The forest floor is underground, so sunlight cannot enter at all
Trees at the bottom grow so tall that they shade the top layer
Rain clouds form inside the forest and block light from entering
explanation: As you move down through the rainforest layers, the leaves above block more and more sunlight, so the forest floor receives very little light.

q: In a chemical reaction, heat is released and you feel warmth. What does this tell you about the energy of the products compared to the starting materials?
options: The products have lower energy than the reactants, so the extra energy was released as heat
The products have higher energy than the reactants because heat was added to them
The products and reactants have the same energy because energy is always conserved
The reactants release energy only after being cooled down below room temperature
explanation: In an exothermic reaction, the products end up at a lower energy level than the reactants, and the difference is released as heat.

q: What type of germ causes common illnesses like the cold and flu?
options: Viruses
Bacteria
Fungi
Parasites
explanation: The common cold, cough, and flu are caused by viruses, not bacteria.

q: What would most likely happen to a plant that had no roots at all?
options: It would fall over easily and wilt quickly because it cannot drink water
It would grow sideways along the ground and still get water from rain
It would live fine as long as someone watered its leaves every day
It would grow faster because the stem could take in water directly
explanation: Without roots, a plant would fall over easily and could not absorb water, so it would wilt quickly.

q: Once an insect falls inside a pitcher plant, what stops it from climbing back out?
options: Tiny hairs inside the pitcher point downward, blocking the insect's escape
The plant releases a sticky liquid that glues the insect's feet to the wall
The walls of the pitcher are perfectly smooth and too slippery to climb
The plant quickly closes a lid over the opening to trap the insect inside
explanation: Tiny downward-pointing hairs inside the pitcher prevent a trapped insect from climbing back out.

q: Litmus paper turns red in both vinegar and kalamansi juice, even though they are different liquids. Why do both turn it the same color?
options: Both release hydrogen ions, and it is the hydrogen that changes the indicator's color
Both contain the same amount of water, and water always turns litmus red
Both are orange-colored liquids and that color transfers to the litmus paper
Both have the same smell, which reacts chemically with the paper dye
explanation: Both vinegar and kalamansi are acids because they release hydrogen ions, and it is the hydrogen that causes litmus to turn red.

q: In the 'Go, Grow, Glow' food guide, which group includes vegetables and fruits that protect the body?
options: Glow foods
Go foods
Grow foods
Fuel foods
explanation: 'Glow' foods such as vegetables and fruit provide vitamins and minerals that protect and keep the body healthy.

q: How does the anglerfish catch its prey?
options: It stays still and ambushes prey that comes close to its lure
It chases prey at high speed through the deep ocean
It uses electric shocks to stun fish swimming nearby
It traps prey inside a bubble of mucus it produces
explanation: The anglerfish is an ambush predator — it waits quietly and catches prey that is attracted to and comes near its lure.

q: Besides making sugar, what is one direct way people enjoy sugarcane?
options: They drink its fresh juice or chew the stalk to taste its sweetness
They grind the dried stalks into flour for baking bread
They boil the roots to make a sweet tea
They press the leaves to extract a sweet syrup
explanation: Fresh cane juice can be drunk directly, or you can chew the stalk to taste its natural sweetness straight from the plant.

q: Why do some animals like bears go into a very long sleep during winter?
options: There is no food in winter, so their bodies slow down to save energy until warmth and food return
They get sick from the cold temperatures and need to rest until they recover
They are protecting their young by keeping them warm inside a den
Winter days are too short, so they sleep to avoid being out in the dark
explanation: Hibernation lets animals like bears survive a cold season with no food by slowing their bodies down to save energy until conditions improve.

q: When an atom gains an extra electron, what does it become?
options: A negative ion called an anion
A positive ion called a cation
A neutral particle called a neutron
A radioactive atom called an isotope
explanation: When an atom gains an electron it becomes negatively charged and is called an anion; losing an electron makes it a cation (positive).

q: What often causes a 'fish kill' in Laguna de Bay, where many fish suddenly die?
options: Oxygen levels in the water drop too low for fish to survive
The lake water becomes too cold during the rainy season
Fishermen accidentally use the wrong type of fish net
Typhoon winds push all the fish into one crowded area
explanation: Fish kills in Laguna de Bay often happen when oxygen levels drop because of heat, weather changes, or overcrowding in fish pens.

q: How long is one year on Mars compared to one year on Earth?
options: About 687 Earth days — almost twice as long
About 365 Earth days — exactly the same length
About 24 Earth days — much shorter than Earth's year
About 4,000 Earth days — more than ten times longer
explanation: One year on Mars lasts about 687 Earth days, which is almost twice the length of a year on Earth.

q: After a jellyfish's stinging cells stun its prey, what happens next?
options: The tentacles slowly carry the food to the central mouth to be digested
The prey dissolves immediately in the stinging fluid released by the cells
The jellyfish swims away and returns later when the prey stops moving
The prey is stored in a pouch on the outside of the body for later use
explanation: After stinging cells catch and stun prey, a cnidarian's tentacles slowly carry the food to its central mouth, where it is digested inside the body.

q: The platypus is unusual compared to most other mammals. What makes it so different?
options: It lays eggs but still feeds its babies milk
It breathes underwater like a fish but is warm-blooded
It has no fur even though it is classified as a mammal
It gives birth to live young but never nurses them with milk
explanation: The platypus is an unusual mammal because it lays eggs, yet it still feeds its young with milk just like other mammals.

q: How does a woodpecker keep its balance while pecking into a tree trunk?
options: It uses its stiff tail feathers as a prop against the trunk
It grips the bark with extra-long curved claws on each foot
It wraps its wings tightly around the trunk for support
It inserts its beak into the wood to lock itself in place
explanation: A woodpecker uses its stiff tail feathers as a brace or prop against the tree trunk while it pecks, helping it stay stable.

q: What happens when too much current flows through a circuit that has a circuit breaker?
options: The circuit breaker automatically switches off the current to protect the circuit
The circuit breaker stores the extra current and releases it slowly later
The circuit breaker speeds the current up so devices can handle it better
The circuit breaker signals a light to warn the user and keeps the current flowing
explanation: A circuit breaker automatically switches off the current when too much flows through, and it can be switched back on once the problem is fixed.

q: About what percentage of Earth's atmosphere is nitrogen?
options: About 78%
About 21%
About 50%
About 1%
explanation: Earth's atmosphere is about 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen, with nitrogen being by far the largest component.

q: What is the capital city of Italy?
options: Rome
Milan
Venice
Florence
explanation: The capital of Italy is Rome.

q: Why is fresh fruit generally more nutritious than fruit that has been stored for a long time?
options: Some vitamins fade the longer produce is stored or exposed to heat and light
Stored fruit gains extra sugar that replaces the vitamins it originally had
Vitamins move from the fruit into the container it is stored in over time
Refrigeration destroys vitamins, so stored fruit always has fewer nutrients
explanation: Some vitamins slowly fade from fruits and vegetables the longer they are stored or exposed to heat and light, making fresh produce more nutritious.

q: How can a ray find a crab that is completely buried under sand?
options: Special sensors on its snout detect the faint electricity the crab's body produces
Its excellent eyesight can see the outline of the crab through the thin layer of sand
It smells chemicals released by the crab as it breathes underwater
It feels the vibrations made by the crab moving its legs under the sand
explanation: A ray has special electroreceptors on its snout that detect the faint electrical fields produced by animals, letting it find prey hidden in sand.

q: Why does aluminum resist corrosion better than iron?
options: Aluminum forms a thin protective layer on its surface that blocks further corrosion
Aluminum contains no iron, and only iron-based metals can corrode
Aluminum is always painted at the factory, and the paint keeps moisture out
Aluminum is a liquid at room temperature and does not react with air
explanation: Aluminum does not rust like iron because it naturally forms a thin oxide layer that blocks further corrosion.

q: Why is Apo Island in Negros Oriental famous in the Philippines?
options: It is a community-managed marine sanctuary where fish populations recovered after protection began
It is the deepest fishing ground in the Philippines and exports the most tuna
It is the only island where the rare tamaraw now lives in the wild
It has the largest coral reef in Southeast Asia, protected by the national government
explanation: Apo Island is a successful community-managed marine sanctuary — after protection was established, fish populations recovered and it became a model for other communities.

q: What happens to a satellite that is traveling too slowly as it tries to orbit Earth?
options: It falls back toward Earth because its speed is not enough to stay in orbit
It flies off into outer space because low speed reduces gravity's pull
It stays at the same height but drifts sideways out of its path
It speeds up automatically and returns to the correct orbit on its own
explanation: A satellite needs just the right sideways speed to orbit — too slow and gravity pulls it back down toward Earth.

q: What is the role of the Philippine Supreme Court?
options: It is the highest court in the country and makes sure laws follow the 1987 Constitution
It writes new laws and sends them to the President for approval
It manages the national budget and checks government spending
It oversees elections and counts the votes for national positions
explanation: The Philippine Supreme Court is the highest court in the country and ensures that laws comply with the 1987 Constitution.

q: Why is moss useful for keeping soil from drying out quickly?
options: Moss soaks up and holds water like a sponge, keeping soil moist and slowing rain runoff.
Moss grows very deep roots that pull water up from underground into the soil.
Moss releases a waxy coating that seals moisture inside the soil.
Moss breaks down into nutrients that help soil hold water.
explanation: Moss acts like a sponge that soaks up and stores lots of water, helping keep the soil moist and slow down rain runoff.

q: Where did the world's first powered airplane flight take place?
options: Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, USA
Dayton, Ohio, USA
Paris, France
London, England
explanation: The first powered airplane flight took place at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, in the United States.

q: At what place was Jose Rizal executed by the Spanish colonial government?
options: Bagumbayan, now known as Luneta or Rizal Park
Fort Santiago in Intramuros, Manila
Paco Cemetery in Manila
Calamba, Laguna, his birthplace
explanation: Jose Rizal was executed at Bagumbayan, now called Luneta or Rizal Park.

q: How does electricity travel from a power plant to homes in a distant city?
options: Through long wires called transmission lines
Through underground water pipes that carry electrical current
By being stored in large batteries and shipped by trucks
Through wireless radio towers that beam electricity through the air
explanation: Electricity from the power plant travels through long wires called transmission lines to towns and cities.

q: How is cassava planted?
options: A piece of its stem is buried directly in the soil
Seeds are soaked in water and then scattered on the ground
A cutting from the root is dried and then planted
Leaves are pressed into the soil to grow new plants
explanation: Cassava is planted using pieces of its stem, not seeds — a piece of stem is simply buried in soil and it grows.

q: Which of the following everyday objects uses a screw as a simple machine?
options: A jar lid that twists open and shut
A door that swings on hinges
A ramp used to push a heavy box up
A pulley used to lift a bucket of water
explanation: Jar lids, bottle caps, and light bulb bases all use a screw.

q: How do baleen whales catch their tiny food from the ocean?
options: They strain water through comb-like filters inside their mouth instead of biting with teeth.
They use their teeth to grind up small shrimp before swallowing them.
They suck in whole schools of fish and digest them slowly.
They use long tongue muscles to trap small creatures against the roof of their mouth.
explanation: Some whales have no teeth but instead have comb-like baleen filters that strain tiny food from the water.

q: Why is the nautilus called a 'living fossil'?
options: It has barely changed in appearance for millions of years.
Its shell is made of the same minerals as ancient rock.
It can only survive in places where fossils are commonly found.
Scientists discovered it by studying fossil records, not the ocean.
explanation: The nautilus is called a 'living fossil' because it has barely changed for millions of years.

q: How do doctors confirm that a patient has schistosomiasis?
options: They examine a stool sample under a microscope to look for blood fluke eggs.
They do a skin-prick test to check for an allergic reaction to the parasite.
They take an X-ray of the liver to look for visible damage caused by the worm.
They measure the patient's temperature over several days to track the pattern of fever.
explanation: A stool sample examined under a microscope for blood fluke eggs confirms schistosomiasis; a blood test can also be used.

q: Where in the eye can an uneven curve cause astigmatism?
options: Either in the cornea at the front or in the lens inside the eye
Only in the retina at the back of the eye
Only in the cornea; the lens cannot cause astigmatism
Only in the optic nerve that sends signals to the brain
explanation: Astigmatism usually starts in the cornea but can also come from the lens inside the eye, because both bend light.

q: Which statement about Rafflesia in the Philippines is correct?
options: Several Rafflesia species are endemic to the Philippines, found in places like the Visayas and Mindanao.
Only one Rafflesia species exists in the Philippines, found only in Luzon.
Rafflesia is common and easy to grow because it spreads its own seeds widely.
The Philippines has no native Rafflesia; all specimens were brought from Borneo.
explanation: Several Rafflesia species are endemic to the Philippines, including Rafflesia speciosa in the Visayas and others in Mindanao; all are rare.

q: What is the correct order of a frog's life cycle?
options: Egg → Tadpole → Frog
Tadpole → Egg → Frog
Egg → Frog → Tadpole
Frog → Frog → Egg
explanation: A frog starts as an egg, then becomes a tadpole, and finally grows into a full frog.

q: Where does a tree store the carbon it takes in from the air?
options: Inside its trunk, branches, and roots as it grows
It releases all the carbon back into the air at night
In its leaves, which then fall and bury the carbon in the soil
In the water it absorbs through its roots
explanation: A tree stores carbon inside its trunk, branches, and roots as it grows, which is why big trees help lower carbon in the air.

q: How does a remora attach itself to a shark?
options: Using a flat suction disc on top of its head
By wrapping its long tail tightly around the shark's fin
By clinging on with sharp claws on its belly
By biting gently into the shark's skin with strong jaws
explanation: The remora has a flat suction disc on its head that it uses to stick onto a shark's body.

q: Why do Philippine fishermen catch fewer fish when mangroves are cut down?
options: Because mangroves are a nursery and shelter for young fish, which disappear without them.
Because mangroves provide food that adult fish eat directly.
Because mangroves block sea currents that carry adult fish toward the shore.
Because the roots of mangroves clean the water and without them the sea becomes too salty.
explanation: Mangroves are a home and nursery for young fish; cut them down and the fish have no shelter, so fishermen catch less.

q: Why are small fish like dilis and tuyo especially good for building strong bones?
options: You eat them bones and all, and fish bones are full of calcium.
They contain more protein than any other food, which builds bone tissue.
They are cooked in vinegar, which releases iron that strengthens bones.
Their soft scales are made of a mineral that the body turns into bone.
explanation: Fish bones are full of calcium, and since you eat tiny fish like dilis and tuyo whole — bones included — they really help make your bones strong.

q: What are the two main advantages a colugo gets by gliding?
options: It can escape from predators and save energy when moving between trees.
It can find food faster and keep its body temperature cool.
It can communicate with other colugos and mark its territory.
It can dry its fur after rain and spot enemies from a higher position.
explanation: By gliding, the colugo can escape predators and save energy when moving from tree to tree.

q: What did Galileo Galilei discover in 1610 that helped support the idea that Earth goes around the Sun?
options: Jupiter's four large moons, craters on the Moon, and the phases of Venus
The rings of Saturn and the distance between Earth and the Sun
The existence of comets and the shape of the Milky Way galaxy
The spin of Earth and the true size of the Moon
explanation: In 1610, Galileo discovered Jupiter's four large moons, the Moon's craters, and Venus's phases — all supporting Copernicus's heliocentric model.

q: What are ornithopters, and what inspired engineers to build them?
options: Machines that flap wings like a bird, inspired by studying how birds fly
Machines that spin rotors like a helicopter, inspired by dragonfly wings
Machines that glide without flapping, inspired by how albatrosses soar
Tiny underwater robots that mimic the wing motion of penguins
explanation: Ornithopters are machines that flap wings like a bird; engineers study bird flight to design better small flying machines and drones.

q: How do mangroves protect Philippine coastal towns during typhoons?
options: Their thick roots and branches block big waves and storm surge like a natural wall.
They release chemicals into the sea that calm the waves before they reach shore.
They grow so tall that they redirect wind upward, away from houses.
They absorb the rain so much that floodwaters never reach coastal roads.
explanation: The thick roots and branches of mangroves block big waves and storm surge during typhoons, acting like a natural wall for coastal towns.

q: What is the capital city of the province of Davao del Sur?
options: Digos City
Davao City
General Santos City
Tagum City
explanation: The capital of Davao del Sur is Digos City, not Davao City.

q: Which feature makes the needlefish easy to recognize?
options: It is long and thin with a pointed, needle-like jaw.
It is round and flat like a disc with a beak-shaped mouth.
It has a very short body but an extremely long tail fin.
It has two long spines on its back that look like needles.
explanation: The needlefish is a long, thin fish with a pointed, needle-like jaw.

q: Which insect holds the record for being the heaviest in the world?
options: The Goliath beetle from Africa
The Atlas moth from Southeast Asia
The titan beetle from South America
The elephant beetle from Central America
explanation: The heaviest insect is the Goliath beetle, a large beetle from Africa.

q: Why do phytoplankton live near the surface of the ocean rather than in deep water?
options: Sunlight they need for photosynthesis can only reach the upper layers of water.
The water near the surface is saltier, which phytoplankton need to survive.
Deep-water currents are too strong for phytoplankton to stay in one place.
The seafloor is too dark for phytoplankton to find the minerals they eat.
explanation: Phytoplankton live near the ocean surface because that is where the sunlight they need can reach.

q: Which is the only monkey that is native to the Philippines?
options: The long-tailed macaque
The proboscis monkey
The tarsier
The crab-eating gibbon
explanation: The long-tailed macaque is the only kind of monkey native to the Philippines.

q: How does Venus's surface gravity compare to Earth's?
options: Venus's gravity is almost as strong as Earth's, at about 8.9 m/s² versus Earth's 9.8 m/s².
Venus has much weaker gravity than Earth, about half as strong.
Venus has stronger gravity than Earth because it is closer to the Sun.
Venus has no measurable gravity because it has no moon to create a gravitational pull.
explanation: Venus's surface gravity is about 8.9 m/s², almost as strong as Earth's 9.8 m/s².

q: How do echinoderms like sea stars get the oxygen they need?
options: Through their tube feet and tiny skin gills that absorb oxygen from the water
Through gills on the sides of their bodies, similar to a fish
By swimming to the surface to breathe air directly like a whale
By absorbing oxygen through a special organ inside their central disk
explanation: Echinoderms breathe through their tube feet and tiny skin gills that take oxygen from the water.

q: How do many single-celled pond micro-organisms reproduce?
options: They split their single body into two identical cells.
They lay tiny eggs that hatch into new micro-organisms.
They merge with another micro-organism to form a larger one, then separate.
They release spores into the water that later grow into new cells.
explanation: Many pond micro-organisms reproduce by splitting their single body into two, which lets them multiply very quickly.

q: What famous nickname are the Banaue Rice Terraces often given?
options: The Eighth Wonder of the World
The Crown of the Cordillera
The Stairway to Heaven
The Green Wall of Asia
explanation: The Banaue Rice Terraces are often called the 'Eighth Wonder of the World.'

q: Why are electric wires made of metal?
options: Because most metals conduct electricity well.
Because metals are flexible enough to bend around corners easily.
Because metals are lighter than other materials, making wires easy to hang.
Because metals are waterproof, protecting the electricity from rain.
explanation: Most metals conduct both heat and electricity well, which is why wires are made of metal.

q: What happens to a healthy cell after new viruses are fully made inside it?
options: The cell is often burst open as new viruses escape to infect more healthy cells.
The cell repairs itself and becomes immune to further virus attacks.
The cell shrinks and is absorbed safely by the immune system.
The cell stays alive and keeps producing viruses indefinitely without breaking.
explanation: New viruses leave the cell, often by bursting it open, and then go on to infect other healthy cells.

q: Why do deer and mouse-deer run away so quickly when they sense danger?
options: Because they are prey animals hunted by larger predators like pythons and eagles.
Because they protect their territory from other deer that want to take their food.
Because they are chasing after the insects and small animals they eat.
Because running exercises their legs so they can grow bigger and stronger.
explanation: Deer and mouse-deer are prey for bigger animals such as pythons and eagles, so they run away quickly.

q: Why do baseball batters and soccer players follow through with their swing or kick instead of stopping right at the ball?
options: Keeping contact longer with the same force produces a bigger change in motion, sending the ball farther.
Following through transfers weight to the back foot, which improves balance after impact.
Stopping at the ball would break the bat or injure the foot from the sudden shock.
Following through redirects the force sideways to make the ball curve in the air.
explanation: The longer a force of the same strength acts, the bigger the change in motion — that is why a follow-through sends the ball farther.

q: What is the purpose of molting in birds?
options: Old feathers fall out and are replaced by new ones so the bird can keep flying well.
The bird sheds feathers to make itself lighter before a long migration.
The bird loses feathers to cool itself down during hot weather.
Old feathers are eaten by the bird to recycle nutrients before winter.
explanation: From time to time a bird's old feathers fall out and are replaced by new ones so it can keep flying well.

q: How did ancient builders move huge heavy stones to higher positions?
options: They put logs as rollers under the stones to reduce friction, then used ramps to raise them.
They tied ropes to the stones and had hundreds of workers lift straight up.
They carved the stones into spheres so they would roll by themselves.
They flooded the ground with water so the stones could float and be pushed easily.
explanation: Ancient builders used logs as rollers to reduce friction when dragging heavy stones, and used ramps to raise them to higher positions.

q: Which mountain is the highest peak in the Visayas region of the Philippines?
options: Mount Kanlaon on Negros island
Mount Apo on Mindanao island
Mount Pulag in the Cordillera
Mount Mayon on Luzon island
explanation: The highest mountain in the Visayas is Mount Kanlaon, located on Negros island.

q: Which best describes where tardigrades can be found on Earth?
options: Almost everywhere — from the highest mountains to the deepest seas.
Only in tropical rainforests where humidity is constantly high.
Only in polar ice caps and very cold mountain streams.
Only in soil, because they cannot survive in water.
explanation: Tardigrades are found almost everywhere on Earth, from the highest mountains to the deepest seas.

q: What must happen BEFORE you pour off the clear liquid in the process of decantation?
options: The heavy solid must settle to the bottom of the container first.
The mixture must be heated until the liquid turns into steam.
The liquid must be filtered through paper to remove all particles.
The solid must be scooped out using a spoon before pouring begins.
explanation: In decantation, the heavy solid is allowed to settle to the bottom first, then the clear liquid on top is gently poured off without disturbing the sediment.

q: What is ozone made of?
options: Three oxygen atoms joined together (O3)
Two oxygen atoms and one nitrogen atom
One oxygen atom and two hydrogen atoms
Four oxygen atoms bonded in a ring
explanation: Ozone is a form of oxygen made of three oxygen atoms joined together, written as O3.

q: What is the MAIN difference in purpose between sweat and urine in the human body?
options: Urine is the body's main blood-cleaner; sweat is mainly the body's cooler.
Sweat is the body's main blood-cleaner; urine is mainly the body's cooler.
Both have the same main job: removing carbon dioxide from the blood.
Sweat removes salt only; urine removes only excess sugar from the blood.
explanation: Urine (from the kidneys) is the body's main blood-cleaner, while sweat is mainly the body's cooler; both remove some water and waste.

q: Why are bananas curved instead of straight?
options: As they grow, they turn upward toward sunlight instead of hanging straight down.
They are squeezed into a curved shape by the tight bunch they grow in.
The heavy weight of the banana pulls one side down more than the other.
They grow along a curved vine and take on that shape permanently.
explanation: Bananas are curved because as they grow, they turn upward toward the sunlight instead of hanging straight down.

q: What part of Earth's structure makes up each tectonic plate?
options: The rigid outer layer called the lithosphere
The hot, flowing layer called the asthenosphere
The liquid outer core deep below the surface
The soft inner mantle just below the crust
explanation: Each tectonic plate is made of the rigid outer part of Earth called the lithosphere.

q: If an astronaut goes from Earth to the Moon, what happens to their mass?
options: Their mass stays the same; only their weight changes because the Moon has less gravity.
Their mass decreases because the Moon's weaker gravity pulls less on their body.
Both their mass and weight stay exactly the same as on Earth.
Their mass increases slightly because they are farther from Earth's gravity.
explanation: Your mass stays the same on Earth and on the Moon; only your weight changes because gravity is different.

q: What does the inside of an atom mostly consist of?
options: Empty space surrounding a tiny nucleus
Tightly packed protons and neutrons with no empty space
A solid core of electrons with a thin outer shell
Equally spaced particles that fill the entire atom uniformly
explanation: An atom is mostly empty space surrounding a tiny nucleus.

q: What makes double fertilization in flowering plants unique?
options: One sperm fertilizes the egg to form the embryo, and a second sperm fertilizes another cell to form the endosperm that feeds it.
Two eggs are fertilized by the same sperm cell to produce twins inside the seed.
A single sperm cell fertilizes the egg twice in a row to create extra food reserves.
Both the male and female parts of the same flower fertilize each other at the same time.
explanation: In angiosperms, one sperm forms the embryo and another forms the endosperm that feeds it — a process called double fertilization.

q: Which statement about Philippine animals is TRUE?
options: Most Philippine animals are harmless and are an important part of nature.
Most Philippine animals are dangerous because the country has so many different species.
The more kinds of animals a place has, the more dangerous it is to live there.
Animals in the Philippines are more dangerous than animals in other countries.
explanation: Most Philippine animals are harmless and are an important part of nature; having many species does not mean most are dangerous.

q: What is a community or urban garden?
options: A place in the city where residents grow vegetables and plants together, providing fresh food and cleaner air.
A large private farm on the edge of the city that sells produce to supermarkets.
A park in the city that is designed only for flowers and trees, not food crops.
A greenhouse inside a school building where students grow plants for science class.
explanation: A community or urban garden is a place in the city where residents grow vegetables and plants together, providing fresh food and cleaner air.

q: How do small fish help control mosquito populations?
options: They eat mosquito larvae in the water, reducing the number that grow into adults.
They create ripples on the water surface that prevent mosquitoes from laying eggs.
They release a chemical into the water that kills mosquito eggs.
They compete with mosquitoes for the same food, leaving mosquitoes too weak to reproduce.
explanation: Small fish help reduce mosquitoes because they eat the larvae in the water.

q: Which statement about the structure of the liver is correct?
options: The liver is divided into lobes, with the right lobe larger than the left, and it sits in the upper belly protected by the ribs.
The liver has only one lobe and is located in the lower belly near the kidneys.
The right and left lobes of the liver are exactly the same size.
The liver is found in the chest cavity, protected by the breastbone.
explanation: The liver is divided into lobes — the right lobe is bigger than the left — and it sits in the upper belly, protected by the rib bones.

q: Why is red cabbage juice considered a natural indicator?
options: Because it contains anthocyanin, a natural pigment that changes color in acids and bases.
Because it turns permanently red when heated and stays that color in any liquid.
Because it was the first indicator discovered by scientists before synthetic ones were made.
Because it grows naturally in the wild and does not need to be made in a laboratory.
explanation: Red cabbage is a natural indicator because of its anthocyanin pigment, which changes color depending on whether a solution is acidic or basic.

q: Which part of a lanzones fruit tastes sweet, and which part tastes bitter?
options: The flesh is sweet; the seed is bitter
