The flesh is bitter; the seed is sweet
Both the flesh and seed are sweet
Both the flesh and seed are bitter
explanation: The flesh of lanzones is sweet, but the seed inside it tastes bitter.

q: Why is the Philippines one of the world's largest producers of geothermal energy?
options: It has many fast-flowing rivers suitable for dams
It has many volcanoes that produce underground heat
It receives the most sunlight of any country in Asia
It sits above very large underground coal deposits
explanation: The Philippines is one of the world's largest producers of geothermal energy because of its many volcanoes.

q: How many times can a mother rat give birth in a single year?
options: Only once, like most large mammals
Exactly twice — once in summer and once in winter
Several times, producing many young throughout the year
Only during the rainy season, once a year
explanation: In one year a mother rat can give birth several times, producing many young.

q: How many bones does an adult human body have?
explanation: There are 206 bones in the adult human body.

q: What is the correct order of a flowering plant's life cycle?
options: Seeds → flower → fruit → pollination → fertilization
Flower → pollination → fertilization → seeds and fruit → new plant
Fruit → fertilization → pollination → flower → seeds
Pollination → flower → seeds → fertilization → fruit
explanation: A plant follows the cycle: flower → pollination → fertilization → seeds and fruit → new plant.

q: If an earthquake strikes, where would you feel the strongest shaking?
options: Far away from the epicenter, where the waves spread out
Near the epicenter, where the intensity is highest
Deep underground, where the rock is harder
At the coast, because water carries the shaking further
explanation: A single earthquake has different intensities in different places — intensity is higher near the epicenter and weakens farther away.

q: What can happen to your stomach when you eat too much food at one time?
options: It shrinks and stops digesting
It feels uncomfortable or achy
It immediately sends the extra food to your muscles
It produces extra acid that gives you more energy
explanation: When we eat too much, our stomach can feel uncomfortable or achy.

q: What does the small round scar on a person's upper arm usually show?
options: That they were bitten by an insect as a baby
That they received the BCG vaccine against tuberculosis as a baby
That their arm was injured before it fully healed
That they were born with a birthmark on their skin
explanation: The small round scar on the upper arm is a normal sign that a person received the BCG vaccine against tuberculosis as a baby.

q: What does PHIVOLCS Alert Level 1 at a volcano mean?
options: The volcano is erupting violently and everyone must evacuate
There are small signs of unrest like weak earthquakes, but eruption is not certain
The volcano is completely calm with no activity at all
Lava is already flowing and the area is dangerous
explanation: Alert Level 1 means there are small changes like weak earthquakes or more steam, and people should avoid the crater because of possible sudden steam blasts.

q: At which special position in space is the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) located?
options: L1 Lagrange point between the Sun and Earth
L2 Lagrange point of the Sun-Earth system
The Moon's orbit around Earth
A geostationary orbit directly above the equator
explanation: The JWST is at the L2 Lagrange point of the Sun-Earth system, a stable position where gravity and centrifugal force balance out.

q: Why is ozone found near the ground considered harmful, while ozone high in the stratosphere is considered good?
options: Ground-level ozone keeps us warm, but stratospheric ozone makes it too cold
Stratospheric ozone shields us from UV rays, while ground-level ozone is a pollutant that harms our lungs
Ground-level ozone produces rain, while stratospheric ozone creates wind
Stratospheric ozone creates oxygen we breathe, while ground-level ozone destroys it
explanation: Stratospheric ozone shields us from harmful UV rays, but ozone at ground level is part of smog and harms our lungs when we breathe it.

q: How does a plant cell divide differently from an animal cell?
options: Plant cells pinch inward in the middle to split apart
Plant cells form a cell plate between two new cells, which becomes the new cell wall
Plant cells split lengthwise along the outer membrane
Plant cells break apart and then fuse into new cells
explanation: When plant cells divide, they form a cell plate between the two new cells, which eventually becomes the new cell wall — unlike animal cells, which pinch inward.

q: Why do many grazing animals like zebras and deer live in herds?
options: It is easier to find water when animals travel in large groups
More animals together means it is easier to spot and avoid predators
Living in herds keeps animals warmer in cold weather
Herds help animals find mates more quickly each season
explanation: Many grazers live in herds because it is easier to spot and avoid predators when there are many of them together.

q: How can a plant bulb produce more plants without using seeds?
options: It releases spores into the soil that grow into new bulbs
It forms small new bulbs at its side, which grow into separate plants
It sends out long underground runners that sprout at the tips
It sheds its outer layers, and each layer grows into a new plant
explanation: One bulb can form new small bulbs at its side, allowing it to multiply even without seeds.

q: Who performed the first-ever spacewalk in history, and when did it happen?
options: Yuri Gagarin from the Soviet Union, in April 1961
Neil Armstrong from the USA, in July 1969
Alexei Leonov from the Soviet Union, in March 1965
Valentina Tereshkova from the Soviet Union, in June 1963
explanation: Soviet cosmonaut Alexei Leonov was the first person to walk in space in March 1965, and his spacesuit ballooned outward during the 12-minute spacewalk.

q: How do baby spiders travel to a new place after they hatch?
options: They crawl along the ground until they reach a new habitat
They release a strand of silk and let the wind carry them
They are carried by their mother in a silk pouch
They jump from plant to plant using their strong back legs
explanation: Baby spiders release a strand of silk so the wind can carry them to a new place, a behavior called ballooning.

q: Why does a rainbow look like a full circle from an airplane but only a half arc from the ground?
options: The airplane's speed makes light bend in a complete ring around it
From the ground, land blocks the lower half of the circular rainbow
Rainbows are only half arcs naturally; airplanes create a different type
Airplane windows focus light into a full circle that eyes cannot see from below
explanation: From the ground we see only a half arc because the land blocks the lower part; from an airplane or tall mountain, a rainbow can appear as a full circle.

q: How long is the term of the President of the Philippines, and can they be re-elected?
options: 4 years, and they can run for a second term
6 years, and they cannot be re-elected
5 years, and they can serve two terms in a row
6 years, and they can run for one more term after resting for six years
explanation: The President of the Philippines serves a term of 6 years and cannot be re-elected.

q: In 2021, who was the Filipino scientist who dived to the bottom of the Emden Deep in the Philippine Trench?
options: Mahar Lagmay
Deo Florence Onda
Teodoro Corpuz
Joanne Yap
explanation: In 2021, Filipino scientist Deo Florence Onda became one of the first people to dive to the bottom of the Emden Deep, riding a special submersible with explorer Victor Vescovo.

q: What does your body do with the sugar made when you eat a 'go food' like rice or bread?
options: It stores all the sugar in the liver and only uses it during sleep
It sends the sugar into the blood, and muscles use it to make energy
It converts the sugar directly into fat before using any of it
It filters the sugar through the kidneys and removes it from the body
explanation: When you eat a go food, your body breaks it down into sugar that travels in your blood, and your muscles use this sugar to make energy.

q: Which of the following is the most common cause of air pollution in cities?
options: Rain clouds releasing chemicals into the air
Smoke and gases from vehicles and factories
Animals breathing out carbon dioxide all day
Plants releasing too much pollen in spring
explanation: Air pollution is dirty smoke and gases in the air, often coming from vehicles and factories.

q: What is the temperature like in the deep sea, and how does that affect the animals there?
options: The deep sea is warm because of underwater volcanoes, so animals prefer heat
The deep sea is very cold, near freezing, so the animals must be adapted to the cold
The deep sea is moderate and comfortable, so no special adaptations are needed
The deep sea alternates between hot and cold depending on the season
explanation: The water in the deep sea is very cold, near freezing, so the animals there must be adapted to the cold.

q: What is special about the stag beetle's jaws?
options: They can spin silk to build a nest underground
They glow in the dark to attract prey at night
They are large pincer jaws that are very strong for its small size
They are hollow and inject venom into other insects
explanation: The stag beetle has large pincer jaws that are very strong for its small size.

q: Who coined the word 'radioactivity' to describe the energy given off by elements like uranium?
options: Albert Einstein
Ernest Rutherford
Marie Curie
Niels Bohr
explanation: Marie Curie coined the word 'radioactivity' for the energy given off by elements like uranium.

q: What actually gets 'used up' when a light bulb glows in a circuit?
options: The electric current, which is smaller leaving the bulb than entering it
The wires, which slowly lose their ability to carry electricity
The energy, which is converted into light and heat — not the current itself
The voltage, which disappears completely after passing through the bulb
explanation: The current entering and leaving a bulb is the same amount; what gets used up is the energy, converted into light and heat.

q: What is the unit used to measure electric current?
options: Volt
Watt
Ampere
Ohm
explanation: The unit of electric current is the ampere, with the symbol A.

q: What causes earthquakes to happen?
options: Hot magma boiling inside the Earth's core pushes upward and shakes the ground
Large tectonic plates in the Earth's crust suddenly move or grind against each other
Strong ocean waves crash against the seafloor and send vibrations inland
Heavy rainfall seeps into the ground and causes the soil layers to collapse
explanation: Earthquakes happen when the Earth's large tectonic plates suddenly move or grind against each other.

q: Why is taking too many vitamin D tablets potentially harmful, even though sunlight cannot cause a vitamin D overdose?
options: Tablets make skin too sensitive to sunlight, causing burns
Too many tablets can put too much calcium in the blood and cause harm
Vitamin D from tablets blocks the absorption of vitamin C
Excess vitamin D from tablets turns into a toxin that weakens bones
explanation: While the body stops making vitamin D from sunlight once there's enough, taking too many vitamin D tablets can raise blood calcium to harmful levels.

q: How many bones does an adult human body have, and how does this compare to a baby?
options: Adults have 300 bones; babies are born with only 206 that grow over time
Adults have 206 bones; babies are born with about 300 that gradually fuse together
Adults and babies both have exactly 206 bones from birth
Adults have 270 bones; about 64 extra bones appear as children grow
explanation: An adult human has 206 bones, but babies are born with about 300 bones that gradually fuse together as the body grows.

q: What can a chameleon do with its eyes that most animals cannot?
options: It can see colors that humans cannot, like ultraviolet light
It can move each eye in a different direction at the same time
It can close one eye completely while the other stays wide open all night
It can change the color of its pupils to match its surroundings
explanation: A chameleon can move its right eye one way and its left eye another way at the same time, letting it see in almost every direction without turning its head.

q: Which lake is the fifth largest in the Philippines?
options: Lake Sebu
Lake Mainit
Lake Buhi
Lake Naujan
explanation: The fifth largest lake in the Philippines is Lake Naujan.

q: What is the name of the larger of Mars's two moons?
options: Deimos
Titan
Phobos
Callisto
explanation: Phobos is the larger of Mars's two moons.

q: What does the Calvin cycle in photosynthesis produce for the plant?
options: Oxygen, which the plant releases into the air as waste
Chlorophyll, which the plant uses to capture more sunlight
Glucose, which serves as the plant's food
Water, which the plant stores in its stem and leaves
explanation: In the Calvin cycle, plants use ATP and CO2 to build glucose, which serves as the plant's food.

q: Why should a sick person stay home instead of going to school or work?
options: Resting at home makes medicines work faster
Staying home prevents them from infecting other people
Being around crowds would make them feel worse emotionally
Cold air outside would worsen their symptoms quickly
explanation: When a person is sick, they should stay home so they do not infect other people.

q: Which animal found in mangroves can crawl and breathe out of water?
options: The sea horse, which hides among the mangrove roots
The mudskipper, a fish that can crawl and breathe on land
The octopus, which walks on the mud between the roots
The jellyfish, which washes into mangroves during high tide
explanation: The mudskipper is a fish adapted to mangrove life that can crawl and breathe out of water.

q: Why are small silica gel packets placed inside gadget boxes?
options: They release a gas that keeps electronic circuits running longer
They absorb moisture from the air to prevent rust and corrosion inside
They produce a mild electric charge that powers gadgets in standby mode
They contain a dye that changes color if the box has been opened
explanation: Silica gel packets absorb moisture from the air to prevent rust and corrosion of the metal components inside gadget boxes.

q: Why is coconut oil a popular ingredient in making natural soap in the Philippines?
options: It makes the soap completely clear and odorless
It produces a hard, creamy soap with rich lather
It allows the soap to melt slowly in hot and humid weather
It gives the soap a yellow color that is preferred by buyers
explanation: Coconut oil is used in Philippine natural soap making because it produces a hard, creamy soap with rich lather.

q: If a child in the Philippines keeps sneezing due to allergies, what is most likely causing it?
options: A highly contagious virus that spreads quickly in warm weather
Sensitivity to triggers like dust, mold, or animal fur — not a contagious sickness
Breathing in sea salt air that irritates the nose near the coast
Eating too many spicy Filipino foods that affect the nasal passages
explanation: Many kids in the Philippines sneeze a lot because of allergies to dust, mold, or animal fur — this is not a contagious sickness but nose sensitivity.

q: How long does a pineapple plant usually take before it produces its first fruit?
options: About one month, since pineapples grow in warm tropical weather
About three to four months under good growing conditions
Over a year, and it usually gives only one fruit per stalk
About six months if the plant gets enough water and fertilizer
explanation: A pineapple plant takes over a year before it fruits and usually gives just one fruit per stalk.

q: How are whales and dolphins able to communicate across long distances underwater?
options: They use flashes of bioluminescent light to send signals to each other
They swim to the surface and use high-pitched calls through the air
Sound travels far underwater, so their calls can be heard from a great distance
They touch each other's fins in a pattern that works like a code
explanation: Sound travels far underwater, so whales and dolphins can communicate across long distances using their calls.

q: Why do birds like herons and ducks visit ponds?
options: To cool off by swimming when the weather is very hot
To find soft mud for building their nests on nearby trees
To feed on fish and insects that live in the pond
To drink fresh water because ponds have no salt
explanation: Many birds such as herons and ducks come to the pond to feed on fish and insects.

q: How far back in history was soap first made?
options: About 500 years ago during the Renaissance in Europe
About 2,000 years ago in ancient Rome
Thousands of years ago in ancient Babylon
About 200 years ago during the Industrial Revolution
explanation: Soap was made as far back as ancient Babylon, thousands of years ago.

q: What happens to the animals and plants that live in a forest when the forest is destroyed?
options: They quickly migrate to nearby forests without any lasting harm
They lose their habitat and many become endangered or go extinct
They adapt and thrive in cities built in place of the forest
They move into the ocean, where more resources are available
explanation: When forests are destroyed, the animals and plants living there lose their habitat, and many become endangered or go extinct.

q: In a series circuit with two bulbs and a battery, what is true about the voltage drops across the bulbs?
options: Each bulb receives the full battery voltage, just like in a parallel circuit
The sum of all voltage drops across the bulbs equals the battery's total voltage
The first bulb takes all the voltage and the second bulb receives none
Voltage drops only in the wires, not in the bulbs themselves
explanation: In a series circuit, voltage drops across each component, and the sum of all voltage drops equals the battery's voltage.

q: A shrew looks like a mouse, but it is actually more closely related to which animals?
options: Rats and squirrels, which are also small rodents
Bats and rabbits, which have similarly shaped ears
Moles and hedgehogs, and it belongs to a different group from mice
Lizards and salamanders, since it has a similarly pointed snout
explanation: A shrew belongs to a different animal group from mice and is more closely related to moles and hedgehogs; its pointy snout is a key clue.

q: How does an owl fly so quietly when hunting at night?
options: Its wings are very large, so each flap pushes air more slowly
It holds its wings still and glides without flapping for most of its flight
Its soft feathers muffle the sound of its wings beating through the air
It flies very high above prey so the distance reduces the sound
explanation: The soft feathers on an owl's wings let it fly almost silently so it can surprise its prey.

q: How does a crab get out of its old shell when it molts?
options: It uses a rock to crack the old shell open from the outside
The old shell dissolves in seawater and falls away on its own
The old shell splits open along the back and the crab slowly backs out of it
Its claws cut the shell into pieces so it can step out easily
explanation: When a crab molts, its old shell splits open along the back and the crab slowly backs out — including pulling its legs and claws out of the old covering.

q: If a moth uses camouflage to blend into a tree, does that mean predators can never find it?
options: Yes — camouflage makes a moth completely invisible to all predators
No — some predators can still find it by smell or with sharp eyes, so camouflage helps but is not perfect
Yes — predators rely only on sight, so a perfectly hidden moth is completely safe
No — camouflage actually attracts predators because it produces a scent
explanation: Camouflage does not make a moth invisible; some animals can still find it by smell or sharp eyes, so hiding helps but is not perfect.

q: What is the wind speed range for a Category 1 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson scale?
options: Below 62 km/h — a tropical depression, not yet a hurricane
63 to 118 km/h — strong but not yet hurricane force
119 to 153 km/h — the lowest category of true hurricane
154 to 177 km/h — a moderate and dangerous hurricane
explanation: A Category 1 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson scale has winds of 119 to 153 km/h (74–95 mph).

q: What is a 'shooting star' really?
options: A star that has run out of fuel and is falling toward Earth
A small rock or dust from space that burns up in the atmosphere
A satellite reflecting sunlight as it passes overhead
A comet with a bright tail that crosses our sky for a few seconds
explanation: A shooting star is not a real star — it is a small rock or dust from space that burns up from speed and friction as it enters our atmosphere.

q: When it is summer in the Northern Hemisphere during the June solstice, what season is it in the Southern Hemisphere?
options: Winter
Summer
Spring
Autumn
explanation: Seasons are opposite in the two hemispheres, so when the Northern Hemisphere has summer at the June solstice, the Southern Hemisphere has winter.

q: What must happen for a shadow to form?
options: An object must block light from passing through
Light must be very bright and close to the object
The surface behind the object must be white
The object must be transparent
explanation: A shadow forms when an object blocks light from passing through, leaving a dark area behind it.

q: How many laws of planetary motion did Johannes Kepler describe?
options: Three
Two
Four
One
explanation: Johannes Kepler described exactly three laws of planetary motion.

q: How does water travel from the roots all the way up to the leaves of a tall plant?
options: Water molecules stick together and to narrow tube walls, allowing water to climb up thin tubes inside the plant
The plant's leaves pull water upward using suction like a straw from the outside
Roots pump water up using tiny muscles that squeeze the tubes
Water evaporates from roots and the vapor moves up through large hollow spaces
explanation: Water can climb up thin tubes inside a plant because water molecules stick to one another and to the narrow surfaces of those tubes.

q: Besides flamingos, which group of birds is also known to stand on one leg to keep the resting leg warm?
options: Herons and ducks
Eagles and hawks
Penguins and ostriches
Parrots and toucans
explanation: Herons, ducks, and other birds also stand on one leg for the same reason as flamingos — to keep the resting leg warm.

q: What is the safe way to unplug a device from a wall socket?
options: Hold the plug firmly and pull it out
Pull on the cord to yank the plug out quickly
Use a wet cloth to grip the cord for better hold
Push the plug sideways to loosen it before pulling the cord
explanation: You should hold the plug, not the cord, when unplugging a device so the wire does not get damaged or become dangerous.

q: What do cleaner fish eat when they clean larger fish?
options: Dead skin, mucus, and parasites on the bigger fish
Leftover food scraps floating near the bigger fish
Algae and seaweed stuck to the bigger fish's scales
Plankton gathered around the bigger fish's body
explanation: Cleaner fish eat the dead skin, mucus, and parasites that stick to the larger fish they are cleaning.

q: Why does eating a lot of candy and sweet foods lead to tooth decay?
options: Sugar is the favorite food of the bacteria that cause tooth decay
Sweet foods make teeth soft so they break apart easily
Sugar sticks directly to teeth and eats through the enamel on its own
Candy makes saliva too acidic, which dissolves the teeth
explanation: The bacteria that cause tooth decay feed on sugar from candy and sweet foods, so eating too much sugar gives those bacteria more to eat.

q: How does a marine sanctuary help fishermen who fish just outside it?
options: When the sanctuary fills with fish, the extra fish spill out beyond it so fishermen nearby can catch more
Fishermen are allowed to fish inside the sanctuary once a month during special seasons
The government pays fishermen a bonus for every fish they catch near a sanctuary
Sanctuaries attract fish from far away, completely replacing the fish that were already there
explanation: When a sanctuary fills up with fish, the extra fish spill out beyond its borders, allowing nearby fishermen to catch more.

q: Why does hair turn gray or white as a person gets older?
options: The body gradually stops making melanin, the pigment that gives hair its color
Old hair cells absorb air and slowly lose all moisture, turning transparent
Sunlight bleaches the hair shafts over many years of exposure
The roots move farther from blood vessels so less color reaches the hair
explanation: As a person ages, the body slowly stops producing melanin, and without melanin the new hair grows out white or gray.

q: Why was the discovery of antibiotics considered very important for human health?
options: Before antibiotics, many people died from infections that are easy to treat today
Antibiotics were the first medicines ever made by scientists
Antibiotics helped doctors perform surgery without pain for the first time
Before antibiotics, no one understood what caused diseases
explanation: Before antibiotics were discovered, many people died from infections that are now easy to treat, making the discovery extremely important.

q: Who made the first compass, and what material did they use?
options: Ancient Chinese people, using lodestone
Ancient Greeks, using magnetized iron bars
Ancient Egyptians, using naturally occurring magnets from the desert
Ancient Romans, using pieces of volcanic rock
explanation: The first compass was made by the ancient Chinese, who used lodestone — a naturally magnetic rock — to find direction.

q: Which scientist discovered the electron, and in what year?
options: J.J. Thomson in 1897
Ernest Rutherford in 1911
Niels Bohr in 1913
Marie Curie in 1898
explanation: J.J. Thomson discovered the electron in 1897, revealing that atoms contain even smaller charged particles.

q: What happens to gulaman when it is placed in hot water?
options: It dissolves in the hot water
It melts into a thick oil
It turns into a solid lump right away
It floats and keeps its jelly shape
explanation: Gulaman dissolves in hot water and then sets into a firm jelly when it cools down.

q: Which part of a typhoon usually causes the greatest damage when it hits land?
options: The eyewall
The calm eye at the center
The outer rain bands far from the center
The spiral feeder clouds ahead of the storm
explanation: When a typhoon makes landfall, the eyewall — the ring of fierce winds and rain surrounding the calm eye — usually causes the greatest damage.

q: When paper burns and turns into ash, what kind of change is that?
options: A chemical change
A physical change
A melting change
A mixing change
explanation: When paper becomes ash, it turns into a totally different substance — that is called a chemical change.

q: Where does a firefly's light come from?
options: A special light-making part at the bottom of its belly
A glow inside its head near the eyes
Tiny holes along the sides of its body
A layer of shiny scales on its wings
explanation: A firefly's light comes from a special organ located at the bottom of its belly.

q: Which of the following best describes a colloid?
options: A mixture whose particles are too small to settle out but too large to form a true solution, like milk or fog
A mixture that separates completely when left to stand, like oil and water
A mixture in which particles dissolve completely and disappear, like salt water
A mixture that only forms when two liquids are heated together
explanation: A colloid has particles that are too small to settle out but too big to count as a true solution — examples include milk, gelatin, and fog.

q: Which statement about how camouflage works in most animals is correct?
options: Most camouflage is built-in — the animal is born with the right colors and does not decide to change them
Animals choose to change their color the same way a person decides what to wear
Animals learn camouflage by watching their parents hide from predators
Camouflage only works for animals that can actively think and plan their movements
explanation: Most camouflage is built into the animal from birth; even the octopus changes color through an automatic body response, not a thought-out decision.

q: What is refraction?
options: The bending of light when it passes from air into water or glass
The bouncing of light off a smooth, shiny surface
The splitting of white light into all the colors of the rainbow
The slowing down of light inside a black object
explanation: Refraction is the bending of light that happens when it passes from one medium, like air, into another, like water or glass.

q: How can you tell a cuttlefish apart from a squid?
options: A cuttlefish has a wider body and a hard cuttlebone inside
A cuttlefish has a much longer and narrower body than a squid
A cuttlefish has ten long tentacles while a squid has only eight
A cuttlefish is always much larger than any squid found in Philippine seas
explanation: Cuttlefish look similar to squid but have a wider body and a cuttlebone inside — features that distinguish them from squid.

q: Which of the following is an example of using a push?
options: Closing a door
Pulling a drawer open
Lifting a bag off the floor
Picking up a pencil
explanation: Closing a door is an example of a push — you use a push when you close a door or push a cart.

q: Why is it dangerous to look at the sun through a convex lens?
options: A convex lens concentrates the sun's rays into a hot point that can burn and seriously damage your eye
A convex lens makes the sun look much larger, which tricks the brain and causes headaches
A convex lens reflects sunlight back at your face, causing sunburn on the skin around the eye
A convex lens blocks most sunlight so your eyes suddenly adjust and become permanently sensitive
explanation: A convex lens concentrates the sun's rays into a point so hot it can burn paper, so if pointed at the eye it can cause serious damage.

q: What is the main goal of the Philippines' National Greening Program?
options: To plant millions of trees nationwide to restore forests and stop soil erosion
To build green-colored public buildings to save energy across the country
To teach every Filipino student how to grow vegetables in school gardens
To replace all old vehicles with electric ones to reduce air pollution
explanation: The National Greening Program aims to plant millions of trees nationwide to restore forests and prevent soil erosion.

q: What happens in a covalent bond between atoms?
options: Two atoms share their electrons to form a molecule
One atom gives away all its electrons to another atom permanently
Two atoms are held together only by their opposite electrical charges
Atoms trade protons with each other to become stable
explanation: In a covalent bond, two atoms share electrons to form a molecule — for example, two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom share electrons to form water.

q: What are the three main layers of the Earth, listed from the outside to the inside?
options: Crust, mantle, core
Mantle, crust, core
Core, mantle, crust
Crust, core, mantle
explanation: The Earth's three main layers from outside to inside are the crust (the thin hard outer shell), the mantle (hot thick rock), and the core (extremely hot metal at the center).

q: Why does detergent work better than soap in hard water?
options: Detergent does not form scum with the minerals found in hard water
Detergent is hotter than soap, so it breaks down minerals more easily
Detergent has a stronger smell that drives dirt away from hard water
Detergent contains salt, which softens hard water before cleaning begins
explanation: Detergent works better than soap in hard water because it does not react with the minerals in hard water to form scum.

q: What is the nickname of Mount Pulag, the high mountain known for its beautiful sea of clouds?
options: Playground of the Gods
Roof of the Philippines
Crown of Luzon
Garden in the Sky
explanation: Mount Pulag is nicknamed the "Playground of the Gods" because of its stunning sea of clouds.

q: What makes the mudskipper unusual compared to most other fish?
options: It can crawl on land using strong fins while breathing through its skin and mouth
It can fly short distances above the water surface using its large pectoral fins
It lives its whole life buried under sand and only surfaces to eat
It can survive in both freshwater and saltwater by changing its body chemistry
explanation: The mudskipper is unusual because it can crawl on land using strong fins while breathing through its skin and mouth, something most fish cannot do.

q: What does your heart do when you run or play hard?
options: It beats faster to deliver more blood to your busy body, but it never stops
It beats more slowly to save energy while your muscles do the hard work
It temporarily stops for a moment to refill with blood before speeding up
It beats at the same steady rate no matter how active you are
explanation: When you run or play, your heart beats faster to deliver more blood to your busy body — but it still never stops.

q: What nickname is the jeepney known by in the Philippines?
options: King of the Road
Pride of the Streets
Heart of the Nation
Star of Luzon
explanation: The jeepney is nicknamed the "King of the Road" in the Philippines.

q: What causes high tide on the side of Earth facing the Moon?
options: The Moon's gravity pulls the ocean water upward, causing it to bulge
The Sun heats the ocean on that side, making the water expand and rise
Earth's spin throws the water outward toward the Moon by centrifugal force
The Moon's light warms the water molecules, causing them to spread out
explanation: The Moon's gravity pulls on the ocean's water, causing it to bulge upward on the side of Earth facing the Moon — this creates high tide.

q: What country was the famous scientist Isaac Newton from?
options: England
France
Germany
Italy
explanation: Isaac Newton was from England, where he developed his famous laws of motion and gravity.

q: What is the first step when growing salt crystals?
options: Dissolve salt in water until it seems to disappear into the liquid
Boil the water until it completely evaporates and leaves salt behind
Mix salt with oil until a thick paste forms
Freeze salt water until ice crystals appear on the surface
explanation: To grow crystals, you first dissolve salt in water until it seems to disappear into the liquid, creating a saturated solution.

q: What can filtering do to water, and what can it NOT do?
options: Filtering can remove dirt and make water look clearer, but it cannot remove tiny germs
Filtering can remove both dirt and germs, making water completely safe to drink
Filtering can kill germs by heating the water as it passes through the filter
Filtering can make water safe to drink but it leaves the water looking cloudy
explanation: Filtering removes dirt and makes water look clearer, but it does not remove tiny germs — the water still needs boiling to be safe.

q: What makes the Rafflesia flower found in the Philippines unusual?
options: It is one of the largest flowers in the world and has an unpleasant smell
It is the only flower in the world that grows underwater in Philippine rivers
It can glow at night and release a sweet scent to attract birds for pollination
It has the strongest stem of any plant, making it impossible to uproot by hand
explanation: Rafflesia is a parasitic plant found in the Philippines known for being one of the largest flowers in the world and for its unpleasant smell.

q: What nuclear process powers a nuclear power plant?
options: Nuclear fission
Nuclear fusion
Nuclear decay
Nuclear radiation
explanation: A nuclear power plant is powered by nuclear fission — the splitting of atoms — not by fusion.

q: How are wild leeches in Philippine rice fields different from medical leeches?
options: Wild leeches live in muddy fields and are not raised for treatment, while medical leeches are specially raised in a laboratory
Wild leeches are much larger and more dangerous than the tiny leeches used in medicine
Wild leeches attach only to plants, while medical leeches are trained to attach to human skin
Wild leeches produce a numbing chemical, while medical leeches do not
explanation: Wild leeches found in Philippine rice fields are different from medical leeches, which are specially raised in a laboratory for treatment purposes.

q: In some Philippine traditions, what is water with boiled guava leaves used for?
options: As a bath for the skin
As a drink to cure stomachaches
As a spray to keep insects away from the home
As a cleaning liquid to wash vegetables
explanation: In some Philippine traditions, water with boiled guava leaves is used as a bath for the skin.

q: What is the weather usually like in the Philippines during the transition between the amihan and habagat winds around March to May?
options: The winds are weak and the weather is hot
There are strong storms and heavy rainfall every day
The temperature drops and cool dry air blows from the north
Thick fog and cloudy skies cover most of the country
explanation: Between the amihan and habagat, around March to May, the winds are weak and the weather in the Philippines is hot.

q: If you mix salt and pepper together, what happens to each ingredient's properties?
options: Each substance keeps its own properties, so you can still taste the salt and pepper separately
The two substances combine into a new substance with a completely different taste
Salt's properties disappear because pepper's strong flavor takes over
The mixture becomes a new substance that can never be separated back into salt and pepper
explanation: In a mixture, each substance keeps its own properties — you can still taste salt and pepper separately even after mixing them.

q: How are electrons arranged inside a metal?
options: The atoms share their outer electrons in something like a sea of free electrons
Each atom holds its electrons very tightly so none can move at all
Electrons are locked in fixed positions between every pair of metal atoms
Electrons in metals belong to a single central atom and orbit all the others
explanation: In a metal, atoms share their outer electrons in something like a sea of free electrons that can move through the material.

q: What happens to a runny egg yolk when it is heated?
options: It thickens and becomes firm
It melts into a thin liquid
It evaporates and disappears
It stays runny but changes color
explanation: When an egg yolk is heated, it thickens and becomes firm — this is an example of a chemical change caused by heat.

q: Why are humans classified as vertebrates?
options: Because we have a backbone in our spine as part of our skeleton
Because we have a large brain compared to the size of our body
Because we breathe air using lungs, just like most land animals
Because our bodies are covered with skin rather than scales or feathers
explanation: Humans are vertebrates because we have a backbone in our spine, just like fish, birds, and dogs.

q: Where does the bleeding-heart dove find its food?
options: On the forest floor, eating seeds, insects, and small invertebrates
High in the tree canopy, eating fruit and nectar from flowers
In ponds and streams, catching small fish near the water surface
In open grasslands, pecking at grass seeds in large flocks
explanation: The bleeding-heart dove forages on the forest floor, eating seeds, insects, and small invertebrates.

q: Besides being used as firewood and livestock fodder, how does the ipil-ipil tree help the soil?
options: It is a legume that fixes nitrogen, enriching the soil
It releases acidic sap that breaks down rocks into fertile soil
Its deep roots bring up water from underground to keep the soil moist
It sheds large leaves year-round that form a thick layer of ash when burned
explanation: Ipil-ipil is a legume, so it fixes nitrogen from the air into the soil, enriching it alongside its uses as fodder and firewood.

q: Why can X-rays pass through skin and muscle but not through bones?
options: X-rays are blocked by denser materials like bone and metal, but pass through softer tissues like skin and muscle
X-rays are too weak to pass through any living tissue, so they reflect off the skin surface
X-rays heat up soft tissues so they become transparent, but bones stay cool and opaque
X-rays change direction when they hit wet tissue and go around bones instead of through them
explanation: X-rays are high-energy electromagnetic radiation that pass through soft tissues like skin and muscle but are blocked by denser materials like bone and metal.

q: Where does most of the electricity in the Philippines come from?
options: Coal, providing over 60% of the country's total power
Hydropower from dams on large rivers
Geothermal energy from the country's many volcanoes
Solar panels installed on homes and buildings
explanation: Most electricity in the Philippines comes from coal, which provides over 60% of the country's total power.

q: In mimicry, why do predators avoid a harmless animal that copies a dangerous one?
options: Predators cannot tell the harmless animal apart from the dangerous one, so they avoid it just in case
Predators smell a chemical the harmless animal releases that smells exactly like the dangerous species
The harmless animal makes the same sounds as the dangerous animal, frightening predators away
Predators are naturally programmed to avoid all brightly colored animals, even harmless ones
explanation: In mimicry, a harmless animal copies the look of a dangerous or poisonous animal, so predators avoid it because they cannot tell it is actually harmless.

q: How long can a male Hercules beetle grow, including its horn?
options: Up to 17 centimeters
Up to 7 centimeters
Up to 30 centimeters
Up to 3 centimeters
explanation: Male Hercules beetles (Dynastes hercules) of Central America can reach 17 centimeters in length including the horn, making them the world's longest beetles.

q: What happens when a bird's old feathers fall out?
options: New feathers grow in to replace them
The bird grows scales instead
The bird can no longer fly at all
The feathers grow back thicker and darker
explanation: Birds molt by losing old feathers and growing new ones, keeping them healthy and their feathers working well.

q: How does a hummingbird stay in one spot in the air while it drinks nectar?
options: It beats its wings in a figure-eight pattern very fast
It grabs onto the flower with its feet while drinking
It glides on a warm air current rising from the ground
It slows its heartbeat so it barely needs to move
explanation: A hummingbird beats its wings incredibly fast in a figure-eight motion, which lets it hover in one spot while sipping nectar.

q: Why do farmers place wide leaves like taro or papaya leaves in rice fields?
options: To attract golden apple snails so they gather underneath and can be collected
To block sunlight and keep the soil cool for the rice roots
To give the rice plants extra nutrients as the leaves decompose
To mark rows so farmers can walk without stepping on young plants
explanation: Snails are drawn to gather under wide leaves, making it easy for farmers to pick them all up the next morning.

q: Where do meerkats live compared to prairie dogs?
options: Meerkats live in Africa while prairie dogs live in North America
Both meerkats and prairie dogs live in Africa
Meerkats live in South America while prairie dogs live in Asia
Both meerkats and prairie dogs live in North America
explanation: Even though both animals live in burrows, meerkats are found in Africa and prairie dogs live in North America — different continents.

q: Why is the dugong threatened in the Philippines?
options: Destruction of seagrass beds and illegal hunting
Pollution from plastic bags blocking its blowhole
Overfishing of the small fish it eats
Rising water temperatures killing the coral reefs it depends on
explanation: The dugong is threatened by the destruction of seagrass beds, which is its food source, and by illegal hunting.

q: What does a porcupinefish do when it faces a predator?
options: It gulps water to swell into a ball and stick out its spines
It releases a cloud of ink to escape in the dark water
It camouflages itself by changing color to match the coral
It drops to the sea floor and pretends to be a rock
explanation: The porcupinefish gulps water to swell into a ball and stick out its spines, making it hard for predators to swallow.

q: After a person is rescued from nearly drowning, why should they still see a doctor?
options: Because water may still be in their lungs even if they seem fine
Because they likely have broken bones from struggling in the water
Because they need medicine to prevent a fever from the cold water
Because their heart always stops briefly during a near-drowning
explanation: Even after rescue, water may remain in the lungs, so a doctor needs to check the person to be safe.

q: Can smoke from another person's cigarette harm you even if you do not smoke yourself?
options: Yes, breathing in a nearby smoker's smoke can still harm you
No, the smoke is only dangerous to the person actually smoking
No, the smoke becomes harmless once it mixes with outside air
Yes, but only if you stand in the smoke for more than an hour
explanation: Secondhand smoke — the smoke you breathe from a nearby smoker — can still harm your health even though you are not the one smoking.

q: What role do decomposers play in the nutrient cycle?
options: They break down dead plants and animals so nutrients return to the soil
They carry nutrients from the soil up into the stems of plants
They store nutrients inside their bodies and release them only in spring
They compete with plants so fewer nutrients are wasted on dead matter
explanation: Decomposers rot dead plants and animals, returning nutrients to the soil so new plants can absorb them — completing the cycle.

q: What keeps a growing hailstone suspended inside a cloud before it falls?
options: A very strong upward wind called an updraft
A layer of cold air that freezes it in place
Electric charges in the cloud that push it upward
The weight of other ice crystals pressing against it
explanation: Hail needs a very strong updraft inside the cloud to hold the growing hailstone up — once it gets too heavy, it finally falls.

q: What kind of rock is shale, and how is it formed?
options: A sedimentary rock formed from fine mud and clay pressed into layers
An igneous rock formed when lava cools slowly underground
A metamorphic rock formed when limestone is heated under pressure
A volcanic rock formed from ash that settles after an eruption
explanation: Shale is a sedimentary rock that forms when fine mud and clay are pressed together in layers over time.

q: What would happen to a forest if all decomposers like fungi and bacteria disappeared?
options: Dead matter would pile up and new plants could not get nutrients from the soil
Plants would grow faster because there would be no competition for nutrients
The soil would become richer because nothing would be consuming it
Animals would take over the role of decomposers and nothing would change
explanation: Decomposers return nutrients to the soil by breaking down dead matter; without them, nutrients stop cycling and new plants starve.

q: Who is the unit of power called the watt named after?
options: James Watt, the Scottish engineer who improved the steam engine
Thomas Edison, the American inventor of the light bulb
Michael Faraday, who discovered electromagnetic induction
Nikola Tesla, who developed alternating current electricity
explanation: The watt is named after James Watt, the Scottish engineer famous for improving the steam engine.

q: Which space mission discovered most of the more than 5,000 confirmed exoplanets found so far?
options: NASA's Kepler space telescope, using the transit method
The Hubble Space Telescope, using direct imaging
The Mars Rover, using ground-penetrating radar
The International Space Station, using spectroscopy
explanation: Most of the 5,000+ confirmed exoplanets were discovered by NASA's Kepler space telescope using the transit method, along with the TESS mission.

q: Why can't soldier termites feed themselves even though they are the strongest in the colony?
options: Their jaws are too big for chewing food, so workers feed them mouth to mouth
They are underground with no access to leaf litter above the soil
They spend all their energy guarding and have no time to eat
They rely entirely on stored fat from when they were larvae
explanation: Soldier termites have jaws too big for eating, so worker termites feed them mouth to mouth.

q: Where do fruit bats in the Philippines like to roost?
options: In tall forest trees and in mangroves near the sea
In caves deep underground far from any trees
In hollow coconut trunks on open farmland
Beneath the roots of bamboo groves near rivers
explanation: Fruit bats roost in tall forest trees and even in mangroves near the sea.

q: What is the other name of the Mindanao River?
options: Rio Grande de Mindanao
Rio Verde de Mindanao
Rio Largo de Mindanao
Rio Fuerte de Mindanao
explanation: The Mindanao River is also known as the Rio Grande de Mindanao.

q: Who discovered stainless steel, and where?
options: Harry Brearley, in Sheffield, England in 1913
Thomas Edison, in New Jersey, America in 1905
Marie Curie, in Paris, France in 1898
Alfred Nobel, in Stockholm, Sweden in 1920
explanation: Harry Brearley discovered stainless steel in 1913 in Sheffield, England.

q: Why does the makahiya leaf stay spread open when no one touches it?
options: Water pressure inside the leaf cells keeps them firm and stretched open
A sticky substance holds the leaflets flat against each other
Sunlight stiffens the leaf's midrib so it cannot fold
The leaf is too heavy to close unless a strong force pushes it
explanation: When the tiny leaf cells are full of water, water pressure keeps them firm and stretched open, so the leaf stays spread out.

q: Why do rubber-soled shoes cause more static electricity to build up on your body?
options: Rubber is an insulator that blocks electric charge from flowing to the ground
Rubber attracts extra electrons from the floor as you walk
Rubber is a conductor that collects charge from the air around you
Rubber creates friction that generates more heat than other shoe materials
explanation: Rubber is an insulator, so it stops charge from flowing to the ground, causing static to build up on you.

q: How do indigenous communities in the Philippines treat various illnesses?
options: Using medicinal plants passed down through generations
By visiting modern hospitals in the nearest city
By trading for imported medicines from neighboring islands
By using only prayer and rest without any plant-based remedies
explanation: Indigenous Filipino communities use medicinal plants that have been passed down through generations to treat illnesses.

q: What is added to iron to make stainless steel resistant to rust?
options: Chromium
Sulfur
Copper
Calcium
explanation: Special types of steel have metals like chromium added to iron to give traits such as resisting rust.

q: Who invented the first practical typewriter?
options: Christopher Latham Sholes of America in 1868
Thomas Edison of America in 1876
Alexander Graham Bell of Scotland in 1872
James Watt of Scotland in 1855
explanation: The first practical typewriter was invented by Christopher Latham Sholes of America in 1868.

q: What is the result of mitosis?
options: Two new cells with identical chromosomes to the original cell
Two new cells each with half the chromosomes of the original
Four new cells identical to the parent cell
One larger cell formed by two cells joining together
explanation: Mitosis is the process by which one cell divides to produce two new cells with identical chromosomes.

q: How do most tardigrades reproduce?
options: By laying eggs, and the babies look like tiny adults
By splitting in half, with each half growing into a new tardigrade
By releasing spores that drift through the air
By budding off small copies from the side of their body
explanation: Most tardigrades reproduce by laying eggs, and the hatchlings look like miniature versions of the adults.

q: What do some animals like snails do during a severe drought to survive?
options: They enter a sleep-like state called estivation to save water and energy
They migrate to wetter regions until the rains return
They shed their outer shell to lose water faster
They eat extra food to store fat reserves for the dry period
explanation: Some animals enter estivation — a sleep-like dormant state — during drought to conserve water and energy until rain returns.

q: What does the spleen do in the human body?
options: It filters and cleans the blood
It breaks down food and absorbs nutrients
It produces insulin to control blood sugar
It stores air to help with breathing underwater
explanation: The spleen is an organ on the left side of the belly that filters the blood and cleans it.

q: What is a polyatomic ion?
options: A group of atoms bonded together that acts as a single ion with one charge
A single atom that has gained or lost exactly one electron
Two atoms of the same element sharing electrons equally
An ion found only in metals that conduct electricity
explanation: A polyatomic ion is a whole group of atoms stuck together sharing one charge — like the ion found in baking soda — and it acts as a single piece.

q: Where in the body is the thyroid gland, and what shape is it?
options: In the front of the neck, shaped like a butterfly
In the chest behind the heart, shaped like a triangle
In the upper arm, shaped like a small oval
In the belly near the stomach, shaped like a leaf
explanation: The thyroid is a small butterfly-shaped gland located in the front of the neck.

q: Why does the Philippines have many volcanoes?
options: Tectonic plates sink at subduction zones, melt, and form magma that rises to create volcanoes
The islands float on very hot ocean water that pushes lava through cracks
Strong earthquakes break the ground open and molten rock pours out
The Philippines sits directly above Earth's inner core where it is hottest
explanation: As a plate sinks at a subduction zone, part of it melts and creates magma that rises to form volcanoes — that is why the Philippines has many volcanoes.

q: What is the role of the spongy mesophyll layer inside a leaf?
options: Its air spaces allow carbon dioxide and oxygen to be exchanged
It traps sunlight and turns it into sugar through photosynthesis
It carries water from the roots to the outer edges of the leaf
It protects the leaf from insects by producing a waxy surface
explanation: The spongy mesophyll lies below the palisade layer and has air spaces that allow gas exchange of carbon dioxide and oxygen.

q: What is the difference between active and inactive ingredients in a medicine?
options: The active ingredient treats the illness; inactive ingredients just help with the tablet's shape or taste
The active ingredient gives the tablet its color; the inactive ingredient is what cures you
Both ingredients treat the illness equally, but the active one works faster
The inactive ingredient treats the illness; the active ingredient only prevents side effects
explanation: The active ingredient is what actually treats the illness (like paracetamol for fever), while inactive ingredients help with shape or taste but do not cure you.

q: What are scientists still finding on the mountains of Luzon today?
options: New kinds of shrew rat not seen before
New species of saltwater crocodile
Previously unknown freshwater dolphins
Undiscovered breeds of water buffalo
explanation: Scientists are still discovering new kinds of shrew rat on different mountains of Luzon.

q: In a closed system with no energy entering or leaving, what happens to the total amount of energy?
options: It stays the same — if one form decreases, another increases by the same amount
It slowly decreases over time due to friction and heat loss
It increases slightly each time energy changes from one form to another
It doubles each time the system converts kinetic energy to potential energy
explanation: By the law of conservation of energy, total energy in a closed system never changes — a drop in one form is matched by a rise in another.

q: Why is it wrong to think eating just a few red tide-contaminated shellfish is safe?
options: Because even a small amount of saxitoxin can cause poisoning
Because the toxin is only dangerous if you eat shellfish raw, not cooked
Because only people with allergies are harmed by small amounts
Because the danger comes from the shell, not the meat inside
explanation: Saxitoxin is so powerful that even a small amount can cause poisoning — just a few pieces with high toxin can harm you.

q: Which fossil fuel is most commonly made into gasoline for vehicles?
options: Oil
Coal
Natural gas
Charcoal
explanation: Oil is refined into gasoline used for vehicles, while coal is mainly burned in power plants and natural gas is used for cooking and heating.

q: How does a lever make work easier compared to a ramp?
options: A lever pivots on a fulcrum to lift things; a ramp stretches the path to make climbing less steep
A lever stretches the path upward; a ramp pivots to multiply force
Both work the same way but a lever is faster than a ramp
A lever reduces weight; a ramp increases speed instead
explanation: Both are simple machines, but a lever pivots on a fulcrum to lift, while a ramp spreads the path out so the climb is not so steep.

q: What is the main danger of a pufferfish to humans?
options: The poison inside it that harms you if you eat it
The sharp spines that stab you if you touch it
The electric shock it delivers when threatened
The ink it sprays that can blind you temporarily
explanation: It is not mainly the spines that are dangerous, but the poison inside the pufferfish that harms you when it is eaten.

q: How deep must a well be dug for it to keep supplying water?
options: Deeper than the water table
Only as deep as the layer of topsoil
Just below the surface of the ground
Down to the bedrock layer, no deeper
explanation: For a well to keep giving water, it must be dug deeper than the water table.

q: Besides insects, what else does the mudskipper eat?
options: Small worms and snails that live in the mud
Tiny fish eggs floating on the water's surface
Algae and water plants growing along the shore
Fallen fruit and seeds washed into the mud
explanation: Besides insects, the mudskipper also eats small worms and snails that live in the mud.

q: What does humidity measure?
options: The amount of water vapor in the air
The speed at which rain falls from clouds
The temperature difference between day and night
The thickness of clouds in the sky
explanation: Humidity is the amount of water vapor in the air; the Philippines is very humid because it is hot and near the sea.

q: What are the three ingredients that make up gunpowder?
options: Sulfur, saltpeter, and charcoal
Sulfur, sand, and charcoal
Salt, saltpeter, and coal
Phosphorus, saltpeter, and ash
explanation: Gunpowder is made from three ingredients: sulfur, saltpeter, and charcoal.

q: Why do scientists think the megalodon went extinct?
options: The oceans cooled and there were fewer large animals for it to eat
A massive asteroid hit the ocean and wiped it out suddenly
It grew too large to swim quickly enough to catch prey
A disease spread among megalodons and killed them all
explanation: Scientists think the megalodon went extinct when the oceans cooled and there were fewer of the large animals it preyed on.

q: How many days are in the month of December?
explanation: December has 31 days.

q: Where was the Philippine flag first raised, and who declared independence on that day?
options: In Kawit, Cavite, by Emilio Aguinaldo on June 12, 1898
In Manila, by Jose Rizal on July 4, 1896
In Malolos, by Andres Bonifacio on August 23, 1896
In Cavite, by Apolinario Mabini on June 12, 1900
explanation: The Philippine flag was first raised on June 12, 1898, in Kawit, Cavite, when Emilio Aguinaldo declared independence from Spain.

q: What are goats raised for on a farm?
options: Milk, meat, and hair
Eggs, feathers, and meat
Silk, honey, and wool
Milk, eggs, and leather
explanation: A goat is a farm animal that people raise for its milk, meat, and hair.

q: Why does a compass not point to the exact geographic North Pole?
options: The magnetic North Pole is in a slightly different place from the geographic North Pole
Compasses point south in the Southern Hemisphere and north everywhere else
The Earth's rotation causes the needle to drift slightly eastward
Gravity from the moon pulls the needle away from true north
explanation: The magnetic North Pole sits in a slightly different place from the geographic North Pole, so a compass points a little off from true north.

q: What property of a mineral describes how it reflects light?
options: Luster
Hardness
Streak
Cleavage
explanation: Luster is the property that describes how a mineral reflects light — it can be metallic (like shiny metal) or non-metallic.

q: Where do typhoons form?
options: Over warm ocean waters
Over cold mountain peaks
Over flat desert land
Over frozen polar ice
explanation: A typhoon is a large spinning storm that forms over warm ocean waters, where heat and moisture fuel its strong winds and heavy rain.

q: What fuel do most nuclear power plants use to produce energy?
options: Uranium-235
Plutonium-239
Coal dust
Hydrogen gas
explanation: Most nuclear power plants use uranium-235 as the fuel for fission, the process that releases enormous amounts of energy.

q: What is 'blue carbon'?
options: Carbon stored by coastal plants like mangroves
Carbon released when ocean water evaporates
Carbon found deep inside ocean trenches
Carbon produced by burning ocean fish
explanation: Blue carbon refers to the carbon stored by coastal plants like mangroves, which absorb and lock away carbon from the atmosphere.

q: What do decomposers like fungi and bacteria do for the soil?
options: They return nutrients to the soil by breaking down dead plants and animals
They make soil harder by adding minerals from rocks
They remove nutrients from soil and store them in plant roots
They protect soil from rain by forming a hard crust on top
explanation: Decomposers such as fungi and bacteria break down dead plants and animals and return their nutrients to the soil, keeping the ecosystem's nutrient cycle going.

q: Which type of star arrangement is most common in our galaxy?
options: Binary or multiple star systems
Single stars like our Sun
Triple star systems orbiting a black hole
Stars grouped in rings around a galaxy center
explanation: Roughly half of all stars in the Milky Way are in binary or multiple star systems, making our Sun's single-star status relatively uncommon.

q: How do some tuna species keep their muscles warmer than the surrounding water?
options: By using a counter-current heat exchange system
By swimming near warm volcanic vents on the seafloor
By storing fat around their muscles as insulation
By basking at the water surface to absorb sunlight
explanation: Some tuna use a counter-current heat exchange system — a form of partial endothermy — to keep their muscles warmer than the water, letting them swim faster.

q: A big drum makes a very loud, low boom. What does the low pitch tell us about the drum's vibration?
options: The drum vibrates slowly, but can still be very loud
The drum vibrates slowly and must also be very quiet
The drum vibrates quickly, which is why the sound is low
The drum does not vibrate at all when making a low sound
explanation: A low pitch means slow vibration, but slow vibration can still be very loud — like the boom of a big drum — because pitch and loudness are different properties of sound.

q: What two things are produced when an acid and a base react together?
options: A salt and water
A gas and a new acid
Carbon dioxide and a solid powder
Two new bases
explanation: When an acid meets a base in a neutralization reaction, the products are always a salt and water.

q: What happens to the energy a wave carries when it reaches the shallow shore and breaks?
options: It is suddenly released as noise, foam, and a push of water onto the sand
It is absorbed quietly into the sand without any sound or movement
It bounces back out to sea as a new wave of equal size
It sinks straight down to the seafloor
explanation: When a wave breaks on the shore, it suddenly releases the energy it carried as noise, foam, and a push of water onto the sand.

q: How is civet coffee, also known as kopi luwak, made?
options: From coffee beans collected from civet droppings
From coffee beans soaked in civet milk overnight
From coffee beans that civets carry in their fur
From coffee berries that civets bury underground
explanation: Civet coffee (kopi luwak) is made from coffee beans collected from civet droppings after the animals eat and digest the coffee berries.

q: What starts a tsunami?
options: The seafloor suddenly shifts and pushes a huge amount of water upward
Strong surface winds blow ocean water into tall waves
A sudden drop in air pressure above the ocean
Underwater volcanoes release hot steam that lifts the water
explanation: A tsunami begins when the seafloor suddenly shifts, pushing a huge amount of water upward and spreading energy outward as massive waves.

q: What part of a ballpoint pen spreads ink onto paper?
options: A tiny metal ball that rolls across the paper
A small sponge that soaks ink onto the surface
A thin wire that scratches ink into the paper
A spring that pushes a flat tip against the page
explanation: A ballpoint pen works because a tiny metal ball at its tip rolls across the paper, picking up ink from the reservoir and spreading it onto the surface.

q: Why is food pressed down tight and covered with brine when put in a jar to ferment?
options: To remove all air, because trapped air lets mold and rot start
To make the food softer so it ferments more quickly
To keep the food cold and slow down the fermentation
To add salt flavor throughout every layer of food
explanation: Food is packed tightly and covered with brine so no air is left in the jar, because trapped air is what allows mold and rot to begin.

q: At what speed do radio, Wi-Fi, and phone signals travel?
options: At the speed of light
At the speed of sound
At half the speed of sound
At a speed that depends on how far they need to travel
explanation: Radio, Wi-Fi, and phone signals travel at the speed of light — the fastest speed possible — so they arrive with almost no delay even from far away.

q: What is the correct order of soil layers from top to bottom?
options: Topsoil, then subsoil, then bedrock
Bedrock, then topsoil, then subsoil
Subsoil, then topsoil, then bedrock
Topsoil, then bedrock, then subsoil
explanation: Soil is layered with dark, nutrient-rich topsoil on top, subsoil below it, and solid bedrock at the bottom.

q: Why are banana leaves a good choice for wrapping kakanin instead of plastic?
options: They are wide, natural, and break down easily without becoming plastic waste
They keep food cold longer than plastic bags
They add a sweet flavor that plastic cannot give
They are waterproof and never let any moisture through
explanation: Banana leaves are used to wrap kakanin because they are wide, natural, and break down easily, so they do not become plastic waste the way synthetic packaging would.

q: The image formed on the retina inside your eye is actually upside down. Why do we still see things the right way up?
options: The brain flips the image so we see things correctly
The lens in the eye flips the image before it reaches the retina
The retina automatically corrects the image as it forms
The optic nerve rotates the image on its way to the brain
explanation: The image on the retina is indeed upside down, but the brain flips it so that we perceive everything the right way up.

q: How does a parasitic plant like dodder get water and nutrients?
options: It attaches to a host plant and uses special root-like organs called haustoria to extract them
It grows extra-long roots deep into the soil to find underground water
It captures insects and digests them to get nutrients
It collects rainwater in its leaves and absorbs it through its surface
explanation: Dodder and similar parasitic plants attach to a host plant and use haustoria — special root-like organs — to extract water and nutrients because they cannot make enough food on their own.

q: How do deep-sea animals survive the extreme water pressure in the deep ocean?
options: They have soft, flexible bodies that are not crushed by the pressure
They have extra-thick, rigid shells that block the pressure
They stay in air pockets trapped between underwater rocks
They produce a special fluid that pushes back against the water pressure
explanation: Deep-sea animals have soft, flexible bodies that are not crushed by the intense water pressure found at great depths.

q: Where can a thermometer be placed to measure your body temperature?
options: Under your tongue, in your armpit, or in your ear
Only under your tongue
Only in your ear canal
Only against the skin of your forehead
explanation: A thermometer can be placed under the tongue, in the armpit, or in the ear to measure body heat and show whether a person has a fever.

q: How do mangroves help protect coral reefs?
options: By filtering out dirt and extra nutrients from coastal water before it reaches the reefs
By blocking large waves so the reefs are never exposed to the open sea
By providing shade that keeps the water cool enough for corals
By releasing oxygen that corals need to survive
explanation: Mangroves filter out dirt and excess nutrients from coastal water, helping to keep the water clean before it reaches nearby coral reefs.

q: If an object is in free fall near Earth, how much does its speed increase every second?
options: 9.8 meters per second faster each second
1 meter per second faster each second
9.8 meters per second total, then it stops speeding up
98 meters per second faster each second
explanation: Because g = 9.8 m/s², a falling object speeds up by 9.8 meters per second with every second that passes.

q: What is the capital city of Canada?
options: Ottawa
Toronto
Vancouver
Montreal
explanation: The capital of Canada is Ottawa, not Toronto, which is the largest city but not the capital.

q: What color does litmus paper turn when dipped in lemon juice?
options: Red
Blue
Green
Yellow
explanation: Litmus turns red in lemon juice because lemon juice is an acid, and acids cause litmus to turn red.

q: On what date is the Pahiyas festival celebrated every year?
options: May 15
June 12
December 8
January 1
explanation: The Pahiyas festival is held every May 15, a colorful harvest celebration in Lucban, Quezon.

q: Which vitamin helps keep your eyes healthy and prevents night blindness?
options: Vitamin A
Vitamin C
Vitamin D
Vitamin B12
explanation: Vitamin A is essential for eye health and preventing night blindness; it is found in orange and yellow vegetables and fruits like squash and sweet potato.

q: Is human blood acidic, neutral, or basic?
options: Slightly basic, with a pH of about 7.4
Slightly acidic, with a pH of about 6.8
Exactly neutral, with a pH of exactly 7.0
Strongly basic, with a pH of about 9.0
explanation: Human blood is slightly basic, with a pH of about 7.4, which is just above the neutral value of 7.

q: In circular motion, what is the relationship between period and frequency?
options: They are inverses of each other — a longer period means a lower frequency
They are equal to each other when speed is constant
They add up to one when measured in the same units
Period measures distance while frequency measures time
explanation: The period is the time for one full revolution and the frequency is the number of revolutions per second, so the two are mathematical inverses of each other.

q: Why does a hot air balloon rise into the sky?
options: The heated air inside becomes lighter than the cooler air outside, so it floats upward
The burner pushes the balloon up like a rocket engine
The balloon is filled with a gas lighter than air, like helium
Hot air expands and escapes through holes, pushing the balloon upward
explanation: When air inside the balloon is heated, its particles spread out and it becomes lighter than the surrounding cool air, causing the balloon to rise.

q: Why can a glass crack when suddenly filled with boiling hot water?
options: Its parts expand unevenly because the heat reaches some parts before others
The water molecules hit the glass walls too hard and break them
Boiling water is heavier than cold water and creates too much pressure
The glass absorbs so much heat that its chemical bonds dissolve
explanation: A glass can crack when suddenly exposed to very hot or very cold liquid because different parts of the glass expand or contract unevenly, creating internal stress.

q: What is the chemical formula of ordinary table salt?
options: NaCl
KCl
NaOH
CaCl₂
explanation: The chemical formula of table salt is NaCl, representing one sodium (Na) atom bonded with one chlorine (Cl) atom.

q: In a circuit, conventional current flows from positive to negative. Which direction do electrons actually move?
options: From negative to positive — the opposite of conventional current
From positive to negative — the same as conventional current
In random directions depending on the material
From the middle of the circuit outward to both ends
explanation: Conventional current is treated as flowing from positive to negative, but electrons — the actual moving particles — flow from negative to positive, the opposite direction.

q: How does an unglazed burnay jar keep water cool inside?
options: Water seeps through the walls and cools the inside as it evaporates outside
The thick clay walls block heat from the surrounding air
The clay absorbs heat from the water and stores it in its walls
The dark color of the clay reflects sunlight away from the jar
explanation: Many burnay jars have no shiny coating, so a little water seeps through their walls; as that water evaporates on the outside, it takes heat with it and cools the water inside.

q: What happens when you try to make soap lather in hard water?
options: It makes only a little foam because it does not lather well in hard water
It lathers just as well as in regular tap water
It lathers faster and creates more bubbles than usual
It turns the water a different color instead of forming bubbles
explanation: Soap does not lather well in hard water, producing only a little foam instead of the rich lather you would get in soft water.

q: What wind speed range causes PAGASA to raise Typhoon Signal No. 1?
options: 39 to 61 km/h expected within 36 hours
62 to 88 km/h expected within 24 hours
89 to 117 km/h expected within 18 hours
118 km/h and above expected within 12 hours
explanation: PAGASA Signal No. 1, the lowest warning level, is raised for winds of 39 to 61 km/h expected within 36 hours.

q: About how long ago did the giant shark Megalodon go extinct?
options: About 3.6 million years ago
About 65 million years ago
About 10,000 years ago
About 500 million years ago
explanation: The Megalodon went extinct about 3.6 million years ago; it was a giant shark that could grow up to 17 meters long with teeth as large as a human hand.

q: What are the small brown dots found on the underside of fern leaves?
options: Spore cases called sori
Eggs of tiny leaf insects
Signs of a plant disease
Pores that release water vapor
explanation: The little brown dots on the underside of a fern leaf are spore cases called sori — they are not a disease but the fern's way of reproducing.

q: What is the chemical formula of hydrochloric acid?
options: HCl
H₂SO₄
HNO₃
H₂O₂
explanation: The chemical formula of hydrochloric acid is HCl, made of one hydrogen atom and one chlorine atom.

q: Which signs suggest that a wound may be infected?
options: The wound becomes swollen, red, or has pus
The wound itches and forms a dry scab quickly
The wound turns pale and feels numb
The wound stops bleeding completely within a minute
explanation: Swelling, redness, or pus forming in a wound are signs that it may be infected and needs medical attention.

q: What are the two main stages of photosynthesis?
options: The light reactions that capture energy, and the Calvin cycle that builds glucose
The dark reactions that capture sunlight, and the bright reactions that store sugar
The absorption stage in roots and the production stage in flowers
The water-splitting stage in leaves and the carbon release stage in roots
explanation: Photosynthesis has two stages: the light reactions that capture energy from sunlight, and the Calvin cycle that uses that energy to build glucose.

q: How does medical ultrasound create images of the inside of the body?
options: It sends high-frequency sound waves in and uses the echoes from different tissues to build images
It uses X-rays that pass through soft tissue and are blocked by hard organs
It measures the heat given off by organs to create a color map of the body
It uses radio waves that bounce off bones to produce a picture
explanation: Medical ultrasound sends high-frequency sound waves into the body and uses echoes returning from different tissues to build images of organs and unborn babies.

q: How does a stick insect breathe?
options: Through tiny holes along the sides of its body
Through a nose at the front of its head
Through gills on its back legs
Through its mouthparts when it eats
explanation: A stick insect has no nose or lungs; instead it breathes through tiny holes called spiracles along the sides of its body.

q: Why does a bimetallic strip bend when it is heated?
options: Because one metal expands faster than the other, curving the strip
Because both metals shrink equally, squeezing the strip into a curve
Because the heat melts the glue holding the two metals together
Because the metals change color and one side becomes heavier
explanation: A bimetallic strip bends when heated because it is made of two metals that expand at different rates — the faster-expanding metal pushes the strip into a curve.

q: What are two typical properties of limestone?
options: It is usually white or grayish and soft enough to be cut or carved
It is usually black and extremely hard, like granite
It is usually red and crumbles into clay when wet
It is usually clear and as hard as glass
explanation: Limestone is usually white or grayish and is soft enough to be cut or carved easily, which is why it has been used as a building and carving material for thousands of years.

q: What color are the newly sprouted leaves of a mango tree?
options: Reddish or copper-colored before turning green
Bright yellow before turning green
Pale white before turning green
Dark purple before turning green
explanation: Newly sprouted mango leaves are often reddish or copper-colored and gradually turn green as they mature.

q: What do wasps and bees have in common that makes them both insects?
options: Each has three body parts, six legs, two pairs of wings, and antennae
Each has four body parts, eight legs, and no wings
Each has two body parts, four legs, and one pair of wings
Each has five body parts, ten legs, and three pairs of wings
