The salt is filtered out through a very fine mesh that water molecules can pass through
The mixture is frozen so the salt sinks to the bottom while pure ice forms on top
An electric current is passed through the water to pull the salt to one side
explanation: In distillation, salt water is boiled until the water becomes vapor; the vapor is then cooled back into pure liquid water, leaving the salt and other impurities behind.

q: Why is the 'flying lemur' an inaccurate name for the colugo?
options: Because the colugo is neither a true lemur nor a true flier
Because the colugo lives in water, not in the air or trees
Because the colugo is actually a type of bat related to true fliers
Because the colugo is a rodent and lemurs are primates, but they look similar
explanation: The colugo's common name 'flying lemur' is misleading on both counts — it is not a true lemur and it cannot truly fly, only glide.

q: Why does a cormorant sink more easily in water than a pelican?
options: Because the cormorant's body floats less in the water than a pelican's body
Because the cormorant is a heavier bird with denser bones than the pelican
Because the cormorant holds its wings tightly to reduce air trapped under feathers
Because the pelican has a large air-filled pouch that adds extra buoyancy
explanation: A cormorant sinks more easily than a pelican because its body floats less in the water, which helps it dive but means it must dry its wings after swimming.

q: What should you do right away when you hear a tsunami warning?
options: Move quickly to high ground away from the shore
Stay near the beach to watch the waves
Hide inside a low-lying building close to the water
Wait for the waves to arrive before deciding to move
explanation: When there is a tsunami warning, you should quickly move to high ground away from the shore to stay safe.

q: How does the katala help the forest grow?
options: It spreads seeds to different places when it eats fruits
It digs holes in the ground where new trees can grow
It cleans dead leaves so sunlight reaches the forest floor
It drives away animals that would eat young plants
explanation: The katala helps the forest by spreading the seeds it eats to different places, allowing new plants to grow.

q: What is the name of the space agency that belongs to the United States?
options: NASA
ESA
JAXA
Roscosmos
explanation: The space agency of the United States is called NASA.

q: Why does everything look blurry when you open your eyes underwater without goggles?
options: Water stops the cornea from focusing light the way air does
The eyes close slightly when submerged to protect themselves
Saltwater dissolves the lens inside your eye
Water bends light so strongly that the eye cannot detect colors
explanation: The cornea at the front of the eye needs air to help focus light, and water cancels that focusing effect, causing blurry vision.

q: After a wind turbine generates electricity, how does that electricity reach homes and buildings?
options: It flows through wires connected to the grid
It is stored in large tanks and delivered by trucks
Wind pushes it through pipes underground
It is beamed wirelessly to nearby houses
explanation: The electricity made by a turbine flows through wires to homes and buildings.

q: Where is the Asian palm civet — the animal used to make kape alamid — found?
options: In the Philippines, where it climbs trees
Only in the rainforests of central Africa
In the deserts of the Middle East
Exclusively on the island of Borneo
explanation: The Asian palm civet that makes kape alamid is found in the Philippines and climbs trees.

q: Which plant did Gregor Mendel famously use in his experiments about heredity?
options: Pea plants
Rose bushes
Corn plants
Sunflowers
explanation: Gregor Mendel used pea plants in his experiments on heredity.

q: How do bees turn nectar from flowers into honey?
options: They collect nectar and let water evaporate from it inside the hive until it thickens
They mix nectar with wax from the honeycomb to solidify it
They chew the nectar repeatedly until it changes color
They add a chemical from their stingers to make the nectar sweet
explanation: Bees make honey by collecting nectar and letting it evaporate inside the hive until the water content drops enough to thicken and sweeten it.

q: What is special about the three bones found in the middle ear?
options: They are the smallest bones in the entire body and pass sound along
They are the hardest bones and protect the brain from damage
They are connected directly to the eye to help with balance
They produce a fluid that allows us to hear underwater
explanation: The middle ear holds the three smallest bones in the body, which pass and boost sound vibrations.

q: How does a chick get out of its egg?
options: It pecks the eggshell from the inside to break out
Its mother taps the shell from the outside to crack it open
The shell cracks on its own when the chick is ready
The warmth of the nest melts the shell away
explanation: The chick pecks the eggshell from the inside to break out on its own.

q: Which object is the largest known dwarf planet in our solar system?
options: Pluto
Eris
Ceres
Makemake
explanation: Pluto is the largest known dwarf planet in our solar system.

q: What does a legume plant give to the bacteria living in its roots in exchange for nitrogen?
options: Sugar made from sunlight
Water drawn up from the soil
Oxygen produced during photosynthesis
Minerals absorbed from the ground
explanation: In exchange for nitrogen, the plant gives the bacteria sugar that it makes from sunlight.

q: How many kidneys does a person need to stay healthy?
options: Only one kidney is enough to live healthily
You must have both kidneys or your body will fail
You need at least three-quarters of both kidneys working
Having only one kidney always causes serious illness
explanation: People have two kidneys, but a person can still live healthily with only one working kidney.

q: When are childhood vaccines usually given, and where can Filipino children get them for free?
options: While children are young, at health centers in the Philippines
Only during outbreaks, at hospitals that charge a fee
When children turn 18, at government offices
At birth only, and only in private hospitals
explanation: These vaccines are usually given while children are young, and they are free at health centers in the Philippines.

q: How does an island arc like the Philippine archipelago form?
options: It forms when tectonic plates collide and subduction creates a curved chain of volcanic islands
It forms when a meteor crashes into the ocean and pushes up a ring of land
It forms when underwater rivers deposit so much sand that islands appear
It forms when a large continent slowly splits apart and the pieces spread out
explanation: An island arc is a curved chain of volcanic islands that forms from subduction; the Philippine archipelago itself is an island arc built up over millions of years as plates collided.

q: What does extra carbon dioxide released by people do to the Earth?
options: It traps heat in the air, slowly warming the Earth and affecting climate
It blocks sunlight completely, causing the Earth to cool rapidly
It mixes with rain to create acid that dissolves rocks
It pushes the ozone layer farther from Earth, increasing UV radiation
explanation: The extra carbon dioxide that people release stays in the air and traps heat, slowly warming the Earth and affecting the climate.

q: Who was the first woman to travel to space, and when did it happen?
options: Valentina Tereshkova of the Soviet Union, in 1963
Sally Ride of the United States, in 1983
Yuri Gagarin of the Soviet Union, in 1961
Christa McAuliffe of the United States, in 1986
explanation: The first woman in space was Valentina Tereshkova of the Soviet Union, in 1963.

q: How many colors does a rainbow have?
options: Seven
Five
Eight
Six
explanation: A rainbow has seven colors.

q: What is a glaze and why is it put on ceramics?
options: A glassy coating that makes ceramics shiny and waterproof
A rough sand layer that strengthens the ceramic against cracking
A dye soaked into the clay to give it permanent color
A wax covering that keeps the ceramic lightweight
explanation: A glaze is a glassy coating put on ceramics to make them shiny and waterproof.

q: When a vehicle suddenly passes close to you and you flinch without thinking, what kind of body response is that?
options: A reflex that protects you from sudden dangers
A voluntary reaction that you choose to make
A habit your brain learned from repeated practice
An emotional response caused by fear of traffic
explanation: Flinching or shutting your eyes when a vehicle suddenly passes close is a reflex that protects you from sudden dangers.

q: What happens to a falling object's energy as it drops toward the ground?
options: Its gravitational potential energy decreases while its kinetic energy increases
Its kinetic energy decreases while its potential energy increases
Both potential energy and kinetic energy increase equally
Both types of energy stay the same until it hits the ground
explanation: As an object falls, its gravitational potential energy decreases while its kinetic energy increases, so it speeds up until it hits the ground.

q: Even though a large wind turbine looks like it turns slowly, how fast can the tip of one blade actually move?
options: Faster than a car on the highway, because each blade tip travels a huge distance per rotation
At about the same speed as a walking person, since the blades are very heavy
Only as fast as the wind itself, never faster
A few meters per second, since slowing them down makes more electricity
explanation: The tip of a long wind turbine blade can move faster than a car on the highway because it travels a huge distance with every rotation.

q: What were the very first passengers ever to fly in a hot air balloon?
options: A sheep, a duck, and a rooster
Two human volunteers and a dog
A horse and a goat
Three scientists from France
explanation: The first passengers in the Montgolfier hot air balloon were animals: a sheep, a duck, and a rooster.

q: Why is a forklift called a compound machine?
options: It combines hydraulic cylinders, wheels and axles, and an engine to do its work
It uses only one simple machine but in a very powerful way
It relies entirely on electricity stored in batteries
It is made from a single piece of steel shaped into different tools
explanation: A forklift is a compound machine because it uses hydraulic cylinders, wheels and axles, and an engine together.

q: During the development of an embryo, what causes the fingers to become separate instead of webbed?
options: Cells between the fingers die on a programmed schedule
Finger bones grow so fast they push the webbing apart
Blood vessels cut through the webbing as they form
Skin cells migrate away from between the fingers toward the tips
explanation: Apoptosis (programmed cell death) causes cells between the fingers to die on schedule during embryo development, creating separate fingers.

q: How does knowing when the habagat and amihan arrive help Filipino communities?
options: People can prepare early — for example, by storing food or getting ready for floods before the heavy rain comes
People can ignore weather forecasts because the monsoons are perfectly predictable
It helps farmers know exactly how many sunny days they will get each year
It tells people when to go to the beach safely without risk of rain
explanation: Because we know when the habagat and amihan arrive, people can prepare — for example, storing food or getting ready for floods before the heavy rain comes.

q: How do bacteria reproduce?
options: By splitting one cell into two
By laying tiny eggs that hatch later
By budding off a smaller copy that slowly grows
By exchanging DNA with a partner cell first
explanation: Bacteria multiply by splitting one cell into two.

q: Why is it impossible to stop a tsunami from happening?
options: Because tsunamis come from powerful natural forces like earthquakes that humans cannot control
Because no country has built a large enough sea wall yet
Because tsunamis form in outer space before they reach the ocean
Because warning systems are too slow to stop them once they start
explanation: We cannot stop a tsunami because it comes from powerful natural forces like earthquakes; we can only prepare by knowing warning signs and finding safe high ground.

q: How do wolves and tigers tell other animals that a territory is already taken?
options: They mark the area with scent from urine or special glands
They leave large scratch marks on the highest trees
They roar or howl nonstop at the borders of their territory
They bury food around the edges to create a visible boundary
explanation: Many animals like wolves and tigers mark their territory with scent from urine or special glands, so others know the area is already taken.

q: What does the color of a star tell us about it?
options: Blue stars are the hottest, while red stars are cooler
Red stars are the hottest, while blue stars are cooler
All stars are the same temperature but look different colors from Earth
Yellow stars are hotter than blue stars
explanation: Stars come in different colors — blue stars are the hottest, while red stars are cooler.

q: What do schools in the Philippines give children to help fight intestinal worms?
options: Safe deworming medicine
A special vitamin drink
A vaccine injection
A medicated soap for bathing
explanation: There is safe deworming medicine given in schools in the Philippines to help children fight intestinal worms.

q: How many baby teeth do children grow, and how many adult teeth replace them?
options: 20 baby teeth that fall out, then 32 stronger adult teeth
16 baby teeth that fall out, then 28 adult teeth
24 baby teeth that fall out, then 36 adult teeth
20 baby teeth that fall out, then 20 matching adult teeth
explanation: Children grow 20 baby teeth that fall out to make room for 32 stronger adult teeth that must last a lifetime.

q: Why does the carrying capacity of an environment differ from one species to another?
options: Because different animals need different amounts of food and space
Because larger animals always have a higher carrying capacity
Because carrying capacity only depends on rainfall, which varies by region
Because predator species always outnumber prey species
explanation: Each kind of animal has its own carrying capacity because they need different amounts of food and space.

q: In what year did Alexander Graham Bell receive the patent for the telephone?
explanation: Alexander Graham Bell received the patent for the telephone in the year 1876.

q: What can happen to a body of water when too much fertilizer washes into it?
options: Algae grow rapidly, use up the oxygen, and create dead zones where fish cannot survive
The water becomes cleaner because plants filter out pollutants
Fish grow larger because the extra nutrients act like food for them
The water cools down, which actually helps fish live longer
explanation: Eutrophication occurs when excess nutrients from fertilizers cause rapid algae growth that depletes oxygen and creates dead zones where fish cannot survive.

q: During which era did the very first land plants appear on Earth?
options: The Paleozoic Era
The Mesozoic Era
The Cenozoic Era
The Precambrian Era
explanation: The first land plants appeared during the Paleozoic Era.

q: Who was the first Filipino leader to resist foreign rule in the Philippines?
options: Lapu-Lapu
Jose Rizal
Emilio Aguinaldo
Andres Bonifacio
explanation: Lapu-Lapu was the first to resist foreign rule in the Philippines.

q: What is El Nino in simple terms, and how does it usually affect the Philippines?
options: Pacific seawater becomes warmer than usual, bringing less rain and hotter weather to the Philippines
Pacific seawater becomes cooler than usual, causing more typhoons to hit the Philippines
Strong winds from the Pacific push cold air over the Philippines, lowering temperatures
The ocean releases more carbon dioxide, making Philippine weather more humid
explanation: El Nino is when Pacific seawater becomes warmer than usual, and because of this the Philippines often gets less rain and hotter weather.

q: When and where did Emilio Aguinaldo declare Philippine independence?
options: June 12, 1898 in Kawit, Cavite
July 4, 1946 in Manila
June 12, 1896 in Batangas
August 23, 1898 in Bulacan
explanation: Emilio Aguinaldo declared Philippine independence on June 12, 1898 in Kawit, Cavite.

q: Which four planets in our solar system have rings?
options: Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune
Saturn, Mars, Jupiter, and Venus
Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, and Earth
Mercury, Jupiter, Saturn, and Uranus
explanation: Four planets have rings: Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune.

q: What makes the diaphragm unusual compared to most muscles in the body?
options: You can voluntarily control it when awake, yet it also works automatically while you sleep
It is the only muscle that never gets tired, even during heavy exercise
It controls your heartbeat as well as your breathing
It grows throughout your entire life, unlike other muscles
explanation: The diaphragm is unusual because we can voluntarily control our breathing, yet it also works automatically to keep us breathing while we sleep.

q: On a distance-time graph, what does a steeper line tell you about an object's speed?
options: A steeper line means the object is moving faster
A steeper line means the object has stopped moving
A steeper line means the object is slowing down
A steeper line means the object is moving backward
explanation: On a distance-time graph, the slope (steepness) of the line shows average speed — a steeper line means faster movement.

q: What is remarkable about the songs that male humpback whales sing?
options: All males in one population sing the same song, and it slowly changes over time showing a form of animal culture
Each whale has a completely unique song that no other whale can copy
Only very old whales can sing; young males are silent until fully grown
The songs last only a few seconds and are used solely to warn of predators
explanation: Male humpback whales sing complex songs lasting hours, and within one population all males sing the same song that slowly changes over time, demonstrating a form of animal culture.

q: In a food chain diagram, which direction does the arrow point, and why?
options: Toward the eater, because that is the direction energy flows
Away from the eater, because energy comes from the sun above
Toward the plant, because plants are the start of all food chains
Sideways between two animals, because they share energy equally
explanation: In a food chain, the arrow points toward the eater because that is the direction energy flows.

q: Why are rice farmers and people who wade in rivers more likely to catch schistosomiasis?
options: They are frequently in water that contains infected snails that carry the disease
They eat more raw fish, which carries the schistosomiasis parasite
They drink unboiled river water, which spreads the infection
They breathe in infected mud particles that float in the air near rivers
explanation: Rice farmers and people who wade in rivers are more at risk because they are frequently in water that has infected snails that carry schistosomiasis.

q: Some people believe vaping is safe because it is not a real cigarette. Why is this idea wrong?
options: Most vapes still contain nicotine, which harms the heart just like regular cigarettes
Vaping is actually completely safe because vapor does not enter the lungs
Only flavored vapes are harmful; unflavored ones have no health effects
Vaping harms the lungs but has no effect on the heart at all
explanation: Most vapes still contain nicotine, so they still harm the heart even though they are not real cigarettes.

q: How do scientists monitor El Nino and La Nina?
options: They measure the surface temperature of Pacific water using satellites and floating buoys
They track rainfall amounts in South America and count typhoon occurrences
They study ice cores from Antarctica to find patterns in ancient climate records
They measure wind speed at weather stations along the Philippine coast
explanation: Scientists measure El Nino and La Nina using the surface temperature of Pacific water, with the help of satellites and floating buoys in the ocean.

q: What happens to nitrogen in the nitrogen cycle over time?
options: The same nitrogen is used and returned over and over, so it is never used up
Nitrogen is gradually lost into outer space, so Earth slowly runs out
Plants permanently lock up nitrogen in their roots, removing it from the cycle
Nitrogen is destroyed each time it passes through an animal and must be replaced by rainfall
explanation: In the nitrogen cycle, the same nitrogen is used and returned over and over, so it is never used up.

q: What double benefit do floating solar panels on reservoirs provide?
options: They generate electricity from sunlight and reduce water evaporation from the reservoir
They cool the water below to increase fish production and generate extra electricity
They block rain from polluting the water and convert wind energy at the same time
They purify the water underneath while producing electricity from sunlight
explanation: Floating solar panels generate electricity from sunlight while reducing evaporation from the water beneath, preserving more water for hydro and irrigation.

q: Why is the Philippines especially at risk from the effects of greenhouse gas warming?
options: As an island nation with long coastlines, it faces greater danger from rising seas and flooding
The Philippines produces the most greenhouse gases in Asia, causing local warming
The Philippines is near the equator, where the ozone layer is thinnest
The Philippines has no mountains, so there is nowhere safe to move if seas rise
explanation: Warming from greenhouse gases raises sea levels and can strengthen storms; as an island nation with long coastlines, the Philippines faces greater danger from flooding and rising seas.

q: What is the original source of energy for almost every food chain on Earth?
options: The sun
The soil
Water
Wind
explanation: The sun is the original source of energy for almost every food chain on Earth.

q: Which mission was the first to land humans on the Moon?
options: Apollo 11
Apollo 13
Voyager 1
Sputnik 1
explanation: Apollo 11 was the first mission to land humans on the Moon, in 1969.

q: Before a vaccine is approved for the public, what do scientists and doctors do first?
options: Test it on many volunteers over a long time to check safety
Sell it immediately to see if it works on sick people
Test it only in laboratories without using any volunteers
Approve it as soon as it is made in the factory
explanation: Before a vaccine is used, it is tested on many volunteers over a long time to make sure it is safe and works, and results are closely watched before it is approved.

q: What do baby mudskippers eat when they first live in the water?
options: Tiny water creatures called plankton
Insects found near the mud
Small fish eggs from the riverbed
Decaying leaves floating on the surface
explanation: Baby mudskippers first live in the water and eat very tiny water creatures called plankton.

q: Which seed is the largest in the world?
options: The double coconut (coco de mer)
The mango seed
The avocado seed
The jackfruit seed
explanation: The largest seed in the world is the double coconut (coco de mer), which is bigger and heavier than a regular coconut.

q: What does global warming refer to?
options: The slow rise in Earth's average temperature over the past decades
A temporary heat wave that happens every summer
The warming of oceans caused by underwater volcanoes
An increase in the number of sunny days each year
explanation: Global warming is the slow rise in Earth's average temperature over the past decades.

q: Which snake is the heaviest in the world?
options: The green anaconda
The reticulated python
The Burmese python
The king cobra
explanation: The heaviest snake is the green anaconda, which can weigh more than 200 kilograms.

q: In the body's negative feedback system, what happens when something drifts from its normal level?
options: The body produces a response that reverses the change and restores balance
The body increases the change to make it stronger
The body shuts down that system until the change corrects itself
The body signals the brain to ignore the change
explanation: In negative feedback, when something drifts from normal the body produces a response that reverses the change and returns it toward balance.

q: Which type of dog ears can often pick up faint sounds a little more easily?
options: Upright, pointed ears
Floppy ears that hang down
Both types hear exactly the same
Floppy ears because they are larger
explanation: Dogs with upright ears can often pick up faint sounds a little more easily than those with floppy ears.

q: What do puppies drink to grow and stay healthy?
options: Their mother's milk
Water and soft food
A special liquid from the vet
Rainwater collected near the den
explanation: Puppies drink their mother's milk to grow and stay healthy.

q: Where on the tongue can you sense all the different tastes?
options: Across the whole tongue
Only at the very tip for sweet flavors
In separate zones — sweet at the tip, bitter at the back
Only along the sides of the tongue
explanation: All tastes can be sensed across the whole tongue, not in separate zones — the old picture of taste zones is wrong.

q: Which type of wave has the longest wavelengths in the electromagnetic spectrum and is used by cellphones and Wi-Fi?
options: Radio waves
Infrared waves
Ultraviolet waves
X-rays
explanation: Radio waves have the longest wavelengths in the spectrum and are used to carry sound and information for radio, television, cellphones, and Wi-Fi.

q: Whose X-ray photo was the key clue to discovering the double-helix shape of DNA?
options: Rosalind Franklin
James Watson
Francis Crick
Gregor Mendel
explanation: Rosalind Franklin's X-ray photo was the key clue to discovering the double-helix shape of DNA.

q: Which spider holds the record as the largest by weight and body size?
options: The Goliath birdeater tarantula from South America
The giant huntsman spider from Southeast Asia
The Brazilian wandering spider
The black widow spider from North America
explanation: The largest spider by weight and body size is the Goliath birdeater, a giant tarantula from South America.

q: Why do most objects not show any static electricity effect under normal conditions?
options: They have equal amounts of positive and negative charge, so they are neutral
They are made of materials that do not carry any electric charge
Their charges are locked inside and can never move
They only have negative charges that cancel each other out
explanation: Most objects are normally neutral because they have equal amounts of positive and negative charge, and they only show a static effect when this balance is upset.

q: Which of the following is a common misconception about recycling?
options: All trash can be recycled
Plastic bottles can be recycled
Reducing waste is better than recycling
Cardboard boxes can often be recycled
explanation: It is a misconception that all trash can be recycled — items like dirty paper, used tissue, and certain styrofoam are hard or impossible to recycle.

q: How many climate types does PAGASA recognize in the Philippines?
options: Four
Two
Three
Five
explanation: PAGASA recognises four climate types in the Philippines: Type I, Type II, Type III, and Type IV.

q: What did Samuel Morse's telegraph use to send messages over long distances in the 1840s?
options: Dots and dashes (Morse code) carried through a wire
Light flashes sent through glass tubes
Sound vibrations traveling through metal rails
Electric sparks fired through the open air
explanation: The telegraph sent messages using dots and dashes (Morse code) carried through a wire — it was the first fast long-distance communication before the telephone.

q: What property of substances allows distillation to separate a mixture?
options: They have different boiling points
They have different colors
They have different densities when solid
They dissolve at different rates in water
explanation: Distillation separates mixtures because substances with different boiling points turn to vapor at different temperatures.

q: Why do you sometimes get a small shock when touching a metal doorknob after walking on a carpet?
options: Static charge built up in your body suddenly grounds through the metal
The metal doorknob has its own stored electric charge
Your body absorbs electricity from the carpet fibers
Cold air between you and the doorknob creates electricity
explanation: Walking on carpet builds up static charge in your body; when you touch the metal doorknob, electrons jump in a tiny spark as your body grounds — that is the shock you feel.

q: Why do most strong earthquakes happen at plate boundaries?
options: Pressure builds up as plates grind together until the rock suddenly slips, releasing seismic waves
Volcanoes at the boundaries melt the rock and cause it to collapse
Ocean water seeps into cracks and makes the ground shake
The plates spin around each other, creating vibrations
explanation: Most strong earthquakes happen at plate boundaries where plates grind against each other; pressure builds until the rock suddenly slips, sending seismic waves outward.

q: Why is our galaxy called the Milky Way?
options: Its faint band across the night sky looks like spilled milk
It contains many white dwarf stars that glow like milk
Early astronomers named it after the color of moonlight
It moves in a swirling path like milk stirred in water
explanation: It is called the Milky Way because its faint band across the sky looks like spilled milk.

q: Why is the Philippines one of the top producers of geothermal electricity in the world?
options: It sits on the Ring of Fire and has many volcanoes
It has many fast-flowing rivers suitable for dams
Its coastline receives very strong ocean winds
It has large deposits of natural gas underground
explanation: Because the Philippines sits on the Ring of Fire and is full of volcanoes, it is one of the countries that produces the most geothermal electricity in the world.

q: Besides making electricity, what else does Magat Dam in Isabela provide?
options: Irrigation water for the rice farms of Cagayan Valley
Drinking water piped directly to Metro Manila
Flood barriers to protect the city of Cauayan
Cooling water for a nearby nuclear power plant
explanation: Magat Dam in Isabela makes hydroelectric power and also supplies irrigation water to the rice farms of Cagayan Valley.

q: Why is geothermal power considered a stronger base for a power supply compared to wind or solar?
options: It gives steady electricity all day long, unlike wind or sun which sometimes stop
It produces more electricity per kilogram of fuel than any other source
It is cheaper to build than wind farms or solar panels
It can be transported easily to other countries as a liquid fuel
explanation: Unlike wind or sun which sometimes stop, geothermal gives steady electricity all day long, making it a reliable base for a power supply.

q: Why do astronauts grow a few centimeters taller while living in space?
options: Their spine stretches because there is no weight pressing on it
Their bones absorb extra calcium from space food
Microgravity pulls their limbs outward, lengthening them
Their muscles relax and allow the body to fully unfold
explanation: In space, astronauts grow a few centimeters taller because their spine stretches without weight pressing on it — but they shrink back once they return to Earth.

q: How does the fuzzy mold on old bread get its food?
options: It releases enzymes that digest the bread
It absorbs sunlight through its fuzzy surface
It draws water and minerals up from the bread like roots
It traps tiny insects on its surface and absorbs them
explanation: The mold on old bread is a fungus that releases enzymes to digest the bread, which is why the bread gets soft and spoiled as the mold grows.

q: Where do real clownfish actually live in the ocean?
options: Inside sea anemones
Inside coral caves on the ocean floor
Floating near the surface in open water
Buried in sand near the shore
explanation: It is true that clownfish live in anemones, just like in the movie Finding Nemo.

q: What causes typhoid fever?
options: The bacterium Salmonella Typhi from contaminated food and water
A virus spread through the air when an infected person coughs
A parasite that enters the body through mosquito bites
A fungus found on improperly stored grains
explanation: Typhoid fever is caused by the bacterium Salmonella Typhi that enters the body from contaminated food and water.

q: What is the main job of lymph nodes?
options: They filter the lymph and trap germs before the fluid returns to the blood
They produce red blood cells that carry oxygen around the body
They store extra water and release it when the body is dehydrated
They make digestive enzymes that break down fats
explanation: Lymph nodes are small lumps that filter the lymph and trap germs before the fluid returns to the blood.

q: Which indigenous peoples regard Mount Pulag as a sacred place?
options: The Ibaloi and Kalanguya peoples
The Igorot and Tagalog peoples
The Maranao and Tausug peoples
The Aeta and Mangyan peoples
explanation: Mount Pulag is regarded as a sacred place by the indigenous Ibaloi and Kalanguya peoples.

q: What happens when something touches your eyelashes?
options: You blink right away to protect the eye
Your eye waters to wash away the object
Your pupil shrinks to block out extra light
Your eyelid slowly closes after a short delay
explanation: When something touches the eyelashes, we blink right away to protect the eye.

q: What is the best way to remove fly germs from your hands and food before eating?
options: Wash with soap and water
Wipe with a dry cloth
Blow on the food to remove germs
Leave food in the sun to kill germs
explanation: Water and soap remove the germs that flies leave on hands and food.

q: How do chemicals in cigarettes affect the blood and raise the risk of a heart attack?
options: They make blood cells stick together so blood clots more easily, which can block a vessel
They thin the blood so much that vessels burst and bleed inside
They destroy red blood cells so less oxygen reaches the heart
They cause the heart to beat so fast that vessels wear out quickly
explanation: Chemicals in cigarettes make blood cells stick together so blood clots more easily; a clot can block a vessel and trigger a heart attack.

q: Where does the venom of a male platypus come from?
options: A gland in the thigh connected to the spur by a tube
A sac behind the beak that fills with venom when threatened
Glands along the tail that release venom through the skin
A pouch near the stomach that makes the venom
explanation: A gland in the thigh of the male platypus makes the venom and connects to the spur through a tube.

q: What are head lice?
options: Tiny wingless insects that live in human hair and on the scalp
Small mites that burrow into the skin of the scalp
Tiny worms that feed on dead skin cells in hair
Microscopic bacteria that cause an itchy rash
explanation: Head lice are tiny wingless insects that live in human hair and on the scalp.

q: What is a symptom?
options: A sign that something is happening in the body, not the disease itself
The exact same thing as the disease that caused it
The name doctors give to a group of sick people
A medicine taken to treat an illness
explanation: A symptom is not the disease itself but only a sign that something is happening in the body.

q: What makes a rock an ore?
options: It holds enough metal to be worth taking out
It is harder than any other type of rock
It glows when brought close to a magnet
It formed deep underground near a volcano
explanation: Ore is a kind of rock that holds enough metal to be worth taking out.

q: Why are broad-spectrum antibiotics more likely to disturb the gut than narrow-spectrum ones?
options: Because they target a wider range of bacteria, including helpful gut bacteria
Because they are stronger chemicals that damage the stomach lining
Because they are taken in larger doses that overwhelm the digestive system
Because they travel to the gut first before reaching the infected area
explanation: Broad-spectrum antibiotics target a wider range of bacteria, so they are more likely to disrupt the beneficial gut microbiome than narrow-spectrum types.

q: How does reverse osmosis desalination produce fresh water from seawater?
options: It forces seawater through a membrane that blocks salt ions
It boils seawater and collects the steam, leaving salt behind
It adds chemicals to seawater that make salt sink to the bottom
It freezes seawater so the salt separates from the ice
explanation: Reverse osmosis desalination forces seawater through a semi-permeable membrane that blocks salt ions, producing fresh water.

q: How do scientists prepare a germ to be used in some vaccines?
options: They weaken or kill it so it can no longer cause disease but the body can still recognize it
They make it stronger so the body learns to fight the hardest form
They remove it completely and replace it with a harmless copy made of plastic
They freeze it so it becomes inactive and can be stored safely
explanation: To make some vaccines, scientists weaken or kill the germ until it can no longer cause disease, so the body can recognize it safely.

q: Where is the sweet juice found in a sugarcane plant?
options: Inside the stalk, between the joints called nodes
In the long leaves at the very top of the plant
In the roots that absorb water from the soil
In a special sac just below the topmost leaves
explanation: The sweet juice is inside the stalk of the sugarcane plant, between the nodes (joints).

q: When an ionic bond forms between a metal and a nonmetal, what happens to the metal atom?
options: It loses electrons
It gains electrons from the nonmetal
It shares electrons equally with the nonmetal
It stays unchanged while only the nonmetal changes
explanation: When an ionic bond forms, metal atoms tend to lose electrons while nonmetal atoms tend to gain them.

q: Why do many people grow ferns at home?
options: For decoration, because of their beautiful green leaves
To eat the roots as a vegetable
To repel insects from the house
To produce oxygen faster than other houseplants
explanation: Many people grow ferns at home as decoration — they look beautiful, especially the hanging kinds with green leaves that dangle down.

q: Why do people sometimes get diarrhea while taking antibiotics?
options: Antibiotics can also kill the helpful bacteria in the gut
Antibiotics make the stomach produce too much acid
Antibiotics slow down digestion by relaxing the gut muscles
Antibiotics change the color of food in the stomach
explanation: Antibiotics can also kill the helpful bacteria in our gut, which is why people sometimes get diarrhea while taking them.

q: What wind speed is associated with PAGASA Typhoon Signal No. 5?
options: 185 km/h or higher
120 to 149 km/h
150 to 184 km/h
100 to 119 km/h
explanation: Signal No. 5 means winds of 185 km/h or higher — the level of a super typhoon.

q: What is the unit used to measure momentum?
options: Kilogram-meter per second (kg·m/s)
Newton (N)
Joule (J)
Watt (W)
explanation: The unit of momentum is the kilogram-meter per second (kg·m/s).

q: What makes metals look shiny and able to bounce light back?
options: Their free electrons
Their tightly packed atoms
The smooth surface created when they are mined
The layer of air trapped between metal crystals
explanation: The free electrons in metals are why metals look shiny and bounce light back.

q: Why is it important to stay home and rest when you have the flu or a cold?
options: To stop germs from spreading to classmates and family
To recover faster because the school air makes you sicker
To avoid getting medicine that might cause side effects
Because the school rules require it even for mild illness
explanation: Staying home and resting when you are sick helps because it stops germs from spreading to classmates and family.

q: In a Filipino dish like sinigang na hipon, which two parts of the shrimp are most often eaten?
options: The head and the tail
The legs and the eyes
The shell and the claws
The antennae and the body
explanation: In Filipino shrimp dishes like sinigang na hipon, the flavor-rich head and the meaty tail are the two parts most commonly eaten.

q: A shorter guitar string produces a higher pitch than a longer one. Why?
options: It vibrates more times per second, giving it a higher frequency.
It vibrates fewer times per second, giving it a lower frequency.
It is made of thicker material that pushes air harder.
It has more tension that slows down its movement.
explanation: A shorter string moves back and forth more times each second, so it has a higher frequency and produces a higher pitch.

q: Marble is a metamorphic rock. What was it before it became marble?
options: Limestone changed by heat and pressure underground
Granite cooled slowly from melted rock
Sandstone compressed by the weight of other rocks
Basalt erupted from a volcano and cooled quickly
explanation: Marble forms when limestone is changed by intense heat and pressure deep underground, making it a metamorphic rock.

q: Which of the following best describes an endemic species like the tarsier?
options: It is found only in one specific country and nowhere else in the world.
It can survive in many different countries across Asia.
It was brought to the Philippines from another country long ago.
It lives in the ocean and visits land only to breed.
explanation: Endemic species like the tarsier are found only in the Philippines and nowhere else, making their protection very important.

q: About how much of Earth's surface is covered by water?
options: About 71 percent
About 50 percent
About 29 percent
About 90 percent
explanation: About 71 percent of Earth's surface is covered by water, leaving only about 29 percent as land.

q: You look up and see big, puffy white clouds that look like cotton. What kind of weather do they usually mean?
options: Fair, sunny weather
Heavy rain is coming soon
A typhoon is approaching
Cold, foggy weather
explanation: Cumulus clouds are puffy and look like white cotton, and they usually mean fair, sunny weather.

q: Which sense still helps you find things even when the room is completely dark?
options: The sense of touch
The sense of sight
The sense of color vision
The sense of balance only
explanation: The sense of touch works even in the dark, so we can feel for things we cannot see.

q: Where does abaca fiber come from on the abaca plant?
options: From the outer layers of the leaf stalks that form its trunk-like stem
From the roots buried deep in the soil
From the seeds inside the fruit
From the broad surface of its leaves
explanation: Abaca fiber is taken from the outer layers of the leaf stalks that form the plant's trunk-like stem.

q: How can a house lizard escape when an enemy grabs it?
options: It drops its own tail and runs away.
It bites the enemy with sharp teeth.
It releases a bad-smelling liquid.
It changes color to blend in with the wall.
explanation: When caught, a house lizard can drop its own tail to escape from an enemy.

q: Hormones are found in very tiny amounts in the body. What is surprising about them?
options: Even in tiny amounts, they have a very strong effect on the body.
They only work when many of them build up over time.
They are too small to do anything useful on their own.
They need to be combined with vitamins before they can work.
explanation: Even though hormones are present in very tiny amounts, they have a strong effect on the body.

q: You see tiny water droplets on the grass early in the morning. How did they get there?
options: Water vapor in the air turned to liquid on cool surfaces overnight.
Underground water seeped up through the soil and grass.
It rained lightly just before sunrise.
The plants pushed water out through their roots.
explanation: Dew forms when the night cools and water vapor in the air turns to liquid on cold surfaces like leaves and grass.

q: Why does fresh carabao milk spoil quickly if left out in a warm place?
options: Bacteria multiply fast when it is warm.
The fat in the milk melts and goes bad.
Warm air pushes oxygen into the milk.
The milk dries out and loses its water.
explanation: Fresh carabao milk spoils quickly because bacteria multiply when it is warm, so it must be kept cold and clean.

q: What caused most of the deaths when Typhoon Yolanda struck the Philippines?
options: A storm surge—a wall of seawater—that flooded the land
Extremely strong winds that blew down houses
Landslides triggered by heavy rainfall
Lightning strikes during the typhoon
explanation: The storm surge, a wall of seawater, caused most of the deaths in Typhoon Yolanda.

q: On the Mohs hardness scale, which mineral comes right after talc at number 2?
options: Gypsum
Quartz
Feldspar
Calcite
explanation: Gypsum is number 2 on the Mohs scale, just above talc, and it can still be scratched with a fingernail.

q: Which part of the radish (labanos) plant do we eat?
options: Its swollen root that grows underground
Its large green leaves on top
Its small yellow flowers
Its thin fibrous stem above the soil
explanation: The radish's swollen root, which has a slightly spicy taste, is the part that grows underground and that we eat.

q: Why does a carabao overheat so easily on a hot sunny day?
options: Its dark skin absorbs more heat and it produces very little sweat to cool down.
Its thick layer of fat traps too much heat inside its body.
It breathes too slowly to release enough body heat.
It cannot drink enough water because of its large body.
explanation: A carabao's dark skin soaks up more of the sun's heat, and because it makes very little sweat, it struggles to cool itself.

q: Who built early powerful microscopes that allowed him to observe microbes for the first time?
options: Anton van Leeuwenhoek
Galileo Galilei
Louis Pasteur
Robert Hooke
explanation: Anton van Leeuwenhoek built his own powerful single-lens microscopes, which let him see microbes.

q: In fermentation, what do microbes do to food that changes its flavor, smell, and texture?
options: They break down proteins and sugars into smaller parts.
They add new minerals by pulling them from the air.
They freeze the food to preserve its original taste.
They coat the food with a protective layer of acids.
explanation: In fermentation, microbes break down proteins and sugars, which changes the food's flavor, smell, and texture.

q: How do forest trees make their own food?
options: They use sunlight, water, and air through their green leaves.
They absorb nutrients directly from other plants nearby.
They collect insects in their bark and digest them.
They get energy from the warmth of the soil around their roots.
explanation: Forest trees make their own food using sunlight, water, and air through their green leaves.

q: Where in the world are epiphytes like orchids and ferns most commonly found?
options: In warm, wet tropical rainforests
In cold, dry deserts near the equator
On the rocky cliffs of mountain peaks
At the bottom of deep ocean trenches
explanation: Epiphytes are most common in warm, wet tropical rainforests; in the Philippines, many epiphytic orchids and ferns grow in our forests.

q: During a chemical reaction, what happens to the atoms that were in the original substances?
options: They are rearranged into new molecules, but the number of each type of atom stays the same.
Some atoms are destroyed to release energy for the reaction.
New atoms are created from the energy produced by the reaction.
The atoms shrink in size so the new substance weighs less.
explanation: In any chemical reaction the number of each type of atom does not change; the atoms are only regrouped and rearranged into new molecules.

q: What must an eggplant grow first before it can produce its fruit?
options: A flower
A second set of leaves
A thick woody stem
A deep taproot
explanation: Eggplant, tomato, and okra must first grow flowers before they can produce fruit.

q: What is a coral actually made of?
options: Thousands of tiny creatures called polyps
Layers of calcium rock built up over time
A colony of seaweed that hardens over time
Sand and minerals stuck together by ocean currents
explanation: A coral is an animal made of thousands of tiny creatures called polyps, not a rock or a plant.

q: What is a bacteriophage?
options: A virus that attacks and destroys bacteria
A medicine that kills viruses inside the body
A type of bacteria that destroys other bacteria
A white blood cell that fights infections
explanation: Bacteriophages are viruses that attack bacteria instead of people, and they destroy bacteria.

q: Besides holding up the plant, what else does the stem do with food?
options: It carries food made by the leaves to the rest of the plant.
It stores extra sunlight to use at night.
It produces food on its own using water from the soil.
It releases food into the air to attract insects.
explanation: The stem carries the food made by the leaves to the rest of the plant.

q: During the amihan season, which parts of the Philippines receive the most rain?
options: The eastern regions like Bicol and eastern Visayas
The western regions like Ilocos and Palawan
The central mountain ranges of Luzon
The southern islands of Mindanao and the Sulu Sea
explanation: During the amihan, the eastern parts of the country like Bicol and eastern Visayas get rain because the wind hits there first.

q: Why is piña cloth so expensive?
options: Every step of making it is done by hand and takes a very long time.
The pineapple plants that produce the fibers are very rare.
It must be dyed with costly imported chemicals.
Machines that weave it are extremely difficult to operate.
explanation: Piña cloth is expensive because every step of its production is done by hand and takes a long time.

q: Scientists measure huge distances in space using a unit called a light-year. What is this unit based on?
options: The distance light travels in one year at 300,000 km per second
The time it takes a rocket to travel from Earth to the Moon
The distance from Earth to the nearest star multiplied by 100
The number of kilometers in one full orbit around the Sun
explanation: Scientists use the speed of light—about 300,000 km per second—as a cosmic measuring stick, expressing star distances as light-years.

q: Besides being spread by mosquito bites, how else can Zika virus be passed on?
options: From a pregnant mother to her unborn baby
Through sharing food or drinking water with an infected person
By touching the skin of someone who has the virus
By breathing the same air as an infected person
explanation: Besides mosquitoes, Zika can also pass from a pregnant mother to her baby.

q: What does a tamaraw do during the hottest part of the day?
options: It hides and rests inside dense thickets so it won't be seen.
It wades into rivers to cool itself down.
It climbs trees to find shade among the branches.
It burrows into the ground to escape the heat.
explanation: During the heat of the day, the lone tamaraw rests and hides inside dense thickets so that it will not be seen.

q: Coal and oil are both fossil fuels, but they formed from different living things. What did coal mostly form from?
options: Ancient swamp plants
Tiny sea creatures like plankton
Large marine reptiles like dinosaurs
Shellfish that lived on the ocean floor
explanation: Coal usually formed from ancient swamp plants, while oil and natural gas formed mostly from tiny sea creatures like plankton.

q: Why does Earth's air stay around the planet instead of floating off into space?
options: Earth's gravity holds the atmosphere in place.
The Sun's heat pushes the air back toward Earth.
The Moon's pull keeps the air pressed against Earth.
Air is too heavy to be moved by anything in space.
explanation: Earth's gravity holds the atmosphere in place so the air does not drift off into space.

q: Why does Philippine law forbid killing or capturing the tamaraw?
options: Because it is a protected species that needs to be conserved
Because it is sacred in indigenous Filipino religion
Because it is domesticated and owned by the government
Because it provides milk and meat to Filipino farmers
explanation: Philippine law forbids killing or capturing the tamaraw because it is a protected species.

q: Why is the carabao a fitting national animal of the Philippines?
options: It can be found in almost every province, from Luzon to Mindanao.
It is the largest and strongest animal found in the country.
It has been used in Philippine festivals for thousands of years.
It is found only in the Philippines and nowhere else in the world.
explanation: The carabao is fitting as the national animal because it can be found in almost every province of the Philippines, from Luzon to Mindanao.

q: When you peel an orange, what do you find inside it?
options: Small segments full of juice
A single large seed surrounded by pulp
Layers of dry fiber with a liquid center
Two halves separated by a hard membrane
explanation: Citrus fruits like oranges are divided inside into small segments full of juice.

q: How can scientists tell one whale shark apart from another?
options: Each whale shark has a unique spot pattern, like a fingerprint.
Each whale shark has a different shaped tail fin.
Each whale shark has a different number of gill slits.
Each whale shark has a different color on its belly.
explanation: Each whale shark has a unique pattern of white and yellow spots on its back, and no two whale sharks share the same pattern.

q: Besides killing harmful bacteria, what unintended effect can antibiotics have?
options: They can also kill the good bacteria living in our gut.
They can destroy the white blood cells that fight infection.
They can cause the immune system to attack healthy cells.
They can prevent new bacteria from ever growing in the body.
explanation: Antibiotic medicines can kill not only disease-causing bacteria but also the good bacteria in our gut.

q: The Philippines mines a lot of gold and copper. Why are almost all diamonds in Filipino jewelry brought in from other countries?
options: The Philippines does not mine diamonds, so they must be imported.
Philippine diamonds are too small to be used in jewelry.
It is illegal to sell locally mined diamonds in the Philippines.
All diamonds found here are used only by the government.
explanation: The Philippines mines gold and copper but not diamonds, so almost all diamonds in jewelry here are imported from other countries.

q: What makes the peanut plant unusual compared to most other crops?
options: Its pods grow and ripen underground rather than above the soil.
Its roots grow above the ground and collect sunlight.
It produces fruit before it grows any flowers.
Its seeds must be planted upside down to grow properly.
explanation: The peanut is unusual because its pods grow and ripen underground, unlike most crops whose fruit develops above the soil.

q: How big is the pilandok, one of the smallest hoofed animals in the world?
options: About the size of a rabbit
About the size of a small dog
About the size of a sheep
About the size of a young deer
explanation: The pilandok is one of the smallest hoofed animals in the whole world, roughly the size of a rabbit.

q: Why do many birds build nests?
options: To hold their eggs and keep their chicks safe
To store food during cold or dry seasons
To attract a mate by showing off building skills
To protect themselves from rain and wind at night
explanation: Many birds build a nest to hold their eggs and keep their chicks safe.

q: What is the purpose of the Philippines' Expanded Program on Immunization (EPI)?
options: To provide free vaccines to Filipino children against diseases like TB, hepatitis B, and measles
To give free vitamins to malnourished children in public schools
To train health workers to treat tropical diseases in rural areas
To distribute free medicines to families below the poverty line
explanation: The Philippines EPI provides free vaccines to Filipino children against BCG (TB), hepatitis B, DTP, polio, measles, and other diseases.

q: How does venom help the Komodo dragon catch its prey?
options: It thins the blood and lowers blood pressure, making the prey slowly weaken.
It paralyzes the prey's muscles so it cannot move at all.
It causes the prey to fall asleep within seconds.
It makes the prey lose its sense of direction and get lost.
explanation: The Komodo dragon's venom thins the blood and lowers the blood pressure of its prey, causing the prey to slowly weaken.

q: Purple sulfur bacteria perform photosynthesis differently from plants. What do they produce instead of oxygen?
options: Sulfur
Carbon dioxide
Nitrogen gas
Water vapor
explanation: Purple sulfur bacteria use hydrogen sulfide instead of water and produce sulfur instead of oxygen during their anoxygenic photosynthesis.

q: Who invented the first practical electric light bulb for everyday use?
options: Thomas Edison
Alexander Graham Bell
Nikola Tesla
Benjamin Franklin
explanation: Thomas Edison invented the first practical electric light bulb for everyday use.

q: A woodpecker hammers its beak into hard wood thousands of times a day. What body features work together to protect its head?
options: Its thick skull, long tongue, and strong neck all work together.
Its hollow bones and lightweight feathers absorb the shock.
Its curved beak and large eyes cushion the impact.
Its soft head feathers and flexible spine reduce the force.
explanation: Many parts of a woodpecker's body—thick skull, long tongue, and strong neck—work together to keep its head from getting hurt.

q: Why is the tardigrade (water bear) considered the toughest animal on Earth?
options: It can survive extreme heat, extreme cold, and even the conditions of outer space.
It has a shell harder than any known material on Earth.
It can regrow any part of its body that is cut off.
It produces a poison that kills anything that tries to eat it.
explanation: The tardigrade is considered the toughest animal because it can survive extreme heat, cold, and even outer space.

q: In what year did the Philippines gain independence from the United States?
explanation: The Philippines officially gained independence from the United States on July 4, 1946.

q: What do scientists call a fault that has moved recently and is likely to move again?
options: An active fault
A dormant fault
A transform fault
A passive fault
explanation: PHIVOLCS watches active faults because they have moved recently and could cause earthquakes by moving again.

q: How does a biofertilizer using Rhizobium bacteria help a plant grow?
options: It converts nitrogen from the air into a nutrient the plant can absorb
It breaks down rocks in the soil to release minerals
It produces its own food through photosynthesis in the roots
It drives off pests by releasing a natural chemical
explanation: Rhizobium bacteria fix atmospheric nitrogen, turning it into a usable nutrient for plants and reducing the need for chemical fertilizers.

q: How does a tailorbird build its nest?
options: It pokes holes in a leaf and threads plant fibers through them to stitch the leaf into a nest
It weaves dry grasses into a cup shape and glues it with mud
It hollows out a tree trunk with its beak and lines it with feathers
It collects spider webs and wraps them around a branch to form a sack
explanation: The tailorbird uses its beak like a needle, stitching leaves together with plant fibers or spider silk to form its nest.

q: What does the inside flesh of a guyabano look like and taste like?
options: White and juicy with a sweet-and-sour taste
Yellow and dry with a purely sweet taste
Green and crunchy with a bitter taste
Purple and watery with no strong flavor
explanation: The flesh of the guyabano is white, juicy, and has a taste that is both sweet and sour.

q: How does washing hands with soap help protect your body?
options: It helps prevent intestinal worms from entering your body
It kills the viruses that cause colds and flu inside your stomach
It removes excess oil that causes skin rashes
It strengthens your immune system by training white blood cells
explanation: Washing hands often with soap is a simple way to prevent intestinal worms from being swallowed.

q: What happens to speed and turning force when a small gear drives a larger gear?
options: Speed decreases but turning force increases
Speed increases and turning force also increases
Speed decreases and turning force also decreases
Speed increases but turning force decreases
explanation: When a small gear drives a big gear, you trade speed for more turning force, which is useful for doing heavy work.

q: What is the purpose of the row of holes along the side of an abalone's shell?
options: They let exhaled water exit after the gills have absorbed oxygen
They are used to attach the abalone firmly to rocks
They allow the abalone to sense vibrations in the water
They are passages through which the abalone lays eggs
explanation: The holes along the abalone's shell let used water escape after the gills inside have taken in oxygen.

q: How does smoking affect the heart and blood vessels?
options: It harms them and raises the risk of heart disease
It strengthens them by making the heart beat faster over time
It has no direct effect on the heart but harms only the lungs
It thickens artery walls in a way that lowers blood pressure
explanation: Smoking harms the heart and blood vessels, raising the risk of heart disease.

q: Why is early treatment so important when someone is exposed to a rabid animal?
options: Because rabies is almost always fatal once symptoms begin
Because symptoms appear within minutes if treatment is delayed
Because the virus spreads to other people through touch
Because the only cure works only on children, not adults
explanation: Rabies is nearly always fatal once symptoms start, so treatment must begin as early as possible before symptoms appear.

q: What does it mean if you gently pinch the skin on the back of your hand and it returns slowly instead of snapping back?
options: It is a sign of dehydration
It means your blood pressure is too high
It shows you have enough body water
It indicates an allergic reaction
explanation: When pinched skin returns slowly and stays tented, it is a sign that the body is dehydrated and needs water.

q: Why do root vegetables like carrots and sweet potatoes need to be scrubbed harder than fruits that hang on a tree?
options: They grow under the soil and hold more clinging dirt and sand
They have a harder outer skin that is more difficult to remove
They absorb more pesticides than fruits that grow above ground
They have more bacteria inside their flesh than other vegetables
explanation: Root vegetables grow right in the soil, so more dirt and sand clings to them and they need extra scrubbing.

q: How do restored forests help communities that depend on streams?
options: They help store clean water in streams and watersheds
They prevent all flooding by absorbing rain instantly
They filter saltwater and turn it into freshwater
They cool the air enough to reduce evaporation from rivers
explanation: Restored forests help store clean water in streams and watersheds, protecting water sources for communities.

q: What happens when you place a celery stalk in a glass of colored water?
options: The colored water climbs up through the stalk by capillary action
The stalk pushes water down because plants only absorb water at the roots
The color stays at the bottom and does not enter the stalk
The stalk dissolves and the water turns colorless
explanation: Capillary action causes the colored water to travel upward through tiny tubes inside the celery stalk.

q: A single stalk of malunggay has many small leaflets on it. What kind of leaf is this?
options: A compound leaf
A simple leaf
A parallel-veined leaf
A needle leaf
explanation: Malunggay has compound leaves — one stalk bearing many small leaflets that are all part of one leaf, not separate leaves.

q: Which action is the best example of 'reuse'?
options: Turning an old can into a pencil holder instead of throwing it away
Sorting plastic bottles into a recycling bin
Buying a new bag to replace a torn one
Burning old newspapers to reduce trash
explanation: Reuse means using something again instead of discarding it, like making an old can into a pencil holder.

q: How does a mother civet care for her newborn babies?
options: She feeds them her milk until they grow and can find their own food
She hides them inside a hollow tree and brings insects every hour
She carries them on her back until they are fully grown
She teaches them to hunt by bringing live prey to the den
explanation: A mother civet nurses her tiny, helpless babies with her milk until they grow up and learn to find food on their own.

q: What part of your body is responsible for giving you the feeling of hunger or thirst?
options: A small part of the brain that monitors food and water levels
The stomach, which shrinks when empty and sends pain signals
The kidneys, which release hormones when water is low
The tongue, which detects lack of saliva and tells you to drink
explanation: A small part of the brain constantly monitors your body's food and water levels and sends the signals we feel as hunger or thirst.

q: Why do antibiotics NOT work when you have a viral infection like the flu?
options: Antibiotics only target bacteria, not viruses
Antibiotics are too weak to reach the bloodstream where viruses live
Viruses hide inside bone marrow where antibiotics cannot go
Antibiotics destroy the white blood cells needed to fight viruses
explanation: Antibiotics are designed to attack bacteria, so they have no effect on viruses at all.

q: How does a sea sponge get the oxygen it needs to survive?
options: It absorbs oxygen straight from water that flows through its body
It rises to the surface to breathe air like dolphins do
It uses photosynthesis to make oxygen from sunlight
It absorbs oxygen through a set of small, simple lungs
explanation: A sponge has no lungs and gets oxygen directly from water flowing through its body.

q: How does tuberculosis (TB) spread from one person to another?
options: Through the air when a sick person coughs
Through contaminated food and water only
By touching the skin of an infected person
Through mosquito bites like dengue fever
explanation: TB is a bacterial disease that usually attacks the lungs and spreads through the air when an infected person coughs.

q: Why are female ducks, not male ducks, raised for egg production?
options: Only female ducks lay eggs
Male ducks lay eggs but in much smaller numbers
Both sexes lay eggs, but female eggs are larger
Only male ducks lay fertilized eggs that can be eaten
explanation: Only female ducks lay eggs, which is why egg farms raise females.

q: A student says the ozone hole causes global warming. What is wrong with this statement?
options: The ozone hole and global warming are two different problems — the ozone hole is about UV rays, not trapped heat
The ozone hole is actually good because it cools the planet by letting heat escape
Global warming creates the ozone hole, so they are the same problem viewed differently
The ozone hole only affects the poles, while global warming affects only the equator
explanation: The ozone hole and global warming are separate issues: the ozone hole allows harmful UV rays in, while global warming is caused by heat being trapped by greenhouse gases.

q: What is the smallest piece of an element that still keeps that element's identity?
options: The atom
The molecule
The cell
The compound
explanation: The atom is the smallest unit that retains an element's identity; splitting it further by chemistry means it is no longer that element.

q: Why does a leech bite keep bleeding for a few hours after the leech is removed?
options: A substance in the leech's saliva that prevents clotting is still in the skin
The leech leaves tiny teeth behind that keep the wound open
The skin takes hours to close because leech bites are very deep
The blood becomes thinner after a leech bite due to a chemical reaction
explanation: The leech's saliva contains an anti-clotting substance that stays in the wound and keeps it bleeding even after the leech is gone.

q: Why do ecosystems with more species recover better from disasters than those with few species?
options: More species and more interconnected food webs make the ecosystem more resilient
More species means more competition, which keeps the ecosystem in perfect balance
Few species make it easier for the surviving ones to adapt quickly
More species means more food for humans, which motivates conservation efforts
explanation: Ecosystems with greater species diversity and more interconnected food webs are more resilient and better able to recover from disturbances.

q: How does a silkworm form its cocoon?
options: It moves its head around and around to wrap itself in a continuous thread of silk
It collects loose silk from the ground and packs it into a ball around itself
It spins silk outward from its body like a spider spins a web
It bites silk from another cocoon and weaves it into a new one
explanation: The silkworm spins its cocoon by moving its head in circles, wrapping itself in a single long silk thread.

q: Which crocodile was recognized by Guinness World Records as the largest ever held in captivity?
options: Lolong, from the Philippines
Gustave, from Burundi
Rex, from Australia
Dominator, from Papua New Guinea
explanation: Lolong, a saltwater crocodile captured in the Philippines, holds the Guinness World Record for the largest crocodile ever held in captivity.

q: How do cleaner fish and large fish benefit each other in a mutualistic relationship?
options: The cleaner fish gets food by eating parasites off the large fish, while the large fish gets cleaned
The large fish protects the cleaner fish from predators in exchange for being guided to food
The cleaner fish shares its mucus coating with the large fish to prevent disease
The large fish digests food faster because the cleaner fish removes harmful bacteria from its skin
explanation: In this mutualism, the small cleaner fish gains food while the large fish benefits from having parasites and dead skin removed.

q: Why do invasive species often grow in huge numbers in a new place?
options: There are no natural predators, diseases, or competitors to keep their numbers in check
They reproduce faster in warmer climates than in their home region
The new soil contains nutrients their bodies have never had before
They evolve new traits within one generation that help them survive anywhere
explanation: Invasive species spread quickly because their new environment lacks the natural enemies and competitors that limited their numbers at home.

q: What property of metals allows them to be pulled and stretched into thin wires?
options: Ductility
Malleability
Conductivity
Brittleness
explanation: Metals are ductile, meaning they can be stretched and pulled into thin wires without breaking.

q: Why do your hands feel warmer when you rub them together?
options: Friction between the hands produces heat
The blood vessels widen when hands move, releasing stored heat
The skin absorbs heat from the surrounding air more easily when moving
Static electricity builds up and warms the skin
explanation: When you rub your hands together, friction converts the motion into heat energy, warming your hands.

q: What type of roots does the kapok tree have that help it stand firmly?
options: Wide, wing-like buttress roots at its base
Long, deep taproots that reach the water table
Shallow, spreading prop roots around its trunk
Aerial roots that hang down from its branches
explanation: The kapok tree has wide buttress roots that spread out at its base and support it like wings.

q: Compared to a worker bee that lives only a few weeks, how long can a queen bee live?
options: About 5 years
About 6 months
About 1 year
About 2 weeks
explanation: A queen bee can live for about 5 years, far longer than a worker bee that lives only a few weeks.

q: What do the bright colors of a nudibranch warn other animals about?
options: That the nudibranch is distasteful or toxic
That the nudibranch is ready to mate
That the nudibranch is the dominant animal in that area
That the nudibranch is closely related to poisonous corals
explanation: Nudibranchs use bright colors as a warning signal, telling predators that they are toxic or bad-tasting.

q: How is granite formed?
options: From magma that cooled slowly deep underground
From layers of sediment pressed together over time
From existing rocks changed by heat and pressure
From lava that cooled quickly on Earth's surface
explanation: Granite is an igneous rock that forms when magma cools slowly deep beneath the surface, allowing large crystals to develop.

q: What is the purpose of a weather chart that students fill in each day?
options: To track whether each day is sunny, rainy, or cloudy so we can see weather patterns
To predict exactly when a typhoon will arrive next month
To record temperatures around the world for global scientists
To count the number of rainy days needed before planting crops
explanation: A weather chart records daily conditions — sunny, rainy, or cloudy — so students can observe patterns in the weather over time.

q: What does a Storm Signal No. 4 warning mean for people in an area?
options: Very strong, destructive winds may arrive within about 12 hours and can heavily damage many houses
Light rains and gentle winds are expected throughout the day
A moderate storm will arrive within 36 hours with some flooding possible
Extreme flooding is certain and all residents must evacuate immediately
explanation: Signal No. 4 warns of very strong destructive winds expected within about 12 hours that can cause heavy damage.

q: How can you identify a sperm whale by its blowhole spray?
options: The spray shoots out slanted to the left, not straight up
The spray is the tallest of any whale and reaches 10 meters high
The spray comes from two blowholes and forms a V shape
The spray is invisible because the water is forced back into the sea
explanation: A sperm whale's blowhole is positioned so that its spray shoots out to the left at an angle, making it easy to identify.

q: Where does a mango seed originally come from?
options: It forms inside the fruit of a mango tree after the flower becomes a fruit
It falls from the sky as part of the rain cycle
It grows directly out of the ground without needing a parent tree
It is carried by birds who deposit it as a fully formed seed
explanation: A mango tree flowers first, the flower becomes a fruit, and the seed forms inside that fruit — so every seed comes from a parent tree.

q: Why is solar power especially useful for remote Philippine islands?
options: They are not connected to the main power grid, so solar panels and batteries can supply electricity without long undersea cables
They have more sunlight than other parts of Asia, making solar the cheapest option everywhere
The national government requires all islands to use renewable energy by law
Islands need less power than cities, so small solar panels are enough for any community
explanation: Remote Philippine islands without grid connections can use solar panels and batteries to generate electricity independently.

q: What happens when you push the north pole of one magnet toward the north pole of another magnet?
options: They push each other away (repel)
They pull strongly toward each other (attract)
They stick together and cannot be separated
Nothing happens because north poles are neutral
explanation: Like poles repel each other, so two north poles (or two south poles) will push away from each other.

q: What is one key difference between chikungunya and dengue fever?
options: Chikungunya causes worse joint pain while dengue lowers blood platelets
Chikungunya lowers blood platelets while dengue causes worse joint pain
Chikungunya is spread by mosquitoes while dengue is spread by ticks
Chikungunya requires hospitalization while dengue can always be treated at home
explanation: Although dengue and chikungunya are easy to confuse, chikungunya is known for severe joint pain while dengue is known for lowering blood platelet counts.

q: What is hydrophobia, and which disease causes it?
options: A strong fear of water caused by painful throat spasms, which is a symptom of rabies
An extreme thirst that cannot be satisfied, caused by dehydration after a snake bite
A fear of drowning that develops after any animal scratch near the neck
An inability to swallow liquids, caused by food poisoning from raw meat
explanation: Rabies causes painful throat spasms when a person tries to swallow water, leading to a well-known fear of water called hydrophobia.

q: How is a wheel and axle similar to a lever?
options: The axle acts as the fulcrum, and the wheel lets you push continuously around instead of just one stroke
They both use pulleys to multiply force along a straight line
Both machines must be used with a counterweight to work properly
They are completely different — a lever lifts while a wheel-axle only rolls
explanation: A wheel and axle is like a rotating lever: the axle is the fulcrum, and turning the wheel lets you apply force round and round instead of one stroke at a time.

q: Besides carbon dioxide, what other gas is released when fuels like wood or gas burn?
options: Water vapor
Nitrogen gas
Oxygen gas
Helium gas
explanation: Wood and gas contain hydrogen, so when they burn they release water vapor along with carbon dioxide.

q: The Philippine monsoon is part of which larger weather system?
options: The Asian monsoon system that also affects India, Bangladesh, Vietnam, and Thailand
The Pacific Ocean current system that controls rainfall across all Pacific islands
The El Niño cycle that originates near South America
The Intertropical Convergence Zone found only above the equator
explanation: The Philippine monsoon is one part of the broader Asian monsoon system shared by many countries including India, Bangladesh, Vietnam, and Thailand.

q: Why do doctors test a patient's reflexes, such as the knee-jerk test?
options: To check that the nerves and spinal cord are working well
To measure how strong the patient's leg muscles are
To test whether the patient is suffering from dehydration
To check if the patient's heart rate is within a healthy range
explanation: Reflex tests like the knee-jerk help doctors confirm that the nerves and spinal cord are functioning properly.

q: What is the main difference between conductive hearing loss and sensorineural hearing loss?
options: Conductive loss is often treatable because sound is blocked in the outer/middle ear, while sensorineural loss from nerve or cochlea damage is usually permanent
Conductive loss is permanent because it involves nerve damage, while sensorineural loss is temporary and clears on its own
Both types are permanent, but conductive loss is louder while sensorineural loss affects only high-pitched sounds
Sensorineural loss is treatable with surgery while conductive loss requires a hearing aid forever
