explanation: Conductive hearing loss is often treatable since it involves a blockage in the outer or middle ear, whereas sensorineural loss from cochlea or nerve damage is usually permanent.

q: How do animals get the nitrogen they need?
options: By eating plants or other animals that already contain nitrogen
By breathing it in directly from the air like oxygen
By drinking water that contains dissolved nitrogen
By absorbing it through their skin from the soil
explanation: Animals obtain nitrogen by eating plants or other animals, passing nitrogen along through the food chain.

q: What is the Sun mostly made of?
options: Hydrogen
Helium
Oxygen
Iron
explanation: The Sun is mostly made of hydrogen, with some helium making up most of the rest.

q: How does an evaporative air cooler make the air feel cooler?
options: It evaporates water into the air, which absorbs heat
It blows air over frozen ice blocks
It compresses the air to lower its temperature
It pushes warm air out through a vent
explanation: Water evaporation absorbs a large amount of heat from the air, making it cooler.

q: When do neap tides — the weakest tides — occur?
options: When the Sun and Moon are at right angles to the Earth
When the Sun, Moon, and Earth are all in a straight line
When the Moon is closest to Earth
When the Moon is on the opposite side of Earth from the Sun
explanation: Neap tides happen at first and last quarter, when the Sun and Moon are at right angles to the Earth, so their gravitational pulls partly cancel each other.

q: Why do flies gather on garbage and rotting food?
options: They feed and lay their eggs there
They are looking for clean water nearby
They are attracted only by bright colors
They hide there to escape predators
explanation: Flies are drawn to dirty, smelly places like garbage and rotting food, where they both feed and lay their eggs.

q: Why is it important to wash your hands with soap and water before eating?
options: It removes germs so you do not get sick
It makes food taste better
It helps your body digest food faster
It prevents the food from spoiling
explanation: Washing hands with soap and water before eating removes germs that could make you sick.

q: Why does the false cleanerfish look like the real cleaner wrasse?
options: So it can sneak close to other fish and bite a chunk off them
So larger fish will not eat it
So it can share food with the real cleaner
So it can attract a mate more easily
explanation: The false cleanerfish mimics the real cleaner so other fish trust it and let it close enough to bite a chunk off them.

q: On which country's border does Mount Everest sit?
options: Nepal and Tibet (China)
India and Pakistan
Bhutan and China
Nepal and India
explanation: Mount Everest sits on the border between Nepal and Tibet (China) in the Himalaya mountains.

q: Which chromosome combination is usually found in biological males?
options: XY
XX
YY
XO
explanation: Biological sex is determined by sex chromosomes; females are usually XX and males are usually XY.

q: What is special about sounds in the 2,000–5,000 Hz range and your ear canal?
options: The ear canal's shape naturally amplifies those frequencies
The ear canal blocks those frequencies to protect the eardrum
The ear canal converts those frequencies into electrical signals faster
Those frequencies are too high for the ear canal to detect
explanation: The shape and length of the ear canal create a natural resonance that amplifies sounds in the 2,000–5,000 Hz range, which is most important for understanding speech.

q: About how fast does Earth travel as it orbits the Sun?
options: About 30 kilometers per second
About 3 kilometers per second
About 300 kilometers per second
About 0.3 kilometers per second
explanation: Earth orbits the Sun at a speed of about 30 kilometers per second.

q: Which of the following is NOT a job of the skin?
options: Producing red blood cells
Protecting the body from germs
Releasing heat through sweat
Blocking out harmful microbes
explanation: The skin protects the body, releases heat through sweat, and blocks out germs, but red blood cells are made inside bones, not in the skin.

q: How have whole mammoths been preserved so that even their fur and flesh survived?
options: They were frozen in ice in very cold places
They were buried quickly under volcanic ash
They were covered in tree resin that hardened into amber
They sank into peat bogs and were pickled by acid
explanation: In very cold places, whole mammoths have been found frozen in ice, preserving even their fur and flesh.

q: What do seeds need to start growing (germinate) after being planted in soil?
options: Water and warmth
Only sunlight and air
Salt and fertilizer
Darkness and cold temperatures
explanation: Seeds stay dormant until they are planted in soil, where water and warmth trigger them to germinate into new plants.

q: What happens to fat-soluble vitamins like A and D in the body, unlike water-soluble vitamins?
options: They are stored in the body
They are used up quickly and must be replaced daily
They dissolve in water and leave in urine
They are only found in fruits and vegetables
explanation: Fat-soluble vitamins like A and D are stored in the body, while water-soluble vitamins like C are used up quickly.

q: What do the kidneys help keep in the right balance inside the body?
options: Water and salt
Sugar and protein
Oxygen and carbon dioxide
Calcium and iron
explanation: The kidneys filter the blood and help keep the right balance of water and salt in the body.

q: After pollen lands on the stigma of a flower, what is the next step that eventually produces a seed?
options: A pollen tube grows down to the ovule, where fertilization occurs
The petals fall off immediately and the ovule becomes a fruit
The stamen releases more pollen to attract insects
The ovary swells with water to protect the seed
explanation: After pollen lands on the stigma, it grows a pollen tube down to the ovule where fertilization occurs, creating a seed that becomes part of the fruit.

q: What role do fungi and worms on the forest floor play in the ecosystem?
options: They break down fallen leaves and branches, returning nutrients to the soil
They compete with tree roots for water underground
They eat insects to keep pest populations low
They trap moisture in the soil to prevent drought
explanation: On the forest floor, fungi and worms break down fallen leaves and branches, returning nutrients to the soil.

q: What instrument is used to measure the strength (magnitude) of an earthquake?
options: Seismograph
Barometer
Anemometer
Richter scale reader
explanation: A seismograph is the instrument used to measure the strength, or magnitude, of an earthquake.

q: Why do people sometimes put guppies into ponds or water tanks?
options: The fish eat mosquito larvae, reducing mosquito numbers without chemicals
The fish keep the water clean by filtering it
The fish scare away adult mosquitoes
The fish compete with mosquito larvae for food
explanation: Guppies eat mosquito larvae, lowering the number of mosquitoes without the use of any chemicals.

q: Why do many reef sharks prefer to hunt at night or in the dark?
options: They can surprise sleeping fish and are harder to see in the dark
They have better eyesight in the dark than in daylight
Their prey is only active at night
They need cooler water temperatures to swim fast
explanation: Many reef sharks hunt more actively at night because it is easier to surprise sleeping fish and harder for prey to see them.

q: Why are birds light enough to fly even when they are large?
options: Many of their bones are hollow and filled with air
Their feathers are made of very light plastic-like material
They have fewer bones than other animals
Their muscles are smaller and lighter than in mammals
explanation: Birds are light enough to fly because many of their bones are hollow, filled with air inside, keeping their overall weight low.

q: What are the two parts that make up the stamen of a flower?
options: The anther and the filament
The stigma and the style
The petal and the sepal
The ovary and the ovule
explanation: The stamen consists of the anther (the pollen-containing sac at the tip) and the filament (the thin stalk supporting the anther).

q: Why do insects shed their hard outer skin (molt) as they grow?
options: Because their outer skin does not grow with them
Because the old skin becomes poisonous over time
Because they need to change color with the season
Because shedding removes harmful parasites
explanation: Insects molt (shed their hard outer skin) in order to grow, because that skin does not grow with them.

q: What happens to an atom when it loses or gains an electron?
options: It becomes charged and is called an ion
It becomes a new element
It splits into two smaller atoms
It releases energy as light
explanation: When an atom loses or gains an electron, it becomes electrically charged and is called an ion.

q: How do sponges help the ocean ecosystem?
options: They filter out tiny bits of dirt and microbes, keeping the seawater clean
They provide shelter for large predatory fish
They produce oxygen by photosynthesis underwater
They break down dead whales on the seafloor
explanation: Sponges help keep seawater clean by filtering out tiny bits of dirt and microbes.

q: How does the brightness of light affect the rate of photosynthesis in a plant?
options: Brighter light speeds it up; shade or darkness slows it down
Plants photosynthesize at the same rate in any amount of light
Dim light speeds up photosynthesis by reducing water loss
Too much bright light stops photosynthesis completely
explanation: Photosynthesis goes faster in brighter light and slows down in shade or darkness because there is less light energy available.

q: How does the size of a reef shark compare to that of a whale shark?
options: A reef shark is much smaller than a whale shark
A reef shark and a whale shark are about the same size
A reef shark is slightly larger than a whale shark
A reef shark can grow bigger than a whale shark
explanation: A reef shark is not as big as the giant whale shark and is usually smaller than a person, which is why it fits among reef cracks.

q: Why does food often taste bland when your nose is blocked?
options: Most of what we call flavor is actually smell; without the nose, flavor is reduced
The tongue stops working when there is pressure in the head
Blocked noses cause the taste buds to swell up
Chewing becomes harder, so less taste is released
explanation: Most of the flavor we experience is actually smell, so when the nose is blocked, much of what we taste disappears.

q: What makes an automatic weather station different from a traditional one?
options: Its sensors measure and send data by themselves over the internet without a person
It only measures temperature and does not need electricity
A person visits it once a week instead of every day
It uses radar instead of sensors to detect weather
explanation: Automatic weather stations have sensors that measure and send data over the internet on their own, even in hard-to-reach places.

q: How does planting trees help fight global warming?
options: Trees take in carbon dioxide from the air
Trees release oxygen that cools the atmosphere directly
Trees create rain clouds that lower temperatures
Trees block sunlight from reaching the ground
explanation: Planting trees helps fight warming because trees take in carbon dioxide, a greenhouse gas, from the air.

q: What is inside a malunggay pod?
options: Seeds that can sprout into new trees
Nectar that attracts insects
Roots waiting to grow into the soil
Leaves rolled up for protection
explanation: A malunggay pod is the long fruit of the malunggay tree that holds seeds inside, which can sprout into new trees.

q: Where do most leeches prefer to live?
options: In fresh water or in damp places like swamps and rice fields
In dry, rocky deserts and sandy beaches
In saltwater oceans and coral reefs
In treetops and leaf litter in forests
explanation: Most leeches live in fresh water or in damp, wet places such as swamps and rice fields.

q: What shape does DNA have, and what makes it a code for life?
options: A double helix (twisted ladder); the order of its four bases (A, T, C, G) forms the instructions
A straight ribbon; the length of the strand determines the instructions
A ring; the number of loops determines each trait
A spiral spring; the tightness of the coil stores genetic data
explanation: DNA is shaped like a double helix (twisted ladder), and the order of its four bases — A, T, C, and G — is the genetic code or instructions for life.

q: What are the two main jobs of a plant's roots?
options: To anchor the plant and to take in water and nutrients
To make food using sunlight and to store seeds
To produce flowers and to release oxygen
To transport water to leaves and to make fruit
explanation: Roots have two main jobs: anchoring the plant in the soil and taking in water and nutrients.

q: According to Kepler's laws, what shape are planetary orbits, and when does a planet move fastest?
options: Elliptical (oval); when closest to the Sun
Circular; when farthest from the Sun
Square-shaped; when at equal distance from the Sun
Elliptical (oval); when farthest from the Sun
explanation: According to Kepler's laws, planets orbit in elliptical (oval) paths and move fastest when they are closest to the Sun.

q: Which two very different materials are both made entirely from the element carbon?
options: Diamond and graphite
Diamond and coal tar
Graphite and quartz
Coal and limestone
explanation: Carbon can form hard diamond or soft graphite — the 'lead' inside a pencil — depending on how the carbon atoms are arranged.

q: What is the main difference between arteries and veins?
options: Arteries carry blood away from the heart; veins carry blood back to it
Arteries carry blood back to the heart; veins carry blood away from it
Arteries carry only oxygen; veins carry only nutrients
Arteries are found only in the arms; veins are found only in the legs
explanation: Arteries carry blood away from the heart, while veins carry blood back to it.

q: What determines how loud a sound is?
options: The amplitude (size) of the vibration
The frequency (pitch) of the vibration
The speed at which the sound travels
The material the sound travels through
explanation: The bigger the vibration's amplitude, the louder the sound we hear.

q: About how much can a large African elephant weigh?
options: Up to about 6 tonnes (6,000 kilograms)
Up to about 1 tonne (1,000 kilograms)
Up to about 3 tonnes (3,000 kilograms)
Up to about 10 tonnes (10,000 kilograms)
explanation: A large African elephant can weigh up to about 6 tonnes, which is around 6,000 kilograms.

q: Besides the videophone, what else did Filipino inventor Gregorio Zara build?
options: A solar-powered stove and water heater
An electric tricycle and a water pump
A wind turbine and a solar lamp
A rice cooker and a water desalination device
explanation: Gregorio Zara also built a solar-powered stove and water heater, in addition to inventing the videophone.

q: What does a seahorse use its long tail for?
options: To grip onto seagrass or coral
To sting predators that come near
To paddle forward through the water
To carry its eggs until they hatch
explanation: The seahorse uses its long tail to grip onto seagrass or coral so it is not swept away by currents.

q: How does a shark's skin help it sneak up on prey?
options: The denticles smooth the water flow, making the shark swim more quietly
The rough skin creates bubbles that confuse the prey's senses
The skin absorbs light, making the shark invisible in dark water
The skin produces a chemical that numbs the prey's sense of hearing
explanation: The denticles on shark skin smooth the flow of water, so the shark makes less noise as it swims and can sneak close to prey.

q: How does a spider eat its prey?
options: It dissolves the insides of the prey and sucks up the liquid
It chews through the hard shell with its strong fangs
It swallows the prey whole and digests it slowly
It cuts the prey into small pieces with its legs
explanation: A spider does not chew its food; it dissolves the inside of its prey and sucks up the liquid.

q: How is earthquake intensity determined, unlike magnitude?
options: By observing what people felt and how buildings and objects were affected
By measuring ground movement with a seismograph
By calculating the energy released at the epicenter
By recording the depth of the fault that caused the quake
explanation: Intensity is not measured by a machine; it is judged from what people felt and how buildings and objects in a place were affected.

q: Which parent carries the eggs in a seahorse family?
options: The male (father)
The female (mother)
Both parents take turns
Neither — the eggs are attached to seagrass
explanation: In seahorses, it is the male (father) who carries the eggs, not the female.

q: Which type of elephant has bigger ears?
options: The African elephant
The Asian elephant
Both have the same ear size
The Indian elephant (a different species)
explanation: The African elephant has bigger ears than the Asian elephant.

q: Which birds are found living in wetlands, rice fields, and lakes in the Philippines?
options: Herons, egrets, and the Philippine duck
Eagles, hornbills, and the Philippine cockatoo
Pigeons, sparrows, and the Philippine tarsier
Owls, bats, and the Philippine swift
explanation: Wetlands, rice fields, and lakes are home to herons, egrets, and the Philippine duck.

q: What happens to a virus when it is outside a living cell?
options: It becomes inactive and cannot do anything until it enters a host.
It multiplies quickly by feeding on nutrients in the air.
It stays active but moves slowly looking for a new host.
It breaks down completely and disappears after a few minutes.
explanation: Outside a living cell, a virus is like something asleep — it is inactive and can do nothing until it gets inside a host.

q: What happens as the Philippine Plate moves westward and goes under the Eurasian Plate?
options: Volcanoes, mountains, and earthquakes form in the Philippines.
The islands slowly sink deeper into the ocean over time.
Strong ocean currents form that change the weather patterns.
New flat plains are created by the grinding of the two plates.
explanation: The Philippine Plate's westward movement, subducting beneath the Eurasian Plate, is the process that creates the Philippines' volcanoes, mountains, and earthquakes.

q: What does it mean when a person has a fever?
options: The body is fighting an infection — fever is a sign, not a disease itself.
The person has caught a disease called fever that must be treated separately.
The body temperature is too low and needs to be warmed up quickly.
The immune system has stopped working and can no longer fight germs.
explanation: A fever is not a disease itself but a sign that the body is actively fighting an infection.

q: How does a termite digest the wood it eats?
options: Tiny microbes living inside the termite's gut help break the wood down into food.
The termite has a very powerful stomach acid that dissolves wood on its own.
The termite stores wood pieces in a special pouch until they soften enough to digest.
The termite mixes wood with saliva from special glands to break it down.
explanation: A termite cannot digest wood alone — protozoa and bacteria living in its gut break the cellulose down into food, so termite and microbes work together.

q: Scientists have discovered that protons and neutrons are actually made of even smaller particles. What does this tell us about atoms?
options: Atoms can be broken down further than just protons, neutrons, and electrons.
Atoms are the smallest possible particles and cannot be divided any further.
Protons are made of electrons packed tightly together inside the nucleus.
Neutrons split into protons when enough energy is applied to an atom.
explanation: Scientists discovered that protons and neutrons themselves are made of even smaller particles, showing atoms can be broken down further than originally thought.

q: Why must bitter cassava be cooked thoroughly before eating?
options: Because bitter cassava contains more poison that cooking helps remove.
Because raw bitter cassava is too hard for our stomachs to break down.
Because bitter cassava turns a harmful color when eaten without cooking.
Because the seeds inside bitter cassava are toxic and must be boiled out.
explanation: Bitter cassava has more poison than sweet cassava, so it must be cooked well to make it safe to eat.

q: What does the thresher shark use its very long tail for?
options: To slap and stun small fish before eating them.
To steer through strong ocean currents near the surface.
To hold onto rocks on the seafloor while it rests.
To attract a mate during the breeding season.
explanation: The thresher shark uses its very long tail to slap and stun small fish, making them easier to catch.

q: A blue star and a red star are both shining in the sky. Which one will run out of fuel first, and why?
options: The blue star, because it uses up its fuel very quickly due to its high temperature.
The red star, because it is older and has already used most of its fuel.
The blue star, because its color means it is actually cooler and less stable.
They run out of fuel at the same rate because all stars have similar amounts of fuel.
explanation: A hot blue star burns its fuel very quickly and has a much shorter life than a cool red star that burns slowly.

q: What is special about the Mariana Trench?
options: It is the deepest place on Earth, reaching about 11,000 meters at the Challenger Deep.
It is the longest underwater mountain range in the Pacific Ocean.
It is a warm shallow trench where most of the world's coral reefs are found.
It is the widest ocean trench and stretches across three different oceans.
explanation: The Mariana Trench is the deepest place on Earth, about 11,000 meters down at a spot called the Challenger Deep.

q: Why is it better to breathe through your nose than through your mouth?
options: The nose filters, warms, and moistens air, while the mouth does not do this as well.
The nose lets in more air per breath so the lungs get more oxygen each time.
The mouth gets tired quickly from breathing, while the nose can breathe all day.
The nose blocks germs completely, while the mouth allows a small number through.
explanation: The nose filters, warms, and moistens air much better than the mouth, so breathing through the mouth all the time can dry your throat and let in more germs.

q: On a bicycle, a large front sprocket drives a smaller rear sprocket through a chain. What is the result?
options: The wheel's speed is multiplied, so the bike goes faster than the pedaling rate.
The rear wheel gets more force so the bike can climb steep hills more easily.
The pedals become harder to push because the gear ratio reduces mechanical advantage.
Both sprockets spin at the same speed because they are connected by the same chain.
explanation: The large front sprocket driving a smaller rear sprocket through the chain multiplies the wheel's speed.

q: Why is it important for a pregnant mother to know her Rh blood type?
options: Because her Rh type can affect the health of her baby.
Because Rh type changes during pregnancy and must be monitored weekly.
Because Rh-positive mothers cannot receive blood transfusions while pregnant.
Because only Rh-negative mothers are allowed to donate blood during pregnancy.
explanation: Knowing the Rh type of a pregnant mother is important because it can affect her baby.

q: Which of the following is an effective way to save electricity at home in the Philippines?
options: Turning off lights not in use and unplugging chargers when full.
Leaving the air conditioner on all day so it does not have to restart frequently.
Using a fan instead of the aircon only when the temperature goes above 35°C.
Keeping all appliances plugged in so they are always ready to use instantly.
explanation: In the Philippines, turning off lights not in use, unplugging full chargers, and setting the aircon to 25°C or higher are effective ways to reduce the electricity bill.

q: In what kind of climate do rubber trees grow best?
options: Hot and rainy tropical climate, like parts of the Philippines.
Cold and dry highland climate found in mountain regions.
Mild and seasonal climate with cold winters and warm summers.
Desert climate with very little rain but lots of direct sunlight.
explanation: Rubber trees grow best in the hot, rainy climate of the tropics, like parts of the Philippines.

q: Mayon Volcano is famous for what feature?
options: Its nearly perfect cone shape.
Its location in the middle of a large lake.
Its twin peaks visible from Manila.
Its bright blue crater lake at the top.
explanation: Mayon Volcano in Albay is famous for its nearly perfect cone shape.

q: How can sea turtles sleep underwater for hours without coming up for air?
options: Their metabolism slows down while resting, so they need much less oxygen.
They absorb oxygen directly from the water through their skin while asleep.
They hold one large breath before sleeping and slowly release it underwater.
They have a special chamber inside their shell that stores extra air for breathing.
explanation: Sea turtles' metabolism slows significantly while resting, allowing them to stay asleep underwater for hours without needing to surface.

q: How does tuberculosis (TB) usually spread from one person to another?
options: Through close, repeated contact with an infected person over time.
By briefly passing near someone who has TB in a public place.
By touching objects that a TB patient has touched, like a doorknob.
By drinking water from the same source as someone who has TB.
explanation: TB usually needs close, repeated contact with a sick person to spread — a brief passing encounter is not enough.

q: Why do elements in the same family (column) of the periodic table behave in similar ways?
options: They all have the same number of valence electrons, which controls how they react.
They were all discovered in the same country and were made from similar minerals.
They all have the same atomic mass, so they react with the same amount of energy.
They are all gases at room temperature, giving them the same chemical properties.
explanation: Elements in a family behave alike because they share the same number of valence electrons, which lets scientists predict how they will react.

q: When you watch a water wave move across the ocean surface, does the water itself travel forward with the wave?
options: No — the water particles move in small circles but stay roughly in place as the wave energy moves forward.
Yes — the water moves forward in the same direction as the wave at the same speed.
Yes — the top layer of water moves forward while the deeper water stays still.
No — the water actually moves backward as the wave moves forward, like a conveyor belt.
explanation: Water surface waves are gravity waves — water particles move in small circles as wave energy travels horizontally, but the water itself does not travel forward.

q: Why is ipil-ipil considered a good fuel source that is not easily used up?
options: Because it grows back from a cut stump, making it a renewable resource.
Because it burns longer than coal and produces more heat per kilogram.
Because it does not produce any smoke when burned, keeping the air clean.
Because it can be grown indoors and does not need sunlight to survive.
explanation: Ipil-ipil is a good fuel because it grows back from a cut stump, making it a renewable resource that is not easily used up.

q: On what date does the Philippines celebrate its Independence Day each year?
options: June 12
July 4
August 19
September 24
explanation: Philippine Independence Day is celebrated every June 12, marking the declaration of independence on June 12, 1898.

q: For work on which fruit was Ramon Barba named a National Scientist of the Philippines in 2014?
options: Mangoes
Bananas
Pineapples
Coconuts
explanation: Ramon Barba was named a National Scientist of the Philippines in 2014 for his important work on mangoes.

q: What opportunity does the internet provide for Filipinos?
options: Access to education and work opportunities online.
Free unlimited calls to any country in the world.
A way to send physical packages faster across islands.
Automatic translation of all content into Tagalog.
explanation: The internet provides Filipinos with opportunities for education and work, and the Philippines is one of the world's top countries in social media use.

q: The climbing perch is a fish with a surprising weakness. What is it?
options: It can actually drown if it cannot reach the surface to breathe air.
It cannot survive in saltwater even for a short time.
It will die if it stays out of water for more than ten minutes.
It loses its ability to see underwater if kept in the dark for too long.
explanation: The climbing perch depends so much on breathing air that it must surface from time to time — it can actually drown if kept underwater and unable to reach the surface.

q: Why does the narra tree help the soil where it grows?
options: It belongs to the legume family and enriches the soil with nitrogen.
Its deep roots break up rocks, releasing minerals that plants need.
Its large leaves block sunlight, keeping the soil cool and moist.
It produces a sap that kills harmful fungi and bacteria in the ground.
explanation: The narra belongs to the legume family and helps enrich the soil with nitrogen, benefiting other plants growing nearby.

q: What happens to a spring if you stretch it beyond its elastic limit?
options: It stays permanently deformed and does not return to its original shape.
It snaps back faster than normal and may bounce dangerously.
It returns to its original length but takes longer than usual.
It becomes stronger and harder to stretch the next time you pull it.
explanation: If a spring is overstretched past its elastic limit, it stays permanently deformed — it can no longer return to its original length.

q: What gas do plants release when they use sunlight to make their own food?
options: Oxygen
Carbon dioxide
Nitrogen
Water vapor
explanation: Plants release oxygen as a result of making food from sunlight through the process of photosynthesis.

q: What element is graphite made of, and where do we commonly find it?
options: Pure carbon — it is the 'lead' inside a pencil.
Pure silicon — it is used in the tips of mechanical pencils.
A mixture of carbon and lead — which is why pencils are called 'lead pencils'.
Pure iron — it leaves marks on paper because iron is dark gray.
explanation: Graphite is made of pure carbon and is the material used as the 'lead' inside a pencil.

q: Which of the following best describes sineguelas (Spanish plum)?
options: A small egg-shaped, sweet-sour summer fruit with one large seed inside.
A large round fruit with many tiny seeds and a thick green skin.
A long, yellow summer fruit with no seeds and a strong sweet smell.
A small red berry that grows in clusters and has no pit or seed inside.
explanation: Sineguelas is a small egg-shaped, sweet-sour summer fruit with a single large seed inside.

q: Compared to adults, how quickly do children's broken bones usually heal?
options: Children's bones heal faster than adults' bones.
Children's bones heal at about the same speed as adults' bones.
Children's bones heal more slowly because they are still growing.
Children's bones take twice as long to heal because they are softer.
explanation: Children's bones usually heal faster than adults' bones.

q: How does the bee-eater manage to catch flying insects?
options: It has sharp eyesight that lets it spot a flying insect from far away.
It uses its keen sense of smell to follow the scent trail insects leave in the air.
It listens for the buzz of an insect's wings and flies toward the sound.
It waits motionless on a branch and only lunges when an insect lands nearby.
explanation: The bee-eater has sharp eyesight, so it can spot a flying insect from far away and catch it in flight.

q: How did Charles Lyell show that the Earth is extremely old?
options: By studying rock layers and fossils, which showed the Earth took an incredibly long time to form.
By measuring the temperature at the Earth's core and calculating how long it took to cool.
By observing that the continents are still moving apart at a rate of a few centimeters per year.
By counting annual growth rings in ancient trees and calculating backwards thousands of years.
explanation: Charles Lyell showed from rock layers and fossils that the Earth is in fact extremely ancient, overturning the earlier belief that it was only a few thousand years old.

q: What is a watershed?
options: The whole area of land where all rainwater drains into the same river, lake, or sea.
A special reservoir built by people to collect rainwater for drinking.
The highest point in a mountain range where rain clouds form most often.
An underground layer of rock that stores rainwater like a natural sponge.
explanation: A watershed is the whole area of land where all the rainwater drains down into the same river, lake, or sea.

q: What happened to the fish population at Apo Island in Negros Oriental after the locals created a fish sanctuary?
options: The fish came back in large numbers, and now tourists visit to snorkel and see fish and sea turtles.
The fish population stayed the same because fish move too quickly to be protected by a sanctuary.
The fish population continued to decline because pollution from nearby towns increased.
The sanctuary helped only sea turtles, not fish, because fish kept swimming out of the protected area.
explanation: After the Apo Island community made a fish sanctuary, the fish came back in numbers, and tourists now visit to snorkel and see the fish and sea turtles.

q: A stalactite in a cave looks like an icicle on a roof. What is the key difference between them?
options: A stalactite is solid rock that took thousands of years to grow, while an icicle is frozen water that forms in hours and melts quickly.
A stalactite is made of ice while an icicle is made of minerals dripping from the cave ceiling.
A stalactite grows upward from the cave floor while an icicle always hangs downward.
A stalactite forms only in volcanic caves while icicles form only in polar regions near ice sheets.
explanation: Unlike an icicle — frozen water that forms in hours and melts quickly — a stalactite is real rock that took thousands of years to grow.

q: Even though sloths are sometimes called 'bears' in English, what animal are they actually most closely related to?
options: The anteater, which eats ants.
The bear, which also climbs trees.
The monkey, which also hangs in trees.
The koala, which also moves very slowly.
explanation: Despite their nickname, sloths are not related to bears or monkeys — they are closer relatives of the anteater, even though the two animals look very different.

q: How does fire spread from one object to another?
options: It heats up nearby fuel until that fuel also catches fire.
It releases a chemical that floats through the air and ignites objects nearby.
It needs oxygen to jump from one object to the next, like a bridge.
It grows a thin invisible layer across surfaces that suddenly burst into flame.
explanation: Fire spreads because it heats up nearby fuel until that fuel also catches fire.

q: Why does a banca (wooden boat) keep gliding forward even after you stop paddling?
options: Because of its momentum, which keeps it moving until water drag slows it down.
Because the current always pushes the boat forward when it is not being steered.
Because the paddle leaves a trail of water that pushes the boat from behind.
Because the boat's smooth wooden hull has no friction with the water underneath.
explanation: After paddling stops, the banca keeps gliding because of its momentum — it slows down gradually as water drags against the hull.

q: How do most adult sponges spend their lives?
options: Attached to rocks or the seafloor, without moving around.
Swimming slowly near the surface searching for food particles.
Burrowing into sandy seafloors and moving short distances each day.
Floating freely in open water, carried around by ocean currents.
explanation: Most adult sponges stay attached to rocks or the sea floor and do not move around.

q: The Big Dipper is a famous star pattern in the night sky. Which constellation does it belong to?
options: Ursa Major (the Great Bear)
Orion (the Hunter)
Cassiopeia (the Queen)
Leo (the Lion)
explanation: The Big Dipper is part of the constellation Ursa Major, also known as the Great Bear.

q: How long does it take for Uranus to complete one trip around the Sun?
options: About 84 Earth years
About 29 Earth years
About 165 Earth years
About 12 Earth years
explanation: One year on Uranus lasts about 84 Earth years because it is very far from the Sun.

q: What does nitinol, a shape memory alloy, do when it is heated?
options: It returns to its original shape that it had before being bent or deformed.
It becomes liquid because its melting point is lower than most metals.
It becomes permanently harder and cannot be bent into a new shape again.
It expands uniformly in all directions, becoming slightly larger than before.
explanation: Nitinol is a shape memory alloy that returns to its original shape when heated — this property makes it useful in medical stents and dental braces wire.

q: Which of the following correctly describes what can happen to an object's speed?
options: An object's speed can change — it can speed up or slow down.
An object's speed can only slow down over time, never speed up on its own.
Once an object is moving, its speed stays exactly the same unless it hits something.
An object can only change speed if it is pushed from behind, not from the front.
explanation: An object's speed can change — it can speed up or slow down depending on the forces acting on it.

q: What can you do with a jackfruit seed to grow a new tree?
options: Plant it in the soil and it will grow into a new jackfruit tree.
Dry it in the sun for a week before planting so it does not rot.
Soak it in water for a month to remove the hard outer coating first.
Grind it into powder and mix it with fertilizer before planting.
explanation: A jackfruit seed can simply be planted in the soil to grow into a new jackfruit tree.

q: What is a rooster, and what is one feature that makes it easy to recognize?
options: A male chicken with a bright red comb that crows loudly at dawn.
A female chicken with colorful tail feathers that lays eggs every day.
A large male bird with a long blue neck used for racing in festivals.
A young chick with a red beak that signals it is ready to become an adult.
explanation: A rooster is a male chicken with a bright red comb, known for its loud crowing at dawn.

q: Octopuses have been seen carrying halved coconut shells with them. Why does this make octopuses unusual?
options: It shows they use tools — they carry the shells to use as portable shelters, which few non-human animals do.
It shows they eat coconuts, which scientists thought was impossible for a sea creature.
It shows they can survive on land, since coconuts only grow above the water line.
It shows they communicate with each other by exchanging objects found on the seafloor.
explanation: Scientists observed octopuses carrying halved coconut shells to use as portable shelters, making them one of the few non-human animals that demonstrate genuine tool use.

q: Why do you sometimes feel a small shock when you touch a metal doorknob after walking on carpet?
options: Charge builds up on your body from the carpet, then jumps into the metal when you touch it.
The doorknob stores electricity from the building's wiring and releases it when touched.
Your body conducts electricity from the floor, and metal doorknobs attract that electricity.
Dry air removes electrons from the metal doorknob, causing it to shock the next person who touches it.
explanation: Walking on carpet builds up charge on your body, and when you touch the metal doorknob, the charge jumps into the metal — causing a tiny shock called static electricity.

q: Why does food spoil and go moldy faster during the rainy season in the Philippines?
options: Because fungi digest food faster in warm, wet conditions — exactly what the rainy season provides.
Because rain carries mold spores from outside directly into homes and onto food surfaces.
Because the cold rainy air slows down the food's natural defenses against bacteria and fungi.
Because people eat less during the rainy season, leaving food sitting out longer than usual.
explanation: Fungi digest food faster when surroundings are warm and wet — during the Philippine rainy season, the moist weather provides perfect conditions for mold to grow quickly.

q: How does a reef shark find fish or other food in the water from far away?
options: It has a very strong sense of smell that can detect tiny amounts of blood or food in the water.
It uses its large eyes to see prey moving from hundreds of meters away.
It produces sound waves that bounce off nearby fish, like a living sonar system.
It follows the trails of bubbles that fish leave behind as they swim through the water.
explanation: A reef shark has a very strong sense of smell that lets it detect a tiny bit of blood or food in the water from far away, helping it find fish.

q: What happens to the dead skin cells on the outer surface of your skin every day?
options: They quietly flake off and are replaced by new cells underneath
They dissolve in sweat and wash away in the shower
They harden and turn into a protective shell over time
They are reabsorbed into the body to make new blood cells
explanation: The outer surface of skin is made of dead cells that flake off every day, while new cells form underneath to replace them.

q: Which part of Super Typhoon Yolanda struck Tacloban directly in 2013, bringing the strongest winds and a deadly storm surge?
options: The eyewall
The outer rainbands
The spiral arms
The eye
explanation: The eyewall of Super Typhoon Yolanda struck Tacloban directly in 2013, bringing the most destructive winds and storm surge.

q: What can happen to a child who has a long-lasting worm infection?
options: Their growth and learning may slow down
They develop stronger immunity against all diseases
They become more energetic as the body fights the infection
Their appetite increases and they grow faster than normal
explanation: Long-lasting worm infection can slow down a child's growth and learning.

q: Why does the handle of a metal spoon left in hot soup become warm?
options: Heat travels through the spoon as neighboring particles touch and collide
Hot steam rises up the spoon and heats the handle from above
The spoon absorbs heat radiation that jumps through the air
Water molecules inside the metal carry heat from one end to the other
explanation: In conduction, heat is transferred as neighboring particles touch and collide, which is why the spoon handle becomes warm.

q: Why are sea turtles (pawikan) considered endangered?
options: Their nesting beaches are being destroyed and they get caught in nets or eat plastic
They are hunted only for their meat by professional fishermen
Rising ocean temperatures make their eggs hatch too quickly
They cannot find enough jellyfish to eat in Philippine waters
explanation: Pawikan are endangered because their nesting beaches are being destroyed and they get caught in nets or accidentally eat plastic.

q: How does groundwater move underground?
options: Very slowly, seeping through tiny spaces in rock and sand
Quickly through underground rivers that flow like streams
In large bursts whenever it rains heavily on the surface
Instantly when gravity pulls it straight down through solid rock
explanation: Groundwater moves very slowly as it seeps through the tiny spaces in rock and sand.

q: How are a pangolin's scales arranged on its body?
options: They overlap like the tiles on a roof, forming a strong shield
They lie flat and smooth like fish scales in a single layer
They stand upright like spines so they point outward
They are scattered randomly across the skin for flexibility
explanation: A pangolin's scales overlap like roof tiles, making a strong protective shield.

q: A banana ripens from green and firm to yellow and soft. What type of change is this?
options: A chemical change that cannot be undone back to unripe
A physical change because only the color and texture shift
A reversible change that could be reversed by cooling the banana
A mixture change because the banana mixes with air as it ripens
explanation: The ripening of a banana is a chemical change that cannot be reversed back to its unripe state.

q: What does a virus do before it enters a cell?
options: It first attaches to the surface of the cell, fitting like a key into a lock
It immediately breaks through the cell wall using sharp proteins
It waits outside the cell until the cell divides and opens up
It releases chemicals that dissolve the cell membrane completely
explanation: A virus first attaches to the cell surface like a key fitting into a lock before it can enter.

q: Who is called the 'Father of Railways' and built the famous steam locomotive called the Rocket?
options: George Stephenson
James Watt
Richard Trevithick
Isambard Kingdom Brunel
explanation: George Stephenson is called the 'Father of Railways'; his steam locomotive the Rocket won a famous race in 1829.

q: What two raw materials are burned in a very hot kiln to make cement?
options: Limestone and clay
Sand and gravel
Salt and sulfur
Iron ore and coal
explanation: Cement is made by burning limestone and clay in a kiln reaching about 1,400 degrees Celsius until they form clinker.

q: Which type of plastic is used for clear water bottles and soda containers, and has recycling code 1?
options: PET (polyethylene terephthalate)
PVC (polyvinyl chloride)
HDPE (high-density polyethylene)
Polystyrene
explanation: PET plastic is used for clear water bottles and soft-drink containers and carries recycling code 1.

q: What do adult lacewing insects eat?
options: Nectar and pollen from flowers
Aphids and other small insects
Blood from mammals and birds
Rotting leaves and dead wood
explanation: Adult lacewings feed on nectar and pollen from flowers, unlike their larvae which eat pest insects.

q: What blood pressure reading is considered normal for most adults?
options: 120/80 mmHg
80/120 mmHg
160/90 mmHg
100/60 mmHg
explanation: A blood pressure reading around 120/80 mmHg is considered normal for most adults.

q: How does sweating help cool down your body?
options: When sweat evaporates from your skin, it takes heat away from the body
Sweat is cold water that lowers your skin temperature directly
Sweat blocks pores to prevent more heat from building up inside
The salt in sweat reacts with air to create a cooling chemical reaction
explanation: When sweat evaporates from the skin, it carries heat away from the body, cooling us down.

q: How many laws of planetary motion did Johannes Kepler develop?
options: Three
Two
Four
Five
explanation: Kepler developed three laws of planetary motion that describe how planets orbit the Sun.

q: How do aquatic snails help keep ponds and fish tanks clean?
options: They graze on algae growth using their radula
They filter tiny particles from water through their gills
They eat dead fish and decaying plant material
They release chemicals that stop algae from growing
explanation: Aquatic snails eat algae using their radula, helping to keep water in ponds, rivers, and fish tanks clean.

q: What happens to iodine crystals when they are gently heated?
options: They turn directly into a purple gas without becoming a liquid first
They melt into a brown liquid before slowly turning into gas
They change color from dark to white before dissolving in air
They break apart into smaller crystals that float away as dust
explanation: Iodine undergoes sublimation when heated — it turns directly from a dark solid into a purple gas, skipping the liquid stage.

q: Which of the following is a common cause of stress for children?
options: Upcoming tests and problems with friends or classmates
Eating too much food at lunch and feeling sleepy
Getting a new pet that needs to be trained
Growing taller faster than other kids in class
explanation: Common causes of stress for kids include tests, problems with friends or classmates, and conflicts at home.

q: Why does a carabao have thick skin?
options: To protect it from insect bites, scratches, and the heat of the sun
To help it float easily when it swims across rivers and rice fields
To store water inside so it can go a long time without drinking
To make it heavier so it can pull farm equipment more powerfully
explanation: A carabao's thick skin protects it from insect bites, scratches, and the heat of the sun.

q: When can fog appear over a river or lake?
options: When the air above the water is cooler than the warm water below
When strong winds blow tiny water droplets up from the surface
When fish breathe out carbon dioxide that mixes with dust in the air
When the lake water freezes at the surface on very cold nights
explanation: Fog can form over a warm river or lake when the cooler air above causes water vapor to condense into tiny droplets.

q: At what temperature does tin melt?
options: 232 degrees Celsius
1,538 degrees Celsius
660 degrees Celsius
1,085 degrees Celsius
explanation: Tin melts at a relatively low temperature of 232 degrees Celsius.

q: What temperature do bees try to keep inside their hive for brood development?
options: About 35 degrees Celsius
About 20 degrees Celsius
About 50 degrees Celsius
About 10 degrees Celsius
explanation: Bees maintain hive temperature at about 35 degrees Celsius by fanning their wings to cool the hive or clustering together to warm it.

q: In the rock cycle, what can igneous rock eventually become?
options: It can weather into sediment that forms sedimentary rock, or melt and form new igneous rock
It can only stay as igneous rock forever since it starts from lava
It can only turn into metamorphic rock by gaining more minerals over time
It can only dissolve in water to form limestone at the ocean floor
explanation: In the rock cycle, igneous rock can weather to form sedimentary rock, be heated and pressured to form metamorphic rock, or melt again into magma — any type of rock can become any other type.

q: Why does a large colorful tail on a bird signal that the bird is healthy and strong?
options: It is heavy and easy for predators to spot, so only a truly fit bird can survive with it
It provides extra warmth during cold seasons, proving the bird has enough energy
It helps the bird fly faster by acting like a rudder that steers through the air
It scares away predators with its bright patterns, showing bravery
explanation: A big colorful tail is heavy and makes the bird more visible to predators, so carrying it proves the bird is strong and healthy.

q: Why is a strong electric shock dangerous to the human body?
options: Because the human body conducts electricity, allowing current to flow through it
Because electricity bursts into flames when it touches warm skin
Because electric charges get trapped inside cells and cannot escape
Because electricity turns into heat only inside the body but not outside it
explanation: The human body conducts electricity, which is why a strong electric shock is dangerous and can be deadly.

q: Which three types of food nutrients can the enzymes made by the pancreas digest?
options: Carbohydrates, proteins, and fats
Vitamins, minerals, and water
Fiber, sugar, and salt
Proteins, vitamins, and starch only
explanation: The pancreas makes enzymes that digest carbohydrates, proteins, and fats all together.

q: What do a leech's tiny eyes near its head allow it to detect?
options: Light and movement, though it cannot see clear pictures
Colors and shapes of objects up to one meter away
The temperature of warm-blooded animals nearby
The chemical smell of blood in the water
explanation: A leech has several tiny eyes near its head that sense light and movement, but cannot form clear images.

q: Which two structures do plant cells have that animal cells do not?
options: A stiff cell wall and chloroplasts
A nucleus and a cell membrane
Mitochondria and a cell membrane
Vacuoles and ribosomes
explanation: Plant cells have a stiff cell wall and chloroplasts, which they use to make food from light — structures not found in animal cells.

q: If you use red cabbage juice as a pH indicator, what color does kalamansi juice (an acid) turn it?
options: Red
Green
Yellow
Blue
explanation: Kalamansi juice is acidic and turns red cabbage juice indicator red; basic substances like soapy water turn it green.

q: Why is it comfortable to rest under a mango tree on a hot day?
options: Because the mango tree is large and tall, giving a shady place to rest
Because mango trees release a cool mist from their leaves in the heat
Because the sweet smell of mango fruit makes people feel relaxed
Because mango tree roots spread out and create a cooler ground temperature
explanation: The mango tree is large and tall, so it provides a shady place to rest in the heat of the sun.

q: Why does sweating help your body cool down on a hot day?
options: Water needs a large amount of heat to evaporate, so sweat carries heat away from your skin as it turns to vapor
Water is naturally cold when it comes out of sweat glands, lowering your skin temperature directly
Sweat blocks your pores to prevent more heat from getting inside the body
The salt in sweat reacts with air to produce a cooling chemical effect on the skin
explanation: Water needs a huge amount of heat to turn into vapor, so when sweat evaporates from your skin it carries heat away and cools you.

q: Cogon and talahib are both grasses. How are they different?
options: Talahib is much taller and bigger than the low-growing cogon
Cogon is always found near rivers while talahib grows on dry hilltops
Talahib grows underground while cogon grows above the soil surface
Cogon produces seeds while talahib only spreads by underground roots
explanation: Although both are grasses, talahib is much taller and bigger than the low-growing cogon.

q: Why can you see a blend of orange, pink, and violet colors at twilight?
options: Different amounts of light scatter in different parts of the sky
The sun's surface changes color as it cools down at sunset
Clouds act like prisms and split white light into separate colors
The reflection of the ocean creates colored patterns in the sky
explanation: At twilight, different amounts of light scatter in different parts of the sky, creating a blend of orange, pink, and violet.

q: What is the largest lake in the Philippines?
options: Laguna de Bay
Lake Lanao
Taal Lake
Lake Sebu
explanation: Laguna de Bay, located near Metro Manila, is the largest lake in the Philippines.

q: Why are measurement units like the volt, watt, and newton named the way they are?
options: They are named after scientists to honor their discoveries
They are abbreviations of the Latin words for the quantities they measure
They were chosen randomly by an international committee of engineers
They come from the names of the machines that first measured those quantities
explanation: Units such as the volt, ampere, watt, and newton are named after scientists to honor their discoveries.

q: What drives the movement of Earth's tectonic plates?
options: Convection currents in the mantle caused by heat from deep inside the Earth
The gravitational pull of the Moon tugging on the ocean floor
Magnetic forces from the iron core that push the plates outward
The weight of mountains pressing down and pushing other plates sideways
explanation: Heat from deep inside Earth causes convection currents in the mantle — hot rock rises, cools, and sinks — and this slow circulation helps push the tectonic plates.

q: In which layer of the atmosphere do most meteors burn up before reaching the ground?
options: The mesosphere
The stratosphere
The thermosphere
The troposphere
explanation: Most meteors burn up in the mesosphere, which is why we see them as shooting stars.

q: What is the shape of the spine's natural curves, and what do they help you do?
options: S-shaped curves that help you balance, support body weight, and protect the spinal cord
C-shaped curves that keep the body stiff so you can stand perfectly straight
Straight with no curves, so all weight is distributed evenly along each vertebra
Z-shaped curves that allow the torso to twist easily in all directions
explanation: The spine has natural S-shaped curves that help us balance, support body weight, and protect the spinal cord inside.

q: What are the three main parts of a fleshy forest fruit?
options: The skin, the soft flesh, and the seed inside
The roots, the stem, and the leaves
The petal, the stamen, and the pollen
The bark, the sap, and the flower
explanation: A fleshy forest fruit has three main parts: the skin, the soft flesh that animals eat, and the seed inside that becomes a new plant.

q: Which Philippine volcano's powerful 1991 eruption shows that the Philippines sits on the Ring of Fire?
options: Mount Pinatubo
Mayon Volcano
Taal Volcano
Mount Apo
explanation: The 1991 eruption of Mount Pinatubo, which had been quiet for a long time before suddenly erupting very powerfully, shows how active the Ring of Fire is in the Philippines.

q: What mineral makes both eggshells and human bones hard and strong?
options: Calcium
Iron
Phosphorus
Magnesium
explanation: Eggshells are made of calcium, and the same mineral that makes an eggshell hard is the one that makes your bones strong.

q: How does washing hands regularly with soap help reduce antibiotic use?
options: It prevents infections from spreading, so we need antibiotics less often
It kills antibiotic-resistant bacteria before they can enter the body
It strengthens the immune system so antibiotics work more effectively
It removes viruses that cause bacterial infections to spread faster
explanation: Washing hands often with soap prevents infections, which lowers how often we need antibiotics.

q: How does a jellyfish protect itself and catch food?
options: It has thousands of tiny stinging cells on its tentacles that fire venom when touched
It squirts a cloud of dark ink to confuse and blind its attackers
It uses suckers on its tentacles to grip and squeeze its prey
It produces an electric shock through special organs in its bell
explanation: A jellyfish has thousands of tiny stinging cells on its tentacles that fire out venom when something touches them.

q: Which animals are examples of species found only in the Philippines?
options: The Philippine eagle and the tarsier
The komodo dragon and the proboscis monkey
The king cobra and the giant panda
The saltwater crocodile and the Javan rhinoceros
explanation: The Philippines has hundreds of endemic species found nowhere else, including the Philippine eagle and the tarsier.

q: Why are layers of sedimentary rock compared to a record of Earth's history?
options: Each layer may contain the remains of organisms that lived at that time, showing what life was like then
Each layer is a different color that scientists can use to measure how far the Earth has moved
Each layer traps air bubbles that tell scientists what the ancient atmosphere was made of
Each layer forms at an exact rate of one millimeter per year, acting like a clock
explanation: The thousands of layers of sedimentary rock act like a record of Earth's long history because each layer may contain the remains of organisms from that time.

q: Why is a medical leech used only once and never on a second patient?
options: So it cannot spread illness from one patient to another
Because it dies immediately after feeding on human blood
Because it loses its special saliva chemicals after the first use
Because doctors are required by law to use new tools for each surgery
explanation: Each medical leech is used only once on one patient and never reused so it cannot spread illness.

q: Compared to the age of the solar system, how old are Saturn's rings believed to be?
options: Relatively young — possibly only 100 to 400 million years old
About the same age as the solar system at roughly 4.5 billion years old
Much older than the solar system, forming before the Sun itself ignited
Exactly one billion years old according to measurements by the Cassini spacecraft
explanation: Data from the Cassini spacecraft suggests Saturn's rings are relatively young — possibly only 100 to 400 million years old — and may have formed when a moon or comet was broken apart by Saturn's gravity.

q: What does a hermit crab do when it senses danger?
options: It pulls into its shell and blocks the opening with its big claw
It sprays a cloud of ink to blind the attacker and then swims away
It pinches the attacker with both claws before running sideways
It buries itself quickly under the sand until the danger passes
explanation: When in danger, a hermit crab pulls into its shell and blocks the opening with its big claw.

q: Where do fungal hyphae get longer as they grow?
options: Only at their tips
Along their entire length
Only at their base
From small side branches that appear anywhere
explanation: Hyphae grow by extending only at their tips, allowing the fungus to reach nutrients far away.

q: What can strong outbursts from the Sun disturb on Earth?
options: Electricity, GPS, and satellite signals
Ocean tides, rainfall, and wind direction
Soil temperature, plant growth, and rainfall
Mountain height, river flow, and air pressure
explanation: Strong solar outbursts disturb Earth's magnetic field and can affect electricity, GPS, and satellite signals.

q: What major crop disaster was caused by a water mold called Phytophthora?
options: The Great Irish Famine, which destroyed potato crops
The Great Bengal Famine, which destroyed rice crops
The Dust Bowl, which destroyed wheat crops
The Great Chinese Famine, which destroyed corn crops
explanation: Phytophthora is the water mold responsible for destroying potato crops and causing the Great Irish Famine.

q: What is the name for the pressure in the arteries created when the heart beats?
options: Blood pressure
Pulse rate
Oxygen level
Breathing pressure
explanation: Blood pressure is the pressure in the arteries as the heart pumps blood at high pressure around the body.

q: How do many tardigrades feed on moss or plants?
options: They poke a tiny needle-like part into plant cells and suck out the juice
They tear off plant material with small claws and swallow it whole
They absorb nutrients through their skin by pressing against leaves
They spray a liquid that dissolves the plant surface and then drink it
explanation: Many tardigrades have a tiny needle-like mouthpart that they poke into plant or moss cells to suck out the juice inside.

q: Why does a caterpillar eat so many leaves during its life cycle?
options: To store energy for the next stage of metamorphosis
To make silk for spinning its cocoon
To grow wings before becoming a butterfly
To feed younger caterpillars in the same colony
explanation: In complete metamorphosis, the caterpillar eats lots of leaves to store energy for the next stage.

q: Which statement about Mount Pulag is TRUE?
options: It is NOT an active volcano and is safe to climb
It is an active volcano that erupts every few years
It is a dormant volcano that could erupt again soon
It is a shield volcano with a very wide flat top
explanation: Mount Pulag is NOT an active erupting volcano — it is an old mountain that no longer spews lava, so it is safe to climb.

q: Which tick is one of the most common in the Philippines and is often found on dogs?
options: The brown dog tick
The black-legged tick
The lone star tick
The paralysis tick
explanation: The brown dog tick is one of the most common ticks in the Philippines and is often seen on dogs' skin.

q: Which set lists all four Galilean moons of Jupiter?
options: Io, Europa, Ganymede, and Callisto
Titan, Rhea, Dione, and Tethys
Phobos, Deimos, Charon, and Triton
Enceladus, Mimas, Oberon, and Miranda
explanation: The four Galilean moons are Io, Europa, Ganymede, and Callisto.

q: What features help a bee's stinger deliver venom?
options: Backward-pointing barbs and a venom sac connected to the stinger
Forward-pointing hooks and a venom gland inside the abdomen
A hollow tube that squirts venom like a syringe
A sharp double blade that tears skin and releases poison
explanation: A bee's stinger has small backward-pointing barbs along its edges and is connected to a venom sac that pumps venom in when the stinger pierces skin.

q: Which mineral is rated 1 on the Mohs hardness scale, making it the softest?
options: Talc
Quartz
Feldspar
Calcite
explanation: Talc is the mineral with Mohs hardness 1 — it is the softest mineral on the scale.

q: What is the name of the very strong poison found in a pufferfish?
options: Tetrodotoxin
Venom X
Saxitoxin
Ciguatoxin
explanation: The poison in a pufferfish is called tetrodotoxin, and it is very strong.

q: Why is it important to warm up and stretch before exercising?
options: To get your muscles ready and help prevent strains and injuries
To increase your heart rate as fast as possible at the start
To build muscle faster by using more energy from the beginning
To cool down your body temperature before it gets too hot
explanation: Warming up and stretching before exercise gets the muscles ready and helps prevent strains and injuries.

q: Which island in the Philippines is known for growing bananas and pineapples that are shipped to other places?
options: Mindanao
Luzon
Palawan
Cebu
explanation: Mindanao is known for growing fruits like bananas and pineapples that are shipped to other places.

q: How do fungi in the forest help create rich soil?
options: They rot fallen leaves and logs and turn them into soil
They absorb sunlight and release minerals directly into the ground
They break rocks into small pieces using their roots
They trap rainwater under dead wood and release it slowly
explanation: In the forest, fungi rot fallen leaves and logs to turn them into rich soil.

q: Why are children more at risk from red tide toxin than adults?
options: A child's smaller body means even a small amount of toxin has a bigger effect
Children eat more seafood than adults on average
Children's immune systems react more slowly to toxins
Children are more likely to eat uncooked shellfish
explanation: Because a child's body is smaller, even a small amount of red tide toxin has a bigger effect on them.

q: What is it called when tiny scent particles spread on their own and mix into the air across a room?
options: Diffusion
Evaporation
Condensation
Sublimation
explanation: The spreading of tiny scent particles through the air on their own is called diffusion.

q: What does the word 'plankton' mean in Greek?
options: Wanderer or drifter
Tiny creature
Water dweller
Light seeker
explanation: The word plankton comes from Greek meaning wanderer or drifter, because plankton cannot swim against the current.

q: Who became President of the Philippines after President Quezon died in 1944?
options: Sergio Osmeña
Manuel Roxas
Elpidio Quirino
Ramon Magsaysay
explanation: Sergio Osmeña became President after Quezon died in 1944 and was the fourth President of the Philippines.

q: Why is it easier to float in the sea than in a freshwater pool?
options: Salt water is denser than fresh water, so it pushes your body up more
Salt water is warmer, which makes your muscles more relaxed
The waves in the sea help push your body to the surface
Sea water contains more oxygen that helps the body stay buoyant
explanation: It is easier to float in salty seawater because salt water is denser than fresh water.

q: What happens to ocean surface temperatures in the central and eastern Pacific during La Nina?
options: They become cooler as stronger westward winds push warm water away
They become warmer because weaker winds trap heat near the surface
They stay the same because La Nina only affects rainfall, not temperature
They rise sharply because the sun shines longer over that region
explanation: During La Nina, stronger westward winds push warm water away, making the ocean surface in the central and eastern Pacific cooler.

q: What natural warning sign after an earthquake should tell people to run to high ground immediately?
options: The sea water suddenly pulls back and exposes the sea bottom
The sky turns an unusual orange or red color
Strong winds begin blowing toward the shore
The ground shakes a second time after the first quake
explanation: If the sea water suddenly pulls back and exposes the sea bottom after an earthquake, a tsunami may be coming and people should run to high ground at once.

q: In science, how much work is done on a box when you carry it across a flat floor at the same height?
options: Zero work, because the upward force is perpendicular to the horizontal motion
A lot of work, because you are using energy to hold the box up
Some work, because your muscles are working hard to carry the weight
Work equal to the weight of the box times the distance walked
explanation: Carrying a box horizontally at constant height does zero scientific work on the box because the upward support force is perpendicular to the horizontal motion.

q: What happens when electrical charge in clouds builds up strong enough?
options: Electricity jumps as lightning from cloud to cloud or down to the ground
The cloud releases the charge as a steady glow called aurora
The water droplets in the cloud vibrate and produce thunder only
The charge quietly flows through the air as invisible static electricity
explanation: When the charge gets strong enough, electricity jumps as lightning from cloud to cloud or from cloud down to the ground.

q: How does the size of Ganymede, Jupiter's moon, compare to the planet Mercury?
options: Ganymede is bigger than Mercury
Ganymede is roughly the same size as Mercury
Ganymede is slightly smaller than Mercury
Ganymede is about half the size of Mercury
explanation: Ganymede is even bigger than the planet Mercury, making it the largest moon in the solar system.

q: Which flower colors are bees most attracted to because those colors are easy for them to see?
options: Yellow and blue
Red and orange
White and pink
Purple and green
explanation: Bees are often drawn to yellow and blue flowers because those are colors they can see easily.

q: By 1983, which country was the world's second-largest geothermal energy producer?
options: The Philippines
Japan
Indonesia
New Zealand
explanation: By 1983, the Philippines had become the world's second-largest geothermal energy producer, behind the United States.

q: What makes organic farming different from conventional farming?
options: It uses natural fertilizers instead of chemicals that could harm health and the environment
It only grows plants indoors using artificial lighting to save water
It relies on machines to replace all manual labor on the farm
It uses stronger chemical pesticides that break down faster in soil
explanation: Organic farming uses natural fertilizers and methods to grow crops without chemicals that could harm health and the environment.

q: Why can humans produce a fever when sick?
options: Because humans are warm-blooded and can raise their own body temperature
Because viruses release heat inside the body as they multiply
Because the liver stores extra heat that it releases when needed
Because muscles shiver constantly and that friction creates extra heat
explanation: Humans are warm-blooded animals, so the body can raise its own temperature to produce a fever.

q: In a cold-can experiment, what causes the white frost that appears on the outside of a can filled with ice and salt?
options: Water vapor in the air turns directly into frost when it touches the very cold surface
Water seeps through tiny holes in the metal and freezes on the outside
Melting ice inside the can pushes water out through the metal
Salt crystals from inside the can stick to the outer surface of the metal
explanation: The outside of the can gets very cold, so water vapor in the air turns into a thin white frost on its surface — the same thing that happens on grass on a cold night.

q: What causes a metamorphic rock to form?
options: Intense heat and pressure deep underground change an existing rock
Layers of tiny rock pieces pile up and squeeze together over time
Melted rock cools down and hardens at or below the surface
Volcanic ash settles and cements together after an eruption
explanation: Metamorphic rock forms when an existing rock is changed by intense heat and pressure deep underground.

q: When an egg and sperm unite, how many of each chromosome does the new cell end up with?
options: Two of each — one from the mother and one from the father
One of each, taken randomly from either parent
Four of each, to give the baby extra genetic information
Three of each, with two from the mother and one from the father
explanation: When egg and sperm unite, the new cell ends up with two of each chromosome — one inherited from the mother and one from the father.

q: Despite being called the Ring of Fire, what shape does this zone of volcanoes and earthquakes actually form?
options: A horseshoe shape
A complete circle
A straight line along the equator
An oval around the Pacific Ocean floor
explanation: Despite its name, the Ring of Fire is shaped more like a horseshoe than a complete circle.

q: If all the ozone in Earth's ozone layer were gathered into one single layer, how thick would it be?
options: Thinner than two stacked coins
About as thick as a textbook
About one metre thick
About as thick as a window pane
explanation: Even though the ozone layer is important, if you gathered all the ozone into one layer it would be thinner than two stacked coins.

q: What is different about the colors in a double rainbow compared to the main rainbow?
options: The secondary rainbow is fainter and has its colors in reversed order
The secondary rainbow is brighter and has more colors than the main one
Both rainbows have exactly the same colors in the same order
The secondary rainbow only shows red and blue, not the full spectrum
explanation: A double rainbow forms when light reflects twice inside water droplets; the secondary rainbow is fainter and has reversed color order.

q: How does a tamaraw typically behave in the wild?
options: It roams its own area alone and tends to avoid other tamaraws
It lives in large herds and moves together to find food
It pairs up with a mate and stays in the same small spot all year
It migrates in groups to different islands during dry season
explanation: Each tamaraw has its own area that it roams and feeds in, and it tends to avoid running into other tamaraws.

q: What energy transformation happens when you turn the handle of a hand-crank generator?
options: Motion (mechanical energy) is changed into electricity
Heat energy is changed into light
Chemical energy stored in the handle is released as electricity
Sound energy from the turning is converted into electrical energy
explanation: When we turn the handle of a hand-crank generator, the motion is changed into electricity that can light a small bulb.

q: Which statement correctly describes a jackfruit tree?
options: It is tall and keeps thick green leaves all year round
It sheds all its leaves during the dry season to save water
It is a short bush that grows close to the ground
It only grows leaves when it is producing fruit
explanation: The jackfruit tree is tall and keeps thick green leaves all year round.

q: Which vitamin, found in carrots and squash, helps keep the eyes healthy?
options: Vitamin A
Vitamin C
Vitamin D
Vitamin B12
explanation: Foods rich in vitamin A, like carrots and squash, help keep the eyes healthy.

q: How does the nose detect smells from objects?
options: Tiny particles released by objects float in the air and are picked up by sensors in the nose
The eyes send signals to the nose about nearby objects so the nose can react
Smell sensors on the skin detect heat coming from objects and signal the nose
Nerves in the throat taste particles that drift into the mouth and signal the nose
explanation: Objects release very tiny particles that float in the air, and when we breathe in, these enter the nose and are picked up by smell sensors there.

q: How are some dogs able to help find missing people or hidden objects?
options: They use their sharp sense of smell to track scents
They use their excellent eyesight to spot things from far away
They use their sensitive hearing to detect very quiet sounds
They use vibrations felt through their paws to follow underground trails
explanation: Because of their sharp sense of smell, some dogs are used to find missing people or hidden objects.

q: What is a flower called when it has all four of its parts?
options: A complete flower
A perfect flower
A fertile flower
A full-bloom flower
explanation: A flower with all four parts is called a complete flower; one missing a part is called incomplete.

q: How does a strangler fig begin its growth on another tree?
options: It starts high on the host tree and sends roots down that slowly wrap around it
It sprouts from the ground and climbs upward by attaching sticky pads to the bark
It drops seeds onto the forest floor and then grows straight up to reach the host
It spreads underground runners that push up through the roots of the host tree
explanation: The strangler fig starts high on another tree and sends roots down that slowly wrap around the host tree.

q: What is the coccyx?
options: A small bone at the very bottom of the spine, also called the tailbone
A small cartilage pad that cushions the joints between the ribs
A tiny bone in the inner ear that helps with balance
A small curved bone at the base of the skull
explanation: The tailbone, or coccyx, is a small bone at the very bottom of the spine.

q: Why should you never push sharp objects or cotton buds deep into your ear?
options: They can hurt the eardrum
They can cause earwax to harden permanently
They can block sound from entering the ear canal
They can remove important bacteria that protect the ear
explanation: We should not push sharp objects or cotton buds deep into the ear because they can hurt the eardrum.

q: Which animal holds the record as one of the largest animals without a backbone?
options: The giant squid, reaching about 13 metres including its arms
The giant clam, measuring up to 2 metres across its shell
The lion's mane jellyfish, with tentacles stretching 30 metres
The whale shark, growing up to 12 metres in length
explanation: The giant squid is one of the largest invertebrates, reaching about 13 meters long including its long arms.

q: Why does the sun disappear from the sky at night?
options: The Earth turns so our side faces away from the sun
The sun moves behind the moon each night
The sun travels to the other side of space to rest
Clouds block the sun completely when evening comes
explanation: The sun does not really go away — the Earth just turns, so our side faces away from the sun while it remains day on the other side of the world.

q: What does Mendel's Law of Segregation say happens to alleles during sex cell formation?
options: The two alleles for a gene separate so each sex cell carries only one allele for each trait
The two alleles combine into one stronger allele before the sex cell is formed
Both alleles are copied equally into every sex cell so each gets a full set
