explanation: Our Sun belongs to the Milky Way galaxy.

q: In genetics, how is a dominant allele written compared to a recessive one?
options: The dominant allele uses a capital letter; the recessive uses a small letter
The dominant allele uses a small letter; the recessive uses a capital letter
Both dominant and recessive alleles always use capital letters
Both dominant and recessive alleles always use small letters
explanation: In genetics, a dominant allele is written as a capital letter and a recessive allele as a small letter.

q: What does a carabao typically do during the hottest part of midday?
options: It rests in the shade while chewing its cud
It plows the field faster to finish before dusk
It drinks large amounts of water from the river
It grazes more quickly to eat as much as possible
explanation: At hot midday a carabao rests in the shade while chewing its cud, then grazes in the cooler morning and afternoon.

q: A scientific name like Homo sapiens has two parts. What are they?
options: The Genus (capitalized) and the species (lowercase)
The kingdom (capitalized) and the family (lowercase)
The order (capitalized) and the class (lowercase)
The phylum (capitalized) and the division (lowercase)
explanation: An organism's scientific name has two parts: the Genus written with a capital letter and the species in lowercase, for example Homo sapiens.

q: About how cold is the water in the deep sea?
options: About 4 degrees Celsius, close to freezing
About 20 degrees Celsius, like a warm bath
About 0 degrees Celsius, completely frozen
About 40 degrees Celsius, hot like a fever
explanation: In the deep sea the water is very cold, only about 4 degrees Celsius, close to freezing.

q: What causes acid rain, and what can it harm?
options: Air pollution from burning oil and coal; it harms plants, fish, and buildings
Natural volcanic gases; it only affects the sky color
Sea spray mixing with fog; it mainly hurts sand and soil
Lightning breaking apart oxygen; it harms only metal bridges
explanation: Acid rain has a low pH caused by air pollution from burning oil and coal, and it harms plants, fish in rivers, and even buildings and statues.

q: Why are lichens called pioneer organisms on bare rock?
options: They are among the first living things to grow there and help start soil
They grow only after soil is already formed
They feed on the soil to produce new rock
They only appear after trees have already taken root
explanation: Lichens are among the first living things to grow on bare rock, slowly breaking it down to help start soil.

q: Why is the sky black in outer space even when the Sun is shining?
options: There is no air to scatter the Sun's light
Space is too far from the Sun to receive any light
The Moon blocks the sunlight in space
Black holes absorb all light before it can be seen
explanation: In space there are no air molecules to scatter sunlight, so the sky appears black.

q: Why does wiping oil or grease on iron tools help prevent rust?
options: It keeps air and water from reaching the iron
It makes the iron surface harder and unbreakable
It causes the iron to produce its own natural coating
It lowers the temperature of the iron below rusting point
explanation: Oil or grease wiped on tools keeps air and water from reaching the iron, which prevents rusting.

q: What happens to copper when it is exposed to air for a long time?
options: It develops a green coating called patina
It turns bright orange like rust on iron
It becomes completely black and crumbles
It stays shiny because copper never reacts with air
explanation: When copper is exposed to air for a long time, it develops a green coating called patina.

q: Which Filipino doctor invented a bamboo incubator for newborn babies?
options: Fe del Mundo
Josefa Llanes Escoda
Hilario Lim
Eduardo Quisumbing
explanation: Fe del Mundo, a Filipino pediatrician, invented the bamboo incubator that helped save the lives of many newborn babies.

q: Where in the body is the femur bone located?
options: In the thigh, between the hip and the knee
In the lower leg, between the knee and the ankle
In the upper arm, between the shoulder and the elbow
In the foot, connecting the ankle to the toes
explanation: The femur is found in the thigh, between the hip and the knee.

q: Why does the heart need four chambers instead of just one?
options: Four chambers keep oxygen-rich blood separate from used blood so your body always gets fresh blood
One chamber pumps blood twice as fast, which is healthier
Two chambers are enough because left and right sides do the same job
Four chambers are needed only to hold extra blood during exercise
explanation: Four chambers keep the oxygen-rich blood from mixing with already-used blood, so the blood going to the body is always fresh and full of oxygen.

q: Why does a magnet NOT attract wood, plastic, paper, or rubber?
options: Because those materials have no iron
Because those materials are too light to feel a magnetic pull
Because magnets only work in water
Because those materials push back against magnets
explanation: A magnet does not pull wood, plastic, paper, or rubber because they contain no iron.

q: Which Philippine president moved Independence Day to June 12, and in what year?
options: President Diosdado Macapagal, in 1962
President Ramon Magsaysay, in 1955
President Ferdinand Marcos, in 1972
President Manuel Quezon, in 1935
explanation: President Diosdado Macapagal moved Independence Day to June 12 in 1962 to honor the declaration of independence from Spain.

q: Which of the two manta ray species can reach a wingspan of up to 7 meters?
options: The oceanic manta ray (Manta birostris)
The reef manta ray (Manta alfredi)
The spotted eagle ray
The giant stingray
explanation: The oceanic manta ray can reach a wingspan of 7 meters, while the reef manta is the smaller species more commonly seen near Philippine reefs.

q: Where in the Philippines are large deposits of nickel and iron ore found?
options: Surigao del Norte in Mindanao
Benguet in the Cordillera Mountains
Palawan near the Tubbataha Reef
Batanes in the northernmost islands
explanation: Surigao del Norte in Mindanao has large deposits of nickel and iron ore that formed from the weathering of ultramafic rocks like peridotite over millions of years.

q: How does a leech help a swollen body part heal faster?
options: It sucks out the pooled blood, reducing swelling
It releases a chemical that kills harmful bacteria
It covers the wound to keep out dirt and germs
It numbs the area so the patient feels no pain
explanation: A leech helps by sucking out pooled blood, reducing swelling so the affected part heals faster.

q: About what fraction of the air we breathe is nitrogen?
options: About four out of every five parts
About one out of every five parts
About one out of every two parts
About nine out of every ten parts
explanation: Most of the air — about four out of every five parts — is nitrogen, a gas our bodies do not use for breathing.

q: Why do antibiotics NOT cure the common cold?
options: Because antibiotics fight bacteria, not viruses
Because antibiotics only work in hospitals
Because the common cold is not an illness
Because antibiotics destroy the lungs if used for colds
explanation: Antibiotics work against bacteria, not viruses, so they cannot cure a common cold which is caused by a virus.

q: What does a switch do inside an electric circuit?
options: It connects or breaks the path so current can flow or stop
It stores electrical energy like a battery
It converts electrical energy into light on its own
It controls how bright the light is by adding more voltage
explanation: A switch acts like a bridge — when on it connects the path so current flows; when off it breaks the path so current stops.

q: How do scavengers help the environment?
options: They eat carcasses before they rot, cleaning up the environment
They break down rocks into smaller pieces of soil
They filter dirty water to make it clean and safe
They pollinate flowers to help plants reproduce
explanation: Scavengers help clean the environment by eating carcasses before they rot.

q: What is one major effect of global warming caused by greenhouse gases like carbon dioxide?
options: It melts ice and raises sea levels
It makes the sky turn orange permanently
It causes all rivers to dry up completely
It stops wind from blowing across the ocean
explanation: Global warming is caused by greenhouse gases like carbon dioxide, and it melts ice and raises sea levels.

q: Why is a cuttlefish called a 'fish' even though it is not really a fish?
options: 'Cuttle' is just an old name for the animal; the word 'fish' is part of its traditional name, not its classification
It breathes through gills exactly like a true fish
It was reclassified as a fish by scientists in the 1900s
Its bones look identical to the bones of a real fish
explanation: The word 'cuttle' is an old name for this animal, so 'cuttlefish' is a traditional name even though it is neither a real fish nor does it have a real bone.

q: Why can grass grow back after the top part is eaten or cut?
options: Because grass grows from near the base of the plant, close to the ground
Because grass stores all its energy in its seeds and replants itself
Because grass roots release new blades from deep underground
Because the tips of grass blades are where new growth starts
explanation: Grass grows from near the ground, so even after the top is eaten or cut, new growth can continue from the base.

q: A fully grown hummingbird is still very tiny. What does this mean?
options: It has reached its adult size and will not grow any bigger
It must be a young bird that has not grown up yet
It is sick and stopped growing too early
It will double in size once it learns to fly faster
explanation: Even when a hummingbird is fully grown it is still very tiny — that tiny size is normal for an adult hummingbird.

q: What is the scientific term for a skink releasing its own tail on purpose to escape a predator?
options: Autotomy
Camouflage
Metamorphosis
Hibernation
explanation: The scientific name for self-tail-dropping is autotomy, which means 'self-cutting'; the skink releases its tail on purpose to escape.

q: Why is cooking an egg considered a chemical change rather than a physical change?
options: Because the cooked egg cannot be turned back into its raw form
Because cooking only changes the color but not the taste
Because the egg simply melts like ice and can be frozen again
Because the egg shell breaks, which is always a chemical reaction
explanation: Cooking an egg is a chemical change because the clear runny white turns firm and white and cannot be turned back into its raw form.

q: Why does drinking seawater make a person even thirstier?
options: The body needs extra water to flush out the extra salt
Seawater blocks the stomach from absorbing any liquid
Salt in seawater immediately evaporates inside the body
Seawater turns into gas in the stomach, leaving you dry
explanation: Drinking seawater makes you thirstier because your body needs even more fresh water to flush out the extra salt.

q: What will eventually happen to our Sun at the end of its life?
options: It will expand into a red giant and later leave behind a white dwarf
It will explode in a supernova and become a black hole
It will shrink into a small brown dwarf and stay that way forever
It will burn out instantly in a bright flash, leaving nothing behind
explanation: In about 5 billion years the Sun will expand into a red giant, then leave behind a planetary nebula and a small hot white dwarf.

q: What does it mean when a person's blood type is described as 'positive' (e.g., A+)?
options: They have the Rh factor antigen on their red blood cells
They have extra white blood cells to fight disease
Their blood carries more oxygen than a negative type
Their blood clots faster than Rh negative blood
explanation: The Rh factor is an antigen on red blood cells; people who have it are Rh positive (+) and those without it are Rh negative (-).

q: How does the water get inside a coconut?
options: The roots absorb water from the soil and it travels up the trunk into the fruit
Rain falls directly through the top of the coconut shell
The coconut makes its own water from sunlight and air
Underground springs push water up through the coconut tree roots at night
explanation: The roots of the coconut tree absorb water from the soil, and that water travels up the trunk to collect inside the coconut fruit.

q: How do legume plants like mung beans improve the soil around them?
options: Bacteria in their root nodules take nitrogen from the air and enrich the soil
Their fallen leaves release acid that dissolves rocks into nutrients
Their roots pump carbon dioxide into the soil to feed other plants
They absorb minerals from deeper layers and deposit them on the surface
explanation: Legume plants have root nodules where bacteria live and fix nitrogen from the air, enriching the soil.

q: What effect does El Nino have on the Philippines?
options: It brings stronger drought and below-normal rainfall, often lowering rice harvests
It causes more typhoons and floods than a normal year
It makes the Philippines cooler and cloudier than usual
It raises sea levels around the Philippines rapidly
explanation: El Nino is a Pacific Ocean climate event that brings stronger drought and below-normal rainfall to the Philippines, often causing lower rice harvests.

q: Where in the body are white blood cells (the cells that fight disease) produced?
options: Inside the bones, in a part called the bone marrow
In the liver, which filters the blood
In the thyroid gland in the neck
In the lymph nodes under the skin
explanation: White blood cells that defend the body are made inside our bones, in a part called the bone marrow.

q: Which layer of an animal embryo develops into the skin and nerves?
options: Ectoderm
Mesoderm
Endoderm
Blastoderm
explanation: The ectoderm is the embryo's outer layer and gives rise to the skin and nerves.

q: What happens to the ocean when it absorbs too much carbon dioxide?
options: It becomes more acidic
It becomes saltier
It becomes warmer
It becomes deeper
explanation: When the ocean absorbs carbon dioxide, it slowly becomes more acidic, which harms shells and corals.

q: In a laboratory, what forms when a single bacterium multiplies many times on a petri dish?
options: A colony
A spore
A cell wall
A biofilm
explanation: Each bacterium multiplies to form a colony — a visible group of millions of identical bacteria.

q: How does lanzones taste when it is fully ripe?
options: Sweet
Sour
Bitter
Salty
explanation: When lanzones is ripe, its clear white flesh is sweet to eat.

q: Why do many birds migrate away from their home area?
options: Food becomes scarce when the weather turns cold
They want to find a warmer place to sleep
They follow the direction of the wind
They look for a new place to build nests
explanation: Many birds migrate because food becomes scarce in their home when the weather turns cold.

q: Which animals help pollinate mango flowers?
options: Insects like flies and bees
Birds like maya and kalapati
Lizards and geckos
Bats and frogs
explanation: Insects like flies and bees help pollinate mango flowers.

q: What is the name for smaller rivers that flow into a larger river?
options: Tributaries
Deltas
Estuaries
Canals
explanation: Rivers that flow into a bigger river are called tributaries, and they help the Agusan River grow larger on its way to the sea.

q: Who leads the House of Representatives in the Philippines?
options: The Speaker
The Senate President
The Chief Justice
The Vice President
explanation: The Speaker leads the House of Representatives.

q: When will a moray eel most likely bite a person?
options: When it feels cornered or its hiding hole is disturbed
When it is hungry and looking for food
When it sees a diver wearing bright colors
When it is swimming in open water
explanation: A moray eel is not naturally aggressive and usually bites only when it feels cornered or its hiding hole is disturbed.

q: What did scientist Angel Alcala pioneer to help fish stocks recover?
options: Marine sanctuaries where fishing is banned
Fish farming in open ocean cages
Artificial reefs made of old ships
Chemical treatments to grow more coral
explanation: Angel Alcala pioneered marine sanctuaries — no-take zones where fishing is banned so fish stocks can recover.

q: In which part of the Philippines is the Ragay Gulf located?
options: Bicol region, southern Luzon
Eastern Visayas
Mindanao, near Davao
Ilocos, northern Luzon
explanation: The Ragay Gulf is in the Bicol region of southern Luzon, near Camarines Sur.

q: Which of the following fruits grow on large trees?
options: Lanzones, rambutan, and mangosteen
Strawberry, watermelon, and papaya
Banana, pineapple, and coconut
Pumpkin, cucumber, and ampalaya
explanation: Lanzones, rambutan, and mangosteen all grow as fruit on large trees.

q: What determines which bacteria grow in a person's gut?
options: The kind of food the person eats
The person's age and height
The temperature of the body
The amount of sleep the person gets
explanation: The kind of food we eat affects which bacteria grow in our gut.

q: How does pollen travel from one flower to another when a bee visits?
options: Pollen sticks to the bee's body and is carried to the next flower
Pollen falls into the bee's mouth and is spat out later
The bee drinks pollen and releases it through waste
Pollen dissolves in nectar and drips onto other flowers
explanation: Pollen sticks to a bee's body, and the bee carries the pollen to another flower.

q: What happens to the surroundings during an exothermic reaction?
options: They get warmer because heat is released
They get cooler because heat is absorbed
They stay the same temperature
They first cool down then heat up
explanation: An exothermic reaction releases heat, so its surroundings get warmer.

q: Which of the following animals also have kidneys that clean their blood, just like humans?
options: Pigs, dogs, and fish
Butterflies, ants, and bees
Jellyfish, starfish, and sea urchins
Earthworms, snails, and slugs
explanation: Not only people have kidneys; animals like pigs, dogs, and fish also have kidneys that clean their blood.

q: Why does the body shiver when it is very cold?
options: Many muscles tighten and relax rapidly at the same time, causing the body to tremble
One large muscle in the chest squeezes to pump warm blood faster
The skin releases sweat to warm the air around the body
The bones vibrate to produce heat through friction
explanation: Shivering happens because many muscles tighten and relax at the same time, making the whole body tremble.

q: What usually happens when a leech is full of blood?
options: It lets go on its own
It must be pulled off by force
It stays attached forever
It burrows deeper into the skin
explanation: A leech usually lets go on its own once it is full of blood; forcing it off can leave its teeth in the skin.

q: How long would it take light to travel from one side of the Milky Way to the other?
options: About 100,000 years
About 1,000 years
About one million years
About 24 hours
explanation: The Milky Way is so wide that light would take about 100,000 years to cross it from one side to the other.

q: Which cell parts are found in BOTH plant and animal cells?
options: Cell membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus, and mitochondria
Cell wall, chloroplast, vacuole, and nucleus
Cell membrane, chloroplast, cytoplasm, and ribosomes
Cell wall, mitochondria, vacuole, and nucleus
explanation: Both plant and animal cells share the cell membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus, and mitochondria.

q: What does the stem of a plant do with the water absorbed by the roots?
options: It carries water up to the leaves
It stores water in the ground
It pushes water out through the flowers
It breaks water down into food for the plant
explanation: The stem carries water up from the roots to the leaves.

q: Where was the first Mass in the Philippines held?
options: Limasawa
Cebu City
Mactan Island
Manila
explanation: The first Mass in the Philippines was held at Limasawa in 1521.

q: What must happen before an object at rest starts to move?
options: The applied force must exceed the static friction holding it still
The object must be warmed up to reduce its weight
The object must reach the right temperature
Gravity must be temporarily removed from the object
explanation: Before an object starts moving, the applied force must exceed the static friction that holds it still.

q: How is tamilok, the famous Palawan delicacy, often eaten?
options: Raw with vinegar, like kinilaw
Grilled over charcoal
Deep-fried with garlic
Boiled in coconut milk
explanation: In Palawan, the tamilok is often eaten raw with vinegar, like kinilaw.

q: In empty space, how do the speeds of different electromagnetic waves compare?
options: All electromagnetic waves travel at the same speed
Radio waves travel fastest, light waves travel slowest
Light waves travel fastest, radio waves travel slowest
Each type of wave travels at a completely different speed
explanation: In empty space, all electromagnetic waves — from radio to light — travel at the same speed, called the speed of light.

q: What kind of soil do farmers use to grow rice plants?
options: Flooded, wet soil
Dry, sandy soil
Rocky mountain soil
Frozen tundra soil
explanation: Rice is a grass plant that farmers grow in flooded, wet soil, and its grain becomes the rice we eat.

q: How did many of the caves in Cebu form?
options: Rainwater slowly dissolved the limestone over thousands of years
Volcanic eruptions melted and hollowed out the rock
Earthquakes split the ground open over many years
Strong ocean waves carved out tunnels in the cliffs
explanation: Many caves in Cebu formed as rainwater slowly dissolved the limestone over thousands of years.

q: What is the chemical formula of water?
options: H2O
CO2
NaCl
O2
explanation: The chemical formula of water is H2O, meaning two hydrogen atoms bonded to one oxygen atom.

q: What is the main job of detritivores like worms and millipedes in decomposition?
options: They chew and shred dead leaves into smaller bits for bacteria and fungi to finish
They produce chemicals that instantly dissolve dead plant material
They carry nutrients from the soil directly into living plant roots
They produce heat that speeds up rotting in the compost pile
explanation: Detritivores like worms and millipedes chew and shred dead leaves into smaller bits, then bacteria and fungi finish the decomposition.

q: Which situation other than fear can also cause the body to release adrenaline?
options: Excitement, like riding a roller coaster
Sleeping deeply after a long day
Eating a large, heavy meal
Sitting quietly and reading a book
explanation: Even when excited — like riding a roller coaster or joining a contest — adrenaline is released, not just during fear.

q: When does a recessive trait actually appear in a child?
options: When the child carries two recessive alleles
When only one recessive allele is present
When the dominant allele is missing from one parent
When the child is born premature
explanation: A recessive trait appears only when a child carries two recessive alleles.

q: How long does one complete spin of the Earth actually take?
options: About 23 hours and 56 minutes
Exactly 24 hours
About 25 hours
About 23 hours and 10 minutes
explanation: One full spin of Earth actually takes about 23 hours and 56 minutes, which we round to 24 hours.

q: How does a baby in the womb receive food and oxygen from its mother?
options: Through the umbilical cord
Through the amniotic fluid
Through the mother's skin
Through direct contact with the mother's organs
explanation: The baby in the womb receives food and oxygen from the mother through the umbilical cord.

q: How does a refrigerator keep food cold?
options: It removes heat from inside and dumps it out the back
It pumps cold air from outside into the food compartment
It creates a chemical reaction that absorbs heat from the air
It freezes moisture in the air to lower the temperature inside
explanation: A refrigerator does not make cold; it removes heat from inside and dumps that heat out the back.

q: What is the special name for the baby eel that is thin, see-through, and leaf-shaped?
options: Leptocephalus
Larvifish
Elver
Fry
explanation: The baby eel is thin, see-through, and leaf-shaped, so it is called a leptocephalus.

q: Which sense does the eel rely on most to find food and find its way in dark water?
options: Smell
Sight
Hearing
Touch
explanation: The eel has a very keen sense of smell that helps it find food and its way in dark water.

q: Why does Puto Calasiao rise and become slightly sour during preparation?
options: Fermentation by yeast and tiny organisms produces gas from the sugar in the rice
The rice is mixed with baking soda that releases bubbles when heated
The batter is beaten with air until it becomes fluffy
Steam pressure during cooking forces the puto to expand upward
explanation: Puto Calasiao rises and turns slightly sour because of fermentation, where yeast and tiny organisms make gas from the sugar in the rice.

q: How do balanced meals with vegetables, fruit, and fiber help people manage blood sugar?
options: They cause blood sugar to rise only slowly, so insulin can keep up more easily
They block the stomach from absorbing any sugar at all
They cause the pancreas to stop producing insulin temporarily
They convert sugar directly into fat before it enters the blood
explanation: Eating balanced meals with vegetables, fruit, and fiber helps blood sugar rise only slowly, so insulin can keep up and the level stays steady.

q: What is cloud seeding used for?
options: To encourage rainfall in areas suffering from drought
To stop hurricanes before they reach land
To make clouds larger so they block sunlight
To measure how much water is stored in clouds
explanation: Cloud seeding involves releasing chemicals like silver iodide into clouds to encourage rainfall and combat drought.

q: When a candle burns, which TWO types of change happen?
options: Melting wax (physical change) and burning wax (chemical change)
Burning wax (physical change) and melting wax (chemical change)
Only physical changes because nothing new is made
Only chemical changes because fire is always involved
explanation: A burning candle shows two changes: the wax melting is a physical change, but the wax burning to give heat and light is a chemical change.

q: What material are bird feathers made of?
options: Keratin
Calcium
Cellulose
Chitin
explanation: Feathers are made of keratin, the same tough material that forms our hair and nails.

q: What are the names of the two main monsoon winds in the Philippines?
options: Amihan and Habagat
Habagat and Bagyo
Amihan and Bagyong
Hanging Amihan and Hanging Tagulan
explanation: In the Philippines, the strong amihan and habagat monsoon winds can be a source of wind energy.

q: How many main body parts does a spider have?
options: Two — a front section and a rear section (abdomen)
Three — head, thorax, and abdomen
Four — head, chest, belly, and tail
One — a single fused body
explanation: A spider's body has two main parts: the front (head and chest joined together) and the rear abdomen.

q: Why is carbon fiber used in aircraft and racing cars?
options: It is extremely lightweight yet stronger than steel
It can withstand very high temperatures without melting
It is cheap and easy to shape into complex forms
It conducts electricity better than copper wires
explanation: Carbon fiber is extremely lightweight yet stronger than steel, so it is used in aircraft, racing cars, and sports equipment.

q: On average, how much salt is dissolved in every liter of seawater?
options: About 35 grams
About 5 grams
About 100 grams
About 350 grams
explanation: On average, seawater contains about 35 grams of salt in every liter of water.

q: What part of the nutmeg tree is used to make the spice nutmeg?
options: The dried seed inside the fruit
The bark of the trunk
The dried flower petals
The crushed root of the tree
explanation: Nutmeg is a spice made from the dried seed inside the fruit of the nutmeg tree.

q: How do flies spread germs from garbage onto food?
options: Tiny hairs on their legs trap dirt and germs, which they carry to the next surface they land on
They breathe germs out through tiny holes in their wings
They bite food and inject germs through their mouth parts
They leave droppings that contain chemicals attracting germs
explanation: A fly's legs are covered in tiny hairs where dirt and germs stick, letting it carry germs from garbage onto food.

q: Which foods are natural sources of iodine?
options: Fish and seaweed
Beef and pork
Rice and corn
Bananas and mangoes
explanation: Fish and sea plants like seaweed are natural sources of iodine.

q: About how long is the single silk thread inside one silkworm cocoon when it is fully unwound?
options: Nearly a kilometer long
About one meter long
About ten meters long
About one hundred meters long
explanation: A single silkworm cocoon is made from one continuous silk thread that can be nearly a kilometer long when unwound.

q: In a chemical reaction, what happens when the energy released forming new bonds is MORE than the energy needed to break old bonds?
options: The reaction is exothermic and releases energy
The reaction is endothermic and absorbs energy
The reaction stops completely
The reaction produces only water and gas
explanation: If more energy is released than needed, the reaction is exothermic; if more energy is needed than released, it is endothermic.

q: What material makes up the cell walls of fungi, setting them apart from plants?
options: Chitin, the same tough material found in insect shells
Cellulose, the same material found in plant cell walls
Keratin, the same material found in human fingernails
Collagen, the same material found in animal skin
explanation: Fungi cell walls are made of chitin, the same tough material found in insect shells, not cellulose like plants.

q: Why does a cut apple brown more slowly when you wrap it in plastic?
options: It limits the apple's contact with air
It keeps the apple cold and dry
It blocks light from reaching the apple
It stops bacteria from touching the apple
explanation: Wrapping a cut apple in plastic limits its contact with air, slowing the browning process.

q: Besides building body tissues, what else does protein help make inside your body?
options: Enzymes and antibodies that help fight disease
Red blood cells and white blood cells
Vitamins C and D that protect your skin
Calcium and iron for strong bones
explanation: Protein also makes enzymes and antibodies that help the body fight disease, not just body-building materials.

q: What job does iron do inside your blood?
options: It helps red blood cells carry oxygen around your body
It fights bacteria and viruses in your bloodstream
It controls how fast your heart beats
It makes your blood clot when you get a cut
explanation: Iron in your blood helps red blood cells carry oxygen around your body, which is why the body needs iron-rich food.

q: How do some frogs survive even when part of their body freezes?
options: Natural substances in their blood protect their cells from damage
They burrow deep underground where it stays warm
Their thick skin acts as insulation against the cold
They slow their heartbeat to almost zero to save energy
explanation: Some frogs can survive partial freezing because natural substances in their blood protect their cells from damage.

q: A family opens a window while someone smokes indoors. Does this make everyone safe from secondhand smoke?
options: No, tiny smoke particles still linger in the air and on furniture for a long time
Yes, fresh air from the window quickly blows all smoke particles outside
Yes, as long as the smoker stands near the window
No, but a fan blowing toward the window completely solves the problem
explanation: It is a common myth that an open window removes secondhand smoke; the tiny particles still linger in the air and on furniture for a long time.

q: Why is a leech NOT classified as an insect?
options: It has no legs or wings and its body is soft like a worm
It lives in water instead of on land
It cannot fly and does not lay eggs
It is too large to be an insect
explanation: A leech is not an insect because it has no legs or wings and its body is soft like a worm.

q: Where does kangkong (water spinach) typically grow?
options: In water or wet soil
In dry sandy soil in open fields
On tree branches and rocky hillsides
In shaded forest floors away from water
explanation: Kangkong (water spinach) is a leafy vegetable that often grows in water or wet soil.

q: What keeps the Earth's inner core solid even though it is extremely hot?
options: The enormous pressure squeezing it from all sides
A thick layer of rock that insulates it from the heat
Its iron atoms are too large to melt at any temperature
The cold ocean water above cools it down from the outside
explanation: The Earth's inner core is solid iron because the enormous pressure keeps it solid despite the intense heat.

q: What flavor does calamansi add when squeezed over Filipino dishes and dipping sauces?
options: A sour flavor
A sweet flavor
A bitter flavor
A salty flavor
explanation: Calamansi is squeezed over dishes and dipping sauces to give them a tasty sour flavor.

q: What energy source does the BacMan power plant in Sorsogon and Albay use to generate electricity?
options: Hot steam from the volcanic ground near Mayon
Wind from the ocean blowing across the mountains
Water flowing down from the Mayon crater
Solar energy collected on the slopes of Mayon
explanation: The BacMan geothermal power plant uses hot steam from the volcanic ground around Mayon to generate electricity.

q: Which shape best describes a mosquito pupa?
options: A comma or question mark, with a big rounded top and a curled thin tail
A straight tube with a flat head at one end
A round ball with tiny legs tucked underneath
An oval egg shape with no visible head or tail
explanation: A mosquito pupa is shaped like a comma or a question mark, with a big rounded head-and-chest part and a thin curled tail bending downward.

q: How is the vinegar used in Filipino adobo produced?
options: Through fermentation, where bacteria produce sourness from sugar
By mixing water with natural citrus juice like calamansi
By boiling salt water until it becomes concentrated and sour
By cooling fresh fruit juice until it separates into layers
explanation: Vinegar used in Filipino dishes like adobo is made through fermentation, where bacteria produce sourness from sugar.

q: Why are the materials in the world so different from one another?
options: Because there are many different kinds of atoms, such as gold, oxygen, and carbon
Because some materials are made of atoms and others are not
Because atoms change their shape depending on how hot or cold they are
Because living things have atoms but non-living things do not
explanation: There are many different kinds of atoms, and the differences between atoms are why the materials in the world are so different.

q: In the chemical formula NaCl (table salt), what element does 'Na' stand for?
options: Sodium
Nitrogen
Nickel
Neon
explanation: In NaCl, the Na stands for sodium and the Cl stands for chlorine.

q: How does using a proper toilet help protect people from intestinal worms?
options: It stops worm eggs from spreading into the soil and water
It kills worm eggs with the chemicals in toilet cleaners
It keeps the worms trapped in one place away from people
It flushes the worms into the sea where they cannot harm humans
explanation: Using a proper toilet stops worm eggs from spreading into the soil and water, preventing infection.

q: Why do monsoon winds reverse direction twice a year?
options: Because land and sea temperatures change with the seasons, switching which is hotter
Because the Earth's rotation reverses direction every six months
Because ocean currents push the wind in the opposite direction each season
Because the sun moves to the other side of the Earth in winter
explanation: Monsoon winds reverse direction because of seasonal changes in land and sea temperature: in summer the land is hotter and winds blow from sea to land; in winter the sea is warmer and winds reverse.

q: How many protons does a fluorine (F) atom have?
options: 9 protons
7 protons
17 protons
19 protons
explanation: The atomic number of fluorine is 9, which means it has 9 protons.

q: Which combination of features makes a bird's body built for flight?
options: Hollow bones, a light beak, and feathers that keep weight low
Solid bones, a heavy beak, and thick fur for warmth
Large muscles, webbed feet, and a wide flat tail for steering
Dense bones, large eyes, and scales covering the body
explanation: A bird's whole body is built strong but light — hollow bones, a light beak, and feathers — so it can fly.

q: Why can many grassland grazers run so fast?
options: The open, wide grassland gives them space to run on their long legs to escape predators
They are always well-fed on grass so they have more energy than other animals
Their light-colored fur helps them hide in the grass until they are ready to sprint
Their large ears help them hear predators coming and give them extra time to run
explanation: Because grasslands are open and wide, many grazers can run fast on their long legs to escape predators.

q: Where in the world is the Philippine flying lemur found?
options: Only in the Philippines, mostly in the forests of Mindanao and Bohol
Throughout Southeast Asia, including Indonesia and Malaysia
In the forests of both the Philippines and Papua New Guinea
Across the Pacific islands from the Philippines to Hawaii
explanation: The Philippine flying lemur is found nowhere else in the world, mostly in the forests of Mindanao and Bohol, making it endemic to the Philippines.

q: Who heads the Supreme Court of the Philippines?
options: The Chief Justice
The President of the Philippines
The Senate President
The Secretary of Justice
explanation: The Chief Justice heads the Supreme Court of the Philippines.

q: What is the legal voting age in the Philippines?
options: 18 years old
21 years old
16 years old
15 years old
explanation: The legal voting age in the Philippines is 18 years old.

q: What is agar, extracted from red algae, used for in science laboratories?
options: As a solid medium in petri dishes to grow bacteria for study
As a liquid dye to color microscope slides
As a preservative to keep lab specimens fresh longer
As a fuel source for heating equipment in the lab
explanation: Agar extracted from red algae is used in laboratories as a solid medium in petri dishes to grow bacteria for study.

q: Who wrote the original lyrics of the Philippine national anthem?
options: Jose Palma, who wrote a Spanish poem called 'Filipinas' in 1899
Emilio Aguinaldo, the first President of the Philippines
Julian Felipe, who composed the music of the anthem
Jose Rizal, who wrote it as part of his final letter
explanation: The original lyrics of the anthem came from the Spanish poem 'Filipinas,' written by Jose Palma in 1899.

q: What is the fixed point at the top of a pendulum called?
options: The pivot
The fulcrum
The anchor
The node
explanation: A pendulum hangs from a fixed point at the top called the pivot, and it swings around this point.

q: What does the name 'tardigrade' mean?
options: Slow stepper
Water bear
Hard shell
Tiny walker
explanation: The name 'tardigrade' comes from old words meaning 'slow stepper,' fitting because they crawl slowly on their eight stubby legs.

q: Why is it especially important for Filipinos to keep trash out of the water near their shores?
options: Because our islands are surrounded by the sea and keeping shores clean keeps them beautiful
Because fish near the shore are sold in markets and trash changes their flavor
Because the government charges a fine to anyone who throws trash near the sea
Because trash blocks the paths that fishing boats use to go out to sea
explanation: Because the Philippines is surrounded by the sea, keeping shores clean and not throwing trash into the water is important to protect the islands' natural beauty.

q: During which step of mitosis do the chromosomes line up in the middle of the cell?
options: During metaphase, when chromosomes line up in the middle
During prophase, when chromosomes first become visible
During anaphase, when chromosomes are pulled to opposite sides
During telophase, when two new nuclei start to form
explanation: During one step of mitosis called metaphase, the chromosomes line up in the middle of the cell.

q: Why must you eat vitamin C every single day, but you do not need to eat vitamin A every day?
options: Vitamin C is water-soluble so the body cannot store it, while vitamin A is fat-soluble and can be stored
Vitamin C is only found in rare fruits while vitamin A is found in almost every food
Vitamin C breaks down in sunlight so it must be replaced daily
Vitamin A is made inside the body from sunlight so it rarely runs out
explanation: Vitamin C is water-soluble, meaning the body cannot store it and it is needed daily, while vitamin A is fat-soluble and can be stored by the body.

q: Why is a full jeepney harder to stop than an empty one traveling at the same speed?
options: A full jeepney is heavier, so it has more momentum
A full jeepney's engine works harder, making it accelerate more
A full jeepney has more air resistance pushing it forward
A full jeepney's tires grip the road less because of the extra weight
explanation: A jeepney full of passengers is heavier, so it has more momentum and is harder to stop than an empty one.

q: Besides in a factory, how can natural glass be formed?
options: When lightning strikes sand or when volcano lava cools very quickly
When seawater evaporates and leaves behind mineral crystals
When rocks are crushed under very high pressure underground
When ice melts slowly and re-freezes in a different shape
explanation: Natural glass can form when lightning strikes sand or when volcano lava cools quickly.

q: How does the praying mantis avoid being noticed by its prey before it attacks?
options: It stays completely still so its prey does not notice it
It changes color to match leaves and bark
It makes a buzzing sound that confuses nearby insects
It moves very slowly and hides under fallen leaves
explanation: The praying mantis stays completely still while waiting so its prey does not notice it.

q: What happens to the arc of a pendulum if you pull it back higher before releasing it?
options: It swings farther and wider to the other side
It swings back and forth more times per second
It swings at the same width but moves faster
It reaches the other side but stops there instead of swinging back
explanation: The higher you pull a pendulum back before letting go, the farther and wider it swings to the other side.

q: Which nutrient, found in milk and leafy vegetables, keeps bones firm and sturdy so they can protect the body?
options: Calcium
Iron
Vitamin C
Protein
explanation: Calcium — found in milk, fish with bones, and leafy vegetables — helps keep our bones firm and sturdy so they can do their protecting job.

q: How many protons does a lithium (Li) atom have?
options: 3 protons
7 protons
6 protons
1 proton
explanation: The atomic number of lithium is 3, so a lithium atom has 3 protons.

q: What creates the 'sea of clouds' that can be seen from highlands like Mount Pulag?
options: Thick clouds fill the valleys below, making the mountains look like they rise above a cloud ocean
Fog from the ocean rolls in and covers the entire mountain from base to peak
Water vapor from nearby lakes rises and freezes to form a flat white layer
Rain clouds gather above the mountains and press down into the valleys
explanation: In highlands like Mount Pulag, a 'sea of clouds' forms when thick clouds fill the valleys below, making the mountains appear to rise above a cloud ocean.

q: What two things determine the strength of gravity on a planet's surface?
options: The planet's mass and its size
The planet's distance from the sun and its temperature
The planet's speed of rotation and the number of its moons
The planet's atmosphere thickness and its surface material
explanation: A planet's surface gravity depends on its mass and its size.

q: What are many asteroids and meteoroids thought to be?
options: Leftover pieces from when the Solar System formed billions of years ago
Broken-off chunks from planets that exploded long ago
Rocks ejected from the sun during massive solar flares
Frozen comets that lost their ice and shrank over time
explanation: Many asteroids and meteoroids are like leftover pieces from when the Solar System formed billions of years ago.

q: When water reaches a dot of marker ink on paper, what does it do to the ink colors?
options: It carries the different colors different distances apart, separating them
It dissolves all the colors into a single brown or gray mixture
It causes the ink colors to sink into the paper and disappear
It makes all the colors spread out evenly in a large circle
explanation: Water climbs the paper and carries the different colors different distances, separating them through capillary action.

q: Why is drinking enough clean water every day part of healthy eating?
options: Water helps the body stay cool and healthy
Water gives the body energy just like food does
Water contains vitamins and minerals that replace eating vegetables
Water cleans your teeth and stops you from feeling hungry
explanation: Drinking enough clean water every day is part of healthy eating because water helps the body stay cool and healthy.

q: What caused the number of tamaraws to drop?
options: Hunting and the loss of their habitat
Disease and a shortage of food in their forests
Competition from water buffalo introduced to their area
Flooding of the lowlands where they used to live
explanation: The number of tamaraws dropped because of hunting and the loss of their habitat.

q: What was Charles Darwin's nationality?
options: English
French
German
American
explanation: Charles Darwin was an English naturalist from England.

q: Is it true that flowers only grow in Baguio because that is where Panagbenga festival is held?
options: No, flowers like gumamela and santan grow in hot lowland areas too; Baguio is just famous for how many and how beautiful its flowers are
Yes, the cool mountain air of Baguio is the only climate where flowering plants can grow in the Philippines
No, but flowers in the lowlands are so small they are hard to see without a magnifying glass
Yes, lowland plants only produce leaves and never grow flowers because of the heat
explanation: Flowers grow even in hot places like gumamela and santan in the lowlands; Baguio is just famous for how many and how beautiful its flowers are.

q: Because chickens have no teeth, what body part do they use to grind their food?
options: The gizzard
The crop
The beak
The stomach
explanation: Chickens have no teeth, so they use a body part called the gizzard to grind their food.

q: In what year was the sampaguita chosen as the Philippine national flower?
explanation: The sampaguita was chosen as the Philippine national flower in 1934.

q: Which scientist studied falling bodies and motion?
options: Galileo Galilei
Isaac Newton
Albert Einstein
Archimedes
explanation: Galileo Galilei studied falling bodies and motion.

q: How does seaweed help keep coastal water clean?
options: By soaking up extra nutrients from the water
By producing oxygen that kills harmful bacteria
By filtering sand and mud from the seafloor
By releasing chemicals that stop algae from growing
explanation: Seaweed absorbs extra nutrients in coastal water, which helps keep it clean.

q: Why does a mother sea turtle lay so many eggs at one time?
options: Because most hatchlings will not survive, so many eggs are needed to keep the species going
Because the eggs are very small and need to fill a large nest
Because more eggs means the babies grow faster and stronger
Because sea turtles forget where they buried the nest and need extras
explanation: A mother sea turtle lays many eggs because only a few hatchlings survive, and high numbers ensure enough make it to keep the species alive.

q: What makes plants in the kingdom Plantae different from other living things?
options: They make their own food using sunlight
They absorb nutrients from dead animals in the soil
They get energy by eating other plants
They produce food only during the night
explanation: The kingdom Plantae is made of plants that produce their own food through photosynthesis using sunlight.

q: What is special about a euglena compared to most single-celled creatures?
options: It can make its own food from sunlight AND swim using a whip-like tail
It is the only microbe that can be seen without a microscope
It lives only in salt water and feeds on coral
It reproduces by laying tiny eggs on underwater surfaces
explanation: Euglena is unusual because it swims with a whip-like tail like an animal but can also make food from sunlight like a plant.

q: What are the shells of diatoms made of?
options: Glass (silica)
Calcium carbonate like sea shells
Chitin like insect skeletons
Hard wax that hardens in salt water
explanation: Diatoms have hard shells made of silica, which is the same mineral found in glass.

q: What is needed to make a still ball start rolling AND to make a rolling ball stop?
options: A force in both cases
Heat in both cases
Gravity only for stopping
Sound waves only for starting
explanation: A force is needed both to start a still object moving and to stop a moving object.

q: What lives inside coral and helps feed it?
options: Tiny algae that make food from sunlight
Small shrimp that hunt for plankton
Bacteria that break down dead fish
Microscopic worms that filter seawater
explanation: Coral has tiny algae living inside it that use sunlight to make food and share it with the coral.

q: On which day is the Sinulog festival celebrated every year?
options: The third Sunday of January
The last Friday of January
The first Monday of February
The second Saturday of December
explanation: The Sinulog festival is always held on the third Sunday of January.

q: A frog's eyes are partly on the sides of its head, yet it is still a hunter. How does it catch prey?
options: By using its very fast tongue to catch insects
By chasing prey with powerful hind legs
By waiting for prey to walk into its open mouth
By using its eyes to judge exact distance before jumping
explanation: Even though a frog's eyes are somewhat on the sides, it catches insects using a very fast tongue rather than relying on forward-facing vision.

q: What is the chemical symbol for the element iron?
options: Fe
Ir
In
Io
explanation: The symbol for iron is Fe, and it is element number 26 on the periodic table.

q: Which gas is the lightest of all, even lighter than air?
options: Hydrogen
Helium
Oxygen
Nitrogen
explanation: Hydrogen is the lightest gas, even lighter than air.

q: What tools does PAGASA use to figure out the exact start of the habagat in different parts of the Philippines?
options: Weather balloons, satellites, and ground stations
Rain gauges, thermometers, and fishing boats
Underwater sensors, wind mills, and sea buoys
Drones, cloud cameras, and river monitors
explanation: PAGASA uses data from weather balloons, satellites, and ground stations to determine the precise start of the habagat.

q: Why must a slug always stay in damp, dark places while a snail does not need to?
options: A slug has no shell to protect it, so it must hide to avoid drying out and predators
A slug has weak legs and cannot walk in bright sunlight
A slug's eyes are damaged by light, so it stays in darkness to see better
A slug breathes through its skin and needs rainwater to survive
explanation: Unlike a snail, a slug has no shell to hide in, so it must stay in damp, dark places to avoid drying out and being spotted by enemies.

q: Where does the tikling bird build its nest?
options: On the ground or near water
High in the treetops away from flooding
Inside hollow tree trunks
On steep cliffsides above rivers
explanation: The tikling builds its nest on the ground or near water, where it lays its eggs.

q: What causes coral bleaching in Philippine seas?
options: Rising ocean temperatures caused by climate change
Overfishing that removes too many fish from the reef
Pollution from oil spills coating the coral
Typhoon waves physically breaking apart the reef
explanation: Climate change raises ocean temperatures, causing coral bleaching where corals die and reefs turn white in Philippine seas.

q: Which country has the largest population in the world?
options: India
China
United States
Indonesia
explanation: India is the most populous country in the world, with a population of about 1.4 billion people.

q: Why does a doctor feel your neck, armpits, or groin during a checkup?
options: To check if your lymph nodes are swollen, which may signal infection or illness
To feel your pulse and count your heartbeats per minute
To test whether your nerves are working properly in those areas
To measure the amount of fat stored under your skin
explanation: Doctors feel lymph nodes in the neck, armpits, or groin to check if they are swollen, which can indicate an infection or other illness.

q: Where is the appendix located in the human body?
options: Attached to the large intestine
At the bottom of the stomach
Connected to the small intestine near the liver
Inside the lower lung cavity
explanation: The appendix is a small pouch attached to the large intestine, and if it becomes inflamed it may need to be removed.

q: What happens to a banana plant after it bears fruit?
options: That stem dies, but the underground rhizome grows new shoots that become new plants
The plant flowers again and produces another bunch of bananas
The roots dry up and the whole plant must be replanted from seed
The plant shrinks to half its size and rests before growing again
explanation: A banana plant bears fruit only once and then that stem dies, but the underground rhizome grows new suckers that become new plants.

q: What types of land formations are included in the count of thousands of Philippine islands?
options: Large islands, tiny sandbars, and rocks that barely poke out of the sea
Only islands large enough for people to live on
Only islands that have fresh water sources
Islands and underwater mountains that rise above sea level during low tide
explanation: The count of thousands of Philippine islands includes everything from large islands like Luzon to tiny sandbars and rocks that just poke out of the sea.

q: How many legs does a typical human have?
explanation: A human has two legs, which is one feature that sets us apart from four-legged animals.

q: What happens to tooth stains after a person stops smoking?
options: The stains stop getting worse and can improve with a dentist's help
The stains disappear completely on their own within a month
The teeth become more yellow at first before they get better
Nothing changes because the damage from smoking is permanent
explanation: When a person stops smoking, the stains no longer get worse, and with a dentist's help the teeth can gradually return to a cleaner color.

q: Why are Uranus and Neptune called 'ice giants' instead of 'gas giants' like Jupiter and Saturn?
options: They contain more cold ices like water, ammonia, and methane than pure gas
They are completely frozen solid all the way through unlike Jupiter
They orbit closer to the Sun so they collect more ice from comets
They are smaller than gas giants and their gravity pulls in more ice
explanation: Uranus and Neptune are called ice giants because they hold more cold ices (water, ammonia, methane) compared to the mostly-gas Jupiter and Saturn.

q: When is the best time to wash fruit to keep it from spoiling quickly?
options: Right before you eat it, not when you store it
As soon as you bring it home from the market
The night before so it is clean and ready in the morning
Only after you peel it, to remove any leftover juice
explanation: Washing fruit just before eating it prevents early spoilage, because wet fruit stored in a refrigerator or basket rots faster.

q: How does the Asian koel avoid raising its own chicks?
options: It lays its eggs in a crow's nest so the crows will raise them
It hides its eggs under leaves and returns only to feed the chicks
It builds a nest near a crow family and lets them adopt the eggs
It lays eggs only in winter when predators are asleep
explanation: The Asian koel lays its eggs in a crow's nest so that the crows will unknowingly raise its chicks.

q: In Newton's formula F = ma, what does the letter 'm' stand for?
options: Mass
Motion
Momentum
Magnitude
explanation: In F = ma, the letter m stands for mass.

q: How can young grouper fish look different from adult groupers?
options: They may have a different color or pattern than the adults
They are always smaller versions that look exactly like the adults
They are transparent and only gain color after one year
They are born with spots that fade completely as they grow
explanation: Young groupers sometimes have a different color or pattern than adult groupers, which can make them hard to recognize as the same species.

q: What is the regional center of the Davao Region (Region XI)?
options: Davao City
General Santos City
Cotabato City
Cagayan de Oro City
explanation: The regional center of Region XI (Davao Region) is Davao City.

q: About how much does a newborn giant panda weigh?
options: About 100 grams — roughly the size of a stick of butter
About 1 kilogram — roughly the size of a large mango
About 5 kilograms — about the same as a newborn human
About 500 grams — about the size of a large apple
explanation: A newborn giant panda weighs only about 100 grams, which is roughly the size of a stick of butter.

q: About how many eggs can a queen honeybee lay in a single day?
options: Up to about 2,000 eggs
Up to about 200 eggs
Up to about 20,000 eggs
Up to about 500 eggs
explanation: A queen honeybee can lay up to about 2,000 eggs in a single day.

q: How do theatre stagehands raise and lower heavy scenery quickly and safely during a performance?
options: Using pulleys and counterweights in a fly rig system
Using electric motors attached directly to each piece of scenery
Using ramps and wheels on the stage floor to slide pieces up
Using teams of workers who lift by hand on a signal
explanation: Pulleys and counterweights in theatre stage fly rigs allow stagehands to raise and lower heavy scenery quickly and safely.

q: What is pollination?
options: The moving of pollen from the stamen to the pistil, which is the first step in making seeds
The process of a seed absorbing water and beginning to sprout
The release of pollen into the air so insects can breathe it
The growth of new roots after a flower falls to the ground
explanation: Pollination is the transfer of pollen from the stamen to the pistil, and it is the first step in making seeds.

q: After the lungs take in oxygen, how does oxygen reach the rest of the body?
options: The blood carries oxygen and the heart pumps it to the whole body
The lungs push oxygen directly into each organ through air tubes
Oxygen travels through the bones until it reaches every part of the body
The stomach absorbs oxygen from the lungs and distributes it through digestion
explanation: Oxygen from the lungs is carried by the blood and sent by the heart to every part of the body.

q: What is the difference between riverine flooding and coastal flooding?
options: Riverine flooding comes from rivers overflowing while coastal flooding comes from a typhoon's storm surge
Riverine flooding is less dangerous because rivers are smaller than the sea
Coastal flooding only happens far from the shore where storm rain collects
Riverine flooding is caused by heavy rain only, while coastal flooding is caused by earthquakes
explanation: Riverine flooding is caused by river overflow while coastal flooding comes from a typhoon's storm surge, and both can happen at the same time.

q: What is the regional center of the Negros Island Region (NIR)?
options: Bacolod
Dumaguete
Siquijor
Cebu City
explanation: The regional center of the Negros Island Region (NIR) is Bacolod City.

q: What kind of beak does a heron use to catch fish?
options: A long, sharp beak for spearing or grabbing fish
A wide, flat beak for scooping fish from the surface
A hooked beak for tearing fish apart
A short, stubby beak for crushing shells
explanation: Herons have long, sharp beaks designed for spearing or catching fish in the water.

q: What can a dragonfly do that most other insects cannot?
options: Stay in one spot in the air like a hovering helicopter
Fly backward for long distances to escape predators
Breathe underwater and fly without stopping for days
Jump more than ten times its own body length
explanation: A dragonfly can hover in place in the air like a helicopter, which most other insects are unable to do.

q: Why do many soils and natural earth pigments have red and brown colors?
options: The mineral iron in soil oxidizes like rust, giving those red and brown shades
Red soil contains crushed volcanic rock that bleeds its color into the ground
Clay minerals absorb sunlight and turn red when exposed to heat
Roots of trees release red pigments into the soil as they grow
explanation: Iron in soil oxidizes the same way rust forms on metal, which is what gives many soils and natural pigments their red and brown colors.

q: What are muscles made of, and how do they create movement?
options: Many thin fibers that shorten together to make a pull
Solid blocks of tissue that push bones apart when they expand
A network of tubes filled with fluid that squeezes to create force
Layers of fat and cartilage that contract when nerves fire
explanation: Each muscle is made of many thin fibers that shorten together to create the pulling force that moves the body.

q: What does the prairie dog 'jump-yip' usually signal to the rest of the group?
options: That the danger has passed and all is safe
That a predator is approaching and everyone should hide
That it is time to find food and leave the burrow
That a rival group is nearby and a fight may start
explanation: When prairie dogs do a jump-yip wave — stretching up and throwing their front paws up — it usually signals that the danger is over and the group is safe.

q: How does a power strip with a switch help save electricity?
options: It lets you turn off many devices at once so they do not waste standby power
It lowers the voltage going to each device so they use less energy
It stores extra electricity so you need fewer battery replacements
It automatically disconnects the internet to reduce energy use
explanation: A switched power strip lets you cut power to many devices at once, preventing them from drawing standby electricity when not in use.

q: What instrument is used to show the direction the wind is blowing?
options: A wind vane
An anemometer
A barometer
A hygrometer
explanation: Wind direction is measured by an instrument called a wind vane.

q: What is true about the dengue vaccine?
options: It exists, but whether to use it depends on a person's age and whether they have had dengue before
It does not exist yet because the dengue virus changes too fast
It is given to every child automatically as part of the standard vaccine schedule
It works the same for everyone and has no age or history restrictions
explanation: A dengue vaccine does exist, but its use depends on a person's age and prior dengue infection history.

q: How is a cacao pod different from a coffee cherry?
options: A cacao pod is large with many seeds inside, while a coffee cherry is small with only one or two seeds
A cacao pod grows underground while coffee cherries grow on tall trees
A cacao pod has a soft outer skin and a coffee cherry has a hard shell
Both are the same size but cacao seeds are sweeter than coffee seeds
explanation: A cacao pod is large and contains many seeds, while a coffee cherry is small and usually holds only one or two seeds.

q: What happens to Pacific Ocean winds during El Nino that causes warm water to build up?
options: The winds that normally blow westward weaken, so warm surface water piles up in the central and eastern Pacific
The winds reverse direction and blow cold water from Antarctica toward the equator
Strong winds trap warm water near Asia and prevent it from moving eastward
El Nino has nothing to do with wind; it is caused by underwater volcanoes heating the ocean
explanation: During El Nino, the westward winds across the Pacific weaken, allowing warm surface water to accumulate in the central and eastern parts of the ocean.

q: What is the range of the Mohs hardness scale for minerals?
options: From 1 (softest) to 10 (hardest)
From 0 (softest) to 100 (hardest)
From 1 (softest) to 5 (hardest)
From 10 (softest) to 100 (hardest)
explanation: The Mohs scale measures mineral hardness from 1, which is the softest, to 10, which is the hardest.

q: Why might you find seashell fossils on top of a mountain?
options: That land was once under the sea and was pushed up over millions of years
Sea birds carried shells there and they became buried in the rock
Ancient floods were so powerful they washed ocean shells to mountain peaks
Underwater volcanoes built the mountain from the seafloor and shells stuck to it
explanation: Seashell fossils are sometimes found on mountaintops because that land was once below the sea and was later lifted up by geological forces.

q: Why does an air conditioner drip water?
options: Moisture in the air condenses on the unit's cold coils and drips out
The refrigerant fluid inside the unit slowly leaks out as liquid water
The fan blows water vapor out before it can evaporate back into the room
Ice builds up inside and melts, dripping through the front vents
explanation: An air conditioner drips water because the moisture in the warm indoor air condenses when it touches the unit's cold coils.

q: What kind of change happens when leche flan is cooked?
options: An irreversible change — the runny egg-and-milk mix becomes a firm solid that cannot go back to liquid
A reversible change — the solid custard will melt back into liquid if left at room temperature
A physical change only — heating just separates the egg from the milk
No real change — the mixture stays liquid but becomes thicker like a shake
explanation: In leche flan, heating causes the runny egg-and-milk mixture to permanently firm up into a solid custard — a change that cannot be undone.

q: Why do some young skinks have a bright blue tail?
options: To attract a mate during breeding season
To draw enemies to attack the tail instead of the head
To warn predators that the skink is poisonous
To help camouflage the skink on blue rocks
explanation: The bright or blue tail catches an enemy's eye so it attacks the tail instead of the head, giving the skink a better chance to escape.

q: What do cells need to stay alive and do their work?
options: Food, water, and sunlight
Food, water, and oxygen
Minerals, water, and carbon dioxide
Vitamins, oxygen, and glucose only
explanation: Cells need food, water, and oxygen to stay alive and carry out their functions.

q: What does stretching do for our bodies?
options: It makes our bones longer and stronger
It makes our muscles and joints more flexible
It increases the amount of blood in our body
It speeds up our heartbeat so we get more energy
explanation: Stretching makes our muscles and joints more flexible, which helps the body move more easily.

q: Why does stirring help sugar dissolve faster in water?
options: Stirring heats up the water so sugar melts more quickly
Stirring breaks the sugar crystals into smaller pieces
Stirring brings fresh water particles into contact with the sugar
Stirring removes the air that was blocking the sugar from dissolving
explanation: Stirring speeds up dissolving because it constantly brings fresh solvent particles into contact with the undissolved solute.

q: What can chromatography do that an ordinary filter CANNOT?
options: Separate large particles like sand from water
Remove bad smells from a liquid mixture
Separate substances that are already dissolved and invisible, like colors in ink
Filter out bacteria from drinking water
explanation: Unlike a filter that only removes big bits, chromatography can separate dissolved substances — such as the different colors blended inside ink — that pass straight through a filter.

q: What is the correct order of a rice plant's life cycle?
options: Grain → seedling → seed → tall grassy plant
Seedling → grain → tall grassy plant → seed
Seed → seedling → tall grassy plant → grain
Tall grassy plant → seedling → grain → seed
explanation: A rice plant grows from a seed into a seedling, matures into a tall grassy plant, and then produces grains that become the rice we eat.

q: Roughly how much can a blue whale's tongue weigh?
options: About the same as a large dog, around 50 kilograms
About the same as a small car, around 1,000 kilograms
About the same as a whole elephant, around 2,700 kilograms
About the same as a school bus, around 10,000 kilograms
explanation: A blue whale's tongue can weigh about 2,700 kilograms — as much as a whole elephant.

q: Why does a power grid need backup sources or battery storage when using wind turbines?
options: Wind turbines produce too much electricity and can overload the grid
Wind power is intermittent — turbines stop generating when the wind is calm
Wind turbines only work at night, leaving gaps during the day
Wind turbines produce electricity in surges that damage appliances
explanation: Wind power is intermittent, so when the wind stops, turbines generate no electricity and the grid needs backups to keep the supply continuous.

q: Why do you need a little extra force to push something up a real ramp compared with a perfect, frictionless ramp?
options: Because gravity is stronger at the bottom of a ramp
Because friction between the object and ramp surface resists motion
Because the ramp gets steeper the higher you go
Because the object gains weight as it moves upward
explanation: On a real ramp, friction acts against the direction of motion, so you need slightly more force than you would on a perfect frictionless ramp.

q: What is a petri dish used for in a science laboratory?
options: Measuring the volume of liquids precisely
Growing bacteria and microbes so they can be studied
Heating chemicals to very high temperatures
Separating mixtures using gravity
explanation: A petri dish is a shallow container used by scientists to grow bacteria and microbes for study.

q: What tiny animals build coral reefs?
options: Small shrimp called krill
Tiny animals called coral polyps
Microscopic plankton
Young sea anemones
explanation: Coral reefs are built by tiny animals called coral polyps, and the Philippines has some of the richest reefs in the world.

q: Why is steel chosen over plain iron for building bridges and railways?
options: Steel is lighter than iron, so structures weigh less
Steel is much stronger than plain iron
Steel does not rust at all, unlike iron
Steel is cheaper to mine than iron ore
explanation: Steel is much stronger than plain iron, which is why it is used for buildings, bridges, and railways.

q: How does the brain help us speak clearly?
options: It stores words in memory so we remember what to say
It sends signals to the muscles of the larynx and tongue
It produces saliva that keeps the throat moist while speaking
It controls the lungs so we breathe in enough air first
explanation: The brain sends signals to the muscles of the larynx and tongue, allowing us to speak clearly.

q: What does a newly hatched common cuckoo chick do right after it hatches?
options: It calls loudly to attract its cuckoo parents to feed it
It pushes the other eggs out of the nest so only it gets fed
It builds a wall of sticks to protect itself from the other chicks
It pretends to be sick so the host birds give it extra food
explanation: The common cuckoo chick pushes the other eggs out of the nest so it is the only one left for the host birds to feed.

q: What are the names of Mars's two moons?
options: Titan and Ganymede
Phobos and Deimos
Io and Europa
Miranda and Ariel
explanation: Mars has two moons named Phobos and Deimos.

q: How do eyeglasses help a person see clearly?
options: They make the pupil larger so more light enters the eye
They bend light ahead of time so it lands right on the retina
They strengthen the eye muscles so the lens focuses better
They filter out harmful light wavelengths that blur vision
explanation: Eyeglasses bend incoming light so that it focuses precisely on the retina, making vision clear.

q: About how long does one year on Venus last?
options: About 88 Earth days
About 225 Earth days
About 365 Earth days
About 687 Earth days
explanation: One year on Venus — the time it takes to orbit the Sun — lasts about 225 Earth days.

q: Why is it better to chew your food slowly?
options: Slow chewing keeps the food warm so the stomach can digest it better
Slow chewing gives saliva more time to mix with starch and start digestion
Slow chewing uses more jaw muscles, which strengthens them over time
Slow chewing prevents air bubbles from forming in the stomach
explanation: When you chew slowly, saliva has more time to mix with starch and begin digestion before food reaches the stomach.

q: What color and texture is the liver?
options: Pale pink and firm like a muscle
Reddish-brown and soft and rubbery
Dark purple and hard like a bone
Bright red and spongy like a lung
explanation: The liver is reddish-brown in color and feels soft and rubbery to the touch.

q: Which star is the closest to our Sun?
options: Sirius
Betelgeuse
Proxima Centauri
Alpha Centauri A
explanation: The nearest star to our Sun (other than the Sun itself) is Proxima Centauri.

q: What happens to fine soil particles that are carried by the wind?
options: They dissolve into the air and disappear permanently
They drop and pile up when the wind slows or stops, sometimes hundreds of kilometers away
They rise higher until they form clouds and fall as rain
They are carried back to where they started once the wind reverses
explanation: When the wind slows or stops, the particles it carries drop and pile up, and fine dust can travel hundreds of kilometers before building up rich soil in a faraway place.

q: How do hawks, kites, and other birds of prey help keep nature in balance?
options: They eat insects that spread plant diseases across forests
They control the numbers of rats and other small animals
They carry seeds to new areas and help forests grow
They clean up dead animals before bacteria can spread disease
explanation: Raptors such as hawks and kites help balance ecosystems by controlling populations of rats and other small animals.

q: How many islands make up the Philippine archipelago?
options: About 1,700 islands in two island groups
About 3,500 islands in two island groups
About 7,641 islands in three island groups
About 10,000 islands in four island groups
explanation: The Philippines is an archipelago with about 7,641 islands grouped into three island groups.

q: How do bats find their way and hunt in the dark using echolocation?
options: They sense heat given off by prey using special cells in their nose
They make high-pitched sounds and listen for the echoes that bounce back
They use their large eyes to see in very dim light like cats do
They follow scent trails left by insects on leaves and branches
explanation: Bats make high-pitched sounds and listen for the echoes that bounce back, letting them detect their path and food even in total darkness.

q: How is sap like rubber collected from a tree without killing it?
options: The whole trunk is soaked in water so sap floats to the top
A small cut is made through the bark so the liquid drips out carefully
The roots are squeezed using a press to push sap upward
The leaves are boiled and the sap condenses back as a liquid
explanation: A small cut is made through the bark so the sap drips out; this is done carefully so the tree does not die.

q: Why must pitcher plants not be taken from the wild?
options: Their liquid inside is toxic and could harm people who touch them
Some species are endangered and are protected by law
They spread quickly and would become invasive garden pests
They only survive in greenhouses and die immediately outside
explanation: Some pitcher plant species are endangered, so they are legally protected and must not be removed from the wild.

q: How many basic states of matter are there, and what are they?
options: Two: solid and liquid
Three: solid, liquid, and gas
Four: solid, liquid, gas, and plasma
Five: solid, liquid, gas, plasma, and ice
explanation: There are three basic states of matter: solid, liquid, and gas.

q: What is the chemical symbol for the metal lead?
options: Le
Ld
Pb
Pl
explanation: The chemical symbol for lead is Pb, which comes from the Latin word 'plumbum'.

q: What is a brood parasite?
options: A bird that steals food from other birds' nests to feed its own chicks
A bird that tricks other birds into raising its young instead of building its own nest
A bird that chases away other species to take over their nesting spot
A bird whose chicks kill the chicks of the host bird right after hatching
explanation: A brood parasite is a bird that does not build its own nest but tricks other birds into raising its young.

q: Why do ants walk in a line one after another when heading to food?
options: The first ant is the leader and the others are trained to follow it
A worker ant that finds food leaves a special scent on the path that other ants follow
Ants hold each other with their legs to form a chain when traveling
The queen ant sends a sound signal that guides workers in a straight line
explanation: When a worker ant finds food, it leaves a special scent trail, and other ants follow that scent — which is why they walk in a neat line.

q: Why do most earthquakes go unnoticed by people?
options: Most earthquakes happen deep in the ocean far from land
Most earthquakes are very small — around magnitude 2 or less — so people cannot feel them
Most earthquakes only last a fraction of a second, too brief to notice
Most earthquakes occur at night when people are asleep
explanation: Most earthquakes measure around magnitude 2 or less, which is too small for people to feel, though a seismograph can still detect them.

q: How can worn-out stainless steel pots and cutlery help the environment?
options: They can be ground into powder and used as a natural fertilizer
They can be melted down and made into something new, so the metal is not wasted
They can be dissolved in acid to recover rare earth minerals inside
They can be buried in the soil where they slowly break down and add nutrients
explanation: Stainless steel can be melted down and recycled into new products, so the metal is not wasted and the environment benefits.

q: What have scientists recently discovered in the forests of the Philippines?
options: New kinds of pitcher plants that can trap small frogs
New kinds of cloud rats that were previously unknown to science
New coral reef species beneath the deep waters off Palawan
New bird species related to the Philippine eagle
explanation: Scientists have recently discovered new species of cloud rats living in the forests of the Philippines.

q: How did most of the Philippine islands form?
options: Glaciers carved out valleys and the sea filled them, creating islands
