explanation: Geckos do not use suction or glue; they hold on with millions of tiny foot hairs, which is why they can even stick in a vacuum with no air.

q: What is the job of a transformer in an electrical system?
options: It stores electrical energy so homes can use it during power cuts
It converts electrical energy into heat for use in factories
It changes the voltage of electricity — raising it for long-distance travel and lowering it before it reaches homes
It measures how much electricity a home uses and sends the data to the power company
explanation: A transformer changes the voltage of electricity — raising it for long travel and lowering it before it reaches homes.

q: What does the term 'light-year' measure?
options: The number of years it takes for a star to complete one orbit around a galaxy
The amount of light that the sun produces in one year
The distance that light travels in one year, about 9.46 trillion kilometres
The time it takes for light from the sun to reach Earth
explanation: A light-year is the distance light travels in one year — about 9.46 trillion kilometres — used to measure vast distances in space.

q: Why do most places on Earth experience two high tides each day?
options: The sun heats opposite sides of Earth at different times, causing two water swells
The Earth spins so fast that water is pushed outward on two sides at once
There are two water bulges at the same time — one facing the moon and one on the opposite side of Earth
The moon orbits Earth twice every day, pulling water toward it each time
explanation: There are two water bulges at the same time — one on the side facing the moon and one on the opposite side — giving most places two high tides a day.

q: How does a jet engine push an airplane forward?
options: It spins large propellers at the front that pull the plane through the air
It creates a magnetic field that repels against the air to move forward
It sucks in air at the front, burns it with fuel, and blasts hot gas out the back to push the plane forward
It heats the air under the wings to make the plane lighter and let it glide forward
explanation: A jet engine sucks in air at the front, mixes it with fuel and burns it, then blasts the hot gas out the back — and that backward blast pushes the plane forward.

q: How does the queen bee make sure she is the only one laying eggs in the hive?
options: She physically stops worker bees from entering the egg-laying chamber
She lays eggs so quickly that workers have no time or space to lay their own
She releases a special pheromone that prevents worker bees from reproducing
She eats any eggs laid by worker bees before they can hatch
explanation: The queen bee releases a special pheromone that prevents worker bees from reproducing, ensuring she is the only one to lay eggs.

q: Besides making insulin, what other important job does the pancreas do?
options: It filters waste from the blood and turns it into urine
It pumps bile into the stomach to break down fats directly
It makes enzymes that help digest food in the intestines
It stores extra sugar in the form of glycogen for later use
explanation: Besides making insulin, the pancreas also makes enzymes that help digest food in the intestines, so it does double duty.

q: In which region of the Philippines is the province of Guimaras located, and what is its capital?
options: Eastern Visayas region; capital is Tacloban
Central Visayas region; capital is Cebu City
Western Visayas region; capital is Jordan
MIMAROPA region; capital is San Jose
explanation: Guimaras is a province in the Western Visayas region (VI) of the Philippines, and its capital is Jordan.

q: Where does the Philippine flat-headed frog live, and why does it need that particular environment?
options: It lives in warm, still ponds in Luzon where algae provides plenty of food
It lives in dry rocky areas of Mindanao where it can absorb heat from the sun
It lives in cold, fast-flowing streams in Palawan where there is enough dissolved oxygen for skin-breathing
It lives in mangrove swamps along the coast where it can hide from predators in the roots
explanation: The Philippine flat-headed frog lives in cold, fast-flowing streams in Palawan, where the water contains enough dissolved oxygen for skin-breathing.

q: When you jump off the ground, which statement best describes the action-reaction pair?
options: You push up against gravity and gravity pulls you back down with equal force
Your legs push down on the ground, and the ground pushes you upward with an equal force
The air around you pushes up against your body as you rise into the air
Your muscles pull your bones upward while your weight pulls you downward
explanation: Jumping is an action-reaction pair: you push down on the ground and it sends you up with an equal and opposite force.

q: What is at the North Pole?
options: A large continent covered by a thick ice sheet, similar to Antarctica
A small rocky island surrounded by permanently frozen sea ice
No land at all — only a frozen ocean called the Arctic Ocean
A vast flat tundra plain with no trees or mountains
explanation: At the North Pole there is no land, only a frozen ocean called the Arctic Ocean.

q: What is the 'period' of a pendulum?
options: The maximum distance the pendulum swings away from the center
The total number of swings the pendulum completes in one minute
The time it takes for the pendulum to make one complete swing back to where it started
The speed at which the pendulum is moving at the lowest point of its swing
explanation: The period is the time a pendulum takes to make one complete swing back to where it started.

q: What color are emu eggs?
options: Bright blue, similar to the eggs of a robin
Pale cream with brown speckles, similar to turkey eggs
Dark green, unlike the usual white eggs of a chicken
Yellowish-orange with a rough bumpy shell
explanation: Emu eggs are dark green in color, unlike the usual white chicken eggs.

q: What happens to the temperature of a substance while it is melting, even though heat keeps being added?
options: The temperature rises steadily as more heat is added to the substance
The temperature drops slightly because energy is used to break the bonds
The temperature stays constant; the heat being absorbed is called latent heat
The temperature jumps up and down rapidly as parts of the substance melt
explanation: While a substance melts, its temperature stays constant even though it keeps absorbing heat — this absorbed heat is called latent heat and is used to change the state.

q: What does chromatography show when it is used on black ink?
options: That black ink is a pure substance with one single colour component
That black ink only contains carbon particles suspended in water
That black ink is actually a mixture of different colours that separate as water moves up the paper
That black ink becomes clear when it is spread out thinly on paper
explanation: As water moves up the paper in chromatography, the different colour components in black ink travel at different speeds and separate into different colours.

q: What are the tiny light organs on a firefly squid called, and where are they especially found?
options: Bioluminosomes, found mainly along the squid's body sides
Luminocytes, found only on the squid's large central eye
Photophores, found especially on the tips of the squid's arms
Chromatophores, found all over the squid's mantle and head
explanation: The firefly squid has many tiny light organs called photophores, especially on the tips of its arms.

q: What should you do if a grease fire starts in your kitchen?
options: Pour water on it to cool it down
Cover it to cut off its oxygen supply
Blow on it to extinguish the flames
Throw flour over the pan to smother it
explanation: Oil floats on water, so pouring water on a grease fire makes it spread; covering the fire removes the oxygen it needs to burn.

q: Why does a spinning top have a small, pointed tip instead of a wide, flat one?
options: A wide tip would make the top too heavy to spin
A pointed tip makes less contact with the ground, reducing friction
A pointed tip keeps the center of gravity very high
A wide tip would cause the top to bounce off the ground
explanation: The pointed tip creates less contact with the ground, which means less friction, so the top can spin for a longer time.

q: The Surigao Strait connects which two bodies of water?
options: The Sibuyan Sea and Leyte Gulf
The Mindanao Sea and Leyte Gulf
The Visayan Sea and the Pacific Ocean
The Celebes Sea and Camotes Sea
explanation: The Surigao Strait lies between Leyte and Mindanao and connects the Mindanao Sea to Leyte Gulf.

q: What was Charles Darwin's nationality?
options: French
German
American
English
explanation: Charles Darwin was an English naturalist, famous for developing the theory of evolution by natural selection.

q: Why are visitors told NOT to touch stalactites and stalagmites in caves?
options: The formations are sharp and can cut your hand easily
Oil and dirt from your hands can stop new minerals from sticking, halting their growth
The vibrations from touching can cause the cave ceiling to collapse
The minerals in the formations are poisonous to humans
explanation: The oil and dirt from our hands block new mineral deposits from sticking, which stops the growth of cave formations that took thousands of years to form.

q: Which pair of rocks are both examples of metamorphic rock?
options: Granite and basalt
Limestone and shale
Marble and slate
Sandstone and pumice
explanation: Marble is metamorphic rock formed from limestone, and slate is metamorphic rock formed from shale.

q: Why is the hole in the ozone layer slowly healing?
options: Global temperatures have dropped, allowing the ozone to re-form
Chemicals called CFCs that damaged the ozone layer have been banned
Scientists have been releasing repair chemicals into the atmosphere
Increased rainfall has been washing away the harmful pollutants
explanation: After CFCs — the chemicals that created the ozone hole — were banned, the hole has been slowly healing on its own.

q: How long does an open Rafflesia flower last before it wilts?
options: Several weeks
About one year
Only a few days
A full month
explanation: Even though its bud takes a very long time to grow, an open Rafflesia flower lasts only a few days before it turns black and wilts.

q: An animal that eats BOTH plants and meat is called a what?
options: Herbivore
Carnivore
Omnivore
Scavenger
explanation: Consumers are grouped into three by diet: herbivores eat only plants, carnivores eat only meat, and omnivores eat both plants and meat.

q: Where do butterfly wing colors come from?
options: From the blood showing through the thin wings
From thousands of tiny scales containing pigment or light-reflecting structures
From special ink cells just under the wing surface
From the color of the flowers the caterpillar ate
explanation: Butterfly wing colors come from thousands of tiny scales — some colors are from pigment while others result from how light bounces off the scale structure.

q: Why do electricians wear rubber gloves when working with live wires?
options: Rubber keeps their hands warm and prevents sweating
Rubber is an insulator that blocks electricity from flowing through them
Rubber is the only material strong enough to grip slippery wires
Rubber prevents sparks from igniting the surrounding air
explanation: Rubber is an electrical insulator, meaning it blocks the flow of electricity and protects electricians from being shocked.

q: How do rangers track the tamaraw since it is so hard to spot directly?
options: They use drones with cameras to search large areas of forest
They look for signs like footprints, droppings, and grazed grass
They set up cage traps with food bait near water sources
They follow the sounds of its calls at dawn and dusk
explanation: Because the tamaraw is elusive and solitary, rangers track it using indirect signs like footprints, droppings, and grazed grass rather than seeing the animal itself.

q: What effect does cigarette smoke have on the lungs?
options: It strengthens lung tissue by increasing blood flow
It damages the lungs and makes breathing harder
It has no lasting effect if a person only smokes occasionally
It only affects the throat, not the lungs themselves
explanation: Cigarette smoke damages the lungs and makes breathing harder over time.

q: How do baby swiftlets learn to navigate inside dark caves?
options: They are born with fully working echolocation, just like adults
They follow older birds using their eyesight until their night vision develops
They learn to make clicks and understand the returning echoes as they grow
They rely on air currents and never actually use sound to navigate
explanation: Baby swiftlets cannot echolocate right after hatching; they learn to make clicks and understand the returning echoes as they grow older.

q: What happens to a magnet if it gets extremely hot?
options: It becomes even stronger because heat energizes the magnetic particles
Its magnetism fades because the aligned particles inside get jumbled up
It reverses its poles so north becomes south and south becomes north
It stays equally strong but transfers its magnetism to nearby metal objects
explanation: When a magnet gets extremely hot, the tiny aligned particles inside get jumbled, so they no longer point together and the magnetism fades.

q: Why does cutting your hair or trimming your nails not hurt?
options: Your brain ignores pain signals from hair and nails
The parts you cut are dead and have no nerves that feel pain
Hair and nails are protected by a special layer that blocks pain
Pain signals from these areas travel too slowly to reach the brain
explanation: Hair and nails do not hurt when cut because the parts being cut are dead cells with no nerves; it only hurts if you cut so short that you reach the living tissue underneath.

q: Can lightning strike the same place more than once?
options: No, because lightning always seeks a new path each time
No, because the first strike removes all electrical charge from that spot
Yes, especially tall buildings are struck many times
Yes, but only during the same storm, not in separate storms
explanation: Lightning can and does strike the same place many times, especially tall buildings which are more likely to be hit repeatedly.

q: Why is photosynthesis described as endothermic?
options: Because it releases heat energy into the surrounding air
Because it produces carbon dioxide as a waste product
Because plants absorb energy from sunlight to drive the reaction
Because it only happens when temperatures are extremely high
explanation: Photosynthesis is endothermic because plants absorb energy from sunlight to power the process rather than releasing energy.

q: How many astronauts flew on the Apollo 11 mission?
explanation: Apollo 11 had 3 astronauts: Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin, and Michael Collins.

q: How many oceans does Earth have?
explanation: Earth has 5 oceans: the Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern, and Arctic oceans.

q: What food substance is stored inside a plant bulb?
options: Mostly protein and fat from decomposed soil
Mostly sugar and starch made by the leaves from sunlight
Mostly vitamins absorbed directly from rainwater
Mostly minerals drawn up from deep underground
explanation: The food stored in a bulb is mostly sugar and starch that the plant's leaves produced using sunlight through photosynthesis.

q: In natural selection, what happens to a helpful inherited trait over many generations?
options: It disappears because other animals copy the better trait
The proportion of individuals with that trait increases over the generations
It stays at the same level because the environment does not change
It spreads only within one family, not across the whole population
explanation: In natural selection, individuals with advantageous inherited traits are more likely to survive and reproduce, so the proportion of individuals with those traits increases over generations.

q: What does the commutator in a DC motor do?
options: It stores electrical energy to keep the motor running when power is cut
It switches the current direction so the coil keeps spinning the same way
It reduces the voltage to protect the motor from overheating
It amplifies the current to make the motor spin faster
explanation: The commutator switches the direction of the current so that the coil always turns in the same direction, which keeps the motor spinning continuously.

q: When can you most often see frogs jumping in Philippine rice fields and streams?
options: During the hot dry season when frogs look for water
During the rainy season when they are most active
Only at night because frogs cannot stand sunlight
Only in summer because that is when their eggs hatch
explanation: In the Philippines, frogs are most commonly seen jumping in rice fields, canals, and small streams especially during the rainy season.

q: What fish is popularly called the national fish of the Philippines?
options: Tilapia
Galunggong (round scad)
Bangus (milkfish)
Lapu-lapu (grouper)
explanation: The bangus, or milkfish, is popularly called the national fish of the Philippines, though no law officially declares it so.

q: Which cell organelle is often compared to a post office because it packages and ships proteins?
options: The mitochondria
The nucleus
The Golgi apparatus
The vacuole
explanation: The Golgi apparatus is like the cell's post office because it packages, modifies, and ships proteins to the right destinations.

q: What does it mean when an animal is described as nocturnal?
options: It lives in the ocean and comes to shore only to rest
It migrates to warmer places when the weather turns cold
It is active at night and sleeps during the day
It can see in both bright sunlight and complete darkness equally well
explanation: Nocturnal animals are active at night and sleep during the day, which is the opposite of diurnal animals.

q: What process makes the Sun shine?
options: The Sun burns oxygen just like a giant campfire
The Sun uses hydrogen as fuel through fusion in its core
The Sun reflects light from distant stars and concentrates it
The Sun converts carbon dioxide into light energy through a chemical reaction
explanation: The Sun shines by using hydrogen as fuel through nuclear fusion happening in its core.

q: What is the difference between mutualism and commensalism?
options: In mutualism one organism is harmed; in commensalism both are harmed
In mutualism both organisms benefit; in commensalism only one benefits while the other is unharmed
In mutualism one feeds on the other; in commensalism they simply live near each other
In mutualism the animals are the same species; in commensalism they are different species
explanation: In mutualism both animals benefit from the partnership, while in commensalism only one organism benefits and the other is neither helped nor harmed.

q: What causes the bottom of a lake or pond to crack during a long drought?
options: Earthquakes open up fissures in the rock beneath the lake
The mud at the bottom is exposed and dries out when the water drops a lot
Strong winds blow the top layer of soil away, revealing cracks below
The heat from the sun melts the minerals in the soil causing it to split
explanation: When a lake or pond dries up during a long drought, the exposed mud at the bottom dries out and cracks — a clear sign the water level has dropped significantly.

q: How can you get salt back from a cup of salty water?
options: By filtering the water through a cloth to catch the salt
By freezing the water so the salt separates out as ice melts
By letting the water evaporate so the salt crystals are left behind
By boiling the water quickly so the salt rises to the surface
explanation: When salty water is left to evaporate, the water turns to vapor and leaves the salt crystals behind in the container.

q: Why does a bird sitting on a single power line not get an electric shock?
options: Bird feathers are perfect insulators that block all electricity
The power line only carries very low voltage that is harmless to small animals
The bird is not touching anything else, so there is no complete path for electricity to flow
Birds have special organs in their feet that absorb and neutralize electric current
explanation: For electricity to flow through the bird, it needs a complete path to the ground or another wire; since the bird touches only one wire and nothing else, no electricity flows through its body.

q: Why do Philippine coral reefs support so much marine life?
options: The deep, cold water around reefs is rich in dissolved oxygen for fish
Coral skeletons provide hiding places that prevent any predation
Corals hold tiny algae inside them that make food by photosynthesis, fueling the whole reef ecosystem
The strong ocean currents carry large amounts of dead fish that reef animals feed on
explanation: Corals host tiny algae inside them that produce food through photosynthesis, which is why coral reefs teem with so much life.

q: What causes an allergic reaction like itching or swelling?
options: The body runs out of the vitamins it needs to fight off foreign substances
Harmful bacteria enter through the skin and trigger a defensive attack
The immune system overreacts to a normally harmless substance like pollen or dust
Toxins from food destroy blood cells, causing the body to swell up
explanation: Allergies occur when the immune system overreacts to a normally harmless substance — such as pollen or dust — causing symptoms like itching and swelling.

q: What health risk increases when someone eats too many sweets and is overweight?
options: Getting Type 1 diabetes, which is caused by the pancreas shutting down
Getting Type 2 diabetes, which is linked to diet and body weight
Developing vitamin deficiencies because sugar blocks nutrient absorption
Experiencing heart attacks immediately because of sugar blocking the arteries
explanation: Eating too many sweets and being overweight raise the risk of developing Type 2 diabetes.

q: How many stages do bees and ants go through during their life cycle?
options: Two stages — egg and adult
Three stages — egg, nymph, and adult
Four stages — egg, larva, pupa, and adult
Five stages — egg, larva, nymph, pupa, and adult
explanation: Bees and ants go through complete metamorphosis with all four stages: egg, larva, pupa, and adult.

q: What is the minimum age required to become a Philippine senator?
options: 25 years old
30 years old
35 years old
40 years old
explanation: According to the Philippine constitution, a person must be at least 35 years old to become a senator.

q: Approximately how large is Manila Bay?
options: About 500 square kilometers
About 994 square kilometers
About 1,994 square kilometers
About 4,994 square kilometers
explanation: Manila Bay has an area of about 1,994 square kilometers, making it one of the finest natural harbors in the world.

q: How many kidneys does a healthy human body have?
explanation: A human normally has 2 kidneys, which filter waste products from the blood.

q: Why do some deep-sea animals produce their own light through bioluminescence?
options: To keep warm in the cold deep ocean water
To attract prey, find mates, or escape predators
To communicate with animals near the surface
To replace sunlight for the photosynthesis they perform
explanation: Deep-sea animals use bioluminescence — light produced by chemical reactions in their bodies — to attract prey, find mates, or escape predators.

q: Which animal holds the record as the fastest of all animals when it dives?
options: The cheetah, which can reach over 100 km/h on land
The sailfish, which can swim faster than 100 km/h in the ocean
The peregrine falcon, which dives at over 300 km/h
The swift, which can sustain the highest level flying speed
explanation: The peregrine falcon is the fastest animal of all when it dives through the air, reaching speeds over 300 km/h.

q: Which diseases can be carried and spread by the same Aedes aegypti mosquito?
options: Malaria, tuberculosis, and typhoid
Dengue, chikungunya, and Zika
Rabies, measles, and influenza
Cholera, hepatitis, and yellow fever
explanation: The Aedes aegypti mosquito is a shared vector for dengue, chikungunya, and Zika — all three diseases can be transmitted by the same mosquito.

q: Is vaping a safe alternative to cigarette smoking?
options: Yes, because vapes do not produce smoke, so they are completely harmless
Yes, because vape vapor contains no nicotine, unlike cigarettes
No, because vapes also contain nicotine that reduces lung health and is addictive
No, but only because the flavoring chemicals in vapes cause allergies
explanation: Vaping is not a safe swap for smoking because vapes also contain nicotine that reduces lung health and is addictive, just like cigarettes.

q: What country was the famous scientist Galileo Galilei from?
options: Spain
France
Greece
Italy
explanation: Galileo Galilei was from Italy, where he conducted his famous experiments on motion and astronomy.

q: Why is the sea breeze strongest in the afternoon rather than in the morning?
options: Morning winds blow in the opposite direction, canceling the sea breeze
The sea is coldest in the afternoon, making the temperature contrast bigger
The land has had all morning to heat up while the sea stays cool, making the temperature difference greatest in the afternoon
The sun is directly overhead at noon, which blocks the sea breeze until afternoon
explanation: The sea breeze is strongest in the afternoon because the land has had all morning to get very hot while the sea stayed cool, creating the greatest temperature difference and therefore the strongest airflow.

q: Why are LED lights used in traffic lights, flashlights, and phone screens?
options: LEDs produce more heat than other bulbs, keeping devices warm in cold weather
LEDs are the only light source bright enough to be seen from long distances
LEDs last many years and barely get warm, making them tough and energy-efficient
LEDs change color automatically, which is perfect for traffic light signals
explanation: LED lights are used in these applications because they last many years and barely get warm even when left on, making them tough and low-power.

q: How does Vitamin D help keep your bones strong?
options: It directly builds bone tissue by combining with proteins in the blood
It helps the body use calcium to build strong bones
It protects bones from breaking by making them more flexible
It signals the body to produce more red blood cells that deliver nutrients to bones
explanation: Vitamin D, which the body makes from sunlight, helps the body absorb and use calcium to build strong bones.

q: What happens to Earth's temperature when greenhouse gases in the atmosphere increase?
options: It stays the same because Earth automatically adjusts its orbit farther from the Sun
It drops because greenhouse gases reflect more sunlight back into space
The Earth must warm up before it can radiate enough heat back to space to balance again
It drops at first, then rises sharply, then returns to normal within a few years
explanation: When greenhouse gases increase, they trap more heat, so the Earth must warm up before it can radiate enough energy back to space to reach a new balance.

q: What condition can develop if the body does not get enough iodine?
options: Anemia, because iodine is needed to produce red blood cells
Scurvy, because iodine helps the body absorb vitamin C
Goiter, because the thyroid gland in the neck needs iodine to work properly
Rickets, because iodine helps the body use calcium for strong bones
explanation: Iodine is a mineral needed by the thyroid gland in the neck, and a lack of it can cause goiter — an enlargement of the thyroid gland.

q: What is the main crop grown in rice fields all across the Philippines?
options: Rice
Corn
Sugar cane
Coconut
explanation: Rice is the main crop of the Philippines and grows in rice fields throughout the archipelago because the country's land and rainfall are suitable for it.

q: Why might your arm feel sore or you get a slight fever after receiving a vaccine?
options: Your body's defenses are learning and working
The needle was too big for your arm
You caught a mild infection from the vaccine
The vaccine was stored at the wrong temperature
explanation: A sore arm or slight fever after a vaccine is normal — it is a sign that your body's defenses are learning and working.

q: What color is the skin of a typical eggplant fruit?
options: Purple
Green
Red
Yellow
explanation: The eggplant fruit usually has purple skin.

q: What special feature does a pangolin use to reach ants deep inside their nests?
options: A tongue that can be longer than its own body
Front claws that are longer than its tail
A snout shaped like a tube
A sticky saliva that glues ants to its nose
explanation: A pangolin's tongue can be even longer than its body, which lets it reach ants deep inside their nests.

q: How does a kingfisher catch fish?
options: It dives swiftly into the water using its sharp, pointed beak
It wades slowly in shallow water and grabs fish with its feet
It hovers above the water and scoops fish with its wings
It waits on the surface and filters fish through its bill
explanation: A kingfisher dives swiftly into the water to catch fish with its sharp, pointed beak.

q: What do ocean currents carry to distant parts of the sea?
options: Plankton, fish eggs and larvae, and other tiny animals
Only salt and minerals dissolved in the water
Sunlight and warmth from tropical regions
Large fish like sharks and whales
explanation: Currents carry plankton, fish eggs and larvae, and other tiny animals to distant parts of the sea.

q: What kind of water is found in a pond?
options: Freshwater
Saltwater
Brackish water
Distilled water
explanation: A pond is a freshwater habitat, so many kinds of plants and animals can live in it.

q: What triggers a mudflow or debris flow down a slope?
options: The ground becomes soaked with rain, making mud, rock, and branches rush downhill
Strong winds push loose soil over the edge of a cliff
An underground spring suddenly bursts through the hillside
Earthquakes crack the hillside and release trapped gas
explanation: A mudflow or debris flow is a fast rush of mud, rock, and branches down a slope when the ground is soaked with rain, and it can quickly destroy homes.

q: Where do decomposers get their food and energy?
options: From the dead matter they break down
From sunlight through photosynthesis
From eating living plants and animals
From absorbing minerals directly from the soil
explanation: Decomposers get their food and energy from the dead matter they break down.

q: What happens when water seeps into a rock crack and freezes?
options: It expands and slowly splits the rock apart
It shrinks and the crack seals itself shut
It dissolves minerals that cement the crack
It heats the rock from inside and melts it
explanation: When water seeps into a rock crack and freezes, it expands and slowly splits the rock apart — a process called freeze-thaw weathering.

q: Why does the ocean stay salty even though rain is fresh water?
options: During evaporation only water escapes as vapor, leaving the salt behind
Rain washes salt from the ocean before it falls back
Ocean animals produce salt faster than rain can dilute it
Salt enters clouds along with water vapor and falls back as sleet
explanation: During evaporation, only water escapes as vapor while salt remains behind, which is why the ocean stays salty while rain is fresh.

q: About how many days does it take for Earth to orbit the Sun once?
options: 365.25 days
300 days
400 days
180 days
explanation: Earth orbits the Sun in about 365.25 days, which is why one year is the full cycle of the seasons.

q: What happens to a lichen when it dries out completely?
options: It seems to sleep but revives when it gets wet again
It dies and cannot grow back
It produces spores and blows away in the wind
It turns brown and becomes a different organism
explanation: Without water a lichen dries out and seems to sleep, but it revives when it rains or gets wet.

q: How did dinosaurs reproduce?
options: They laid eggs, just like birds and reptiles do today
They gave birth to live young like most mammals
They kept eggs inside their bodies until they hatched
They released eggs into water like frogs
explanation: Dinosaurs laid eggs, just like birds and reptiles do today.

q: Where does a poso (hand pump) get its water from?
options: Underground, where rainwater that soaked into the ground is stored among rocks and sand
A large tank on the roof that collects rainwater
A nearby river or stream connected by pipes
A natural spring that flows from the side of a mountain
explanation: A poso draws water from underground, where rain that soaked down is stored among the rocks and sand below the soil.

q: Which of the following is one of the most commonly farmed fish in the Philippines?
options: Tilapia
Salmon
Tuna
Trout
explanation: Tilapia is one of the most common farmed fish in the Philippines.

q: Which country is the largest in the world by land area?
options: Russia
Canada
China
United States
explanation: Russia is the largest country in the world by land area, covering about 17 million square kilometers.

q: Why do dogs pant and stick out their tongues on a hot day?
options: They do not sweat much, so panting is how they cool down
They are trying to drink moisture from the air
Their tongues detect temperature changes in the environment
They are signaling to other dogs that they are friendly
explanation: Dogs do not sweat much, so they pant and stick out their tongues to cool their bodies down.

q: How are tiny phytoplankton in the ocean similar to plants on land?
options: They both take in carbon dioxide from the air
They both grow roots to absorb water from soil
They both produce seeds to reproduce
They both need soil minerals to survive
explanation: Tiny phytoplankton in the sea take in carbon dioxide just like plants on land do.

q: Approximately how old is the Earth?
options: 4.5 billion years
1 billion years
10 billion years
500 million years
explanation: Earth is about 4.5 billion years old.

q: Why can't we see stars during the day?
options: The Sun's light is so strong it drowns out the faint light of distant stars
The stars move to the other side of Earth during the day
The atmosphere blocks starlight but lets sunlight through
Stars turn off their light during daylight hours
explanation: Stars are still there during the day — we simply cannot see them because the Sun's light is so strong that it drowns out the faint light of distant stars.

q: Why does a burning candle produce black soot?
options: The candle wax does not burn completely because there is not enough oxygen
The candle wick releases carbon that mixes with hot air
The wax melts and reacts with water vapor in the air
The flame burns too hot and turns the wax directly into carbon
explanation: The black soot from a candle is carbon that forms when the candle wax does not burn completely because there is not enough oxygen.

q: What is the safest way to remove an appliance plug from an electrical outlet?
options: Pull the plug itself, not the cord
Pull the cord firmly and quickly
Use a dry cloth to grip the cord before pulling
Push the wall switch off, then yank the cord
explanation: You should pull the plug itself, not the cord — pulling the cord can damage the internal wires and make the appliance dangerous.

q: What was remarkable about the effect of the 1991 Pinatubo eruption?
options: It released so much ash and gas that it cooled the whole planet
It created a new island off the coast of Luzon
Its lava flow reached the sea and formed a new bay
It triggered a massive earthquake felt across Southeast Asia
explanation: The 1991 Pinatubo eruption released huge amounts of ash and gas that even cooled the whole planet.

q: What makes a flower a 'complete flower'?
options: It has all four parts: sepals, petals, stamen, and pistil
It has brightly colored petals that attract insects
It produces both pollen and nectar at the same time
It can reproduce without being pollinated by insects
explanation: A flower with all four parts — sepals, petals, stamen, and pistil — is called a complete flower; if even one part is missing, it is called an incomplete flower.

q: Why do banana leaves tear easily in the wind?
options: Tearing helps the plant avoid being blown over
The leaves are too thin and weak to survive tropical weather
Torn leaves allow more sunlight to reach the lower leaves
The tears help the plant release extra water during storms
explanation: The wide banana leaves tear easily in the wind, which actually helps the plant avoid being blown over.

q: Where do most turtles live?
options: In or near water, such as rivers, lakes, or the sea
In dry deserts where they dig underground burrows
In dense forests where they hide under fallen leaves
On rocky mountain slopes where they bask in the sun
explanation: Most turtles live in or near water, such as rivers, lakes, or the sea.

q: What mammal feature does the platypus have that keeps it warm in the water?
options: Thick fur, like other mammals
A layer of blubber under its skin
Waterproof scales along its back
A hollow tail that traps warm air
explanation: Like other mammals, the platypus has thick fur that keeps it warm and dry in the water.

q: How slowly do most hard corals grow?
options: Only 1 to 3 centimeters per year
About 1 meter per year
Around 10 centimeters per year
Roughly 30 centimeters per year
explanation: Most hard corals grow only 1 to 3 centimeters per year, so a large coral reef takes thousands of years to form.

q: Who discovered the double-helix shape of DNA in 1953?
options: James Watson and Francis Crick
Charles Darwin and Gregor Mendel
Louis Pasteur and Marie Curie
Isaac Newton and Albert Einstein
explanation: James Watson and Francis Crick discovered the shape of DNA, the double helix, in 1953.

q: How does a milkfish (bangus) breathe?
options: It uses its gills to take oxygen from the water
It surfaces regularly to breathe air through a blowhole
It absorbs oxygen through its skin
It has small lungs that work like a snorkel
explanation: Like other fish, the milkfish breathes using its gills, which take oxygen from the water.

q: Which law declared arnis the national sport and martial art of the Philippines?
options: Republic Act 9850
Republic Act 8491
Republic Act 7610
Republic Act 6657
explanation: Arnis was declared the national sport and martial art through Republic Act 9850 in 2009.

q: After salt dissolves in water and the water looks clear, what is true about the salt?
options: The salt is still in the water — you can taste it
The salt has been destroyed by the water
The salt turned into a gas and escaped into the air
The salt sank to the bottom and is invisible
explanation: After salt dissolves, the water looks clear as if the salt is gone, but the salt is still there — you can prove it because the water still tastes salty.

q: Why are nautiluses now protected?
options: Too many are caught to make decorations or souvenirs from their beautiful shells, lowering their numbers
Their meat is considered a delicacy and they are overhunted for food
Pollution from plastics is destroying their habitat rapidly
They are captured for aquariums, reducing their wild population
explanation: Because its shell is beautiful, many nautiluses are caught to be made into decorations or souvenirs, which lowers their numbers, so they are now protected.

q: What causes white sunlight to separate into different colors when it enters a raindrop?
options: The light bends (refracts) inside the raindrop, splitting into separate colors
The raindrop acts like a mirror and reflects only some colors
Water molecules absorb certain wavelengths and let others pass
The angle of the Sun determines which color of light gets through
explanation: When white sunlight enters a raindrop it bends and splits into separate colors, like a prism — that splitting gives both the rainbow and its double their colors.

q: Why should the body only take minerals in the right amounts?
options: Too much or too little of a mineral can both be harmful
Minerals are only needed during childhood growth
The body stores extra minerals and releases them later with no risk
Minerals are harmful and the body tries to remove them quickly
explanation: The body needs minerals only in the right amounts, because too much or too little can both be harmful.

q: What does the color of a star tell you about it?
options: Its temperature
How bright it appears from Earth
Its size compared to our Sun
How far away it is from Earth
explanation: A star's color tells you its temperature; brightness depends on its size and how far away it is, so a faint blue star can be very hot and a bright red star can be cooler.

q: Which Philippine government agency monitors volcanoes and earthquakes?
options: PHIVOLCS
PAGASA
DENR
DOST
explanation: PHIVOLCS is the agency that monitors volcanoes and earthquakes in the Philippines.

q: Why does drinking water help you focus better in class?
options: Your brain is mostly made of water and needs enough water to work well
Water lowers your body temperature, making you feel more alert
Water flushes out sugar from your blood, reducing distractions
Water strengthens the nerve connections in your spine
explanation: Your brain is mostly made of water, so when you are low on water you can get a headache and find it hard to focus — a glass of water helps your mind work better.

q: What did Charles Darwin discover about how seedlings bend toward light?
options: The tip of the shoot senses the light, and covering it stops the plant from bending
The roots sense light signals and send them up to the stem
The entire stem bends equally in response to light it touches
Leaves on the shaded side grow faster, pushing the stem toward the light
explanation: Charles Darwin found that the tip of the shoot senses the light — when the tip is covered, the plant no longer bends toward the light.

q: How does a fish sanctuary help recover fish populations after overfishing?
options: It gives fish a safe place to breed where no one can catch them, so numbers slowly recover
It purifies the water so fish grow faster than usual
It imports fish from other seas to replace those that were caught
It uses nets to trap and relocate fish to deeper, safer water
explanation: A fish sanctuary gives fish a safe place to breed with no one catching them, so the number of fish slowly recovers across the whole sea.

q: Why is tidal and wave energy considered a renewable energy source?
options: The ocean keeps moving, so the energy source never runs out
Sea water produces hydrogen when it moves, which is burned for power
The salt in ocean water acts as a natural battery that recharges itself
Sunlight heats the ocean and is directly converted into electricity
explanation: The movement of the ocean — the rise and fall of tides and the waves — can be turned into electricity, and it is renewable because the ocean keeps moving.

q: What does Mach 1 mean?
options: The speed of sound, about 1,225 km/h at sea level
The speed of light in air, about 300,000 km/s
Twice the speed of a commercial airplane at cruising altitude
The minimum speed needed to escape Earth's gravity
explanation: Mach 1 equals the speed of sound, about 1,225 kilometers per hour at sea level.

q: How many kinds of bases make up DNA?
options: Two — A and T
Three — A, T, and C
Four — A, T, C, and G
Six — A, T, C, G, X, and Y
explanation: DNA is made of exactly four kinds of bases: A, T, C, and G, which work like the letters of a code.

q: What song was played at the very first Philippine independence proclamation in 1898?
options: Bayan Ko
Pag-ibig sa Tinubuang Lupa
Lupang Hinirang
Marangal na Dalit ng Katagalugan
explanation: At the 1898 independence proclamation, the song now known as Lupang Hinirang was first played.

q: In foods like buro and bagoong, why do helpful microbes keep the food from spoiling?
options: They freeze the food so harmful microbes cannot grow
They cook the food at high heat to kill all bacteria
They create sour or salty conditions that block the harmful microbes
They seal the food in a vacuum so no air can enter
explanation: In fermentation like buro or bagoong, helpful microbes create salt-like or sour conditions that block the harmful microbes that cause spoiling.

q: About how many years can an elephant live in the wild?
options: 20 to 30 years
40 to 50 years
60 to 70 years
90 to 100 years
explanation: An elephant can live for about 60 to 70 years in the wild.

q: What happens when two forces push in exactly the same direction?
options: They cancel each other out and nothing moves
Their strengths add together to make a larger force
The bigger force stays the same and the smaller one disappears
They combine into a force that is only half of each
explanation: When two forces push in the same direction, their strengths add together to make a larger force.

q: What does viscosity tell us about a liquid?
options: How heavy the liquid is
How hot the liquid gets
How hard it is for the liquid to flow
How much space the liquid takes up
explanation: Viscosity is about how hard a liquid flows, not about how heavy it is.

q: Why do some vaccines need a booster shot given after some time?
options: Because the first shot causes an allergic reaction that must be reversed
Because the body's memory of a germ can slowly fade and the booster strengthens defenses again
Because the first dose only works for a week before breaking down
Because the booster changes the type of germ the vaccine protects against
explanation: Some vaccines need a booster because the body's memory of a germ can slowly fade, and the extra shot reminds and strengthens the defenses again.

q: When a large light source makes a shadow, what does the shadow look like?
options: It has only one solid dark edge with no lighter area
It has a darkest center and a lighter, fuzzy edge
It is perfectly sharp all the way around with no fuzzy parts
It has a lighter center and a dark fuzzy edge
explanation: A shadow can have a darkest center and a lighter, fuzzy edge when the light source is large.

q: Why can't antibiotics cure measles?
options: Antibiotics are too expensive to use for measles
Measles spreads too fast for antibiotics to reach it
Measles is caused by a virus, and antibiotics only work on bacteria
Measles is caused by a fungus, not a germ that antibiotics can fight
explanation: Diseases caused by viruses like measles are not cured by antibiotics, which only work on bacteria.

q: Where is the tamaraw found in the wild?
options: Only on the island of Palawan
Only on the island of Mindoro
Only on the island of Luzon
Only on the island of Cebu
explanation: The tamaraw is a small wild buffalo that is endemic and found only on the island of Mindoro.

q: When are crickets most active and do most of their singing?
options: Early in the morning at sunrise
During the hottest part of the afternoon
Especially at night
Only during heavy rain
explanation: Crickets are active and sing especially at night.

q: Who discovered the double helix shape of DNA in 1953?
options: Louis Pasteur and Robert Koch
Gregor Mendel and Charles Darwin
James Watson and Francis Crick
Marie Curie and Albert Einstein
explanation: James Watson and Francis Crick discovered the shape of DNA — the double helix — in 1953.

q: How do solar panels make electricity?
options: By using heat from underground rocks
By capturing energy from sunlight
By converting wind energy into electrical energy
By using chemical reactions in batteries
explanation: Solar energy is electricity made from sunlight using solar panels.

q: What makes rattan one of the longest plants in the world?
options: Its roots grow hundreds of meters underground
Its leaves spread out over a wide area reaching hundreds of meters
Its stems can reach hundreds of meters as they climb through trees
Its flowers are connected by stems that stretch hundreds of meters
explanation: Rattan is among the longest plants in the world; some stems reach hundreds of meters long as they climb through the trees.

q: What happens to honey when you heat it?
options: It becomes thicker and flows more slowly
It turns solid and can no longer be poured
It becomes thinner and flows more easily
It becomes heavier and sinks to the bottom
explanation: When you heat honey, it becomes thinner and flows more easily, because heating lowers its viscosity.

q: What tools are used to string sampaguita buds into a garland?
options: A stapler and wire
A knife and string
A needle and thread
A toothpick and rubber band
explanation: A needle and thread are used to string the sampaguita buds one by one.

q: What unusual thing can the mudskipper do that most fish cannot?
options: It can breathe fire when frightened
It can change colors like a chameleon
It can crawl and walk across the mud using its strong front fins
It can jump into the air and glide like a flying fish
explanation: The mudskipper is a fish that can crawl and walk across the mud using its strong front fins.

q: Why do forward-facing eyes help us see depth?
options: They let us see a much wider area by pointing in opposite directions
Their overlapping views help us judge how far away things are
They allow us to see in the dark better than side-facing eyes
They each see different colors, which helps us identify objects
explanation: Forward-facing eyes, like ours, have overlapping views that help us see depth.

q: Why is it important to be careful when gathering wild plants to eat?
options: All wild plants taste very bitter and need cooking first
Wild plants are always more nutritious than store-bought ones
Not all wild plants are safe to eat, so only well-known greens should be gathered
Wild plants must be picked only in the morning or they become poisonous
explanation: Not all wild plants are safe to eat, so only well-known greens like pako should be gathered.

q: When should someone see a doctor to be checked for TB?
options: Only when they have a fever higher than 39°C
After they have been sneezing for one day
If they have been coughing for three weeks
When they feel a pain in their stomach for two days
explanation: If someone has coughed for three weeks, they should see a doctor to be checked for TB and stop it from spreading.

q: What makes the Asian giant hornet special compared to other hornets?
options: It is the only hornet that can sting more than once
It is the fastest flying insect in Asia
It is the largest hornet in the world, with a body nearly as big as a human thumb
It is the only hornet that lives underground in the Philippines
explanation: The Asian giant hornet, found in Asia, is the largest hornet in the world — its body is nearly as big as a human thumb.

q: Where does much of the white sand on tropical beaches come from?
options: Volcanic ash that has been washed ashore over many years
Crushed coral and limestone broken up by waves and some fish
Fine desert sand blown by wind from faraway dry lands
Tiny white shells left by snails that live on the shore
explanation: Much of the white sand on beaches comes from crushed coral and limestone broken up by waves and some fish.

q: When the Earth pulls a falling apple downward, what does the apple do to the Earth?
options: The apple pushes the Earth sideways with a weaker force
The apple pulls the Earth upward with an equal force
The apple has no effect on Earth because it is too small
The apple pushes the Earth downward with twice the force
explanation: While the Earth pulls a falling apple down, the apple also pulls the Earth up with equal strength — but the Earth's huge mass means this force has almost no visible effect.

q: How do people help seeds travel from one place to another?
options: By throwing seeds into rivers so the water carries them away
By saving seeds from their best crops and planting them on other farms
By letting birds eat the seeds and fly to new locations
By blowing seeds through hollow tubes to plant them far away
explanation: People save seeds from their best crops to plant again next season, carrying them from one farm to another.

q: How can fine dust travel thousands of kilometers, even across oceans?
options: It sticks to migratory birds and gets carried to new places
It is so light that wind can carry it those great distances
It dissolves in rainwater and flows through rivers to the sea
Ocean currents carry it along the surface of the water
explanation: Fine dust is so light that wind can carry it thousands of kilometers, even across oceans.

q: Which of these is an example of energy that is stored and ready to be used?
options: The light coming from a lamp
The sound coming from a speaker
The heat coming from a fire
The energy inside a battery
explanation: Some energy is stored and ready to be used, like in a battery, while heat, light, and sound are forms of energy already on the move.

q: Which is the highest mountain in the Philippines?
options: Mount Pulag in the Cordillera
Mount Mayon in Albay
Mount Apo in Mindanao
Mount Kanlaon in Negros
explanation: Mount Apo in Mindanao is the highest mountain in the entire Philippines.

q: What units do we use to measure distance?
options: Liters and milliliters
Grams and kilograms
Degrees Celsius and Fahrenheit
Meters and kilometers
explanation: We measure distance in units such as meters and kilometers.

q: Which part of the body has the thinnest skin?
options: The soles of the feet
The palms of the hands
The eyelids
The back of the neck
explanation: The skin is not the same thickness everywhere: it is thick on the soles of the feet but thin on the eyelids.

q: What does the katala bird look like on its head?
options: It has a bright red crest and black feathers
It has a blue crest and yellow feathers
It has no crest and plain brown feathers
It has white feathers and a crest that it can raise
explanation: The katala has white feathers and a crest of feathers on its head that it can raise.

q: Which type of wave carries the highest energy in the electromagnetic spectrum?
options: Radio waves
Visible light
X-rays
Gamma rays
explanation: Gamma rays carry the highest energy in the electromagnetic spectrum.

q: In an egg-and-spoon race, what must you do to keep the egg from falling off?
options: Run as fast as possible so the egg has no time to roll
Tilt the spoon backward so the egg leans against your hand
Keep the egg centered on the spoon so its center of gravity stays balanced
Hold the spoon with two hands and look only at the egg
explanation: In an egg-and-spoon race you must keep the egg centered on the spoon so its center of gravity stays balanced and it does not roll off.

q: What are the bacteria called that live in the roots of legumes and help them grow?
options: Lactobacillus
Salmonella
Rhizobium
Streptococcus
explanation: The bacteria that help legumes are called Rhizobium and live in the plant's roots.

q: After whom is the Coriolis effect named?
options: An Italian navigator who discovered it during a long sea voyage
A French scientist named Gaspard-Gustave de Coriolis who described it in 1835
A British astronomer who noticed it while studying the Moon
An American meteorologist who observed it in hurricanes
explanation: The Coriolis effect is named after Gaspard-Gustave de Coriolis, a French scientist who described it in 1835.

q: How does the Brahminy kite catch fish?
options: It dives completely underwater and chases fish like a penguin
It waits at the riverbank and snatches fish with its beak
It snatches fish from the surface of the water with its talons while flying
It herds fish into shallow water before stepping in to catch them
explanation: The Brahminy kite often snatches fish from the surface of the water with its talons while flying.

q: Why are a cobra's fangs described as being like a needle?
options: They are long and straight, used only for biting and tearing
They are coated with a sticky substance that traps prey
They are hollow inside, so venom flows through them into the wound
They are made of the same material as needles and are just as sharp
explanation: A cobra's fangs are hollow inside like a needle, so venom flows from the fang into the wound.

q: When a comb rubbed on dry hair is held near a thin stream of water, what happens to the water?
options: The water speeds up and flows faster in a straight line
The water bends away from the comb as if pushed
The water bends toward the comb because it is attracted to the static charge
The water stops flowing completely until the comb is removed
explanation: The water bends toward the comb because it is attracted to the comb's static charge.

q: How fast are the winds in a super typhoon?
options: More than 90 km/h
More than 120 km/h
More than 150 km/h
More than 185 km/h
explanation: A super typhoon has winds of more than 185 km/h, the strongest category of storm.

q: What happens to a diamond when it is exposed to very high heat with oxygen?
options: It melts into a shiny liquid like other hard rocks
It turns black and becomes a lump of charcoal
It shatters into many tiny pieces of glass
It burns away into carbon dioxide gas and disappears
explanation: Because a diamond is pure carbon, at very high heat with oxygen it can actually burn away into carbon dioxide gas.

q: How long have farmers been practicing crop rotation?
options: Only since the discovery of nitrogen in the 1900s
Only since chemical fertilizers were invented about 100 years ago
For hundreds of years, long before they understood the science behind it
Only since the 1950s when modern agriculture began
explanation: Crop rotation is not a new invention — farmers have practiced it for hundreds of years, long before they knew about nitrogen or bacteria.

q: Why is the aerosol breathed out by a vape not safe for people nearby?
options: It smells bad and can cause headaches only in young children
It contains only water vapor, which makes the air too humid
It contains chemicals and tiny particles that nearby people breathe in
It is hotter than cigarette smoke, which burns the lungs of bystanders
explanation: The aerosol a vape breathes out is not just water — it also contains chemicals and tiny particles that people nearby breathe in.

q: What happens to the carbon stored in mangrove mud when mangroves are cut down?
options: It stays locked safely in the mud forever even without the trees
It is washed out to sea where it becomes part of coral reefs
It sinks deeper into the ground where it cannot affect the atmosphere
The disturbed mud lets the buried carbon meet the air and escape back into the atmosphere
explanation: When mangroves are cut or filled in, the disturbed mud lets buried carbon meet air again, releasing it back into the atmosphere and adding to planetary warming.

q: What causes orographic clouds and heavy rainfall on one side of a mountain?
options: Cold ocean currents push moisture up the mountain cliffs
The shadow of the mountain traps heat, causing clouds to form
Moist air is forced to rise over the mountain and cool, forming clouds
Strong winds blow rain clouds directly into the mountain and they pile up
explanation: Orographic clouds form when moist air is forced to rise over mountains and cool, causing heavy rainfall on the windward side.

q: Which government agency manages clean water supply in Manila?
options: DENR
NBI
MWSS
DOH
explanation: The government works to ensure every Filipino has clean and safe drinking water through water districts and the MWSS in Manila.

q: How do animals like barnacles and limpets survive in the wave-battered intertidal zone?
options: They hide in deep sand during high tide so waves cannot reach them
They float on the surface of the water when waves hit the rocks
They have special abilities to cling to rocks and avoid drying out at low tide
They move to calmer deeper water during storms and return after
explanation: Animals in the intertidal zone such as barnacles and limpets have special abilities to cling to wave-battered rocks and avoid drying out at low tide.

q: What animal is widely known as the national animal of the Philippines?
options: The Philippine Eagle
The Tamaraw
The Carabao (water buffalo)
The Tarsier
explanation: The carabao (water buffalo) is widely known as the national animal of the Philippines, though no law officially declares it.

q: How is a temperature correctly written using the Kelvin unit?
options: 300 °K (with the degree symbol before K)
300 Kv (with a letter v to show it is a very cold temperature)
300 K (just the number and K, with no degree symbol)
300 °K° (with the degree symbol on both sides)
explanation: The Kelvin unit is written just as "K" with no degree symbol — for example, 300 K.

q: What should you do to a mango seed before planting it?
options: Soak it in water for a week so it becomes soft
Freeze it overnight to break its hard outer shell
Clean off the stuck flesh and let it dry a little so it does not rot
Paint it with cooking oil to protect it from insects in the soil
explanation: Before planting a mango seed, you clean off the stuck flesh and let it dry a little so it does not rot before it has a chance to sprout.

q: In which island group of the Philippines is the province of Capiz located?
options: Luzon
Mindanao
Visayas
Palawan
explanation: Capiz is a province in the Western Visayas region (VI), part of the Visayas island group, with Roxas City as its capital.

q: What parts make up bagasse, the leftover material from sugarcane?
options: Only dry powder and sugar crystals
Long fibers, a soft inner part called pith, plus leftover moisture and sugar
Hard outer shells and a sweet syrup inside
Tiny seeds and oily liquid squeezed from the cane
explanation: Bagasse is made up of long fibers, a soft inner part called pith, plus some leftover moisture and sugar; those fibers are used for paper or fuel.

q: What does the word 'cnidarian' mean in Greek?
options: Nettle or stinging plant
Shell or hard cover
Jelly or soft body
Tentacle or arm
explanation: The word 'cnidarian' comes from a Greek word meaning 'nettle' or 'stinging plant,' reflecting these animals' stinging cells.

q: About how fast does a passenger plane travel on average?
options: 900 km/h
4 km/h
80 km/h
300 km/h
explanation: A passenger plane reaches about 900 km/h, which is much faster than a car (80 km/h) or a walking person (4 km/h).

q: What do we call it when animals travel to warmer places with food instead of sleeping through a hard season?
options: Migration
Hibernation
Camouflage
Adaptation
explanation: Migration is when animals travel to warmer places with food to survive difficult seasons instead of sleeping.

q: How is patis, the popular Filipino fish sauce, made?
options: By fermenting fish with salt for many months
By boiling fish with vinegar for a few hours
By drying fish in the sun and grinding it
By mixing raw fish juice with soy sauce
explanation: Patis is made by fermenting fish with salt for many months, during which microorganisms break down the fish proteins to create a savory liquid.

q: What do scientists think the spermaceti oil in a sperm whale's head helps the whale do?
options: Sink or float by changing temperature
Produce sounds for communication
Attract prey in deep water
Store energy for long dives
explanation: Scientists think spermaceti helps the sperm whale sink or float by cooling or warming the oil, controlling buoyancy.

q: What happens during a coral mass spawning event?
options: Corals release millions of eggs and sperm into the water at the same time
Corals break apart into smaller pieces to form new colonies
Corals attach to new surfaces by releasing sticky cement
Corals change color to attract fish for fertilization
explanation: During mass spawning, corals release millions of eggs and sperm simultaneously into the water, usually after a full moon.

q: What must a crane operator watch to prevent the crane from tipping over?
options: That the combined center of gravity stays within the crane's base
That the crane's boom is always pointing straight up
That the engine temperature stays below a safe level
That the crane wheels are always locked in place
explanation: Crane operators must ensure the combined center of gravity stays within the crane's base; if it moves outside, the crane will tip over.

q: Why is a magnitude 10 earthquake nearly impossible in real life?
options: No fault is long enough to release that much energy
Seismographs cannot measure anything above 9
The Earth's crust is too thin to hold that much stress
Earthquakes above 9 cancel each other out underground
explanation: A magnitude 10 is almost impossible because no fault is long enough to release that much energy; the largest ever recorded were only about magnitude 9.

q: Which animals eat ripe santol, atis, and guyabano fruits in the forest?
options: Birds and bats
Lizards and snakes
Frogs and insects
Fish and crabs
explanation: Ripe santol, atis, and guyabano are food for birds and bats in the forest.

q: Why is Type AB blood called the universal plasma donor?
options: Its plasma has no anti-A or anti-B antibodies so any patient can receive it
It can donate red blood cells to people of any blood type
It has the most oxygen-carrying cells of any blood type
Its plasma clots faster than other blood types in emergencies
explanation: Type AB plasma has no anti-A or anti-B antibodies, so it can safely be given to patients of any blood type.

q: How does a remora fish stay safe from predators while attached to a shark?
options: Other predators are afraid of the large shark host
The remora becomes invisible by matching the shark's color
The shark's skin produces a chemical that repels attackers
The remora hides inside the shark's gills when danger approaches
explanation: While stuck to a shark, the remora stays safe because other predators are afraid of its big host.

q: How can you tell when a cacao pod is ripe and ready to harvest?
options: It changes color from green to yellow or orange
It becomes smooth and loses its ridges
It falls off the tree on its own
It shrinks and becomes harder to the touch
explanation: A cacao pod's color tells you when it is ripe — many turn from green to yellow or orange when ready to harvest.

q: What happens to a pendulum at the highest ends of its swing?
options: It stops for an instant before swinging back
It reaches its greatest speed before reversing
It stores the most kinetic energy at that point
It swings back immediately without any pause
explanation: At the highest ends of its swing, a pendulum stops for an instant before heading back the other way.

q: How are frog eggs different from toad eggs in the way they are laid?
options: Frog eggs are laid in sticky clumps, while toad eggs are in long string-like rows
Frog eggs are laid on land, while toad eggs are always laid in water
Frog eggs are hard-shelled, while toad eggs have a soft jelly coating
Frog eggs hatch into tadpoles, while toad eggs hatch directly into toads
explanation: Frog eggs are usually laid in sticky clumps, while many toads lay their eggs in long string-like rows.

q: How do mangrove trees help keep coastal water clean?
options: Their roots filter dirt out of the water
Their leaves absorb chemicals from the air above the water
Their fallen leaves neutralize salt in the seawater
Their shade prevents algae from growing in the water
explanation: Mangrove roots filter dirt out of the water, making the coastal water cleaner.

q: What does the Venus flytrap do when an insect lands on its leaf?
options: The leaf quickly snaps shut and traps the insect inside
The leaf rolls up slowly to digest the insect overnight
The leaf releases a sticky liquid to glue the insect down
The leaf turns red to warn nearby insects of danger
explanation: When a fly lands on its leaf, the Venus flytrap's leaf quickly snaps shut like a mouth and traps the insect inside.

q: What can some plants' white or sticky sap do to animals or people?
options: Poison them or irritate their skin
Make them feel sleepy and calm
Attract them with a sweet smell
Cause them to grow faster and stronger
explanation: Some plants release a white or sticky sap that is poisonous or irritates the skin, protecting the plant from being eaten.

q: What is the pale band of light that can be seen across the night sky from a very dark place?
options: The Milky Way, our galaxy made of billions of stars
The asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter
The light trail of a passing comet
A ring of dust surrounding the solar system
explanation: That pale band across the dark night sky is the Milky Way — our galaxy made of billions of stars so far away they blend into a cloud of light.

q: Why does a skydiver spread out their arms and legs while falling?
options: To increase air resistance and slow the fall
To reduce air resistance and fall faster
To balance their weight evenly in the air
To spin in a controlled direction during the fall
explanation: Spreading arms and legs makes the body wider, increasing air resistance and slowing the fall.

q: What two main products does a plant make during photosynthesis?
options: Glucose and oxygen
Carbon dioxide and water
Starch and nitrogen
Chlorophyll and energy
explanation: The photosynthesis equation shows that plants use CO2 and water with light energy to make glucose and release oxygen.

q: On which island is Mount Pinatubo located?
options: Luzon
Mindanao
Visayas
Palawan
explanation: Mount Pinatubo is located in Zambales on the island of Luzon.

q: Which months are typically inter-monsoon periods in the Philippines, known for variable winds and strong afternoon thunderstorms?
options: April and November
June and December
January and July
March and September
explanation: April and November are typically inter-monsoon periods in the Philippines when winds are variable and strong afternoon thunderstorms are common.

q: Why are many impact craters on Earth hard to see compared to those on the Moon?
options: Water, wind, and plants slowly cover or wear them away over time
Earth's craters were formed much longer ago than the Moon's
Earth has stronger gravity that pulls craters back into the ground
The craters are hidden under the ocean where we cannot see them
explanation: Many craters on Earth are hard to see because water, wind, and plants slowly cover or wear them away over time.

q: In a cave, what is the difference between a stalactite and a stalagmite?
options: Stalactites hang down from the ceiling; stalagmites grow up from the floor
Stalactites grow up from the floor; stalagmites hang from the ceiling
Stalactites form in water; stalagmites form in dry caves
Stalactites are made of clay; stalagmites are made of limestone
explanation: Dripping water carrying dissolved limestone builds stalactites hanging down from the ceiling and stalagmites growing up from the floor.

q: In a food chain, about how much energy passes from one level to the next?
options: About ten percent
About fifty percent
About ninety percent
About one percent
explanation: Only about ten percent of energy passes to the next level of a food chain, while roughly ninety percent is lost as heat.

q: Why did the IAU reclassify Pluto as a dwarf planet in 2006?
options: It has not cleared its orbital path of other bodies
It is too small to be seen without a telescope
It does not orbit the Sun like the other planets
It is made of ice rather than rock like the other planets
explanation: The IAU reclassified Pluto as a dwarf planet in 2006 because it has not cleared its orbital path of other bodies.

q: What are the early symptoms of leptospirosis?
options: Fever, headache, and muscle pain
Cough, runny nose, and sore throat
Skin rash, itching, and swelling
Nausea, vomiting, and stomach cramps
explanation: The early symptoms of leptospirosis are fever, headache, and muscle pain.

q: How do many islands form in the ocean?
options: Volcanoes rise from the ocean floor until their tops poke above the water
Large pieces of rock break off continents and drift into the sea
Ocean water drops, leaving underwater hills exposed as islands
Wind piles up sand in one place until an island builds above the waves
explanation: Many islands form when volcanoes rise from the ocean floor until their tops poke above the water.

q: On a speed-time graph, what does a flat horizontal line mean?
options: The object is moving at constant speed
The object is not moving at all
The object is speeding up steadily
The object is slowing down gradually
explanation: On a speed-time graph the height itself is speed, so a flat line means constant speed, not standing still.

q: What two things do the lungs do with gases?
options: Take in oxygen and release carbon dioxide
Take in carbon dioxide and release nitrogen
Take in oxygen and release water vapor only
Take in all gases and release none back out
explanation: The lungs take oxygen from the air and pass it into the blood, and they release carbon dioxide that the body no longer needs.

q: What ended the Paleozoic era and was the largest mass extinction in history?
options: The Permian extinction, which killed most sea life
The asteroid impact that wiped out the dinosaurs
A massive ice age that froze the oceans worldwide
A series of supervolcano eruptions across all continents
explanation: The Paleozoic ended with the Permian extinction, the largest mass extinction in history, which killed most sea life.

q: When was the James Webb Space Telescope launched?
options: December 2021
March 2015
July 2019
November 2024
explanation: The James Webb Space Telescope was launched in December 2021.

q: What can happen to your voice if you shout too much?
options: Your vocal cords get strained and your voice becomes hoarse
Your throat swells up and you lose your voice completely
Your vocal cords grow thicker and your voice gets permanently deeper
Your lungs get tired and you can no longer speak loudly
explanation: Shouting too much strains the vocal cords and can make our voice hoarse.

q: Why is a pushcart (kariton) easier to move than dragging a heavy object along the ground?
options: Its rolling wheels reduce friction with the ground
Its handles let you push at the best angle to save energy
Its flat base spreads the weight so it feels lighter
Its metal frame is stronger and does not bend under heavy loads
explanation: A pushcart is easy to move because its rolling wheels reduce friction with the ground, so it takes much less force than dragging.

q: When does a civet (musang) look for food?
options: At night, because it is nocturnal
In the early morning before sunrise
During the middle of the day when it is warmest
In the late afternoon before sunset
explanation: The civet is nocturnal, meaning it is awake and looks for food at night and sleeps during the day.

q: Why is the calm in the eye of a typhoon dangerous?
options: Strong winds return once the other side of the eyewall passes over
The calm air actually contains the most rainfall of the entire storm
The pressure drop in the eye can cause buildings to explode outward
The eye moves the fastest and can change direction without warning
explanation: The calm of the eye is deceptive because strong winds return once the other side of the eyewall passes over.

q: How does too much carbon dioxide in the ocean harm coral?
options: It makes seawater more acidic, making it harder for coral to build its hard limestone skeleton
It lowers water temperature, which prevents coral larvae from settling on the reef
It reduces sunlight reaching the reef, so the algae inside coral cannot photosynthesize
It increases the salt level, which causes coral to release its symbiotic algae and bleach
explanation: Too much carbon dioxide makes seawater more acidic, which makes it harder for coral to build its hard limestone skeleton.

q: What is one good example of reusing something before throwing it away?
options: Turning an old bottle into a water container or plant pot
Burning old newspapers to make heat for cooking
Breaking glass jars into small pieces to mix with soil
Cutting old clothing into rags and burying them in the garden
explanation: Before throwing something away, it can be reused — for example, an old bottle can become a water container or a plant pot, which reduces trash.

q: Which animal is shown on the front of the Philippine 1,000-peso banknote?
options: The Philippine Eagle
The Sarimanok rooster
The Carabao
The Pawikan sea turtle
explanation: The Philippine Eagle is shown on the front of the new polymer 1,000-peso banknote.

q: Why does a chili plant produce heat in its fruit?
options: To stop animals like mice from eating it, while birds that spread the seeds are not bothered by the heat
To attract insects that help pollinate the flowers on the plant
To store energy that helps the seeds survive cold nights
To make the fruit taste sweeter and more appealing to large mammals
explanation: A chili's heat is a plant defense that discourages animals like mice from eating the fruit, but does not bother birds, which help spread the seeds.

q: What tool do you need to see germs?
options: A microscope
A magnifying glass
A telescope
A thermometer
explanation: Germs are so tiny that the eye cannot see them; a microscope is needed to see them.

q: What does the makahiya plant do when you touch or shake it?
options: Its leaves quickly fold up as if it were shy
Its leaves turn a bright red color to warn you away
Its roots release a bad smell to drive you away
Its stem bends away from you to avoid contact
explanation: When touched or shaken, the makahiya plant's leaves quickly fold up as if it were shy.

q: What does the body of a coral polyp look like?
options: A tiny sac with a mouth in the middle ringed by tentacles
A flat disc with legs extending from its sides
A hollow tube with eyes at the top and a tail below
A round ball with openings spread across its surface
explanation: A polyp's body is like a tiny sac with a mouth in the middle ringed by tentacles.

q: What are hives, as a sign of an allergic reaction?
options: Itchy, red bumps that appear on the skin
Dark blue patches that form under the fingernails
Dry, flaky scales that peel off the skin surface
Watery blisters that form between the fingers and toes
explanation: Sometimes an allergy shows up on the skin as itchy, red bumps called hives.

q: Why do some mangroves grow upright roots that poke above the mud?
options: Because wet mud has little air, and these roots take in oxygen from above
Because the roots need sunlight to produce food for the tree
Because protruding roots anchor the tree against strong ocean waves
Because the roots collect rainwater that the tree needs during dry season
explanation: Because wet mud has little air, some mangroves grow upright roots that poke above the ground to take in oxygen.

q: What are the three parts of a mantle convection cell?
options: Hot rock rising (upwelling), rock moving sideways near the top, and cooler rock sinking (downwelling)
Liquid magma pushing up, solid crust cracking open, and rock melting at the edges
Hot plates sliding apart, cooler plates colliding, and mountains folding upward
Lava erupting from volcanoes, spreading across the ocean floor, and cooling into new rock
explanation: A mantle convection cell has three parts: hot rock rising (upwelling), rock moving sideways near the top, and cooler rock sinking back down (downwelling) in a full repeating loop.

q: How does a lightning rod protect a house during a thunderstorm?
options: It catches lightning and safely carries electricity down into the ground
It repels lightning by creating an electric field around the roof
