It melts the lightning bolt before it can reach the walls of the house
It spreads the lightning equally across all parts of the building
explanation: A lightning rod on a roof catches lightning and safely carries its electricity down into the ground, protecting the house from catching fire.

q: How does venom help the Komodo dragon catch its prey?
options: The deep wounds from its powerful bite let the venom enter easily, and strength and venom work together to weaken the prey
The venom paralyzes prey instantly from a distance before the dragon bites
The venom makes prey stop running so the dragon can simply walk up to it
The venom digests the prey's flesh from the outside before the dragon swallows it
explanation: The Komodo dragon uses its powerful bite to make deep wounds that let the venom enter more easily, and strength and venom work together to weaken the prey.

q: How are worker termites able to get nutrition from wood?
options: Tiny living helpers inside their gut break down the wood into food.
Their strong jaws grind wood into a paste that their stomach absorbs directly.
Special acids in their saliva dissolve the wood before they swallow it.
They store chewed wood in a pouch and let it ferment for several days.
explanation: Worker termites cannot digest wood on their own; tiny living helpers (microorganisms) inside their gut do the breaking down for them.

q: How many legs does a centipede have on each body segment?
options: One pair of legs
Two pairs of legs
Three pairs of legs
Four pairs of legs
explanation: A centipede has exactly one pair of legs on each segment of its body.

q: Your hand is bleeding. What should you do with it to help slow the bleeding?
options: Raise it higher than your heart.
Hold it below your waist and keep it still.
Press it flat against your chest.
Swing it gently to keep blood flowing.
explanation: Raising a bleeding hand or leg higher than the heart uses gravity to help slow the flow of blood.

q: Which group of animals has the most species in the whole world?
options: Insects
Fish
Birds
Reptiles
explanation: Insects are the largest group of animals on Earth, outnumbering every other animal group.

q: What happens when a species becomes extinct?
options: It can never come back — it is gone forever.
It may return if the habitat is restored.
Scientists can bring it back using DNA in a few decades.
It survives in small hidden populations in remote areas.
explanation: Once a species is extinct it can never come back, which is why protecting endangered animals is so important.

q: Why do many carnivores have colors or patterns that match their surroundings?
options: So their prey cannot see them while they wait to hunt.
So other predators of the same species do not compete with them.
So they can absorb more heat from the sun to stay warm.
So they look bigger and more frightening to other animals.
explanation: Carnivores use camouflage — colors or patterns that match their surroundings — to hide from prey before attacking.

q: How is a crab's eye different from a human eye?
options: A crab's eye has many tiny lenses, while a human eye has only one lens.
A crab's eye has a single large lens that sees in color, while humans see only in black and white.
A crab cannot see behind itself, while humans can see almost all the way around.
A crab's eye is fixed in its head, while human eyes are mounted on movable stalks.
explanation: A crab's eye is made of many tiny lenses and sits on a stalk, while each human eye has just one lens that makes a clear picture.

q: What does a muscle do when it moves a bone — does it push or pull?
options: It only pulls; it gets shorter (contracts) and tugs the bone toward itself.
It pushes the bone away by expanding and getting longer.
It pushes and pulls in turn, like a spring, to move the bone both ways.
It stays the same length but vibrates rapidly to create force on the bone.
explanation: A muscle contracts (shortens) to pull the bone it is attached to — muscles can only pull, not push.

q: If you mix an acid and a base, what must you do to get a truly neutral solution?
options: Use exactly the right amounts of each so neither is in excess.
Always add more base than acid, because base cancels acid faster.
Mix them in any amounts and then heat the mixture to complete the reaction.
Add a little salt to the mixture to bring it to neutral.
explanation: Too much acid keeps the mix sour and too much base keeps it bitter, so the correct amounts must be used to reach neutral.

q: Why does a planet keep moving in its orbit around the sun instead of flying off into space?
options: Gravity pulling the planet inward is balanced by the planet's forward motion.
The sun's magnetic field locks each planet on a fixed invisible track.
Friction with space dust slows the planet just enough to keep it curving.
The planet's own gravity pushes back against the sun's pull to stay in place.
explanation: A planet stays in orbit because the sun's gravitational pull is exactly balanced by the planet's forward motion.

q: How does a mosquito pupa breathe even though it lives in water?
options: It pokes two tiny trumpet-shaped tubes above the water surface to take in air.
It absorbs oxygen directly through its thin skin from the water around it.
It rises to the surface and opens a small flap on its back to breathe.
It stores a bubble of air under its wing pads before diving below the surface.
explanation: The mosquito pupa has two tiny trumpet-shaped tubes on top of its head that it pokes above the water to breathe air.

q: What happens when crushed gumamela (hibiscus) flower juice is mixed with an acid or base?
options: The juice changes color because its pigments act as a natural indicator.
The juice forms a thick foam that turns hard and solid after a few minutes.
The juice becomes clear and odorless because its pigments are destroyed.
The juice separates into layers with the acid or base sinking to the bottom.
explanation: Gumamela contains pigments that act as natural indicators — the juice changes color when mixed with an acid or base.

q: How does a palm civet change its diet across the year?
options: It eats more fruit when trees are fruiting and more insects when fruit is scarce.
It eats only insects in summer and switches entirely to plant roots in winter.
It hunts small lizards in the dry season and switches to berries in the rainy season.
Its diet stays the same all year because it lives near human settlements.
explanation: The palm civet's diet shifts with the seasons, relying more on fruit when available and switching to more insects when fruit is scarce.

q: Why does gold settle to the bottom of a pan when river sand is washed?
options: Gold is very heavy and dense, so it sinks first.
Gold is magnetic, so it is pulled downward by the Earth's magnetic field.
Gold particles are much larger than sand grains, so they fall faster.
Gold is smooth and round, so it rolls to the lowest point of the pan.
explanation: Gold is very dense and heavy, so it sinks to the bottom of the pan before lighter sand particles do.

q: A ball is rolled down two ramps — one smooth and one rough. Which rolls farther, and why?
options: The smooth ramp, because it has less friction to slow the ball down.
The rough ramp, because the bumpy surface pushes the ball forward.
Both ramps are the same, because gravity pulls the ball equally on both.
The rough ramp, because friction gives the ball extra grip and speed.
explanation: A ball rolls farther on a smooth ramp because the smooth surface has less friction to hold it back.

q: About how far is the Earth from the Sun on average?
options: About 150 million kilometers
About 15 million kilometers
About 1.5 billion kilometers
About 1.5 million kilometers
explanation: The average distance from Earth to the Sun is about 150 million kilometers.

q: How does a wind turbine produce electricity?
options: Wind spins its blades, which drive a generator that makes electricity.
Wind pushes charged air particles through copper coils to create a current.
The blades heat up from friction, and that heat is converted to electricity.
Wind inflates a large chamber, and the pressure inside powers a turbine.
explanation: A wind turbine converts wind energy into electricity by having the wind spin its blades, which drive a generator.

q: What do doctors do when a ball-and-socket joint in a person's hip wears out?
options: They do surgery to replace it with an artificial ball and socket made of metal or plastic.
They inject a special gel between the bones to make them glide smoothly again.
They fuse the two bones together with metal screws so the joint cannot move.
They transplant a healthy joint taken from a donor who recently passed away.
explanation: When a ball-and-socket joint wears out, doctors perform a joint replacement — installing an artificial ball and socket made of metal or plastic so the patient can walk again.

q: Which gemstone is the birthstone for the month of April?
options: Diamond
Ruby
Emerald
Sapphire
explanation: Diamond is the recognized birthstone for April.

q: Does sneezing always mean a person is sick?
options: No — sneezing can also be caused by dust, pepper, or bright light in a healthy person.
Yes — sneezing only happens when the body is fighting a virus or bacteria.
No — sneezing only happens when the air is too cold and dry for the nose.
Yes — healthy people do not sneeze; it is always a sign of infection.
explanation: Sneezing is often just a response to dust, pepper, or bright light, and a perfectly healthy person can sneeze too.

q: A ball on a string is spinning in a circle when the string suddenly breaks. What path does the ball take?
options: It flies off in a straight line.
It continues in a circle because of its momentum.
It spirals outward in a widening curve.
It falls straight down due to gravity.
explanation: Without centripetal force (from the broken string), the object flies off in a straight line, not a continuing circle.

q: Why are fruits eaten by bats at night often strongly scented rather than brightly colored?
options: Because bats cannot see colors well in the dark, so smell guides them to the fruit.
Because bright colors attract daytime insects that would eat the fruit first.
Because the scent keeps the fruit fresh longer during cool nights.
Because colorful fruits need sunlight to develop their pigment, which is absent at night.
explanation: Since it is dark at night and bats cannot see colors well, the fruit uses strong scent as the 'invitation' for bats to find it.

q: What happens to how often and how much you urinate when you drink more water?
options: You urinate more often and in larger amounts.
You urinate less often because the kidneys store extra water.
You urinate at the same rate because the kidneys filter a fixed amount.
You urinate slightly more but only once extra per day.
explanation: When you drink more water, your body produces more urine, so you pee more often and in larger amounts.

q: What is the job of a tendon in the body?
options: It connects a muscle to a bone so the bone moves when the muscle pulls.
It connects two bones together to hold a joint in place.
It covers the outside of a muscle to protect it from tearing.
It carries signals from the brain to the muscle to tell it when to contract.
explanation: A tendon is a tough cord that connects a muscle to a bone, so when the muscle contracts and pulls, the bone moves with it.

q: How do seagrass meadows compare to land forests in storing carbon?
options: Seagrass meadows can store carbon faster per hectare than typical land forests.
Land forests store carbon much faster than seagrass meadows per hectare.
Seagrass meadows and land forests store carbon at exactly the same rate.
Seagrass meadows store carbon more slowly but hold it for much longer.
explanation: Seagrass meadows can sequester up to 83,000 kilograms of carbon per hectare, which is faster than typical land forests.

q: Waling-waling orchids grow on tree branches to reach sunlight but take no food from the tree. What type of relationship is this?
options: Commensalism — the orchid benefits but the tree is unaffected.
Mutualism — both the orchid and the tree benefit from each other.
Parasitism — the orchid takes nutrients from the tree while harming it.
Competition — the orchid and the tree compete for the same sunlight.
explanation: This is commensalism: the orchid benefits by getting light without harming or helping the tree.

q: What do bacteria and fungi release when they break down dead plants and animals?
options: Carbon dioxide that returns carbon to the air and soil.
Pure water vapor that joins the water cycle.
Nitrogen gas that is absorbed by nearby plant roots.
Oxygen that freshens the air around the decomposing material.
explanation: When decomposers break down dead organisms, they release carbon dioxide, returning carbon to the air and soil.

q: If a plant is grown from a cutting of another plant, how does it compare genetically to its parent?
options: It is identical — a clone carrying exactly the same genes.
It has half the genes of the parent, like offspring from seeds.
It has slightly different genes because cuttings mutate during growth.
It has the same genes only if both parent and cutting are the same age.
explanation: A plant grown from a part of another plant is a clone — it is genetically identical to its parent.

q: What is the chemical formula of table sugar (sucrose)?
options: C6H12O6
C2H5OH
CH3COOH
explanation: The chemical formula of table sugar (sucrose) is C12H22O11.

q: What striking thing happens when magnesium burns?
options: It burns with a very bright white flame.
It burns with a pale blue flame and produces black smoke.
It glows orange and crumbles to a fine red powder.
It burns slowly without a visible flame, releasing heat quietly.
explanation: Magnesium is an alkaline earth metal that burns with a very bright white flame.

q: Why does sweet juice take longer to freeze than plain water?
options: Dissolved sugar lowers the freezing point, so the juice needs a colder temperature to freeze.
Sugar makes the liquid thicker, so ice crystals form more slowly on the surface.
Juice contains natural acids that release heat and keep the liquid from freezing.
Sweet liquids have more air bubbles that act as insulation against cold temperatures.
explanation: When sugar is dissolved in water it lowers the freezing point, so sweet juice needs a colder temperature to freeze than plain water.

q: Why are the Chocolate Hills in Bohol called 'Chocolate' Hills?
options: Their grass turns dry and brown like chocolate in the dry season.
They are made of dark brown chocolate-colored volcanic rock.
Local cacao trees growing on the hills give them a chocolate-brown shade.
Brown clay soil on the hilltops is the same color as milk chocolate.
explanation: The hills are called Chocolate Hills because their grass dries out and turns brown during the dry season, resembling the color of chocolate.

q: When is the best time to harvest and eat okra?
options: While it is still young and tender.
After it has fully ripened and hardened on the plant.
Just after the flower falls off, before the pod begins to form.
When the pod has turned yellow, showing it is fully mature.
explanation: Okra tastes best when it is still young and tender; older okra becomes tough and fibrous.

q: Why does a swinging pendulum gradually slow down and stop on its own?
options: Air resistance and friction slowly take away its energy until it stops.
Gravity becomes stronger the longer the pendulum swings.
The string stretches over time, absorbing the energy of the swing.
The pendulum bob loses mass as it swings, reducing its momentum.
explanation: A pendulum's swings grow smaller because air resistance and friction continuously remove energy from the system until it finally stops.

q: Besides helping us hear, what else do our ears do?
options: They help us keep our balance so we do not fall over.
They detect temperature changes in the air around us.
They sense the direction of gravity to help us sit up straight.
They filter dust and germs before they can enter the throat.
explanation: The ears serve two functions: hearing and helping us maintain our balance.

q: What will you find inside an open cacao pod?
options: About 30 to 50 seeds arranged in rows, wrapped in a soft white pulp.
A single large seed surrounded by a hard dry shell with no pulp.
Dozens of tiny black seeds floating in a dark liquid.
A cluster of 10 to 15 seeds attached to a central woody stem.
explanation: A cacao pod contains about 30 to 50 seeds arranged in rows, each wrapped in a soft white pulp.

q: Why do reef fish have such bright, colorful bodies?
options: They use colors to recognize their own kind, find a mate, or warn others — not just for decoration.
Bright colors reflect sunlight and help them see in the dark parts of the reef.
Their colors come from the coral they eat, and brighter coral makes brighter fish.
Predators avoid brightly colored prey because the colors signal poison.
explanation: Reef fish have good color vision and use their bright colors for important purposes: recognizing their species, finding a mate, and warning others.

q: How does a mussel attach itself firmly to a rock?
options: It produces strong fibers called byssal threads that grip the rock.
It secretes a sticky liquid from its foot that hardens like glue.
It uses a powerful suction cup on the underside of its shell.
It wedges itself into cracks in the rock with its sharp shell edges.
explanation: A mussel sticks to rocks using tough fibers called byssal threads.

q: How often is deworming medicine usually given, and why?
options: Twice a year, because you can catch worms again after being treated.
Once a year, because the medicine stays in your body for twelve months.
Once every five years, because worm infections are very rare.
Only once in a lifetime, because the medicine permanently prevents reinfection.
explanation: Deworming medicine is given twice a year because people can catch worms again even after treatment, so the medicine must be repeated.

q: What does the Moon look like during a quarter moon phase?
options: Exactly half of the Moon's face is lit, so it looks like a half circle.
One quarter of the Moon's face is lit, making it look like a thin crescent.
Three quarters of the Moon's face is lit, so it looks almost full.
The Moon is completely dark and cannot be seen from Earth.
explanation: At first or last quarter, exactly half of the Moon's visible face is lit, making it appear as a half circle.

q: When an element symbol has two letters, how are those letters written?
options: The first letter is capital and the second letter is lowercase, like He for helium.
Both letters are capital, like HE for helium.
The first letter is lowercase and the second is capital, like hE for helium.
Both letters are lowercase, like he for helium.
explanation: The rule is that the first letter of an element's symbol is always capitalized and any second letter is always lowercase, as in He for helium.

q: What can happen if a child's stunting (slowed growth from poor nutrition) is not treated early?
options: The damage is often permanent for the rest of that person's life.
The child will fully catch up in height and development during the teenage years.
Stunting only affects weight, not height, so long-term harm is limited.
The child will recover completely as long as good nutrition begins before age 18.
explanation: If stunting is not addressed early, the resulting developmental damage is often permanent throughout a person's life.

q: How many protons does a potassium atom have?
options: 19 protons
17 protons
20 protons
11 protons
explanation: The atomic number of potassium (K) is 19, which means it has 19 protons in its nucleus.

q: Which of the following countries lies on the Ring of Fire?
options: The Philippines, Japan, Indonesia, and Chile
France, Germany, Spain, and Italy
Egypt, Kenya, Nigeria, and South Africa
Brazil, Argentina, Peru, and Colombia
explanation: The Philippines, Japan, Indonesia, and Chile all lie on the Ring of Fire, a zone of frequent earthquakes and volcanic eruptions.

q: How do mango and calamansi flowers guide bees to visit them for pollination?
options: Their colors and hidden UV patterns guide bees to find and visit them.
They produce a loud buzzing vibration that bees can feel from far away.
They drip sweet nectar onto their petals so bees can see the glistening drops.
They release a pheromone that mimics the scent of a bee queen to attract workers.
explanation: In the Philippines, flowers like those of mango and calamansi use color and UV patterns visible to bees to guide them for pollination.

q: How does the temperature of a lightning bolt compare to the surface of the sun?
options: Lightning is about five times hotter than the surface of the sun.
Lightning and the sun's surface are roughly the same temperature.
The sun's surface is about five times hotter than a lightning bolt.
Lightning is slightly hotter than the sun's surface by only a few hundred degrees.
explanation: The air along a lightning bolt heats up to over 30,000°C — about five times hotter than the surface of the sun.

q: Where do some birds lay their eggs instead of building a nest?
options: Right on the bare ground or sand.
In shallow holes they dig in the soil.
Inside hollow logs near the forest floor.
On floating mats of vegetation in ponds.
explanation: Some birds do not build a real nest and instead lay their eggs directly on the bare ground or sand.

q: After whom is Ohm's law named, and what did he do?
options: Georg Ohm, a German scientist who discovered the rule relating voltage, current, and resistance in 1827.
Alessandro Volta, an Italian scientist who invented the first electric battery.
Michael Faraday, a British scientist who discovered electromagnetic induction.
André-Marie Ampère, a French scientist who defined the unit of electric current.
explanation: Ohm's law is named after Georg Ohm, the German teacher and scientist who discovered the rule in 1827, and the unit 'ohm' comes from his name.

q: On a distance-time graph, what does a steeper line tell you about an object's motion?
options: The object is moving faster
The object is moving slower
The object has stopped
The object is moving backwards
explanation: On a distance-time graph, a steeper line means the object covers more distance in the same amount of time, so it is moving faster.

q: Why should you wash vegetables even if you are going to cook them?
options: Cooking kills germs but does not remove dirt, sand, or chemical residues on the surface
Cooking makes vegetables taste worse if they are dirty
Hot water removes more dirt than cold water during cooking
Steam from cooking cleans the vegetables automatically
explanation: Heat kills many microbes but does not remove dirt, sand, or chemical residue on the surface, so washing before cooking is still necessary.

q: What kind of energy is released when firewood burns in a cookstove?
options: Heat energy
Sound energy
Electric energy
Light energy only
explanation: When firewood burns, the wood turns into fire that releases heat energy used to cook food.

q: What is a gene?
options: A small unit of DNA that carries instructions for a trait
A type of cell found only in the brain
A protein that carries oxygen in the blood
A chemical that breaks down food in the stomach
explanation: A gene is a small unit of DNA that carries the instructions for a trait, determining inherited characteristics.

q: What happened to the church whose ruins are now called the Cagsawa Ruins in Albay?
options: It was buried by the 1814 eruption of Mayon Volcano
It was destroyed by a powerful earthquake in the 1800s
It collapsed during a typhoon and was never rebuilt
It was burned during a war and only the walls survived
explanation: The Cagsawa Ruins are the remains of a church buried by the Mayon volcanic eruption of 1814, with only the tip of the belfry still visible above ground.

q: About how many days does it take the Moon to orbit Earth once?
options: 27.3 days
365 days
12 days
90 days
explanation: The Moon completes one full orbit around Earth in about 27.3 days.

q: Why can a butterfly not fly right away after coming out of its pupa?
options: Its wings are still wet, crumpled, and soft and need time to harden
Its muscles are too weak and need days of eating before they work
It is confused by light and needs to rest its eyes first
Its body is too heavy until it digests its first meal
explanation: When a butterfly first emerges from the pupa, its wings are wet, crumpled, and soft; it must rest while fluid is pumped into the wing veins so they stretch out and harden before it can fly.

q: Why do many poisonous animals have bright red, yellow, or orange colors?
options: To warn predators that they are dangerous to eat
To attract mates during the breeding season
To blend in with colorful flowers and plants
To absorb more sunlight and stay warm
explanation: Many poisonous animals use bright warning colors as a signal to predators not to eat them.

q: What causes the whistling or wheezing sound during an asthma attack?
options: Air is squeezed through narrowed airways
Extra mucus vibrates in the throat
The heart beats faster and shakes the chest
Fluid trapped in the lungs sloshes around
explanation: The wheezing sound in asthma happens because air is squeezed as it passes through narrowed airways.

q: Why do vegetables pickled in vinegar last a long time without spoiling?
options: Vinegar is too acidic for most spoilage bacteria to survive
Vinegar dries out the vegetables so bacteria cannot grow
The salt in vinegar kills all bacteria inside the food
Vinegar lowers the temperature of the food to slow bacteria
explanation: Pickled foods last long because vinegar is too acidic for most spoilage bacteria to survive in.

q: Which river in Bukidnon is one of the main sources of the Rio Grande de Mindanao?
options: The Pulangui River
The Cagayan River
The Agusan River
The Davao River
explanation: The Pulangui River in Bukidnon flows from the mountains toward the Cotabato basin and is one of the main sources of the Rio Grande de Mindanao.

q: How many hydrogen atoms and oxygen atoms are in one molecule of water (H2O)?
options: 2 hydrogen atoms and 1 oxygen atom
1 hydrogen atom and 2 oxygen atoms
2 hydrogen atoms and 2 oxygen atoms
3 hydrogen atoms and 1 oxygen atom
explanation: The formula H2O means each water molecule contains 2 hydrogen atoms and 1 oxygen atom bonded together.

q: Why can you NOT see a synapse gap with just your eyes?
options: It is far thinner than the thinnest hair and requires a very powerful microscope
It is transparent like glass and lets all light pass through it
It is hidden deep inside the brain where no light reaches
It only appears when nerve signals are actively passing through
explanation: The synapse gap is so extremely thin — far thinner than the thinnest hair — that you need a very powerful microscope to see it.

q: How fast can a sloth move when it is on the ground?
options: Slower than about 0.3 km/h — it can barely run at all
About 5 km/h — similar to a slow human walk
Up to 10 km/h when it is in danger
About 2 km/h — half the speed of a walking person
explanation: On the ground, a sloth moves slower than about 0.3 km/h, making it one of the slowest-moving mammals.

q: Lightning can be hotter than the sun's surface, so does that mean lightning is more powerful than the sun?
options: No — lightning is tiny and brief, while the sun constantly pours out enormous heat over the whole Earth
Yes — because temperature is the best measure of total power
Yes — lightning strikes millions of times a day, adding up to more energy
No — because lightning only travels downward and misses most of Earth
explanation: Although lightning is hotter than the sun's surface, it is tiny and brief; the sun continuously releases far more total energy over the entire Earth.

q: What is a reef shark's skeleton made of instead of hard bones?
options: Cartilage — the same soft, bendy material found in our nose and ears
Keratin — the hard material that makes up our fingernails
Calcium shells — similar to the shell of an oyster
Dense muscle tissue that hardens as the shark grows
explanation: Unlike ordinary fish with hard bones, a reef shark's skeleton is made of cartilage — the same soft, flexible material in our nose and ears — making it lighter and more agile.

q: What is the purpose of a fire evacuation floor plan posted on the wall of a building?
options: It shows the fastest and safest route to the exits during a fire
It lists the names of firefighters who respond to that building
It explains how to use a fire extinguisher step by step
It marks the location of flammable materials to avoid
explanation: A fire evacuation floor plan is a map showing the fastest and safest route to the exits so that everyone knows what to do before an emergency happens.

q: Why can a very tall mountain in a hot tropical country have ice or snow on its peak all year?
options: The air gets much colder at high altitudes, even when it is hot at the base
Cold air from the ocean travels up mountain slopes and freezes the top
The shadow from the peak blocks sunlight and keeps the top frozen
Strong winds at the top blow away warm air and replace it with arctic air
explanation: Even near the equator, temperatures drop significantly with altitude, so a very tall mountain can stay cold enough for ice or snow at its peak all year.

q: Which three mountains are the highest in the Philippines?
options: Apo, Dulang-dulang, and Pulag
Mayon, Pinatubo, and Apo
Halcon, Kitanglad, and Pulag
Kanlaon, Dulang-dulang, and Mayon
explanation: The three highest mountains in the Philippines are Apo, Dulang-dulang, and Pulag.

q: Who created the Richter scale used to measure earthquakes?
options: Charles Richter, an American scientist, in 1935
Alfred Wegener, a German scientist, in 1912
Isaac Newton, an English scientist, in 1687
Marie Curie, a Polish scientist, in 1898
explanation: The Richter scale was created by Charles Richter, an American scientist, in 1935.

q: What do the broad, long wing feathers of the Philippine Eagle allow it to do?
options: Glide and soar above the forest
Swim quickly through rivers
Dig nesting burrows in soft soil
Run fast along the forest floor
explanation: The Philippine Eagle's broad, long wing feathers let it glide and soar high above the forest as it hunts.

q: For what reason is kamote (sweet potato) especially important in the Philippines?
options: It is used as a substitute for rice when rice is scarce or during calamities
It is the main ingredient in most traditional Filipino medicines
It is the only crop that can grow in saltwater-flooded fields
It provides more protein per serving than any other local crop
explanation: In the Philippines, kamote is used as a food substitute for rice when rice is scarce or during calamities.

q: A student has a very strong acid. What must be true for a base to fully neutralize it?
options: There must be enough base to match all the H+ ions the acid releases — amount matters, not just strength
The base only needs to be equally strong — strength alone determines neutralization
Any amount of a stronger base will always neutralize any amount of acid
You only need a few drops of base because strong bases work on any volume of acid
explanation: To fully neutralize a strong acid, you need enough base to match all the H+ ions it releases; if there is not enough base, some acid will remain.

q: How are a chameleon's feet specially shaped to help it live in trees?
options: They are shaped like little clamps that grip tightly onto branches
They are flat and sticky like a gecko's feet for climbing smooth bark
They have sharp curved claws like a cat for digging into bark
They are webbed like a duck's feet to help the chameleon balance
explanation: A chameleon's feet are shaped like little clamps that grip tightly onto tree branches, keeping it secure while moving through the trees.

q: How often does a potted cactus need to be watered compared to most houseplants?
options: Only rarely, because it stores water inside its body
Every day, because it dries out quickly in a pot
Twice a week, the same as most other houseplants
Only during rainy season, never in dry season
explanation: A cactus kept in a pot needs watering only rarely because it stores water inside its thick stem.

q: When a beam is loaded from above and bends, what happens to the top fibres of the beam?
options: They are compressed — squeezed together
They are under tension — stretched apart
They remain unchanged because only the bottom is affected
They crack first because tension is stronger than compression
explanation: When a beam bends under a load from above, the top fibres are compressed while the bottom fibres are under tension.

q: What does the PNRI (Philippine Nuclear Research Institute) do with radiation?
options: It uses radiation safely — for example to kill crop pests, sterilize medicine, and run hospital tests
It generates all of the Philippines' electricity using nuclear reactors
It stores radioactive waste from other countries deep underground
It monitors volcanic activity using radiation sensors around Mayon
explanation: The PNRI studies and uses radiation safely in the Philippines, applying it to kill pests on crops, sterilize medicine, and run hospital tests.

q: Which scientist proved that specific germs cause specific diseases such as tuberculosis?
options: Robert Koch
Louis Pasteur
Alexander Fleming
Joseph Lister
explanation: Robert Koch proved that specific germs cause specific diseases, including tuberculosis, laying a foundation for modern medicine.

q: What is Angel Alcala famous for in Filipino science?
options: Studying sea life and helping build artificial reefs so fish could multiply
Discovering a new species of deep-sea whale near Palawan
Inventing a method to purify seawater for drinking in island communities
Mapping the complete ocean floor around the Philippine Sea
explanation: Angel Alcala is a Filipino scientist who studied sea life and helped build artificial reefs to allow fish populations to grow.

q: Hydrogen (H) is placed in Group 1 of the periodic table. Does that make it an alkali metal?
options: No — hydrogen is a gas, not a metal, so it is not an alkali metal
Yes — every element in Group 1 is classified as an alkali metal
Yes — it reacts with water just like the other alkali metals do
No — hydrogen belongs in Group 0 with the noble gases
explanation: Although hydrogen sits in Group 1, it is not an alkali metal because it is a gas, not a metal.

q: What is the correct name for a baby swan?
options: Cygnet
Fledgling
Gosling
Chick
explanation: A baby swan is called a cygnet.

q: Which type of ultraviolet (UV) light does the ozone layer mostly block before it reaches Earth's surface?
options: The most dangerous type — ozone almost completely stops it from reaching the ground
The weakest type — ozone lets the most dangerous type through on purpose
All types of UV equally — ozone blocks every UV wavelength the same way
Only UV from artificial sources like UV lamps — natural solar UV passes freely
explanation: The ozone layer almost completely blocks the most dangerous type of UV before it reaches the ground; the weaker type still gets through and is what burns skin.

q: Why can bees find nectar more easily than humans can when looking at flowers?
options: Bees can see ultraviolet light, revealing hidden guide marks on flowers that humans cannot see
Bees have a better sense of smell and can sniff out nectar from a kilometre away
Bees memorise every flower's shape and return to ones they visited before
Bees are attracted to heat from flowers, guiding them to the warmest spot where nectar is stored
explanation: Bees can see ultraviolet light invisible to us, so flowers have hidden guide marks only bees can see that point them straight to the nectar.

q: How long can a saltwater crocodile live in the wild?
options: More than 70 years
About 20 years
Around 40 years
Up to 10 years
explanation: The saltwater crocodile can live for more than 70 years in the wild, making it one of the longest-lived reptiles.

q: How do army ants build a nest when they stop to rest during a march?
options: They link their own bodies together to form a living temporary nest
They dig a deep hole in the ground using their mandibles
They pile up leaves and sticks and glue them with saliva
They take over an abandoned termite mound and patch up its walls
explanation: Army ants have no permanent nest; they build temporary living nests from their own bodies by linking together while the colony rests.

q: An electromagnetic wave is described as 'transverse.' What does that mean about how it vibrates?
options: The electric and magnetic fields vibrate at right angles to the direction the wave travels
The wave vibrates back and forth in the same direction it is moving, like a compression wave
The wave only vibrates vertically, always moving straight up and down
The vibration spins in a circle around the direction the wave is moving
explanation: An electromagnetic wave is transverse because the changing electric and magnetic fields vibrate at right angles to the wave's direction of travel.

q: Animals called troglobites live their whole lives in totally dark caves. What physical features do they often have?
options: No eyes and pale skin with no pigment, because they do not need vision in the dark
Very large eyes to capture even the tiniest trace of light deep in the cave
Thick, dark-coloured skin to protect against cold cave temperatures
Oversized ears and nose to make up for weak eyes in low-light conditions
explanation: Troglobites typically have no eyes and are pale because they live in complete darkness and have no need for vision or pigment.

q: How does a worker ant share food with other ants that stayed in the nest?
options: It brings food up from its mouth into another ant's mouth
It leaves small pieces of food on the ground near the nest entrance
It releases a scent that guides other ants to food stored outside
It chews the food into a liquid and drips it onto the ground for others
explanation: A worker ant does not eat all the food itself; it brings some up from its mouth directly into another ant's mouth so the whole colony gets fed.

q: Why is the nucleus called the cell's control center?
options: It holds the DNA that tells the cell what to do
It produces all the energy the cell needs to function
It acts as a gate to control what enters and leaves the cell
It breaks down waste materials to keep the cell clean
explanation: The nucleus is the cell's control center because it holds the DNA that carries the instructions directing all cell activities.

q: In a Newton's cradle, you release one ball at one end. What happens at the other end, and why?
options: Exactly one ball flies out because momentum passes through the elastic collisions ball to ball
All the balls swing together because the force spreads evenly across all of them
Two balls fly out because the impact splits into two equal parts
No ball moves at the far end — the energy just makes the whole frame vibrate
explanation: In a Newton's cradle, exactly one ball flies out the far end because momentum and kinetic energy are transferred through each ball via elastic collisions.

q: Which two parts of the human body are true ball-and-socket joints?
options: The shoulders and the hips
The knees and the elbows
The ankles and the wrists
The hips and the knees
explanation: Only the shoulders and the hips are true ball-and-socket joints in the human body, giving them the widest range of movement.

q: When does your heart beat more slowly — when you are resting or when you are exercising?
options: When you are resting
When you are exercising
The heart rate is the same whether resting or exercising
The heart beats slowly only while you are asleep, not while resting awake
explanation: Your heart beats slower when you are resting than when you are exercising, because your body needs less oxygen at rest.

q: What is the capital city of Brazil?
options: Brasília
Rio de Janeiro
São Paulo
Buenos Aires
explanation: The capital of Brazil is Brasília, not the more famous cities of Rio de Janeiro or São Paulo.

q: Which crickets make the chirping sound, and why?
options: Male crickets chirp to call the females
Female crickets chirp to warn males away from their eggs
Both male and female crickets chirp equally to mark their territory
Young crickets chirp to signal to the colony that food is nearby
explanation: Only male crickets make the chirping sound, and they do it to call females during mating.

q: How many bones does a typical adult human body have?
explanation: An adult human body usually has 206 bones, fewer than a baby has because some bones fuse together as we grow.

q: What color does universal indicator turn when placed in a strong acid?
options: Red
Blue
Green
Yellow
explanation: Universal indicator turns red in a strong acid because a strong acid has a very low pH.

q: What do platelets do when you get a cut?
options: They gather at the wound to form a clot and stop the bleeding
They carry oxygen from the lungs to the wound to help healing
They produce the red color of blood that fills the cut
They release pain signals to tell the brain about the injury
explanation: Platelets are tiny pieces in the blood that gather at a wound to form a clot, stopping the bleeding.

q: Which TWO measures help protect you from mosquito bites?
options: Using mosquito repellent and wearing long sleeves
Eating garlic regularly and drinking lots of water
Keeping all lights off at night and sleeping on the floor
Washing hands frequently and avoiding sweets
explanation: Using mosquito repellent and wearing long sleeves are proven personal protection methods against mosquito bites.

q: What makes the Tubbataha Reefs in Palawan internationally recognized?
options: It is a protected reef recognized by UNESCO as a World Heritage Site
It is the largest coral reef in Southeast Asia by total area
It is the only reef in the world where whale sharks breed
It is the only place in Asia where living coral grows above sea level
explanation: The Tubbataha Reefs in Palawan is a protected reef that UNESCO has recognized as a World Heritage Site.

q: Why is it so hard to swat a fly with your hand?
options: A fly's compound eyes are very good at detecting fast motion
A fly's body is too light to be hit by a slow-moving hand
A fly produces a sound warning that tells it to move before you strike
A fly's wings let it teleport short distances to escape quickly
explanation: Compound eyes are very good at detecting fast motion, which is why a fly can see your hand coming and escape before it is hit.

q: What country was the famous scientist Niels Bohr from?
options: Denmark
Germany
Sweden
Norway
explanation: Niels Bohr was a Danish scientist, meaning he came from Denmark.

q: What does a battery actually do with energy?
options: It changes stored chemical energy into electrical energy
It creates brand-new electrical energy from nothing
It stores electrical energy sent in from an outlet
It converts heat from inside into electrical energy
explanation: A battery does not create new energy; it only changes the chemical energy already stored in it into electrical energy.

q: Where do catfish usually look for food?
options: At the bottom of rivers, ponds, and streams
Near the surface where sunlight warms the water
In fast-moving waterfalls and rapids
At the middle depth of the open ocean
explanation: Catfish live at the bottom of rivers, ponds, and streams where they look for food.

q: What is inside most of our bones that makes them strong but not too heavy?
options: A light, spongy part full of tiny holes
Hard rock-like material packed solid throughout
A thick layer of liquid water
Hollow air tunnels like a drinking straw
explanation: Many bones have a light, spongy part inside full of tiny holes, which makes them strong but light — not completely solid like rock.

q: Coral polyps are relatives of jellyfish and sea anemones because they all share which feature?
options: Stinging tentacles
Hard outer shells
Fins for swimming
Green color from algae
explanation: Coral polyps, jellyfish, and sea anemones are all relatives because they all have stinging tentacles.

q: When you pull off a thick shirt in the dark, you sometimes see tiny flashes. What causes those flashes?
options: Static sparks heating up the air as charge jumps across
The shirt fabric glowing from friction heat
Light stored in the fabric releasing at night
Sound waves turning into visible light waves
explanation: Those tiny flashes are static sparks — the light comes from the air heating up as the electric charge jumps across.

q: When blood sugar is too low, which hormone does the pancreas release to raise it back up?
options: Glucagon
Insulin
Adrenaline
Cortisol
explanation: When blood sugar is low, the pancreas releases glucagon, which raises the sugar back up — the opposite of what insulin does.

q: What happens to light when it passes through a concave lens?
options: It spreads apart and makes objects look smaller
It bends together and makes objects look larger
It bends sideways into a rainbow of colors
It passes straight through with no change
explanation: A concave lens, which is thinner in the middle, spreads light apart and makes objects look smaller.

q: What do we call the powerful explosion that happens when a very massive star dies?
options: A supernova
A solar flare
A black hole burst
A neutron flash
explanation: A very massive star ends its life in a powerful explosion called a supernova, which briefly shines like billions of Suns.

q: Why is paper easy to fold and write on?
options: Because it is thin and light
Because it is thick and stiff
Because it is made of metal
Because it is rough and heavy
explanation: Paper is thin and light, which is why it is easy to fold and write on.

q: What is special about a rodent's front teeth?
options: They keep growing for the rodent's whole life
They fall out and are replaced every year
They stop growing when the rodent becomes an adult
They can be shed and regrown three times
explanation: A rodent's front teeth keep growing for its whole life and never stop.

q: Why is it harder to start pushing a heavy box than to keep it moving once it is sliding?
options: Friction is greater at the start when the object is still
The box gets lighter as it picks up speed
Moving objects have more gravity pulling them down
Air pushes harder against still objects than moving ones
explanation: Friction is greater when starting a still object moving than when keeping it already in motion.

q: What material is a snail's shell made of?
options: Calcium carbonate
Keratin
Chitin
Cellulose
explanation: A snail's shell is made of calcium carbonate and is built by a tissue called the mantle; as the snail grows, its shell grows with it.

q: How does a doctor check if the thyroid gland in your neck is healthy?
options: By feeling the neck while you swallow, and sometimes using an ultrasound or blood test
By listening with a stethoscope placed on the throat
By shining a light inside the mouth and looking at the back of the throat
By checking the pulse at the wrist to measure hormone levels
explanation: To check if the thyroid is healthy, a doctor feels the neck while you swallow, and sometimes uses an ultrasound or blood test to check hormone levels.

q: A person has two copies of a gene, and they differ from each other. Which version will usually be seen?
options: The dominant version
The recessive version
Both versions equally
Neither version — a new trait appears
explanation: When two copies of a gene differ, the dominant version is usually shown and the recessive one stays hidden.

q: Who is considered the first Filipino hero because he resisted foreign invaders?
options: Lapu-Lapu
José Rizal
Andres Bonifacio
Emilio Aguinaldo
explanation: Lapu-Lapu is considered the first Filipino hero because he resisted foreign invaders.

q: Who was the first scientist to discover radioactivity coming from uranium in 1896?
options: Henri Becquerel
Marie Curie
Ernest Rutherford
Wilhelm Röntgen
explanation: Henri Becquerel first discovered radioactivity, coming from uranium, in 1896.

q: Why do some people see car headlights as streaky or starburst shapes at night?
options: Their eye focuses bright lights unevenly in the dark due to astigmatism
Their pupils are too small to let in enough light at night
The cornea swells slightly in cold night air and bends light
Their retina gets tired and blurs bright lights after sunset
explanation: People with astigmatism see streaky or starburst lights at night because the eye focuses bright lights unevenly in the dark.

q: Which strong metal is commonly used to build buildings, bridges, and vehicles?
options: Iron
Copper
Silver
Aluminum
explanation: Iron is a strong metal used to build buildings, bridges, and vehicles.

q: What is actually found inside a sugarcane stalk?
options: Sweet juice that must be boiled and processed to make white sugar
Ready-made white sugar crystals that can be eaten directly
Dry powder that turns into sugar when mixed with water
Colorless sap that is already the same as the sugar we put in drinks
explanation: Inside the cane is only sweet juice — it must still be boiled and processed before it becomes the white sugar we know.

q: Why does a drop of water pull into a round shape?
options: Surface tension tugs the water into the smallest possible form
Water molecules are always perfectly sphere-shaped on their own
Gravity squeezes the drop into a ball from all sides
Air pressure pushes the drop inward from the outside
explanation: Surface tension makes a water drop pull into a round shape because it tugs the water into the smallest possible form.

q: How does a geometry compass draw a perfect circle?
options: One point stays fixed while the pencil on the other arm swings around at an equal distance
Both arms move together at the same speed around a central mark
The pencil arm follows a groove carved into the paper
A spring inside keeps both arms the same length automatically
explanation: A geometry compass draws a perfect circle because one point stays fixed while the pencil on the other arm swings around at an equal distance.

q: What type of star is Proxima Centauri?
options: A red dwarf — small and cooler than the Sun
A yellow dwarf — the same size and temperature as the Sun
A blue giant — larger and hotter than the Sun
A white dwarf — the remaining core of a dead star
explanation: Proxima Centauri is a red dwarf, a small star that is cooler than the Sun.

q: How did most of the Philippine islands form?
options: Volcanic activity pushed land up from under the sea due to movement of tectonic plates
Ancient rivers deposited so much mud that land built up above the water
The sea level slowly dropped, exposing the tops of underwater mountains
Coral reefs grew tall enough over millions of years to become dry land
explanation: Most Philippine islands formed from volcanic activity, with land pushing up from under the sea due to tectonic plate movement over millions of years.

q: How are leafy vegetables like pechay grown in a vegetable garden?
options: Planted in rows and cared for with water and sunlight until ready to harvest
Scattered randomly and left to grow without watering
Planted in pots and kept indoors away from direct sunlight
Soaked in water buckets until their roots appear before planting
explanation: In a vegetable garden, leafy vegetables like pechay are planted in rows and cared for with water and sunlight until they are ready to harvest.

q: Which habit helps keep your kidneys working well?
options: Drinking enough water every day
Eating lots of salty snacks to give the kidneys more work
Holding in pee for a long time to strengthen the kidney muscles
Avoiding water after meals so the kidneys can rest
explanation: Drinking enough water, avoiding too much salty food, and not holding in pee for too long all help the kidneys work well.

q: How do some beach plants get rid of extra salt?
options: They push salt out through their leaves or store it in old leaves that drop off
They send all extra salt down into their roots and lock it there permanently
They change salt into sugar inside their stems before using it for energy
They absorb salt and release it as a gas through tiny holes in their bark
explanation: Some beach plants get rid of extra salt by pushing it out through their leaves or storing it in old leaves that will drop off.

q: What country was the pioneer microscopist Anton van Leeuwenhoek from?
options: The Netherlands
Belgium
Germany
England
explanation: Anton van Leeuwenhoek was Dutch, meaning he came from the Netherlands.

q: Which body parts provide the muscle power needed to walk and run?
options: The strong muscles in our legs and thighs
The muscles in our chest and shoulders
The muscles along our spine and back
The muscles in our arms and wrists
explanation: The strong muscles in our legs and thighs help us walk and run.

q: Where and when was the Philippine national anthem first played?
options: In Kawit, Cavite on June 12, 1898 during the declaration of independence
In Manila on June 12, 1896 during a military parade
In Malolos, Bulacan on January 23, 1899 at the opening of Congress
In Batangas on July 4, 1902 to mark the end of the revolution
explanation: The national anthem was first played in Kawit, Cavite on June 12, 1898 during the declaration of independence.

q: What job is the flowerpecker bird better at compared to the sunbird?
options: Spreading plant seeds
Pollinating flowers
Building the largest nests
Catching insects in mid-air
explanation: While the sunbird is better at pollinating flowers, the flowerpecker is better at spreading plant seeds.

q: Why does the anglerfish wait for prey rather than swim around hunting it?
options: Food is scarce in the deep sea, so waiting saves energy
The deep sea is too bright for the anglerfish to see while moving
Its fins are too small to swim fast enough to catch anything
Chasing prey would attract larger predators to its location
explanation: Because food is scarce in the deep sea, the anglerfish saves energy by waiting instead of chasing.

q: What happens when you bring the north pole of one magnet close to the north pole of another magnet?
options: They push each other away (repel)
They pull strongly toward each other (attract)
They spin around each other in circles
Nothing happens — only opposite poles react
explanation: Like poles (north-north or south-south) push each other away, while opposite poles attract each other.

q: How do swiftlets typically nest?
options: Thousands gather and build their nests together inside a single cave
Each pair claims a separate tree branch far from other swiftlets
They dig individual burrows in sandy riverbanks
They build floating nests on the surface of calm lakes
explanation: Thousands of swiftlets gather and build their nests together inside a single cave.

q: Why does the smell of burning incense eventually spread to every corner of a room?
options: Its tiny molecules diffuse through the air
The smoke is too heavy to stay in one place so it falls and rolls outward
Air currents from breathing push the smell around the room
Heat from the incense creates a pump that blows the smell outward
explanation: The smell of incense spreads through a whole room because its tiny molecules diffuse through the air.

q: What happens to your breathing after you stop exercising?
options: It slowly returns to normal
It stays fast for the rest of the day
It immediately stops for a moment before restarting
It becomes slower than your resting breathing for several hours
explanation: When you stop exercising, your breathing slowly returns to normal.

q: Who invented the Band-Aid adhesive bandage?
options: Earle Dickson, a Johnson & Johnson employee
Florence Nightingale, a famous nurse
Louis Pasteur, who also discovered germ theory
Alexander Fleming, who discovered penicillin
explanation: The Band-Aid was invented by Earle Dickson, a Johnson & Johnson employee, for his wife.

q: What do the two special pointed claws on a tarsier's feet help it do?
options: Clean its own fur
Climb steep rock faces
Grip and hold prey firmly
Dig for insects in the soil
explanation: Most of the tarsier's fingers have flat nails, but its two special pointed grooming claws on its feet are used to clean its fur.

q: What is the main role of mitosis in the human body?
options: Replacing old or dead cells, like skin cells
Producing egg and sperm cells for reproduction
Making antibodies to fight off disease
Converting food energy into new body fat
explanation: Mitosis replaces old or dead cells, such as the cells of our skin.

q: Which three metals are easily attracted by a magnet?
options: Iron, nickel, and cobalt
Iron, copper, and gold
Aluminum, nickel, and silver
Steel, tin, and lead
explanation: Three metals — iron, nickel, and cobalt — are easily attracted by a magnet.

q: Which element makes up about 46% of the mass of Earth's crust — making it the most abundant element there?
options: Oxygen
Silicon
Iron
Aluminum
explanation: Oxygen is the most abundant element in Earth's crust, making up about 46% of its mass.

q: What causes dead matter or food to rot, getting soft, changing color, and smelling bad?
options: Fungi and bacteria breaking it down
Sunlight drying it out from the inside
Water soaking in and dissolving it
Insects eating all the nutrients away
explanation: Rotting happens when fungi and bacteria attack dead matter or food — the softening, color change, and smell are visible signs that decomposers are breaking it down.

q: What actually makes an earthquake most dangerous for people?
options: Objects that fall and buildings that can collapse
The shaking of the ground itself under your feet
The loud rumbling sound that can damage hearing
Underground gas released during the quake
explanation: What makes an earthquake dangerous is not the shaking itself but the objects that fall and the buildings that can collapse.

q: Why can radio waves travel through the empty space between planets, even though there is no air?
options: Radio waves are electromagnetic waves made of vibrating electric and magnetic fields, not sound, so they need no medium to travel through
Radio waves bounce off tiny particles floating in space and hop from one to the next
Radio waves travel by vibrating the gravity field that exists everywhere in space
Radio waves are actually sound waves that travel so fast they don't need air
explanation: A radio wave is an electromagnetic wave — made of vibrating electric and magnetic fields, not sound — so it can travel through the airless emptiness of space, just like light.

q: How does a centipede catch its food?
options: It moves quickly and hunts small insects
It spins a web and waits for insects to get trapped
It digs a burrow and ambushes passing worms
It uses a sticky tongue to catch insects from a distance
explanation: A centipede moves quickly and hunts small insects to eat.

q: After getting a vaccine, why might you feel a mild fever or soreness at the shot site?
options: It is a normal sign that the immune system is working
It means the vaccine was given incorrectly and you need another dose
It shows an allergic reaction that requires medicine right away
It happens because the vaccine contains live bacteria that briefly multiply
explanation: After a vaccine, a mild fever or soreness at the shot is normal — a sign the immune system is working.

q: Why does the sky look blue during the day?
options: Blue light from the Sun scatters most easily through the air
The ocean reflects its blue color up into the sky
Blue is the color of oxygen gas which fills the atmosphere
Water vapor in clouds filters out all colors except blue
explanation: The sky looks blue because blue light from the Sun scatters most easily in the air.

q: Why does pushing a swing at just the right rhythm make it go higher and higher?
options: You are matching the swing's natural frequency, causing resonance
The extra pushes add up as stored elastic energy in the chains
Gravity pulls harder each time the swing returns to the bottom
The air resistance decreases each time, letting the swing travel farther
explanation: Every object vibrates most easily at its own natural frequency; pushing a swing at that rhythm causes resonance, making it go higher and higher.

q: According to cell theory, where does every new cell come from?
options: From an existing cell
From nutrients absorbed by the body
From chemical reactions in the bloodstream
From DNA unwinding inside an organ
explanation: According to cell theory, all living things are made of cells and every new cell comes from an existing cell.

q: Long ago, what plant materials were used to make the roofs of nipa huts?
options: Dried cogon and talahib grasses layered together
Flat banana leaves woven tightly in a grid
Split bamboo stalks bent over a wooden frame
Hardened coconut husks tied side by side
explanation: Long ago, people used dried cogon and talahib grasses, layered together, to make nipa hut roofs so rain could not get inside.

q: What is the jet stream?
options: A very fast ribbon of wind high up in the atmosphere that steers weather systems
A current of warm water in the ocean that affects coastal weather
A layer of the atmosphere that protects Earth from ultraviolet radiation
A narrow band of rain clouds that forms along the equator
explanation: The jet stream is a very fast ribbon of wind blowing high in the atmosphere that steers weather systems and can even speed up airplanes flying with it.

q: What is the main difference between selective breeding and genetic engineering?
options: Selective breeding changes genes directly while genetic engineering takes many generations
Selective breeding is only used on plants while genetic engineering is only used on animals
In selective breeding people choose organisms with good traits over many generations, while genetic engineering changes genes directly for a much faster result
Selective breeding produces organisms that cannot reproduce while genetic engineering produces fertile offspring
explanation: Selective breeding works slowly over many generations by choosing organisms with desirable traits, while genetic engineering changes genes directly to get the wanted trait much faster.

q: What can happen to your blood pressure if you eat too much salt over time?
options: It will stay the same because the kidneys always remove excess salt instantly
It can go down because salt helps the heart pump more slowly
It can go up, increasing the risk of heart and blood vessel problems
It will rise briefly then return to normal within a few hours
explanation: Eating too much salt can raise blood pressure over time, which is harmful to the heart and blood vessels.

q: Titan is special because it is the only moon in the Solar System known to have liquid on its surface. What is that liquid?
options: Water
Methane
Liquid nitrogen
Sulfuric acid
explanation: Titan's surface liquid is methane, not water — making it the only body besides Earth with liquid on its surface.

q: What type of magnet do MRI machines use to take pictures of the inside of the body?
options: Permanent bar magnets arranged in a ring
Very strong electromagnets
Small refrigerator magnets placed on the patient's skin
Magnets made from a special radioactive metal
explanation: MRI machines use very strong electromagnets to produce the detailed images of the inside of the body.

q: How does a self-resetting fuse in a gadget protect the circuit — and what does it do after the danger passes?
options: It melts to break the circuit and must be replaced with a new one
It stops letting current through when it gets too hot, then returns to normal by itself once it cools down
It sends extra current to a second path to protect the main circuit, then switches back manually
It makes a loud beep to warn the user, then continues allowing current to flow normally
explanation: Self-resetting fuses stop current when they overheat, then automatically return to normal once they cool — nothing needs to be replaced.

q: In 2022, NASA's DART mission showed that humans can do something important about asteroids. What did DART do?
options: It destroyed an asteroid completely by setting off an explosion on its surface
It changed the orbit of a small asteroid by crashing a spacecraft into it
It landed scientists on an asteroid to study its composition up close
It used a powerful laser beam fired from Earth to push an asteroid away
explanation: NASA's DART mission in 2022 successfully changed the orbit of a small asteroid by crashing a spacecraft into it, proving planetary defense is possible.

q: Why are there fewer flies in a clean environment?
options: Clean air makes flies fly away to other areas
Flies are afraid of soap and cleaning products
With no garbage and waste around, flies have no place to lay their eggs
Sunlight from clean open spaces kills fly eggs automatically
explanation: When surroundings are clean and garbage is properly disposed of, flies have no place to lay their eggs, so fewer flies are found there.

q: Which of the following is NOT a way germs can spread from person to person?
options: Through the air when someone coughs or sneezes
By touching a surface that a sick person touched
Through drinking clean bottled water
Through blood contact
explanation: Germs spread through the air, by touch, through dirty water, or through blood — clean bottled water does not spread germs.

q: A plant makes its own food through photosynthesis. Does it also do respiration to get energy?
options: No — plants only do photosynthesis and never need to break down sugar for energy
Yes — plants also use respiration to break down sugar and release energy for their own use
Only old leaves respire; young leaves only do photosynthesis
Plants do respiration only at night when there is no sunlight for photosynthesis
explanation: Plants both make food in photosynthesis and use sugar in respiration to get energy — they do not stop breathing.

q: What is one important way to lower the risk of getting leptospirosis?
options: Boiling all drinking water and avoiding fruit juices
Taking daily vitamin C tablets during rainy season
Controlling the rat population and keeping surroundings clean
Wearing sunscreen whenever going outside after rain
explanation: Controlling rats and keeping surroundings clean lowers the risk of leptospirosis because rats are a main source of the bacteria.

q: Why are lagundi and sambong used as traditional medicine in the Philippines?
options: They grow very fast and are easy to harvest, making them cheap alternatives
They contain substances that can help the body heal or feel better
They smell pleasant, which helps sick people relax and recover
They were brought by Spanish colonizers who proved they cure diseases
explanation: Philippine medicinal plants like lagundi and sambong contain substances that can help the body, which is why they are used as traditional medicine.

q: What happens to coffee beans after a civet eats them?
options: They are fully broken down and absorbed as nutrients during digestion
They are stored in the civet's cheek pouches and spat out later
They pass through the digestive system undigested and come out whole in the droppings
They are crushed by the civet's strong teeth and dissolved in stomach acid
explanation: Coffee beans are hard and are not digested in the civet's stomach, so they come out whole in its droppings.

q: Why does a drink with ice in it stay cold for a long time, even in a warm room?
options: Ice is so cold that it keeps cooling the drink steadily without needing to melt
Melting ice continuously absorbs large amounts of heat from the surroundings, keeping things cool
The drink has a special chemical that slows down the warming process
Water turns into a gas very quickly, and this gas keeps the liquid cool
explanation: To melt, ice must absorb a lot of heat from its surroundings — so the drink stays cold as long as there is ice still melting.

q: If you connect two batteries end to end in a circuit, what happens to the brightness of a bulb compared to using just one battery?
options: The bulb shines dimmer because the batteries share the load
The bulb shines the same because voltage does not affect brightness
The bulb shines brighter because the voltages add together and push current harder
The bulb flickers because two batteries create an uneven flow of electricity
explanation: Connecting batteries end to end (in series) adds their voltages together, pushing current harder and making the bulb shine brighter.

q: A venomous fish harms you in a specific way. How does it deliver its toxin?
options: You are harmed by eating its meat, which contains the toxin throughout
It sprays a cloud of toxin into the water around it
It delivers the toxin through a sting or prick, not by being eaten
Its skin releases toxin when touched lightly, just like a poison dart frog
explanation: A venomous fish delivers its toxin by a sting or prick, not by being eaten — that is what makes it venomous rather than poisonous.

q: Why do your ears pop when you are on an airplane or climbing a high mountain?
options: The noise of the airplane engine vibrates the eardrum and causes it to pop
Cold dry air at high altitudes enters the ear canal and makes a popping sound
The air pressure around you changes, causing the pressure inside and outside your ear to adjust
Your ears fill with fluid when altitude increases, which makes them pop when it drains
explanation: Your ears pop on an airplane or up a mountain because the air pressure around you changes, and your ears adjust to equalize the pressure.

q: Inside a battery, what is the role of the electrolyte?
options: It stores electrical energy in the form of static charge on metal plates
It separates the two electrodes so they never touch and the battery lasts longer
It is the substance that allows the chemical reaction between the electrodes to happen
It insulates the battery casing to prevent heat from escaping during use
explanation: The electrolyte inside a battery is the substance that allows the chemical reaction between the anode and cathode to take place.

q: Which everyday object behaves most like the way hot rock moves inside Earth's mantle?
options: A spinning top that slows down as its energy is used up
A lava lamp where warm material rises, cools at the top, then sinks again
A boiling pot of water that loses steam until the pot is empty
A candle flame that always points upward and never circulates
explanation: Mantle convection works like a lava lamp — heat from the core makes warm rock rise, cool, and sink in a cycle.

q: If you compare a goose and a duck, which bird is larger and has a longer neck?
options: They are the same size because they are both waterfowl
The duck is larger and has a longer neck than the goose
The goose is larger and has a longer neck than the duck
They are the same size but the goose has a longer neck
explanation: A goose is bigger than a duck and also has a noticeably longer neck.

q: A ball is rolling at a certain speed. If you double the ball's speed, what happens to its kinetic energy?
options: It doubles because speed and kinetic energy always change by the same amount
It triples because each extra unit of speed adds more energy than the one before
It quadruples because kinetic energy depends on speed squared
It stays the same because the mass of the ball has not changed
explanation: The formula KE = 1/2 mv^2 means kinetic energy depends on speed squared — doubling the speed quadruples the kinetic energy.

q: How do some monkeys use their tails when moving through the trees?
options: They use their tails to sweep branches out of the way while running
They use their tails to hold on to branches while climbing
They carry food in their curled tails as they move from tree to tree
They use their tails to signal danger to other monkeys in the treetops
explanation: Some monkeys use their tails to grip and hold on while climbing trees, which helps them move safely through the branches.

q: What does the santol fruit look and taste like?
options: It is a long yellow fruit with sweet flesh and thin skin, like a banana
It is a round fruit with thick skin and sour-sweet flesh, commonly found in Philippine forests and backyards
It is a small red berry with a very bitter taste found only in mountain forests
It is a spiky green fruit with a creamy white flesh that smells very strong
explanation: Santol is a round tree fruit with thick skin and sour-sweet flesh, commonly found in forests and backyards in the Philippines.

q: Why is it important to use clean jars, hands, and tools when fermenting food?
options: Dirty tools make the fermentation happen faster, which spoils the flavor
If unwanted dirty microbes get in, they can take over and spoil the food instead of fermenting it properly
The salt used in fermentation only works if the container is made of clean glass
Fermentation requires a completely germ-free environment or it will not start at all
explanation: If dirty microbes get into a fermentation jar they might take over and spoil the food, so clean tools and hands are essential for safe, successful fermentation.

q: What determines whether an object placed in water floats or sinks?
options: Whether the object is made of metal — metal always sinks and wood always floats
Whether the object is dry or wet when it enters the water
Whether the object is lighter or heavier than the water it pushes aside
Whether the water is warm or cold — objects only float in warm water
explanation: Buoyancy is the upward push of water; an object floats if it is lighter than the water it displaces, and sinks if it is heavier.

q: Where is pako (a fern eaten as a vegetable) usually obtained?
options: It is grown on large farms and sold only in supermarkets
It is imported from other countries and sold in markets
It is usually gathered wild from forests and riverbanks rather than being farmed
It grows only in home gardens and must be planted from seeds bought at stores
explanation: Pako is usually gathered wild from forests and riverbanks rather than being cultivated on farms.

q: What is the first step in making sugar from sugarcane?
options: The cane is dried in the sun to concentrate its natural sweetness
The cane is boiled whole in large pots of water until the sugar dissolves out
The cane is crushed to squeeze out its sweet juice
The cane's outer skin is peeled off and the inside is ground into a fine powder
explanation: The first step in making sugar is crushing the sugarcane to squeeze out its sweet juice.

q: When do a baby's eyes open during development inside the womb?
options: The eyes are open from the very beginning of development
The eyes open at about three months and stay open for the rest of the pregnancy
The eyes stay closed at first and only open later, closer to birth
The eyes never open inside the womb and only open for the first time at birth
explanation: Inside the womb the baby's eyes stay closed at first and only open later, before birth.

q: Why doesn't a haircut hurt?
options: Hair has very few nerve endings so it only hurts a little when cut
The scissors are so sharp that they cut faster than pain signals can travel
The part of hair we see is already dead, so cutting it cannot cause pain
Our brains ignore the pain of haircuts because they happen so often
explanation: A haircut does not hurt because the visible part of hair is already dead — only the root beneath the skin is alive.

q: The Puerto Princesa Underground River is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. In which year was it listed?
explanation: The Puerto Princesa Underground River was listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1999.

q: In which town and province is the colorful Pahiyas festival celebrated every year?
options: Vigan, Ilocos Sur
Lucban, Quezon
Dinagyang, Iloilo
Pakil, Laguna
explanation: The Pahiyas festival is held in Lucban, Quezon, where houses are decorated with colorful rice-wafer kiping.

q: Sweet foods like candy are called 'go foods' because they give us energy. Why should we eat only a small amount of them?
options: Because they contain fat that clogs blood vessels and causes heart disease immediately
Because they are so sweet that eating too much makes other food taste bland
Because too much sugar can harm our teeth and give us more sugar than our body needs
Because sweets slow digestion and make us feel sleepy right after eating them
explanation: Sweet go foods give energy from sugar, but eating too much can damage teeth and give the body more sugar than it needs.

q: Why can't a dolphin breathe while it is fully asleep?
options: Dolphins do not sleep at all because they must keep swimming to stay warm
A dolphin's blowhole closes tightly during sleep, which would cause it to drown
Unlike humans, a dolphin must think about each breath, so breathing is not automatic
Dolphins lose the ability to swim when asleep and would sink before they could surface to breathe
explanation: A dolphin must consciously think about each breath — breathing is voluntary for dolphins — so it cannot breathe while fully unconscious.

q: Why do colorful terraced platforms form around hot springs?
options: Algae and bacteria grow in the hot water and build up layers that form the colored terraces
Volcanic ash falls into the water and slowly piles up into the terraced shapes over time
Minerals dissolved in the hot water deposit as solids when the water cools and evaporates at the surface
The ground around a hot spring sinks due to the weight of the water, forming natural terraces
explanation: Hot spring water carries dissolved minerals; when it cools and evaporates at the surface, those minerals deposit as travertine or silica, creating colorful terraced platforms.

q: How many eyes does a spider have, and what do its large front eyes help it do?
options: Two eyes, which work together to give sharp color vision for spotting prey at a distance
Four eyes arranged in a square pattern that give it a full 360-degree view
Six eyes like most other insects, which detect motion but cannot judge distance
Eight eyes, with the large front ones helping a jumping spider judge distance before leaping onto prey
explanation: A spider has eight eyes; the large front eyes of a jumping spider help it judge distance accurately before it leaps onto its prey.

q: About how long does a human pregnancy last before a baby is born?
options: About six months
About nine months
About twelve months
About fifteen months
explanation: A human pregnancy lasts about nine months before the baby is born.

q: The plates at the Philippine Trench push together every year. How fast do they move?
options: About one meter per year, roughly as fast as a person walks in one second
Only a few centimeters per year, roughly as fast as fingernails grow
About ten centimeters per year, roughly as fast as hair grows in a week
Several kilometers per year but only during earthquake events
explanation: The plates at the Philippine Trench push together only a few centimeters each year — about as fast as fingernails grow — but over millions of years this greatly shapes the seafloor.

q: Why is General Santos City in Mindanao called the 'Tuna Capital of the Philippines'?
options: It is the only city in the Philippines where tuna can be legally caught and sold
The city is located on Tuna Island, the largest tuna habitat in Southeast Asia
