So much tuna is landed and processed there that it earned the nickname
The city hosts the world's largest annual tuna-eating contest every December
explanation: General Santos City earned the title 'Tuna Capital of the Philippines' because an exceptionally large amount of tuna is landed and processed there.

q: Why do clouds look white instead of the blue color of the sky around them?
options: Cloud droplets absorb all colors of light and re-emit only white light
The white color comes from the ice crystals at the top of clouds reflecting sunlight
Clouds look white because their larger water droplets scatter all colors of light equally
Clouds are made of water vapor which is naturally colorless and looks white against the blue sky
explanation: Clouds look white because their larger water droplets scatter all colors of light equally, unlike the sky's smaller air molecules which scatter blue light most.

q: Why does a carabao need to spend many hours grazing every day?
options: Carabaos sleep most of the day and must eat quickly in a short window of time
Carabaos have a very fast metabolism and burn energy quickly when working
Grass has only a little nutrition, so the carabao must eat a large amount to meet its daily energy needs
Carabaos eat slowly and waste most of the grass, so they need more time to get enough food
explanation: A carabao must graze for many hours each day because grass has only a little nutrition, requiring large quantities to meet its energy needs.

q: How does a rocket lift off the ground, according to the action-reaction principle?
options: The rocket's engines heat the air under it, and the hot air lifts the rocket like a balloon
The rocket spins its blades very fast to push air downward the way a helicopter does
The rocket pushes hot gas downward, and in return the gas pushes the rocket upward with an equal force
The rocket uses magnetic repulsion between the launch pad and its metal base to jump upward
explanation: A rocket lifts off by pushing hot gas downward; by Newton's action-reaction law, the gas pushes the rocket upward with an equal force.

q: What kind of animal is the civet, also called alamid or musang, found in the Philippines?
options: A large reptile that climbs trees and eats fruit and small birds
A small tree-climbing mammal that lives in Philippine forests
A nocturnal bird related to the owl that nests in tree hollows
A type of large insect related to beetles that resembles a small cat
explanation: The civet (alamid or musang) is a small tree-climbing mammal found in Philippine forests.

q: How does smoking affect the skin over time?
options: Smoking increases blood flow to the skin, which keeps it looking young and healthy
Smoking has no direct effect on the skin because smoke mostly damages the lungs
Smoking reduces blood flow to the skin, causing the face to wrinkle and age faster
Smoking dries out only the lips and throat but does not affect facial skin at all
explanation: Smoking reduces blood flow to the skin, so a smoker's face wrinkles and ages faster than a non-smoker's.

q: Why does frost on a cold window often form beautiful fern-like branching patterns?
options: The glass is curved, which forces ice crystals to grow in curved fern-like arcs
The patterns copy the fingerprints of people who touched the glass before it froze
Tiny ice crystals slowly join together, following little scratches and specks of dust on the glass as they grow
Cold air blows across the glass in swirling currents that shape the frost into leaf patterns
explanation: Frost forms fern-like patterns because tiny ice crystals slowly join together, following little scratches and dust specks on the glass as they grow.

q: What is happening inside an object when it feels hotter?
options: Its atoms are getting bigger and pressing harder against each other
Its tiny particles are moving faster inside it
A special type of energy called heat energy is being stored in empty spaces between its particles
Its particles are slowing down to release energy as heat to the surroundings
explanation: The hotter an object is, the faster its tiny particles move inside it — temperature is a measure of this particle motion.

q: You just finished eating rice for lunch and your blood sugar went up. Later, before dinner, you feel hungry again and your blood sugar is dropping. Which hormone helps at that later point?
options: Insulin, because it is always working to control blood sugar throughout the day
Glucagon, because it is released when blood sugar drops to help raise it back up
Adrenaline, because hunger is a stressful feeling that triggers the fight-or-flight response
Estrogen, because it regulates energy levels between meals
explanation: After eating rice, insulin works first to lower rising blood sugar; but when blood sugar drops again before dinner, glucagon is the hormone that helps raise it back up.

q: What were the Chocolate Hills in Bohol long ago, before they became the dry land we see today?
options: A range of volcanic mountains that eroded into rounded hills over millions of years
A coral reef under the sea that was lifted up as the land rose
A large lake bed that dried out and left behind thousands of mud mounds
A dense forest whose tree stumps decayed and hardened into the cone-shaped hills
explanation: Long ago the Chocolate Hills area was a coral reef under the sea; it was lifted up over time and became the dry land we see today.

q: The ABO blood type system is an example of 'multiple alleles.' How many versions of the blood type gene exist?
options: Two — one for type A and one for type B, which combine to make AB or cancel out to make O
Three — I-A, I-B, and i — which combine in pairs to give four possible blood types
Four — one for each of the blood types A, B, AB, and O
Six — two versions for each of the three main blood groups
explanation: ABO blood type has three alleles (I-A, I-B, and i) that combine in pairs to produce four possible blood types: A, B, AB, or O.

q: Why is oxidation classified as a chemical change rather than a physical change?
options: Because it always produces heat, which is a sign that energy is involved
Because the color or texture of the material looks different after oxidation occurs
Because it forms a new substance that cannot easily be turned back into the original material
Because it happens slowly over time rather than all at once like a physical change
explanation: Oxidation is a chemical change because it forms a new substance — and that new substance cannot easily be changed back to the original.

q: What did Archimedes discover about buoyant force?
options: The buoyant force equals the weight of the water the object pushes aside.
The buoyant force equals the weight of the object itself.
The buoyant force equals the volume of the object.
The buoyant force equals the depth of the water above the object.
explanation: Archimedes found that the buoyant force on an object equals the weight of the water that object displaces.

q: Which of the following is NOT one of the three main kinds of coral reef?
options: Patch reef
Fringing reef
Barrier reef
Atoll
explanation: The three main reef types are fringing reefs (along the shore), barrier reefs (farther out), and ring-shaped atolls; patch reef is not in this classification.

q: In a cave, where does a stalagmite usually form?
options: Directly below a stalactite on the cave floor
Directly above a stalactite on the cave ceiling
On the cave walls, away from stalactites
At the entrance of the cave where sunlight reaches
explanation: A stalagmite grows on the floor directly below a stalactite because the same dripping water builds both formations.

q: About what percentage of the world's earthquakes happen along the Pacific Ring of Fire?
explanation: About 90% of the world's earthquakes occur along the Pacific Ring of Fire.

q: How does soap help remove germs from your hands?
options: It makes germs slippery so scrubbing and rinsing can wash them away.
It kills all germs on contact without any rubbing needed.
It creates a protective layer that stops germs from entering the skin.
It dries out germs so they fall off by themselves.
explanation: Soap does not kill all germs — it makes them slippery and lifts them off, so scrubbing and rinsing are needed to wash them fully away.

q: How long can a whale shark grow?
options: About 12 to 18 meters, longer than a bus
About 5 to 7 meters, about the size of a car
About 20 to 25 meters, as long as two buses
About 3 to 4 meters, shorter than a classroom door is tall
explanation: A whale shark can grow about 12 to 18 meters long, which is longer than a bus.

q: Why does okra become slimy when you cut or cook it?
options: It has a sticky juice inside that comes out when cut, which also thickens soups.
Its outer skin breaks down and releases a waxy coating.
It produces a chemical reaction with air that creates a gel.
The seeds inside release a liquid that hardens when heated.
explanation: Okra has a sticky juice inside that comes out when cut or cooked, making it slimy and thickening soups or stews.

q: What is causing more frequent coral bleaching in Philippine reefs?
options: Climate change is raising ocean temperatures.
Overfishing is removing the fish that protect corals.
Ocean currents are slowing down and reducing nutrients.
Increased rainfall is making seawater less salty.
explanation: Climate change is raising ocean temperatures, causing more frequent and severe coral bleaching, including in Philippine reefs.

q: In what kind of climate does a jackfruit tree grow best?
options: Warm tropical places like the Philippines
Cold mountainous regions with frequent frost
Dry desert areas with very little rainfall
Temperate zones with four distinct seasons
explanation: The jackfruit tree grows in warm tropical places like the Philippines.

q: Who leads the Philippine Senate?
options: The Senate President
The Senate Majority Leader
The Senate Floor Leader
The Senate Speaker
explanation: The Senate President is the leader of the Philippine Senate.

q: Which of the following is part of a healthy daily hygiene routine?
options: Bathing, brushing teeth, wearing clean clothes, and washing hands
Bathing once a week, brushing teeth after meals only, and wearing the same clothes two days
Only washing hands before meals and brushing teeth at night
Wearing clean clothes daily but bathing only when visibly dirty
explanation: Daily personal hygiene includes bathing, brushing teeth, wearing clean clothes, and washing hands to protect health and prevent infections.

q: Why does heat conduction happen mainly in solids like a metal bar?
options: The particles stay in place and pass heat to neighbors without moving away.
The particles float freely and carry heat from one end to the other.
Metal particles release heat as light energy when they vibrate.
Solids absorb heat faster because they have more mass than liquids.
explanation: In conduction, particles stay in place and pass heat to their neighbors, which is why it happens mainly in solids.

q: Why do earthquake magnitudes often include a decimal point, like 6.3?
options: Because an earthquake's strength is rarely an exact whole number, so the decimal gives a more accurate reading.
Because seismographs can only display decimal numbers, not whole numbers.
Because the decimal shows the depth of the earthquake underground.
Because scientists add a decimal to separate the main quake from its aftershocks.
explanation: Earthquake magnitudes use decimals because shaking strength is rarely an exact whole number, and the decimal gives a more accurate measurement.

q: What should you do if you are sick and not getting better?
options: See a doctor instead of continuing to medicate yourself.
Take a higher dose of the same medicine for a few more days.
Rest at home and wait at least two weeks before seeking help.
Try a different over-the-counter medicine on your own.
explanation: If you are not getting better or get worse, you should see a doctor instead of continuing to medicate yourself.

q: How can floodwater spread leptospirosis?
options: Floodwater mixed with rat urine can carry the bacteria that cause leptospirosis.
Floodwater carries mosquitoes that bite people and inject the bacteria.
Drinking tap water during floods directly transfers leptospirosis germs.
Floodwater evaporates and spreads bacteria through the air you breathe.
explanation: During floods, water mixed with rat urine can carry the bacteria that cause leptospirosis.

q: Which planet has the shortest year because it orbits the Sun in only about 88 days?
options: Mercury
Venus
Mars
Earth
explanation: Mercury orbits the Sun in only about 88 days, giving it the shortest year of any planet in our solar system.

q: Where in the world can you find the tarictic hornbill?
options: Only in the Philippines
Only in Borneo and the Philippines
Throughout Southeast Asia
In the Philippines and Australia
explanation: The tarictic hornbill is a Philippine endemic bird found only in the Philippines and nowhere else in the world.

q: How is one strong silk thread made from silkworm cocoons?
options: Thin strands from several cocoons are twisted together to form one strong thread.
A single thick strand is pulled straight from one large cocoon.
Several cocoons are melted together and poured into a thread mold.
Strands are glued side by side and flattened into a ribbon.
explanation: Thin strands from several cocoons are twisted together to make one strong silk thread.

q: Why does a lacewing place its eggs at the tip of thin stalks?
options: So other insects cannot easily reach and eat the eggs.
So the eggs get more sunlight and hatch faster.
So the eggs stay dry and do not absorb water from leaves.
So wind can carry the eggs to a new location.
explanation: A lacewing places its eggs on thin stalks to protect them from being eaten by other insects that cannot easily reach the tips.

q: Why is the makahiya plant called by that name?
options: Because it folds its leaves when touched, as if it is shy.
Because it only grows hidden under large trees away from sunlight.
Because its flowers bloom only at night when no one is watching.
Because it has a very quiet rustling sound compared to other plants.
explanation: Makahiya means 'shy' because the plant folds its leaves when touched, making it seem bashful.

q: How many stamens does a gumamela flower actually have?
options: Many stamens joined together to look like one tube
Only one long central stamen
Five stamens, one for each petal
Three stamens hidden inside the petals
explanation: Although a gumamela looks like it has one stamen tube, many stamens are actually joined together to form that tube.

q: What is the MAIN purpose of a flower on a plant?
options: To make seeds so the plant can reproduce
To provide food for bees and butterflies
To attract rain by releasing a sweet smell
To protect the plant's leaves from being eaten
explanation: The main job of a flower is to make seeds so the plant can multiply; the nectar it offers bees is just a way to encourage them to help with pollination.

q: How do you read the time on a sundial?
options: Look at which line the sharp edge of the shadow crosses.
Count how many lines the entire shadow covers.
Measure the length of the shadow from the base.
Read the number where the tip of the shadow points.
explanation: You read a sundial by finding which numbered line the sharp straight edge of the shadow crosses.

q: Why is it risky to grow all your crops from cuttings or grafting?
options: All the plants are identical, so a disease that hits one can easily spread to all of them.
Cuttings grow more slowly than seeds, so yields are always lower.
Grafted plants cannot produce fruit, so they are only useful for shade.
Plants from cuttings have weaker roots that break in strong wind.
explanation: Plants from cuttings or grafting are genetically identical, so if one catches a disease the rest are equally vulnerable and can be wiped out together.

q: How is a shrimp different from a person, dog, or bird when it comes to body temperature?
options: A shrimp is cold-blooded so its body temperature changes with the water around it.
A shrimp is warm-blooded so it keeps a steady body temperature like people do.
A shrimp has no body temperature because it lives underwater.
A shrimp switches between warm-blooded and cold-blooded depending on the season.
explanation: Unlike warm-blooded animals such as people, dogs, and birds, a shrimp is cold-blooded, meaning its body warmth changes with the surrounding water.

q: How do some tilapia protect their eggs from danger?
options: They keep the eggs inside their mouth until the baby fish hatch.
They bury the eggs deep in the river mud and guard the spot.
They attach the eggs to underwater plants with a sticky coat.
They carry the eggs in a pouch on their belly like a kangaroo.
explanation: Some tilapia are mouthbrooders — they keep their eggs inside their mouth to protect them until the baby fish hatch.

q: How do some volcanic islands form in the ocean?
options: Underwater volcanoes erupt, and lava builds up until it rises above the water's surface.
Earthquakes lift sections of the ocean floor above sea level.
Strong ocean currents pile up sand and rock until an island appears.
Coral reefs grow so thick they eventually become solid land above water.
explanation: Some islands form from volcanoes on the sea floor — lava erupts and cools, building up until the mound pokes above the water as an island.

q: If you see a blue star in the night sky, what does its color tell you?
options: It is extremely hot — blue stars are the hottest kind.
It is very cool — blue means a star is losing heat quickly.
It is a young star that has not yet reached full brightness.
It is the same temperature as our yellow Sun.
explanation: Blue stars are the hottest stars; the color sequence from hottest to coolest goes blue, white, yellow, orange, and red.

q: Who invented the first pendulum clock, and when?
options: Christiaan Huygens made it in 1656.
Isaac Newton built it in 1687.
Galileo Galilei created it in 1602.
Benjamin Franklin designed it in 1752.
explanation: The first pendulum clock was made by Christiaan Huygens in the year 1656.

q: What does the top of a wind turbine do to keep generating electricity efficiently?
options: It turns so the blades always face into the wind.
It adjusts the blade length depending on wind speed.
It tilts the whole tower toward the direction of the wind.
It locks in place once the strongest wind direction is detected.
explanation: The top of a wind turbine rotates so its blades always face into the wind, keeping it generating power efficiently.

q: What is tuba, and where does it come from?
options: Tuba is sweet coconut sap gathered from the unopened flower of the coconut tree, which ferments into a sour drink.
Tuba is a juice squeezed from ripe coconut meat and sweetened with sugar.
Tuba is water collected inside a mature coconut and left to ferment in sunlight.
Tuba is a cooked paste made from dried coconut and fermented rice.
explanation: Tuba is the sweet sap gathered from the unopened flower of the coconut tree; it becomes a drink when it ferments and turns sour.

q: What is the 'hanging habagat'?
options: When the habagat wind lingers for many days of nonstop rain, often causing flooding.
When a typhoon stalls over the Philippines and the winds become unusually still.
When the habagat suddenly reverses direction and brings dry weather.
When a cold front meets the habagat and produces heavy thunderstorms for one day.
explanation: The 'hanging habagat' is when the habagat (southwest wind) lingers for many days of nonstop rain, which often causes flooding in cities.

q: How do tropisms help a plant survive?
options: They direct leaves toward sunlight and roots toward water and soil.
They allow plants to move away from predators that try to eat them.
They help seeds travel long distances so new plants can grow far away.
They make flowers open and close to protect pollen from the rain.
explanation: Tropisms help a plant survive by directing leaves to get enough sunlight and roots to reach water and nutrients in the soil.

q: Why do many deep-sea animals move slowly, grow slowly, and live a very long time?
options: Because the deep sea is cold and food is scarce, so they conserve energy.
Because the high water pressure crushes their muscles and slows movement.
Because they spend most of their lives sleeping to save oxygen.
Because deep-sea water is thicker than surface water, making it harder to move.
explanation: The deep sea is cold and food is scarce, so many animals there move and grow slowly and can live a very long time.

q: What do the tamaraw and the Philippine eagle have in common?
options: Both prefer a solitary life and do not live in large groups.
Both are found only on the island of Palawan.
Both are endangered because of the same disease.
Both build nests in the same type of forest tree.
explanation: Like the Philippine eagle that keeps its own wide territory, the tamaraw also prefers a solitary life — neither lives in large groups.

q: Which ancient civilization used hieroglyphs — a writing system made of pictures and symbols?
options: The ancient Egyptians
The ancient Greeks
The ancient Romans
The ancient Chinese
explanation: The ancient Egyptians used hieroglyphs, a writing system made of pictures and symbols.

q: Why does a lightning rod protect a building during a thunderstorm?
options: Lightning's electricity flows through the metal rod and is guided safely into the ground.
The pointed metal tip pushes lightning clouds away from the building.
The metal reflects the lightning bolt back into the sky.
The rod absorbs the lightning bolt and stores the electricity for later use.
explanation: A metal lightning rod conducts electricity so well that lightning's electricity flows through it and is safely guided into the ground, away from the building.

q: What does the tail of a colasisi look like?
options: It is short and rounded.
It is long and pointed, like a parrot's tail.
It is split in the middle, like a fork.
It is bushy and fan-shaped, like a peacock's.
explanation: The colasisi has a short, rounded tail, not a long tail.

q: Who is regarded as the first computer programmer in history?
options: Ada Lovelace
Marie Curie
Grace Hopper
Alan Turing
explanation: Ada Lovelace is regarded as the first computer programmer in history.

q: Can inherited color blindness be cured?
options: No, it has no cure, but people learn to live well with it.
Yes, it can be corrected with special eye drops taken daily.
Yes, a simple laser eye surgery can fix inherited color blindness.
No, but it always gets worse over time and can lead to total blindness.
explanation: Inherited color blindness has no cure, though people learn to manage and live well with the condition.

q: Why does your body shiver automatically when you feel cold?
options: Shivering helps make you warmer by generating heat.
Shivering pumps more blood to your skin to warm it up.
Shivering removes cold air from your lungs faster.
Shivering is a signal to the brain to find shelter.
explanation: When you feel cold, your body shivers automatically because the muscle movement of shivering generates heat and makes you warmer.

q: Why do many Filipino families plant a calamansi tree in their backyard?
options: So they always have fresh calamansi fruit close at hand.
Because calamansi trees keep mosquitoes away from the house.
Because the government requires each home to grow one fruit tree.
So the tree's shade keeps the house cool during summer.
explanation: Filipino families often plant a calamansi tree in the backyard so they have fresh fruit readily available at home.

q: Why are children weighed before and during a school feeding program?
options: To find out who is underweight and to track whether they gain proper weight over time.
To make sure no child eats too much and gains unhealthy weight.
To calculate how much food the school cafeteria needs to prepare each day.
To compare the children's weight with national test score averages.
explanation: Children are weighed before and during feeding programs to identify who is underweight and to track whether they are gaining proper weight after months of the program.

q: What happens during budding in organisms like yeast and hydra?
options: A small copy grows out from the parent's body and eventually becomes independent.
The parent splits perfectly in half to form two equal new organisms.
The parent sheds its skin, which then grows into a new organism.
Two parents each donate a cell that joins together to form a new organism.
explanation: In budding, a small copy of the organism grows out from the parent's body and eventually breaks off to become an independent organism, as seen in yeast and hydra.

q: Why does PHIVOLCS create lahar hazard zone maps after a major volcanic eruption?
options: To show which rivers and valleys could be filled with mudflows so residents know when to evacuate during heavy rains.
To mark areas where lava is still flowing so people do not step on it.
To record the exact boundary of the ash fall so farmers know which fields are safe.
To identify hills strong enough to serve as evacuation centers for nearby towns.
explanation: After a major eruption, PHIVOLCS creates lahar hazard zone maps showing which rivers and valleys could be filled with mudflows, helping residents evacuate safely during heavy rains.

q: When do wisdom teeth usually appear, and why might they need to be removed?
options: They emerge between ages 17 and 25 and may need removal if there is not enough space in the jaw.
They appear around age 7, alongside the first permanent teeth, and rarely need removal.
They grow in at age 12 to 14 and are removed because they cause cavities in nearby teeth.
They emerge before age 10 and are removed to make room for the permanent molars.
explanation: Wisdom teeth are the last teeth to appear, usually between ages 17 and 25, and sometimes need to be removed because they lack space in the jaw.

q: What does it mean when we say metals are 'sonorous'?
options: They make a clear ringing sound when struck, like a bell.
They can carry electrical current through a circuit.
They are shiny and reflect light from their surface.
They can be stretched into thin wires without breaking.
explanation: Metals are sonorous, meaning they produce a clear ringing sound when struck, just like a bell.

q: What is capillary action?
options: The way water climbs up narrow spaces or tubes without anything pumping it.
The process by which water evaporates from the surface of leaves.
The force that pulls water downward into the roots of a plant.
The way water molecules cling together to form large drops.
explanation: Capillary action is the way water climbs up narrow spaces or tubes on its own, which is why water rises into paper, soil, and plants.

q: A tow truck uses an electric winch to pull a stuck car free. What simple machine is a winch?
options: A wheel and axle
A lever
A pulley
An inclined plane
explanation: A winch is a wheel and axle — the motor spins a drum (the axle) that winds up a cable, pulling the vehicle free.

q: Why is copper wire so commonly used to carry electricity in homes?
options: It has many free electrons that move easily when electricity flows
It is the heaviest metal so it holds more charge
Its atoms are tightly packed so electricity cannot escape
It gets very hot and that pushes the current forward
explanation: Copper has many 'free electrons' that are not tightly held by their atoms, so they drift along easily when electricity flows.

q: Which two planets in our solar system have no moons at all?
options: Mercury and Venus
Venus and Mars
Mercury and Mars
Earth and Mercury
explanation: Mercury and Venus are the only two planets in the solar system that have no moons.

q: Which small part of the brain monitors body temperature and water levels to keep the body in balance?
options: The hypothalamus
The cerebellum
The medulla oblongata
The pituitary gland
explanation: The hypothalamus monitors temperature, water, and other levels and orders the right responses to keep balance in the body.

q: What protects the soft brain inside your head?
options: The hard skull and a thin fluid around the brain
A layer of muscle surrounding the brain
Thick skin on the scalp and the spine
Cartilage inside the head that cushions impacts
explanation: The brain is protected by the hard skull and a thin fluid around it, which is also why helmets are worn when riding a bike.

q: A refrigerator moves heat from the cold inside to the warmer room outside. What does this require?
options: Energy input, because this is against the natural direction of heat flow
No energy, because cold air naturally flows outward
Gravity, which pulls the heat downward and out
Only insulation, which forces heat to move the wrong way
explanation: A heat pump moves heat from a cooler place to a warmer one — against the natural direction — which requires work (energy input).

q: A forest can support a certain number of deer. Which statement about that limit is correct?
options: The limit changes depending on food, weather, and the condition of the forest
The limit is a fixed number that never changes no matter what
The limit only changes when a new predator enters the forest
The limit stays the same as long as the deer do not leave
explanation: Carrying capacity is not a fixed number; it changes depending on food, weather, and the condition of the place.

q: Some Philippine tree frogs protect their eggs by building what kind of nest?
options: A foam nest on branches or leaves hanging over water
A mud nest buried underground near a river
A leafy nest high up in the canopy away from water
A rock nest beside a mountain stream
explanation: Some Philippine frog species, such as tree frogs, build foam nests on branches or leaves hanging over water to protect their eggs.

q: The Philippines is part of an ocean area called the Coral Triangle. What makes this region special?
options: It has the most kinds of coral in the world
It has the deepest ocean trench on Earth
It is the only place where coral reefs can grow
It is surrounded by the warmest ocean currents
explanation: The Coral Triangle is an ocean area with the most kinds of coral in the world, and the Philippines is part of it.

q: Farmers plant mung beans between crops to improve the soil. How do legumes like mung beans add nitrogen to the soil?
options: Through Rhizobium bacteria living in their roots
By dropping leaves that dissolve quickly into nitrogen
By absorbing nitrogen from rain and storing it in the soil
By releasing nitrogen gas from their flowers into the ground
explanation: Legumes like mung bean naturally add nitrogen to the soil through Rhizobium bacteria in their roots, making them useful in sustainable farming.

q: How does a grasshopper make its chirping sound?
options: By rubbing a row of pegs on its hind leg against the edge of a wing
By vibrating a special pouch in its throat like a frog
By clicking two hard plates in its abdomen together rapidly
By blowing air through tiny holes along the sides of its body
explanation: Grasshoppers make sound by stridulation — rubbing a row of pegs on their hind leg against the edge of a wing, causing vibration.

q: In a food chain, snakes eat rats and rats eat rice. What would happen if all the snakes disappeared?
options: The rats would multiply and eat up the rice with no hunter to stop them
The rats would also disappear because they depended on the snakes
The rice would grow faster without rats eating it as before
Nothing would change because rats find other food sources
explanation: When one link is removed from a food chain, the whole chain is affected — without snakes, rats have no hunter and will multiply and may eat up the rice.

q: Some mushrooms glow with a soft green light in the dark. How do they produce this light?
options: Through a chemical reaction inside them
By absorbing sunlight during the day and releasing it at night
By reflecting moonlight off their smooth surface
By attracting fireflies that rest on their caps
explanation: Some mushrooms glow in the dark because they make their own light through a chemical reaction inside them.

q: Why does the Etruscan shrew stay active in short bursts throughout both day and night?
options: It must constantly search for food to survive
It is afraid of predators and cannot sleep for long
Its body cannot produce heat unless it keeps moving
It is defending territory from other shrews all the time
explanation: The Etruscan shrew stays active in short bursts throughout the day and night because it must always search for food.

q: Why is it dangerous to put metal inside a microwave oven?
options: Microwaves build up sharp electricity at the metal's edges, which can spark and start a fire
Metal absorbs all the microwaves so the food never heats up
Metal melts quickly and ruins the oven's interior coating
The metal reflects microwaves back and breaks the magnetron instantly
explanation: Microwaves build up sharp electricity at the metal's edges, which can spark and start a fire.

q: On a farm, animal waste is placed in a sealed tank with no air. What useful product comes out?
options: Methane gas that can be used as cooking fuel
Liquid fertilizer that powers electric generators
Clean drinking water filtered by bacteria
Compost that hardens into building bricks
explanation: In a biogas digester, bacteria break down animal waste without air and produce methane gas that can be used as cooking fuel.

q: Which group lists three examples of sedimentary rock?
options: Limestone, sandstone, and shale
Granite, basalt, and obsidian
Marble, quartzite, and gneiss
Pumice, feldspar, and schist
explanation: Limestone, sandstone, and shale are three examples of sedimentary rock.

q: In the phosphorus cycle, how does phosphorus get from soil back to the soil again?
options: Plants absorb it, animals eat the plants, and it returns to soil when organisms die and decompose
Rain washes phosphorus from clouds directly back into the soil each season
Plants release phosphorus through their roots after making seeds
Animals breathe out phosphorus gas which falls back onto the ground
explanation: In the phosphorus cycle, phosphorus moves from soil to plants, then to animals, and returns to soil when organisms die and decompose.

q: Why do some vaccines need a booster shot given later?
options: Protection can fade over time, so an extra dose reminds the body again
The first shot is only a test and the booster is the real vaccine
Booster shots use a stronger version of the germ to replace the first
The immune system deletes old vaccine information after one year
explanation: Sometimes protection fades over time, so a booster shot — an extra dose — is needed to remind the body again.

q: How many incisors (front cutting teeth) does an adult have in total?
explanation: An adult has 8 incisors — the flat front cutting teeth.

q: What plant is the source of piña fiber, used to make some traditional barong Tagalog?
options: Pineapple
Abacá banana
Coconut palm
Bamboo
explanation: Piña is a natural fiber taken from pineapple leaves; the fibers are woven into fine cloth used for some barong Tagalog.

q: Which type of rock has alternating light and dark bands and forms deep inside mountains under extreme heat and pressure?
options: Gneiss
Schist
Quartzite
Slate
explanation: Gneiss is a high-grade metamorphic rock with alternating light and dark bands that forms under extreme pressure and heat at the deepest roots of mountain ranges.

q: About how tall can a giraffe stand?
options: About 5.5 meters
About 3 meters
About 8 meters
About 2 meters
explanation: A giraffe can stand about 5.5 meters tall, making it the tallest living land animal.

q: Who was the first person to see bacteria and other microbes using a microscope?
options: Anton van Leeuwenhoek
Louis Pasteur
Robert Hooke
Alexander Fleming
explanation: Anton van Leeuwenhoek was the first person to see bacteria and other microbes through his microscope.

q: How do plants help stop wind from eroding the soil?
options: Their roots hold the soil in place and their leaves slow the wind near the ground
They release moisture that makes the soil too heavy to blow away
Their shade keeps the soil cool so it does not crack and crumble
They attract rain which wets the soil so it sticks together
explanation: Plants stop wind erosion because their roots hold the soil and their leaves slow the wind near the ground.

q: What happens to a plant's stem and leaves when it does not get enough water?
options: They droop and the plant wilts
They turn hard and woody right away
They grow faster to search for water
They drop off so the plant saves energy
explanation: When a plant lacks water, it wilts and its stem and leaves droop; watering it again makes it firm once more.

q: A gymnast bends her knees when landing to make the stop take longer. What effect does this have on the force she feels?
options: The force on her body is smaller because the stopping time is stretched out
The force doubles because her momentum needs to go somewhere
The force stays the same no matter how long she takes to stop
The force is larger because bending adds extra work to the stop
explanation: Stretching out the time of an impact makes the force felt at each instant smaller, even though the total change in momentum is the same.

q: What is the special feature on top of the Philippine eagle's head?
options: A crown of shaggy feathers that stand up like a crest
A bright red patch of bare skin like a rooster
A flat bony plate used to break open eggs
A tuft of white feathers used to attract a mate
explanation: The Philippine eagle has a crown of shaggy feathers on its head that stand up like a crest.

q: Where can bacteria be found?
options: Almost everywhere — in soil, water, air, on skin, and inside the body
Only in dirty water and spoiled food
Only inside the bodies of sick people and animals
Only in very hot or very cold places where other life cannot survive
explanation: Bacteria live almost everywhere — in soil, water, air, on skin, and even inside our bodies; there are more bacteria in our gut than cells in our whole body.

q: How can a singer's voice shatter a glass?
options: When the sound matches the glass's natural frequency, the vibrations grow until the glass breaks
When the sound bounces off the glass and creates enough heat to melt it
When the loud voice pushes air hard enough to physically crack the glass
When the high pitch changes the chemical bonds in the glass instantly
explanation: A very high, loud voice can shatter a glass when its sound matches the glass's natural frequency, causing destructive vibrations.

q: Which list correctly names energy sources used in the Philippines?
options: Coal, natural gas, geothermal, hydro, solar, and wind
Coal, oil, nuclear, tidal, and hydrogen
Geothermal, wave, biomass, oil sands, and nuclear
Solar, wind, tidal, natural gas, and uranium
explanation: The Philippines uses coal, natural gas, geothermal, hydro, solar, and wind as its energy sources.

q: What is the largest animal that lives on land?
options: The African elephant
The white rhinoceros
The hippopotamus
The giraffe
explanation: The African elephant is the largest animal that lives on land.

q: The Philippine flying fox can fly. What kind of animal is it?
options: A mammal — it is a large bat with fur that feeds its babies milk
A bird — it has wings and warm blood like all flying animals
A reptile — it glides using a thin membrane between its legs
An insect — it is the biggest flying creature in the Philippines
explanation: Even though it flies, the Philippine flying fox is a mammal — it has fur, feeds its babies milk, and is a large kind of bat.

q: What is a frog before it grows legs and comes onto land?
options: A tadpole that swims in the water
A larvae that lives inside a cocoon
A nymph that hides under rocks
A pupa that floats near the surface
explanation: A frog is an amphibian that starts life as a tadpole swimming in the water.

q: Two balls roll at the same speed. One ball is twice as heavy as the other. Which ball has more kinetic energy?
options: The heavier ball
The lighter ball
Both have exactly the same kinetic energy
The ball that was pushed harder, regardless of mass
explanation: At the same speed, a heavier object has more kinetic energy.

q: How does a scorpionfish avoid being seen by prey and predators?
options: Its color and shape blend in with the rocks and coral around it
It buries itself in the sand and breathes through a tube
It changes its color rapidly like a squid to confuse enemies
It hides inside empty shells on the sea floor
explanation: The scorpionfish hides among rocks and coral because its color and shape blend right in — a form of camouflage.

q: How does smoking harm the lungs' ability to clean themselves?
options: It damages the cilia so they can no longer sweep out mucus and particles
It shrinks the lungs so there is less room for air to enter
It thickens the lung walls so oxygen cannot pass into the blood
It dries out the lungs completely, making breathing painful
explanation: Smoking damages the cilia in the lungs, so they can no longer sweep out mucus and particles, increasing the risk of infection and lung cancer.

q: What are two important fish found in Laguna de Bay that support the livelihoods of many people?
options: Tilapia and milkfish
Bangus and tuna
Galunggong and tanigue
Maya-maya and dalagang bukid
explanation: Laguna de Bay is an important source of fish such as tilapia and milkfish for many people.

q: What is the opposite role of plants (producers) compared to decomposers in the carbon cycle?
options: Plants take in carbon and nutrients to build their bodies, while decomposers release them back
Plants release carbon into the air, while decomposers lock carbon into the soil permanently
Plants and decomposers both release carbon, just at different times of year
Plants only work during the day, while decomposers only work at night
explanation: Producers take in carbon and nutrients to build their bodies, while decomposers release those same things back — together they complete the cycle.

q: Why are spoons, forks, and cooking pots in Filipino kitchens often made of stainless steel?
options: It does not rust, is easy to clean, and will not taint food with rust
It is the cheapest metal available in the Philippines
It makes food taste better because it is a neutral metal
It conducts heat the fastest of all metals so food cooks quickly
explanation: Stainless steel does not rust and is easy to clean, making it safe for use with food and long-lasting.

q: Approximately how tall is Mayon Volcano in the Philippines?
options: About 2,462 meters
About 1,000 meters
About 4,000 meters
About 500 meters
explanation: Mayon Volcano is about 2,462 meters tall.

q: A metal nail is placed in dry air with no water. Will it rust?
options: No, because rusting needs both oxygen and water — one alone is not enough
Yes, because oxygen in the air is enough to make rust form on its own
No, because rust only forms when metal is heated to a high temperature
Yes, but very slowly, because air has small amounts of moisture in it
explanation: Rusting needs both oxygen from the air and water; one alone is not enough to cause rust.

q: What health risk do doctors warn about from frequent betel chewing?
options: It can harm the teeth and mouth over time
It causes problems only in people who also smoke tobacco
It damages the lungs but leaves the mouth unaffected
It is harmless as long as lime paste is not added
explanation: Doctors know that frequent betel chewing can harm the teeth and mouth over time, even though it is part of culture.

q: Where was the magnetic compass first developed?
options: Ancient China
Ancient Greece
Ancient Egypt
Medieval Europe
explanation: The magnetic compass was first developed in ancient China.

q: A friend says that eating a lot of chicken will put chicken DNA into your body. Is this correct?
options: No — your stomach breaks down the DNA in food into tiny pieces, and your own DNA does not change
Yes — small pieces of chicken DNA enter your cells and mix with your own DNA
Yes — but only if you eat the raw meat, because cooking destroys chicken DNA
No — but only because chicken DNA and human DNA are too different to combine
explanation: It is a mistaken idea; your stomach breaks down the DNA in food into tiny pieces, and your own DNA does not change when you eat.

q: What is the most effective way to protect your heart from smoking-related disease?
options: Never start smoking in the first place
Smoke only a few cigarettes a day to keep the amount low
Eat healthy food to cancel out the effects of smoking
Exercise regularly so the heart stays strong despite smoking
explanation: The most effective way to protect your heart is to never start smoking; it is okay to say no when offered.

q: A child is afraid to touch a millipede because she thinks it will bite and suck her blood. Is she correct?
options: No — a millipede has no fangs to bite or suck blood; it is the centipede that bites
Yes — millipedes have small fangs and will bite if they feel threatened
No — millipedes only bite animals, never humans
Yes — millipedes suck blood but their bite is too small to feel
explanation: A millipede has no fangs to bite or suck blood, so it is safe to hold; it is the centipede that bites.

q: Why do most reef-building corals grow in shallow, clear water and reach toward the sunlight?
options: The algae inside them need light to make food for the coral
Corals need sunlight to warm their bodies since they are cold-blooded
Sunlight bleaches the coral white so predators cannot see them
Corals use sunlight to harden their calcium skeletons faster
explanation: Reef-building corals grow toward sunlight because the algae inside them need light to make food — that is why reefs are rare in deep or muddy water.

q: Why do cities near the ocean usually have less extreme temperatures than cities far inland at the same latitude?
options: Seawater can store a large amount of heat, moderating the temperature nearby
Ocean winds are always cold and they cool coastal cities down all year
The ocean reflects sunlight away from the coast keeping it cooler
Coastal cities are usually at lower elevation where air is warmer and steadier
explanation: Because seawater can store a large amount of heat, places near the ocean have more moderate temperatures than inland places at the same latitude.

q: What tiny parts on your tongue detect whether a food is salty?
options: Taste buds
Nerve endings
Saliva glands
Taste pores
explanation: Taste buds on the tongue sense saltiness when salt dissolves in saliva.

q: Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the Philippines. About how large is it?
options: 900 square kilometers
500 square kilometers
1,500 square kilometers
300 square kilometers
explanation: Laguna de Bay covers about 900 square kilometers, making it the country's largest lake.

q: When you sit on a chair and push down on it, what does the chair do?
options: Pushes back up on you with equal strength
Pushes back up on you with less strength
Stays still because it cannot move
Absorbs your weight without pushing back
explanation: By Newton's third law, the chair pushes back up on you with the same force you push down with, which is why you do not sink through the seat.

q: Where does a mother kangaroo carry her baby?
options: In a pouch on her belly
On her back
In her mouth
Under her tail
explanation: A mother kangaroo carries her baby (joey) in a pouch on the front of her belly.

q: What happens to air pressure as you go higher up a mountain?
options: It decreases because there is less air above you
It increases because the air gets colder
It stays the same throughout the atmosphere
It increases because of stronger winds at high altitudes
explanation: Air pressure decreases with altitude because there is less air pushing down from above.

q: What fills the inside of the eyeball and helps it keep its round shape?
options: A clear jelly-like fluid
Blood vessels
A solid clear crystal
A layer of thin skin
explanation: The inside of the eyeball is filled with a clear jelly-like fluid that maintains the eyeball's round shape and lets light pass through to the retina.

q: If there are 365 days in a year and 24 hours in a day, about how many hours are in one year?
options: 8,760 hours
8,400 hours
6,570 hours
9,125 hours
explanation: 365 days multiplied by 24 hours equals 8,760 hours in one year.

q: What is one way to keep your lungs healthy and strong?
options: Exercise and play regularly
Eat more vegetables
Stay indoors away from dust
Sleep more than twelve hours each night
explanation: Regular exercise and play help keep the lungs healthy and strong.

q: Which metal has the highest melting point, at about 3,422 degrees Celsius?
options: Tungsten
Iron
Gold
Titanium
explanation: Tungsten has the highest melting point of any metal, at about 3,422 degrees Celsius.

q: Where do mangrove trees grow best?
options: Where rivers meet the sea and fresh and salt water mix
In the middle of the ocean far from shore
On top of mountains near freshwater streams
In dry sandy areas along the coastline
explanation: Mangroves grow best where rivers meet the sea, in the zone where fresh water and salt water mix.

q: When a red-flowered plant and a white-flowered plant are crossed and all offspring turn out pink, what type of inheritance is this?
options: Incomplete dominance
Complete dominance
Codominance
Recessive inheritance
explanation: In incomplete dominance, neither gene fully dominates, so the two traits blend and an in-between color like pink appears in the offspring.

q: What is the name of the Philippine colugo that glides between trees and is found only in the Philippines?
options: Kagwang
Tarsier
Dugong
Tamaraw
explanation: The Philippines has its own colugo called the kagwang, found in forests of Mindanao and Bohol, that glides between trees.

q: What happens when raw cassava is grated or crushed?
options: It releases cyanide poison from its cells
It produces a sweet juice that is safe to drink
It turns red because of a chemical reaction
It hardens and becomes difficult to digest
explanation: When raw cassava cells are broken by grating or crushing, the cyanide poison stored in them is released.

q: Even though the binturong looks like a bear, what animal family does it actually belong to?
options: The civet family
The bear family
The weasel family
The raccoon family
explanation: The binturong is a member of the civet family, not the bear family, despite its bear-like appearance.

q: What must a beetle do with its hard outer wing cases before it can fly?
options: Lift them open to reveal the soft flying wings underneath
Fold them tightly against its body to reduce drag
Vibrate them rapidly to generate lift
Shed them on the ground before taking off
explanation: When a beetle flies, it lifts its hard elytra (wing cases) so the soft flying wings hidden underneath can flap.

q: Archimedes was a famous scientist known for his discoveries in math and physics. Where was he from?
options: Ancient Greece
Ancient Rome
Ancient Egypt
Ancient China
explanation: Archimedes was an ancient Greek mathematician and inventor famous for his work in math and physics.

q: Which two units are commonly used to measure temperature?
options: Degrees Celsius and degrees Fahrenheit
Kilograms and grams
Newtons and joules
Liters and milliliters
explanation: Temperature is commonly measured in degrees Celsius (°C) or degrees Fahrenheit (°F).

q: What is a marine protected area?
options: A part of the sea that is guarded so fish, coral, and water animals can live safely
A beach reserved only for tourists and swimmers
An area where fishing boats are allowed to operate freely
A deep part of the ocean mapped for scientific study
explanation: A marine protected area is a section of the sea that is guarded and cared for so that fish, coral, and other water animals can live safely.

q: Which part of salt helps the stomach make the fluid that breaks down the food you eat?
options: The chloride part
The sodium part
The calcium part
The iodine part
explanation: The chloride part of salt helps the stomach produce the digestive fluid that breaks down food and allows nutrients to be absorbed.

q: Who invented the Richter scale, which is used to measure the strength of earthquakes?
options: Charles Richter
Alfred Wegener
Galileo Galilei
Isaac Newton
explanation: The Richter scale for measuring earthquake strength was invented by Charles Richter.

q: What is the main purpose of a cocoon for an insect pupa?
options: It serves as a safe place for the pupa while it changes
It provides food for the pupa as it grows
It attracts a mate for when the adult emerges
It keeps the pupa warm by generating heat
explanation: The cocoon serves as a safe, protective place for the pupa while it undergoes its transformation.

q: Your eyes, ears, and skin collect information about the world. Where are the signals sent so the feeling is actually formed?
options: To the brain
To the heart
To the spinal cord
To the stomach
explanation: The eyes, ears, and skin collect signals and send them to the brain, where the actual feelings and sensations are formed.

q: How does an amoeba capture and eat bacteria?
options: It surrounds the bacteria with its pseudopods and encloses them in a food vacuole
It uses a mouth to swallow bacteria whole
It secretes a poison that kills bacteria before absorbing them
It traps bacteria on its sticky outer surface
explanation: An amoeba feeds by phagocytosis — using its pseudopods to surround food particles and enclose them in a food vacuole where digestion takes place.

q: Why does a diamond sparkle so brilliantly when light enters it?
options: Light undergoes repeated total internal reflection because of diamond's very high refractive index
Light is absorbed by the diamond and then re-emitted as brighter white light
The flat surfaces of a cut diamond act as mirrors that reflect all light back
The carbon atoms in diamond produce light when struck by photons
explanation: Diamond's very high refractive index (2.42) and small critical angle cause light to undergo repeated total internal reflection inside, producing its spectacular sparkle.

q: If you place a third gear (an idler gear) between two gears, how will the first and last gears turn?
options: In the same direction
In opposite directions
One faster and one slower
Both gears will stop turning
explanation: An idler gear placed between two gears causes the first and last gears to turn in the same direction.

q: Why do herbivores like the carabao and horse have wide, flat back teeth?
options: To grind and chew tough plants like grass
To tear meat from bones efficiently
To crush hard insect shells
To hold and carry food without dropping it
explanation: Herbivores have wide, flat back teeth that are adapted for grinding and chewing tough plant material like grass.

q: Who created the two-word scientific naming system for all living things?
options: Carolus Linnaeus
Charles Darwin
Gregor Mendel
Louis Pasteur
explanation: Carolus Linnaeus, a Swedish scientist, created the two-word binomial scientific naming system for living things.

q: What does the Golden Record on the Voyager spacecraft carry?
options: Sounds, music, and greetings in 55 languages from Earth
Photos of every planet in the solar system
A map showing how to find Earth
Instructions for building a radio transmitter
explanation: The Voyager Golden Record carries sounds, music, and greetings in 55 languages representing life on Earth.

q: How are photosynthesis and combustion opposite processes?
options: Photosynthesis stores the sun's energy to make sugar and oxygen, while combustion burns fuel with oxygen to release energy
Photosynthesis happens only in the dark, while combustion only happens in sunlight
Photosynthesis produces carbon dioxide, while combustion produces oxygen
Photosynthesis and combustion both release the same amount of energy
explanation: Photosynthesis and combustion are opposites: photosynthesis uses sunlight to store energy in sugar and release oxygen, while combustion burns fuel with oxygen to release that stored energy.

q: How is a bacterial cell different from an animal cell?
options: Bacteria have no true nucleus, while animal cells have a nucleus surrounded by a membrane
Bacteria have a larger nucleus than animal cells
Bacteria have more organelles than animal cells
Bacteria cells are larger than animal cells
explanation: Prokaryotic cells like bacteria have no true nucleus or membrane-bound organelles, whereas eukaryotic cells like animal cells have a true nucleus surrounded by a membrane.

q: What is the spot called where light rays come together after passing through a convex lens?
options: The focal point
The optical center
The refraction point
The convergence zone
explanation: The focal point is where parallel light rays meet after passing through a convex lens; the light is brightest and most intense here.

q: Why does wrapping rice in a banana leaf or cloth help keep it warm?
options: It slows the escape of heat from the rice
It adds heat from the leaf to the rice
It makes the rice cook faster inside the wrap
It reflects sunlight back onto the rice to reheat it
explanation: Wrapping rice in a banana leaf or cloth acts as insulation by slowing the escape of heat.

q: Why are tilapia considered easy fish to raise on a farm?
options: They are hardy and can survive even when the water is not very clean
They grow faster than any other fish when given the right food
They do not need water and can survive in moist soil
They change color to warn farmers when the water is unhealthy
explanation: Tilapia are hardy fish that can survive even in water that is not very clean, making them easy to raise.

q: Which of these is a simple way every Filipino can save water at home?
options: Close the faucet while brushing teeth
Always leave the shower running for ten minutes before bathing
Use a hose to water indoor plants every hour
Flush the toilet twice to make sure it is clean
explanation: Closing the faucet while brushing teeth is one simple way to conserve water every day.

q: What does the liver do with old, worn-out red blood cells?
options: It breaks them down and removes them
It sends them to the lungs to be refilled with oxygen
It stores them until the body needs more blood
It converts them into white blood cells
explanation: The liver breaks down and removes old, worn-out red blood cells from the body.

q: In what year was the sampaguita declared the national flower of the Philippines?
explanation: The sampaguita (Jasminum sambac) was officially made the national flower of the Philippines in 1934.

q: How is hibernation different from ordinary sleep?
options: Hibernation is much deeper, making the animal hard to wake, and it lasts many days or months
Hibernation is lighter sleep that the animal wakes from each morning
Hibernation is the same as sleep but happens only during summer
Hibernation keeps the animal fully alert so it can sense danger
explanation: Hibernation is not ordinary sleep — it is much deeper, so the animal is very hard to wake, and it can last many days or months.

q: Which Philippine river has the largest drainage area (river basin) in the entire country?
options: The Cagayan River
The Pasig River
The Pampanga River
The Agusan River
explanation: The Cagayan River has the largest river basin, or drainage area, in the entire Philippines.

q: Why do crystals like salt have a regular, repeating shape?
options: Their particles arrange into a neat, repeating pattern as a liquid cools or water evaporates
They are squeezed into shape by the pressure of rocks pressing on them
They grow from seeds, just like plants grow from seeds in soil
Heat melts the particles together to form the same shape each time
explanation: Crystals form when their particles arrange into a neat, repeating pattern as a liquid cools or water evaporates, giving each grain its regular shape.

q: Mining can benefit the Philippines economically, but what kind of environmental damage can it cause if not properly managed?
options: Soil erosion, water pollution, and deforestation
Flooding from too much water being released underground
Earthquakes caused by deep drilling into the earth
Typhoons made stronger by the removal of minerals from mountains
explanation: Mining in the Philippines can cause environmental damage such as soil erosion, water pollution, and deforestation if not properly managed.

q: On a ship, a capstan is used to wind up heavy anchor ropes. What type of simple machine is a capstan?
options: A wheel and axle
A pulley system
A lever
An inclined plane
explanation: A ship's capstan is a wheel and axle: the long handles act as the wheel and the central drum is the axle that winds up heavy ropes.

q: Besides providing shelter, how do mangrove roots help young fish find food?
options: The roots trap drifting bits of food carried by the current so it stays within reach
The roots produce a special sugar that young fish can eat directly
The roots attract insects that fall into the water for fish to eat
The roots glow at night to guide fish to food sources nearby
explanation: Mangrove roots trap drifting bits of food carried by the current, keeping food inside the mangrove so young fish always have something to eat.

q: Why does a swollen lymph node sometimes feel sore when your body is fighting an infection?
options: The node grows quickly during infection, stretching its covering and causing pain
Bacteria inside the node release acid that burns the surrounding tissue
The node becomes too full of blood and presses on nearby nerves
White blood cells fighting inside the node heat it up, causing a burning pain
explanation: When a lymph node grows quickly during an infection, its covering stretches, which causes the tenderness or soreness you feel.

q: How does an octopus change the color of its skin?
options: Muscles stretch open or shut thousands of tiny pigment sacs in its skin
It releases colored ink that coats the outside of its body
It absorbs colored light from its surroundings and reflects it back
Its blood changes color and shows through its transparent skin
explanation: An octopus has thousands of tiny pigment sacs called chromatophores in its skin; muscles stretch them open or shut to change color.

q: If your hand gets cut and infected, which lymph node is most likely to swell up?
options: The lymph node in your armpit
The lymph node in your neck
The lymph node in your groin
The lymph node behind your knee
explanation: Lymph from the arm passes through the armpit lymph node first, so that is where germs from a hand infection are blocked and the node may swell.

q: What is the chemical symbol for the element sodium?
options: Na
So
Sd
Nm
explanation: The chemical symbol for sodium is Na, which comes from the Latin word 'natrium'.

q: What role does the lens of the eye play in helping you see?
options: It focuses light onto the retina, which then sends signals to the brain
It produces the fluid that keeps the eyeball moist and clean
It controls the amount of light entering the eye by changing size
It converts light into electrical signals and sends them directly to the brain
explanation: The eye's lens focuses light onto the retina at the back, and the retina sends signals to the brain so we can see.

q: Which change to a guitar string will make its pitch higher?
options: Making the string shorter
Making the string longer
Making the string thicker
Loosening the string's tension
explanation: A shorter string produces a higher pitch; pitch is also raised by increasing tension or using a thinner string.

q: How does a submarine dive underwater and then rise back to the surface?
options: It fills its tanks with water to sink and pushes the water out with air to rise
It uses propellers pointing downward to push itself underwater and upward to surface
It releases weights to sink and then uses rockets to shoot back up
It changes its body shape to become heavier or lighter as needed
explanation: A submarine sinks by filling its ballast tanks with water to become heavier, and rises by pushing the water out with compressed air to become lighter.

q: Where does the betel leaf (ikmo) used in chewing come from?
options: A climbing vine related to pepper
The areca palm tree
A tropical fern
A type of banana plant
explanation: The betel leaf (ikmo) comes from a climbing vine related to pepper, not from the areca palm.

q: What shape is a cacao pod?
options: Round like a ball
Egg-shaped or like a small football
Flat like a leaf
Long and thin like a banana
explanation: A cacao pod is shaped like an egg or a small football, and is about as big as two hands put together.

q: Why are many Philippine animals in danger of disappearing?
options: They are hunted for food every year
Their forest homes are cut down
Ocean pollution is spreading inland
They cannot find enough water
explanation: When trees are cut down, animals lose their forest homes and are in danger of disappearing completely.

q: In a rainbow, which color always appears on the outer edge?
options: Violet
Blue
Yellow
Red
explanation: The colors in a rainbow are always in the same order, with red on the outer edge and violet on the inner edge.

q: What does the name 'tardigrade' mean?
options: Hard survivor
Slow walker
Water bear
Tiny creature
explanation: The name 'tardigrade' means 'slow walker,' and these tiny animals were first described in 1773.

q: Why does a cold glass get wet on the outside even without being dipped in water?
options: Water seeps through the glass walls
Water vapor in the warm air turns to liquid on the cold surface
The ice inside melts and drips down
Cold air pushes water up from the table
explanation: Water vapor in the warm air touches the cold glass, loses energy, and condenses into tiny drops of liquid water on the outside.

q: How much farther is the Sun from Earth compared to the Moon?
options: About 10 times farther
About 100 times farther
About 390 times farther
About 1,000 times farther
explanation: The Sun is about 390 times farther from Earth than the Moon is.

q: How do many moths hide from birds during the day?
options: They fold their wings to look like leaves
Their wing colors look like tree bark
They sleep deep inside hollow logs
They fly very fast to escape
explanation: Many moths have colors that look like tree bark, helping them hide from birds during the day.

q: Is it safe to hug someone who has Hepatitis B?
options: No, hugging spreads it easily
No, any skin contact spreads it
Yes, hugging and touching do not spread Hepatitis B
Yes, but only with gloves on
explanation: Hepatitis B is not spread by hugging or touching, so it is safe to be around a person who has it.

q: What can very old trees have thousands of inside their trunks?
options: Layers of bark
Growth rings
Seed chambers
Root canals
explanation: Some trees live for thousands of years, so their trunks hold thousands of rings to count.

q: What connects the two halves of the brain so they can work together?
options: The spinal cord
The corpus callosum
The cerebellum
The brain stem
explanation: The two halves of the brain are joined by a thick bridge of nerves called the corpus callosum.

q: Which of the two moons of Mars is the larger one?
options: Deimos
Titan
Phobos
Callisto
explanation: Mars has two moons — Phobos is the larger one and Deimos is the smaller one.

q: Why is the water pressure very strong at the bottom of the sea?
options: Heat from the ocean floor pushes down
The weight of all the water above creates high pressure
Underwater currents squeeze tightly together
Salt water is heavier only near the surface
explanation: The deeper you go in the sea, the higher the water pressure because of the weight of all the water above.

q: What is natural selection in relation to evolution?
options: The fact that living things change over time
A myth rejected by most scientists
The mechanism that explains how evolution happens
The same thing as evolution, just a different word
explanation: Natural selection is the scientific explanation (mechanism) for how evolution — the change of life forms over time — happens.

q: Why do rock climbers put chalk on their hands?
options: To make their skin softer and more flexible
To absorb sweat and increase friction with the rock
To protect their hands from cuts
To keep their hands warm in cold weather
explanation: Chalk absorbs sweat from climbers' hands, which increases friction between the hand and the rock holds.

q: What happens to the pitch of a wind instrument when the tube is longer?
options: The pitch gets higher
The sound gets louder
The pitch gets lower
The sound becomes softer
explanation: A longer air column gives a longer wavelength, which produces a lower pitch in wind instruments.

q: Who should sing the Philippine national anthem when it is played?
options: Only government officials
Only students in school
Only trained singers
Everyone present should sing along
explanation: Everyone present should sing the national anthem together to show that we are one nation.

q: What rocket launched the Apollo 11 mission to the Moon in 1969?
options: Falcon 9
Saturn V
Atlas V
Ariane 5
explanation: Apollo 11 was sent to the Moon by the giant Saturn V rocket in 1969.

q: Which metal is liquid at room temperature?
options: Iron
Lead
Mercury
Aluminum
explanation: Mercury, with the symbol Hg, is the only metal that is liquid at room temperature.

q: How can you check if yeast is still alive before using it in baking?
options: Smell it — live yeast has no smell
Mix it with hot water and salt; it will turn red if alive
Mix it with warm water and a little sugar; it bubbles if alive
Freeze it overnight and check if it changes color
explanation: Mixing yeast with warm water and a little sugar causes it to bubble and foam if it is alive and ready to use.

q: What injury can happen if you look at a welding arc without a proper mask?
options: Temporary blindness called tunnel vision
A painful eye burn called arc eye
Headache and dizziness from the sparks
Ear damage from the loud sound
explanation: The intense light from a welding arc can burn your eyes, causing a painful injury called arc eye.

q: What causes the colorful glowing lights called an aurora in the sky near the poles?
options: Sunlight reflected off polar ice
Particles from the sun hitting gases high in the atmosphere
Lightning storms in the upper atmosphere
Moonlight bending through thick clouds
explanation: An aurora forms when particles from the sun hit gases high in the atmosphere near Earth's poles, creating glowing colors.

q: What is a Punnett square used for?
options: Counting chromosomes under a microscope
Predicting possible traits of offspring based on parents' alleles
Drawing the structure of a DNA strand
Measuring how fast cells divide
explanation: A Punnett square is a grid scientists use to predict the possible traits of offspring based on the parents' alleles.

q: What is the correct way to treat the actual Philippine flag?
options: It can be worn as a costume during national holidays
It may be used as a bandana to show patriotism
It should not be used as clothing or body decoration
It can be turned into a uniform for special events
explanation: The real Philippine flag should not be used as clothing or body decoration — respecting the flag means it is not simply worn.

q: Why is palay (rice grain) spread out under the sun to dry?
options: To make it harder so it is easier to cook
To remove water so mold will not grow and spoil it
To add more nutrients from sunlight before storage
To separate unhulled grains from the hulled ones
explanation: Palay is dried under the sun so the water leaves it, making it less likely to grow mold or spoil before storage.

q: Why are mosquito larvae called 'wrigglers'?
options: They change color like a wriggling rainbow
They spin webs to wriggle up to the surface
They twist and squirm when they swim
They wriggle out of their skin every day
explanation: Mosquito larvae are called wrigglers because they twist and squirm as they swim, flicking their body into an S-shape to push away from danger.

q: How is a moth's body different from a butterfly's body?
options: Moths have a thicker, fuzzier body while butterflies have a thin, smooth body
Moths have a thin, smooth body while butterflies have a thick, fuzzy body
Both insects have the same thick, fuzzy body
Both insects have the same thin, smooth body
explanation: Moths often have a thick, fuzzy body, while butterflies have a thin, smooth body.

q: In some dung beetle species, what do the male and female do together?
options: They fly together to find food for their young
They work together, with one rolling the dung ball while the other pushes or follows
They take turns guarding the nest while the other sleeps
They dig separate burrows and meet only to mate
explanation: In some dung beetle species, the male and female work together — one rolls the dung ball while its partner follows or pushes it toward the burrow.

q: Why should you avoid touching stray or unfamiliar animals?
options: They may steal food from you
You could get bitten and risk getting diseases like rabies
They might make a mess in your yard
They will follow you home if you touch them
explanation: Avoid touching stray or unfamiliar animals so you do not get bitten and risk contracting diseases like rabies.

q: Why does the Philippine rainforest have more kinds of fruits and trees than cold places?
options: Cold places have better soil for farming
The Philippines imports seeds from all over the world
Warm, rainy forests support a much greater variety of plants
Cold places have too much water for fruit trees to grow
explanation: The warm, rainy forest of the Philippines supports a great many kinds of fruits and trees, far more than cold places.

q: Why are laws and reserves set up to protect animals like the Philippine eagle and tamaraw?
options: To study their behavior for school projects
Because they are endangered and at risk of disappearing
To prevent them from attacking farms
Because they are being raised for food
explanation: Animals like the Philippine eagle and tamaraw are endangered, so laws and reserves exist to protect them from disappearing.

q: How does a natural rock arch form along a coastline?
options: A big earthquake splits the rock in half
Volcanic lava cools and leaves a curved gap
Waves slowly carve away the weaker part of the rock until a hole opens
Wind blows sand that cuts a tunnel through the rock
explanation: A natural rock arch forms when strong waves slowly carve away the weaker part of the rock until a hole opens, leaving a bridge of stone.

q: Which of these is an example of a product made from recycled materials?
options: A fresh mango picked from a tree
Clothes made from recycled plastic bottles
A glass of water from a spring
A new piece of wood cut from a log
explanation: Recycled plastic bottles can be turned into new clothes, showing that recycled materials can make useful new products.

q: Why does a person with anemia get short of breath easily?
options: Their lungs are too small to take in air
Their muscles work twice as hard and waste oxygen
Their body struggles to carry enough oxygen because of low red blood cells
They breathe too fast and use up oxygen quickly
explanation: A person with anemia may get short of breath easily because the body struggles to carry enough oxygen.

q: Which cells in the eye help you see colors in bright light?
options: Rods
Cones
Cornea cells
Pupil cells
explanation: The retina contains cones for color vision in bright light and rods for low-light and black-and-white vision.

q: Why is the Rafflesia flower protected by law?
options: It is poisonous and must be kept away from children
Forests being cut down put it in danger of disappearing, so it must not be picked or harmed
It is the national flower and may only be displayed on national holidays
It grows too fast and blocks paths in nature reserves
explanation: The Rafflesia is in danger of disappearing because forests are being cut down, so it is protected and must not be picked or harmed.

q: What do ecologists measure to judge how healthy a land area is?
options: The number of rivers and lakes present
The average temperature and rainfall each month
The percentage of the land covered by plants (vegetation cover)
The depth of the soil layer underground
explanation: Vegetation cover percentage — how much of the land is covered by plants — is a simple measure of habitat quality used by ecologists.

q: How many days are in a normal year?
explanation: There are 365 days in a normal year.

q: Why does a person with blood type AB have both A and B antigens?
options: One antigen hides the other in a process called dominance
Both A and B genes are present and both show themselves because of codominance
The body makes both antigens on its own without genes
Only one gene is needed to make both A and B antigens
explanation: Type AB results from codominance: both the A gene and the B gene are present, and neither hides the other, so both antigens appear.

q: Who built one of the earliest devices that could show changes in temperature, called a thermoscope?
options: Isaac Newton
Charles Darwin
Albert Einstein
Galileo Galilei
explanation: Galileo Galilei built one of the earliest thermoscopes around 1593, a device that showed changes in temperature.

q: What is a structural adaptation?
options: A behavior an animal learns from its parents
A change an animal makes to survive cold weather
A physical body part like wings, teeth, or claws that helps an animal survive
A chemical the body makes to fight disease
explanation: A structural adaptation is a physical body part such as wings, teeth, or claws that helps an animal survive.

q: What gives red algae their red or pink color?
options: Chlorophyll, the same pigment that makes land plants green
A pigment called phycoerythrin that also helps absorb dim light at depth
Iron particles absorbed from the ocean floor
Sunlight reflected off the water surface
explanation: Red algae contain a pigment called phycoerythrin that gives them their red or pink color and helps them absorb dim light at greater ocean depths.

q: Why does a malnourished child get sick more easily?
options: They eat too much sugar which feeds harmful bacteria
They sleep less, giving the body less time to recover
Lacking nutrients weakens the body's defenses against germs
They drink too much water which dilutes their blood
explanation: Lacking nutrients weakens the body's defenses against germs, making a malnourished child easier to get sick.

q: How do some plants like the sandbox tree spread their seeds far away?
options: Birds carry the seeds in their beaks and drop them elsewhere
The seeds float on wind currents for long distances
Their pods burst open explosively when dry, shooting seeds several metres away
The seeds stick to animal fur and are carried away
explanation: Some plants like the sandbox tree explosively burst their pods when dry, shooting seeds several metres away from the parent plant.

q: What happens when the body does not get enough iron?
options: Bones become soft and break easily
Teeth turn yellow and fall out
A person can get anemia, feeling tired and weak
Vision becomes blurry and the eyes hurt
explanation: When the body lacks iron, a person can get anemia, which makes them feel tired and weak.

q: Which part of the malunggay plant besides its leaves can also be eaten as a vegetable?
