It uses a magnet to attract the strongest radio wave nearby
It connects only to the station whose antenna is closest
explanation: A radio uses resonance to pick one station by matching the frequency of that station's signal.

q: Why can a vaccine usually NOT give you the real disease?
options: The germ inside the vaccine is dead or too weakened to infect you
The vaccine travels only to muscles, not to the blood
Your nose and mouth block the vaccine before it can spread
Vaccines are made from plants, not from real germs
explanation: The germ in a vaccine is dead or so weakened that it cannot infect you — it only teaches your body to recognize it.

q: What does the ozone layer in the stratosphere protect us from?
options: Rays that could burn skin and harm plants
Meteorites that fall toward Earth every day
Strong winds that would blow away the atmosphere
The extreme heat coming from the Sun's surface
explanation: The ozone layer protects us from rays that could burn skin and harm plants.

q: What medicine do doctors use in the hospital to treat a venomous snake bite?
options: Antivenom that fights the venom in the body
Antibiotics that kill the bacteria from the bite
A sugar solution that dilutes the poison in the blood
A vaccine to prevent any future snake bites
explanation: Doctors treat venomous snake bites with antivenom, which fights the venom in the body.

q: Scientists insert the human insulin gene into bacteria so the bacteria can produce insulin for diabetic patients. What technology makes this possible?
options: Recombinant DNA technology
Cell membrane transplanting
Selective breeding over many generations
Virus-based gene removal
explanation: Recombinant DNA technology allows scientists to move genes from one organism to another, such as putting the human insulin gene into bacteria.

q: How does a newly hatched baby fish get its first food without drinking milk?
options: It uses a tiny food sac attached to its belly from the egg
It immediately eats tiny plants floating in the water
Its father feeds it by chewing food into small pieces
It absorbs food through its skin from the surrounding water
explanation: A baby fish carries a yolk sac attached to its belly from the egg, which gives it food until it can feed on its own.

q: Why does your skin always stay fresh and strong even though old skin cells die?
options: New cells are constantly made underneath and push old cells upward to flake off
The skin absorbs minerals from sweat to repair any dead cells
Blood vessels bring new skin cells to the surface each morning
The body grows a completely new layer of skin every seven days
explanation: Skin constantly makes new cells underneath that push old cells upward, where they dry out and flake off, keeping the body's shield fresh and strong.

q: On an old water well, which part of the crank is the 'wheel' and which part is the 'axle'?
options: The handle is the wheel and the bar that winds the rope is the axle
The rope is the wheel and the bucket is the axle
The bar is the wheel and the handle is the axle
The pulley at the top is the wheel and the rope is the axle
explanation: In a water-well crank, the handle is the wheel and the bar it turns is the axle, which allows a heavy bucket to be lifted with an easy turning motion.

q: How is sweet cane juice taken out of the sugarcane plant?
options: The stalk is crushed and pressed by a mill machine until the juice comes out
The leaves are boiled in hot water to release the sugar
The roots are soaked in water overnight and the liquid is strained
The stalk is dried in the sun until the sugar crystals appear on the surface
explanation: Cane juice is extracted by crushing and pressing the sugarcane stalk through a mill until the sweet liquid comes out.

q: What simple machine is the sharp tip of a nail?
options: A wedge that pushes wood fibers apart
A lever that multiplies the force of the hammer
A screw that spins into the wood
A pulley that changes the direction of force
explanation: The sharp tip of a nail is a wedge — it pushes wood fibers apart so the nail can slide in when hammered.

q: What happens when you cut a magnet in two pieces?
options: Each piece becomes a new magnet that still has two poles
One piece keeps the north pole and the other keeps the south pole
The two pieces lose their magnetism and become ordinary metal
One piece becomes stronger and the other becomes weaker
explanation: If you cut a magnet in two, each piece becomes a new magnet that still has both a north and a south pole.

q: When fireworks explode far away, you always see the flash before you hear the bang. What does this tell you?
options: Light travels much faster than sound
Sound is blocked by the air between you and the fireworks
Light and sound leave the fireworks at different times
Sound takes longer to start than light does
explanation: You see the flash before the bang because light is millions of times faster than sound, so the light reaches you first.

q: What is a fault in Earth's crust?
options: A crack in the crust where blocks of rock can move, causing earthquakes when they slip
A weak spot in the ocean floor where hot lava slowly leaks out
A deep valley formed when a mountain range wears down over millions of years
A boundary between two different types of rock that never move
explanation: A fault is a crack in Earth's crust where blocks of rock can move, and when they suddenly slip, an earthquake occurs.

q: Why is the tamilok — a strange-looking creature eaten in Palawan — considered nutritious?
options: It is rich in protein
It is high in sugar for quick energy
It contains large amounts of vitamin C
It has the most calcium of any seafood
explanation: The tamilok is rich in protein, making it a nutritious food for some people in the Philippines.

q: What does a butterfly do with its wings right after it comes out of its chrysalis?
options: It pumps fluid into the soft, crumpled wings and lets them dry before flying
It vibrates the wings quickly to shake off any remaining cocoon silk
It rubs the wings together to warm them up in the sunlight
It dips the wings in water to make them flexible enough to open
explanation: When a butterfly first emerges, its wings are soft and crumpled, so it pumps fluid into them and waits for them to dry before it can fly.

q: What is the main job of a sneeze?
options: To push out dust or germs that have entered the nose
To help the lungs take in a larger breath of fresh air
To warn the body that the temperature is getting too cold
To clear the throat so sound can come out more clearly
explanation: Sneezing helps push out dust or germs that have entered the nose, keeping the airway clean.

q: What is an electromagnet?
options: A magnet made by passing electricity through coiled wire
A magnet that only works at very low temperatures
A natural rock that has been magnetized by lightning
A magnet inside a compass that always points north
explanation: An electromagnet is made when electricity flows through coiled wire, creating a magnetic force.

q: What gives brown sugar its brown color compared to white sugar?
options: Brown sugar still contains some molasses that was not removed
Brown sugar is made from a different type of sugarcane than white sugar
Brown sugar is colored by adding caramel during cooking
Brown sugar is less processed so it keeps the natural green color of the cane
explanation: Brown sugar still has some molasses in it, giving it a brown color; white sugar is refined more to remove the molasses.

q: When your arm lifts a heavy book, which part of the arm acts as the fulcrum of the lever?
options: The elbow
The wrist
The shoulder
The upper arm muscle
explanation: In the human arm working as a lever, the elbow is the fulcrum, the muscle provides the effort, and the hand holding the load is the output end.

q: What is the most effective way to stop mosquitoes from breeding around your home?
options: Remove standing water from containers, old tires, and trash
Spray all windows with insect repellent spray every morning
Put mosquito nets on all drains and water pipes
Plant strong-smelling herbs around the house to drive them away
explanation: Removing standing water in containers, old tires, and trash stops mosquitoes from having places to lay their eggs and breed.

q: Why is the katala, the Philippine cockatoo, critically endangered?
options: Widespread capture for the pet trade and loss of its forest home in Palawan
Pollution from fishing boats has destroyed its food supply near the coast
A disease spread by migratory birds wiped out most of the population
Competition with introduced parrots has pushed it out of its nesting areas
explanation: The katala is critically endangered because of widespread capture for the pet trade and forest loss in Palawan.

q: What does a joey do when it starts to get bigger inside its mother's pouch?
options: It pokes its head out of the pouch to look around
It leaves the pouch permanently and walks beside its mother
It moves to a second pouch on the mother's back
It makes loud sounds from inside the pouch to ask for food
explanation: When the joey gets bigger, it pokes its head out of the pouch to look around while still staying inside for safety.

q: Why were schools and workplaces in the Philippines closed during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020?
options: To prevent too many people from getting infected all at once
To give teachers time to prepare new online lesson materials
Because the virus was known to survive only in cold buildings
To allow hospitals to be converted into temporary classrooms
explanation: Lockdowns were put in place so that too many people would not get infected all at once, which would overwhelm hospitals.

q: What are the two main gases that make up a star like our Sun?
options: Hydrogen and helium
Oxygen and nitrogen
Carbon dioxide and methane
Neon and argon
explanation: A star is made mostly of hydrogen and helium, the two lightest gases.

q: How does a dog's color vision compare to a human's?
options: Dogs see fewer colors than people do
Dogs see exactly the same colors as people
Dogs see more colors than people, especially in the dark
Dogs see only in black and white with no color at all
explanation: Dogs see fewer colors than people, so they do not see all the colors the way humans do.

q: Why do Philippine orchids grow so well in their natural environment?
options: The warm and humid tropical climate provides perfect growing conditions
The cool mountain air keeps disease-causing insects away from them
The dry season forces the roots to grow deep and become very strong
Heavy monsoon rains wash minerals down from the mountains to feed them
explanation: Philippine orchids grow well because of the warm and humid climate of the tropics.

q: What does the term 'light-year' actually measure?
options: Distance — how far light travels in one year
Time — how long a ray of light takes to cross the solar system
Speed — how fast light moves through empty space
Brightness — how much light a star sends out in one year
explanation: A light-year is the distance that light travels in one year; it is a unit of distance, not time.

q: Why do most metals need to be put in an extremely hot furnace before they can be shaped?
options: Most metals have a very high melting point, so they need very high heat to melt
Metals are full of trapped air that must be burned away before they soften
The crystals inside metal must be broken by heat before the metal can flow
Metals absorb heat slowly, so a furnace is needed just to warm them up
explanation: Most metals have a high melting point, so they need very high heat to melt.

q: Besides letting the sun evaporate it, how else can you get salt back from seawater?
options: Boil the seawater so it evaporates faster and the salt is left behind
Filter the seawater through sand to catch the salt particles
Freeze the seawater so the salt separates and sinks to the bottom
Shake the seawater in a closed container until the salt settles out
explanation: Seawater can be boiled so the water evaporates faster, leaving the salt behind.

q: You dissolve a spoonful of salt in a glass of water and the salt disappears. What happens to the total weight of the mixture?
options: It stays the same — the salty water weighs as much as the water and salt added together
It becomes lighter because the salt breaks into tiny pieces that weigh less
It becomes heavier because water fills the spaces where the salt grains used to be
It changes slightly because some salt turns into a gas when it dissolves
explanation: When salt dissolves in water it disappears from sight but not from the weight — the salty water weighs the same as the water and salt combined.

q: At a palengke (Philippine market), there is a huge catch of fish today, and the stalls are overflowing. What will most likely happen to the price of fish?
options: Prices will fall because there is plenty of fish available
Prices will rise because the fishermen worked harder to catch so much
Prices will stay the same because the government sets all food prices
Prices will rise because more people will want to buy the extra fish
explanation: When there is a large supply of fish, prices fall according to the principle of supply and demand.

q: Why do chickens swallow small stones?
options: The stones help grind food inside their gizzard
The stones provide minerals that chickens cannot get from seeds
The stones balance the chicken's body weight while walking
The stones keep parasites away from the chicken's stomach
explanation: Chickens swallow small stones that help grind food inside their gizzard, since they have no teeth.

q: Who first proposed the idea that the continents slowly move across Earth's surface?
options: Alfred Wegener
Charles Darwin
Isaac Newton
Galileo Galilei
explanation: Alfred Wegener proposed continental drift — the idea that the continents slowly move.

q: How many hours are there in one full day?
options: 24 hours
12 hours
48 hours
36 hours
explanation: There are 24 hours in one day, the time it takes Earth to complete one full rotation.

q: About how hot is the core of the Sun, where energy is produced by fusion?
options: About 15 million degrees Celsius
About 5,500 degrees Celsius
About 1 million degrees Celsius
About 100,000 degrees Celsius
explanation: The Sun's core reaches about 15 million degrees Celsius, where nuclear fusion takes place and produces the Sun's energy.

q: What is the SI unit used to measure both energy and work?
options: Joule (J)
Watt (W)
Newton (N)
Ampere (A)
explanation: The SI unit of energy and work is the joule, with the symbol J.

q: What makes a material 'transparent'?
options: It lets light pass through it clearly
It reflects all light hitting its surface
It absorbs light and converts it to heat
It bends light so objects behind it look blurry
explanation: A transparent material, such as clear glass, lets light pass through it clearly.

q: An MRI machine takes clear pictures of the inside of the body. What does it use instead of X-rays?
options: A very powerful magnet
A beam of high-energy sound waves
A radioactive dye injected into the blood
A set of spinning mirrors and laser beams
explanation: An MRI machine uses a very powerful magnet to take clear pictures of the inside of the body without using X-rays.

q: Drinking far too much water can also be harmful to the body. Why?
options: It dilutes the salt in your blood too much, upsetting the balance
It stretches the stomach so badly that digestion stops working
It flushes out all the vitamins before your body can use them
It makes blood too thin, so the heart has to pump much faster
explanation: Drinking far too much water is harmful because it dilutes the salt in your blood too much; the key is balance.

q: How do bats in Philippine caves avoid bumping into walls and each other while flying in total darkness?
options: They use echolocation — sending out sounds and listening for echoes
They follow air currents created by other bats flying ahead of them
Their eyes can see a special type of light invisible to humans
They memorize the exact layout of the cave from their first flight
explanation: Many bats in Philippine caves use echolocation to navigate inside dark caves without bumping into anything.

q: What is the SI unit for measuring electric current?
options: Ampere (A)
Volt (V)
Watt (W)
Ohm (Ω)
explanation: The SI unit of electric current is the ampere, with the symbol A.

q: Why is farm fruit usually bigger and sweeter than wild fruit found in the forest?
options: Farmers selected and cared for plants over many generations to produce bigger and sweeter fruit
Farm soil has more rainwater so the fruit grows larger and fills with more sugar
Wild fruit uses its sweetness as a defense against insects that eat it
Sunlight reaches farm trees more easily in open fields, adding more sugar
explanation: Farm fruit was chosen and cared for by people to be bigger, sweeter, and more plentiful, unlike wild forest fruit that grows on its own.

q: What makes the body of a queen ant look different from worker ants?
options: The queen is bigger, especially her egg-filled belly, and her chest is larger where wings used to attach
The queen has a bright red head that shows other ants she is in charge
The queen has six legs while the workers have only four legs
The queen has much longer antennae so she can sense danger from far away
explanation: A queen ant is usually bigger than workers, especially her gaster which is full of eggs, and her chest is larger because that is where her wings used to be attached.

q: Which farm animal is known for being one of the most intelligent and able to learn simple things?
options: Pig
Cow
Goat
Horse
explanation: Pigs are among the most intelligent farm animals and can learn simple things.

q: About how long does sunlight take to travel from the Sun to Earth?
options: 8 minutes
3 minutes
24 hours
1 hour
explanation: The Sun is about 150 million kilometers away, and its light takes about 8 minutes to reach us.

q: What acts like a natural pacemaker in the heart, making sure the chambers beat in the right order?
options: A small part near the top of the heart that sends electrical signals
The aorta, which pumps blood to the body
The ventricles, which receive blood first
Nerve endings in the heart muscle walls
explanation: A small part near the top of the heart acts like a natural pacemaker, sending signals so the atria beat first, then the ventricles — in the correct order.

q: How does food and oxygen reach a baby growing inside its mother's body?
options: Through the umbilical cord
Through the mother's bloodstream directly into the baby's lungs
Through the placenta only, with no cord connection
Through swallowing amniotic fluid
explanation: Food and oxygen pass from the mother's body to the baby through the umbilical cord.

q: In what type of environment does rattan grow, and where are many kinds found?
options: Warm, moist tropical rainforests, especially in the Philippines and Southeast Asia
Cold, dry mountain forests in East Asia
Sandy coastal beaches around the Pacific
Grasslands and open plains in South America
explanation: Rattan grows in warm, moist tropical rainforests, and many kinds are found in the forests of the Philippines and Southeast Asia.

q: How is the sailfin lizard different from the water monitor lizard?
options: The sailfin lizard is smaller, has a sail on its back, and eats plants too, while the water monitor is larger and a hunter
The sailfin lizard is larger and eats only meat, while the water monitor is smaller and eats plants
Both are the same size but differ only in their diet
The sailfin lizard lives only in water, while the water monitor lives on land
explanation: The sailfin lizard is smaller, has its special sail on the back, and eats plants too, while the water monitor is larger and a hunter.

q: What property makes red cabbage juice useful in a science experiment with acids and bases?
options: It changes color when mixed with an acid or base
It produces a gas that you can smell
It heats up quickly when mixed with any liquid
It dissolves completely and disappears in water
explanation: Red cabbage juice is a natural indicator that changes color in acids and bases.

q: Why do some animals have bright colors like yellow, red, or orange?
options: To warn predators that they are poisonous or dangerous
To attract sunlight and keep themselves warm
To blend in with colorful flowers so they can hide
To signal other animals that food is nearby
explanation: Bright colors like yellow, red, or orange warn predators that the animal is poisonous or dangerous — a kind of silent communication.

q: Why does the Philippines have many active volcanoes?
options: It sits on the Pacific Ring of Fire, a zone with many volcanoes and earthquakes
It is the largest island country in Southeast Asia
It is located near the equator, which creates more heat underground
Its mountains are made of very soft rock that melts easily
explanation: The Philippines sits on the Pacific Ring of Fire, a zone with many volcanoes and earthquakes, which is why it has many active volcanoes like Taal, Pinatubo, Kanlaon, and Bulusan.

q: What happens when a falling object reaches terminal velocity?
options: It falls at a steady speed because air resistance equals gravity
It falls faster and faster until it hits the ground
It slows down and eventually stops in mid-air
It bounces upward because air resistance becomes stronger than gravity
explanation: When air resistance grows until it equals gravity, the object stops speeding up and falls at a steady speed called terminal velocity.

q: How does the janitor fish survive in water with very little oxygen?
options: It gulps air from the surface
It burrows into the mud until oxygen returns
It slows down its heartbeat and hibernates
It absorbs oxygen through its skin instead of its gills
explanation: The janitor fish can gulp air from the surface when there is little oxygen in the water, allowing it to survive even in dirty water.

q: What role do roots play when there is a strong storm?
options: They hold the plant firmly so it does not fall over or get blown away
They absorb extra rainwater to feed the plant during the storm
They spread out to make the plant's trunk thicker
They release chemicals that calm the wind around the plant
explanation: Sturdy roots hold the plant in place during strong wind so it does not fall over or get blown away.

q: How do worms grind their food if they have no teeth?
options: They swallow tiny sand grains that grind food inside their gizzard
They use strong stomach acid to dissolve everything they eat
They chew with hard ridges inside their throat
They only eat food that is already fully broken down by bacteria
explanation: Worms swallow soft food along with tiny grains of sand; inside their gizzard, the sand grinds the food so it can be digested.

q: What do red ruby and blue sapphire have in common?
options: They are both made of the same mineral, corundum, and differ only because of tiny traces of different metals
They are both forms of quartz and get their color from iron
They are both found only in tropical rainforests and shaped by heat
They form from the same volcanic rock but harden at different temperatures
explanation: Red ruby and blue sapphire are made of the very same mineral, corundum — they differ in color only because of tiny traces of different metals mixed in.

q: What caused the tall cliffs and wrinkle-like ridges on the surface of Mercury?
options: Mercury's inside slowly cooling and shrinking, causing the surface to wrinkle
Strong meteor impacts that pushed up rock into ridges over time
The heat from the Sun melting and reshaping the surface
Liquid lava flowing and hardening into cliff shapes
explanation: As Mercury's inside slowly cools and shrinks, tall cliffs and wrinkle-like ridges formed on its surface, like skin that wrinkles.

q: What does a sea turtle do with its eggs after laying them on the beach?
options: Covers them with sand and leaves them to be warmed by the heat of the sand
Carries them into the ocean to keep them cool and safe
Guards them in a nest made of leaves and sticks
Buries them underwater near coral reefs
explanation: After laying, the sea turtle covers the eggs with sand and leaves them to be warmed by the heat of the sand.

q: Why are there two high tides each day instead of just one?
options: Water bulges on both the side facing the Moon and the far side of Earth
The Moon pulls water twice as it completes one full orbit each day
The Sun and Moon work together to create a tide every 12 hours
Strong winds push ocean water back and forth twice a day
explanation: Water bulges on the side facing the Moon and also on the far side of Earth, giving two high tides a day.

q: What is the correct order of colors in a rainbow from top to bottom?
options: Red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet
Violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange, red
Red, yellow, orange, green, violet, blue, indigo
Blue, green, yellow, orange, red, indigo, violet
explanation: The order of rainbow colors is red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet.

q: Why does kalamay-hati thicken as it is cooked for a long time?
options: Because water evaporates from the mixture as it boils
Because the sugar breaks down into a solid block when heated
Because the sticky rice absorbs all the coconut milk and expands
Because the mixture cools and hardens inside the pan
explanation: Kalamay-hati is boiled a long time until the water evaporates and the mixture thickens.

q: In gold panning, how does gold separate from sand?
options: The heavy gold sinks to the bottom while the lighter sand washes away
The gold dissolves in water and is collected when the water evaporates
The gold floats on top while the heavier sand sinks
The gold changes color in water, making it easy to pick out by hand
explanation: In gold panning, the heavy gold sinks to the bottom while the lighter sand washes away because of their different weight.

q: What stage of a cyclone is called a tropical storm, and who gives it a name in the Philippines?
options: The stage between a tropical depression and a typhoon, named by PAGASA
The stage after a typhoon when winds are slowing down, named by the Red Cross
The same as a typhoon but with a different name used in other countries
The weakest stage of a cyclone, named by the National Weather Bureau
explanation: A tropical storm is the stage between a tropical depression and a typhoon, with winds of 62–88 km/h, and it receives a local name from PAGASA.

q: What did the centipede's first pair of legs become, and what are they used for?
options: Sharp claws with venom for catching prey
Flat paddles for swimming in water
Sticky pads for climbing smooth surfaces
Long antennae for sensing movement
explanation: A centipede's first pair of legs became sharp claws with venom for catching prey.

q: How can you tell a sea snake apart from an eel?
options: A sea snake has scales and lungs, while an eel has gills and smooth skin
A sea snake is longer and thinner, while an eel is short and wide
A sea snake glows in the dark, while an eel is dark brown
A sea snake has fins on its back, while an eel has none
explanation: A sea snake has scales and lungs, while an eel has gills and smooth skin.

q: Which body system is responsible for breaking down the food you eat?
options: Digestive system
Respiratory system
Circulatory system
Nervous system
explanation: The digestive system breaks down food; the human body has many connected systems — digestive, respiratory, circulatory, skeletal, muscular, and nervous — that all work together.

q: Why does each kind of firefly have its own unique flashing pattern?
options: So the right mate can recognize that they are the same species
To warn predators that they are poisonous and should not be eaten
To light the way when flying through dark forest undergrowth
To communicate the location of food sources to other fireflies
explanation: Each kind of firefly has its own flashing pattern — number and length of flashes — so the right mate can recognize that they are the same species.

q: What is the main job of the ozone layer high in Earth's atmosphere?
options: It absorbs most of the harmful ultraviolet light from the Sun
It traps heat close to Earth's surface to keep the planet warm
It reflects visible sunlight back into space to cool the planet
It produces oxygen that living things breathe
explanation: The ozone layer high in the atmosphere absorbs most of the harmful ultraviolet light from the Sun.

q: Which type of honeybee cannot sting?
options: Drones
Worker bees
The queen bee
Guard bees
explanation: Drones have no stinger, so they cannot sting.

q: What is special about Mount Hamiguitan in Davao Oriental?
options: It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, listed in 2014
It is the highest mountain in the Philippines
It is the location of the country's largest active volcano
It is home to the only remaining lowland rainforest in the Philippines
explanation: Mount Hamiguitan in Davao Oriental is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, listed in 2014.

q: What is the fastest-growing plant in the world?
options: Bamboo
Water hyacinth
Giant sequoia
Sugarcane
explanation: The fastest-growing plant in the world is bamboo.

q: Why does light bend when it moves from air into water or glass?
options: Because it slows down when entering a denser material, and this change in speed turns its path
Because water and glass are magnetic and pull the light sideways
Because light always follows the curve of round objects like lenses
Because the colors in light separate and each color bends at a different angle
explanation: Light bends because it slows down when it enters a denser material like water or glass, and this change in speed is what turns its path.

q: Why can kapok float on water?
options: Each kapok fiber is a tiny hollow tube filled with air
Kapok fibers are coated with a waxy oil that repels water
Kapok is lighter than any other plant material in the world
Kapok fibers tangle together and trap a bubble of water underneath
explanation: Each kapok fiber is like a tiny hollow tube filled with air inside, so it can float on water.

q: What does yeast feed on to stay alive in bread dough?
options: Sugar found in flour or added to the dough
Starch granules inside the wheat grains
Water added to the dough
Salt mixed into the bread recipe
explanation: Yeast stays alive by eating the sugar found in flour or added to the dough, turning it into energy.

q: Why are dishes like sinigang and tinola considered mixtures?
options: Because they are made of water, vegetables, meat, and seasonings combined — but you can still see and pick out each part
Because all their ingredients melt together completely so none can be separated
Because they are cooked at very high heat, which bonds all the ingredients chemically
Because they are made from a single ingredient that is cut into many pieces
explanation: Sinigang and tinola are mixtures because you can still see each part — water, vegetables, meat, and seasonings — and pick out the pieces you want.

q: Which of the following correctly describes a parrot?
options: It has feathers and wings and lays eggs to reproduce
It has scales, breathes underwater, and gives birth to live young
It has fur, is warm-blooded, and feeds its young with milk
It has a hard shell, lives in water, and lays eggs on the seafloor
explanation: A parrot is a bird that has feathers and wings and lays eggs to reproduce.

q: What is one of the biggest causes of death among children worldwide, linked to dirty water?
options: Diarrhea diseases
Respiratory infections from air pollution
Malaria from mosquito bites
Skin diseases from lack of sunlight
explanation: Diarrhea diseases from dirty water are one of the biggest causes of death among children worldwide.

q: In 1854, how did John Snow discover the source of a cholera outbreak in London?
options: He traced it to a single contaminated water pump
He found that sick people had all eaten the same infected food
He identified rats carrying the disease through the sewers
He noticed the outbreak started near a hospital and spread outward
explanation: In 1854 in London, John Snow traced a cholera outbreak to a single contaminated water pump.

q: What does Newton's third law of motion tell us?
options: For every action there is an equal and opposite reaction
An object at rest stays at rest unless a force acts on it
The force on an object equals its mass times its acceleration
Objects always move in the direction of the greatest force
explanation: Newton's third law says for every action there is an equal and opposite reaction.

q: Besides helping it swim, what else does a shark's thick, rough skin do?
options: It acts like armor, protecting the shark from cuts, bites, and sharp rocks
It absorbs sunlight to help the shark stay warm in cold ocean water
It makes the shark harder to see by blending in with the ocean floor
It releases a slippery chemical that makes other fish swim away
explanation: A shark's thick, rough skin acts like armor, protecting its body from cuts, bites from other animals, and sharp rocks or coral.

q: Why does the Moon glow in the night sky but not shine like a perfect mirror?
options: Its surface is rough with rock and dust, so it scatters sunlight in all directions
It produces its own dim light the way a star does
Its dark side absorbs light and slowly releases it as a glow at night
Its atmosphere filters sunlight and turns it into a soft glow
explanation: The Moon's surface is rough with rock and dust, so it scatters sunlight in all directions rather than reflecting it like a mirror.

q: Which planet is the hottest in our solar system, and why?
options: Venus, because its thick atmosphere traps heat, reaching about 465°C
Mercury, because it is the closest planet to the Sun
Mars, because dust storms spread heat across the entire planet
Jupiter, because it is the largest planet and generates its own heat
explanation: Venus is the hottest planet, reaching about 465°C because of its thick atmosphere that traps heat.

q: Why do farmers plant rows of tall trees along the edges of their fields?
options: To block strong wind so the soil is not blown away and the crops are not damaged
To attract rain clouds that water the crops naturally
To provide shade that keeps the soil moist during dry seasons
To mark the boundaries of their land so animals cannot enter
explanation: Rows of tall trees act as a windbreak, blocking strong wind so the soil is not blown away and crops are not damaged — a real-world use of studying wind erosion.

q: What causes the different shapes of the Moon that we see throughout the month?
options: The Moon orbiting the Earth, which changes how much of its lit side we can see
Earth's shadow slowly covering and uncovering the Moon's surface
The Moon rotating on its own axis once a day
Clouds partially blocking our view of the Moon at different times
explanation: The phases of the Moon are the different shapes we see as the Moon orbits the Earth.

q: What type of simple machine is a ramp or a staircase?
options: Inclined plane
Lever
Pulley
Wedge
explanation: A ramp and stairs are examples of the inclined plane — a gentle slope used to climb or raise things more easily.

q: Why does dishwashing liquid remove cooking grease from plates when plain water cannot?
options: It is made to break up grease and wrap it so it slides off when rinsed
It heats up grease so fast that the grease melts and drains away
It dissolves grease by turning it into water during washing
It makes the plate surface so slippery that grease cannot stick
explanation: Dishwashing liquid breaks up thick grease and wraps it, so it slides off the dishes when rinsed — even oil that water alone cannot touch.

q: When playing the kubing, what actually makes the different notes change?
options: The mouth acts as a filter, making certain parts of the tongue's vibration louder, but the vibrating tongue is always the source of sound
The mouth produces the notes by itself when the player changes the shape of their lips
The player's teeth tap the kubing to change the pitch of each note
The jaw opens and closes to let air in, which creates new sounds each time
explanation: The tongue is the source of all the sound in the kubing; the mouth only acts as a filter that chooses which part of the sound gets louder — it can do nothing without the vibrating tongue.

q: What can happen if a child eats too much sugar from candy and soft drinks?
options: Teeth can be damaged and it can cause weight and health problems
The body gains extra energy and becomes stronger than normal
Bones grow faster but become more brittle over time
The digestive system slows down and stops processing other nutrients
explanation: Too much sugar from candy and soft drinks damages teeth and can cause weight and health problems, so it should be eaten only in small amounts.

q: How do insulin and glucagon work together in the body?
options: Insulin lowers blood sugar while glucagon raises it, keeping blood sugar in balance
Both insulin and glucagon lower blood sugar after every meal
Insulin stores fat while glucagon breaks down muscle for energy
Glucagon lowers blood sugar and insulin raises it after exercise
explanation: Insulin lowers blood sugar while glucagon raises it, keeping blood sugar in balance.

q: How does a barnacle attach itself to rocks and ships?
options: It produces its own natural cement that hardens and glues it in place
It uses tiny claws to grip into small cracks in rock surfaces
It wraps thread-like tentacles tightly around whatever it touches
It sucks onto surfaces using a strong suction cup on its underside
explanation: A barnacle glues itself to rocks, wood, and ships using its own natural cement that hardens.

q: You keep adding salt to a glass of water and stirring. At some point the salt just sits at the bottom and won't dissolve. What does this tell you about the water?
options: The water has reached its limit and cannot dissolve any more salt
The salt has turned into a different substance
The water is too cold to dissolve salt at all
The salt grains are too large to mix with water
explanation: When water is saturated, it holds all the dissolved salt it can, so extra salt stays solid at the bottom.

q: Scientists often compare the density of different materials to water. What is the density of water that makes it such a useful reference?
options: About 1 gram per milliliter
About 10 grams per milliliter
About 0.1 grams per milliliter
About 5 grams per milliliter
explanation: Water has a density of about one gram per milliliter, which is why it is used as a standard reference for comparing other materials.

q: Scientists noticed that fireflies disappeared from an area near a new highway with bright streetlights. What does this disappearance most likely signal?
options: Pollution or too much artificial night light is harming the environment
The fireflies migrated to a warmer region for the season
There are no more trees left for the fireflies to rest on
A new predator arrived and ate all the fireflies
explanation: Fireflies thrive in clean, dark places, so their disappearance often signals pollution or excessive night light in the area.

q: An earthworm has no eyes, yet when a flashlight shines on it, the worm wriggles away. How does the earthworm detect the light?
options: It senses light through its skin
It hears the sound of the flashlight clicking on
It smells the heat coming from the light bulb
It feels the shadow moving across the ground
explanation: Earthworms have no eyes but can sense light through their skin, causing them to move away from it.

q: Before Gutenberg's printing press, books were copied by hand one at a time. What did the printing press change?
options: It made it possible to produce many books quickly and cheaply
It allowed books to be printed in color for the first time
It replaced the need for paper by printing on metal sheets
It made books so expensive that only kings could afford them
explanation: Gutenberg's printing press made it possible to produce many books quickly and cheaply, transforming the spread of knowledge.

q: Some egrets (tagak) spread their wings wide over the water while hunting fish. What is the main reason they do this?
options: They cast a shadow that reduces glare so they can see fish more clearly
They cool the water so the fish swim toward the surface
They scare the fish into jumping out of the water
They use their wings to scoop fish out of the water
explanation: Some egrets spread their wings to cast a shadow on the water, cutting glare so they can spot fish below more easily.

q: A butterfly wing looks bright shiny blue, but scientists find almost no blue pigment in it. Where does that shiny blue color come from?
options: The microscopic shape of the scales bends light to create the color
The wing absorbs water from the air which turns it blue
A chemical reaction with sunlight creates the blue color each day
Tiny blue pigment dust from flowers collects on the scales
explanation: Shiny blue or green colors on butterfly wings come from the structure of the scales bending light, not from pigment.

q: A male deer with very large antlers often causes rival males to back away without fighting. What do those large antlers show the rivals?
options: How strong or healthy the deer is
How old the deer is in years
How far the deer's territory extends
How fast the deer can run
explanation: Large antlers and other animal displays signal how strong or healthy an animal is, so rivals may back down without fighting.

q: Ferns and mushrooms do not produce flowers or seeds. How do they reproduce and spread?
options: By releasing tiny spores
By sending out underground runners
By dropping their leaves which grow into new plants
By budding off small copies of themselves
explanation: Ferns, mosses, and fungi reproduce by means of tiny spores rather than through seeds or flowers.

q: A flying fish leaps out of the ocean and spreads its large fins to glide through the air. About how long does each glide usually last?
options: Only a few seconds
About one full minute
Around ten minutes
Several hours
explanation: A flying fish usually stays in the air for only a few seconds during each glide before dropping back into the water.

q: A farmer notices that some of his crop leaves are turning purple or reddish even though the plants get enough water and sunlight. What nutrient is most likely missing from the soil?
options: Phosphorus
Nitrogen
Calcium
Iron
explanation: When phosphorus is deficient, plants produce more anthocyanin pigment, turning leaves purple or reddish.

q: When you get a cut, your blood eventually clots and stops bleeding. Which organ produces the special proteins that make blood clot?
options: The liver
The kidney
The heart
The spleen
explanation: The liver makes special proteins that help blood clot when you have a cut, which is important for wound healing.

q: Maria Cristina Falls in Iligan City is one of the most powerful waterfalls in the Philippines. About how tall is it?
options: About 98 meters
About 20 meters
About 200 meters
About 50 meters
explanation: Maria Cristina Falls is about 98 meters tall, making it one of the Philippines' most impressive waterfalls.

q: After boiling water to make it safe to drink, what is the best way to store it so it stays safe?
options: In a clean, covered container
In an open bowl on the kitchen counter
In a used plastic bag left open
In a bucket next to the door
explanation: Storing water in a clean, covered container prevents it from being contaminated again by germs.

q: Red blood cells do not last forever. After about how many days does the spleen break them down?
options: About 120 days
About 7 days
About 365 days
About 30 days
explanation: Red blood cells live about 120 days before the spleen destroys them and recycles their iron to make new red blood cells.

q: A total solar eclipse is an amazing event, but most people on Earth never see one in their hometown. Why is a total solar eclipse so rare in any one place?
options: The Moon's dark shadow is small and only covers a narrow strip of Earth
The Moon is too far away to ever fully block the Sun
Total solar eclipses only happen once every thousand years
Clouds always block the view of the eclipse
explanation: The Moon's dark shadow is small, so it only touches a narrow strip of Earth during each eclipse, making a total solar eclipse rare in any one location.

q: Scientists link the burning of coal and gasoline to rising sea levels around the world. What connects burning fuel to higher seas?
options: Burning fuel releases greenhouse gases that warm the planet and melt ice, raising sea levels
Burning fuel creates acid rain that fills the oceans with extra water
Burning fuel slows the water cycle so rivers overflow into the sea
Burning fuel creates soot that floats on the ocean surface and pushes water up
explanation: Burning coal and fuel releases greenhouse gases that warm the planet, causing ice to melt and sea levels to rise.

q: Dinoflagellates are the tiny plankton most often responsible for red tide. How do they move through the water?
options: Using two whip-like tails to swim upward toward sunlight
By floating passively with ocean currents
By crawling along the seafloor with tiny legs
By inflating a gas bubble to rise to the surface
explanation: Dinoflagellates have two whip-like tails they use to swim upward in the water toward sunlight and nutrients.

q: Why do most plant leaves look green to our eyes?
options: Chlorophyll absorbs red and blue light but reflects green light back to our eyes
Chlorophyll absorbs all colors of light and emits only green light
The water inside leaves is naturally green and shows through
Leaves are coated in a green wax that reflects sunlight
explanation: Chlorophyll absorbs red and blue light for photosynthesis but reflects green light, which is why leaves appear green.

q: During the rainy season in the Philippines, the southwest monsoon (habagat) brings heavy rains. Where does the moisture for this rain come from?
options: Moist air blown in from the sea by the wind
Water evaporated from rivers and lakes only
Moisture trapped under the soil that rises upward
Clouds carried from neighboring countries
explanation: The southwest monsoon (habagat) is wind from the sea that carries moist air, bringing heavy rain to the Philippines during the rainy season.

q: Even before your immune cells attack invading germs, your body has several first-line defenses. Which of the following is one of those defenses?
options: Mucus in the nose traps germs before they enter the body
White blood cells patrol the skin surface to destroy germs
The blood vessels shrink to stop germs from spreading
Bones release a chemical that kills germs in the air
explanation: Mucus in the nose traps germs, tears clean the eyes, and stomach acid kills germs in food — all before immune cells act.

q: When describing how many times a sound wave vibrates every second, scientists use a specific unit. What is that unit?
options: Hertz (Hz)
Joule (J)
Newton (N)
Watt (W)
explanation: The SI unit of frequency is the hertz (Hz), which means cycles per second.

q: When you feel cold or frightened, tiny bumps called goosebumps appear on your skin. What causes your body hairs to stand up and create those bumps?
options: A tiny muscle attached to each hair pulls it upright
The hair follicles swell with extra blood and push the hair up
Cold air freezes the hair making it stiff and straight
Nerves send electricity through the hair making it stand up
explanation: Every tiny body hair has a small muscle attached to it; when you feel cold or scared, the muscle contracts and pulls the hair upright, causing goosebumps.

q: A dentist holds up a special mirror to give you a bigger view of your teeth. What kind of mirror is this?
options: A concave (curved-inward) mirror
A flat mirror
A convex (curved-outward) mirror
A two-sided mirror
explanation: A mirror that curves inward (concave) makes your image look bigger when you are close, which is why dentists use it to see teeth more clearly.

q: Using a long lever, you can lift a heavy rock with a small push. Does the lever give you free extra energy to do this?
options: No — the lever lets you use a smaller force but you must push through a longer distance
Yes — the lever creates extra energy from the wood it is made of
Yes — the lever borrows energy stored underground and transfers it to the rock
No — the lever simply cuts the weight of the rock in half permanently
explanation: A lever does not create extra energy; it trades a large force for a longer movement distance, keeping total energy the same.

q: Newborn babies have very weak immune systems. How does a mother's breast milk help protect the baby from disease?
options: It passes the mother's antibodies to the baby
It kills all bacteria in the baby's stomach permanently
It helps the baby grow teeth faster to chew solid food
It replaces the need for the baby's white blood cells
explanation: A mother's breast milk passes her antibodies to the baby, protecting the child from some diseases while its own immune system is still developing.

q: Just like human fingerprints, no two giraffes look exactly alike. What feature of a giraffe is unique to each individual?
options: Its pattern of spots
Its number of legs
The length of its neck
The color of its eyes
explanation: Every giraffe has its own unique pattern of spots, similar to how every human has a unique fingerprint.

q: An owl can turn its head almost all the way around to look behind itself. Why does it need to do this instead of just moving its eyes?
options: An owl cannot move its eyes inside their sockets
An owl's eyes are on the sides of its head and already see backward
An owl keeps its eyes closed most of the time to protect them
An owl's eyeballs fall out if they move too fast
explanation: The owl cannot move its eyes inside their sockets, so it turns its head far around to look in different directions.

q: Some animals like bears enter a deep sleep-like state during winter and barely move for months. What is the main reason animals hibernate?
options: To save energy when food is scarce during cold winter months
To keep their bodies from getting too warm in winter
To hide from predators who are more active in cold weather
To allow their young to be born safely inside the den
explanation: Hibernation is a deep sleep-like state that helps animals save energy during cold winters when food is scarce.

q: During a thunderstorm you see a bright flash of lightning in the sky. What is lightning, exactly?
options: A giant spark of electricity jumping between clouds or from a cloud to the ground
A beam of heat energy released when raindrops collide in the clouds
A burst of light created when air molecules explode from strong wind
A reflection of sunlight bouncing off the bottom of storm clouds
explanation: Lightning is a giant spark of electricity that jumps between clouds or from a cloud down to the ground.

q: A total lunar eclipse lasts much longer than a total solar eclipse. Why does a lunar eclipse take so long?
options: Earth's shadow is very large, so the Moon takes a long time to pass through it
The Moon travels much more slowly during a lunar eclipse than usual
The Sun sends out extra light that slows down the eclipse
The Moon stops moving completely while inside Earth's shadow
explanation: A lunar eclipse can last an hour or more because Earth's shadow is much larger than the Moon's shadow.

q: Lions hunt and eat zebras. Does this mean lions are cruel or bad animals?
options: No — lions hunt because meat is their natural food needed for survival
Yes — hunting other animals is always harmful and unnecessary
No — lions only hunt animals that are already sick or injured
Yes — carnivores could survive on plants but choose not to
explanation: Carnivores are not evil when they hunt; they eat meat simply because that is their natural food needed for survival.

q: Galangal is a spice used in some Filipino dishes. How is it related to ginger?
options: It is a relative of ginger and also grows as an edible underground rhizome
It is a type of dried ginger leaf used only as a garnish
It is a seed from the ginger flower that tastes different from the root
It is an unrelated plant that only looks similar to ginger
explanation: Galangal is another edible spice rhizome, a close relative of ginger used in cooking.

q: A newborn macaque monkey stays close to its mother at all times as she moves through the trees. How does the baby manage to travel with her?
options: It clings tightly to its mother's body
It rides on her back inside a pouch
It holds her tail with its hands
It runs on the ground below her
explanation: A baby macaque clings tightly to its mother's body while she moves around.

q: The Banaue Rice Terraces are famous worldwide. Besides growing rice, what environmental problem do these step-like terraces help solve?
options: They slow down water flowing down the slope and reduce soil erosion
They block typhoon winds from reaching the rice crops
They prevent earthquakes from damaging the mountainside
They collect rainwater in deep pools to irrigate lowland farms
explanation: Step-like terraces reduce erosion by slowing water flowing down steep mountainsides, protecting the soil.

q: A petroleum refinery separates crude oil into gasoline, diesel, and other products. What property of crude oil makes this separation possible?
options: Its molecules have different sizes and weights giving them different boiling points
Its molecules are all the same but separate when shaken with water
It contains solid and liquid layers that naturally settle apart over time
It reacts with oxygen in air to split into different substances
explanation: Crude oil can be separated because its molecules come in different sizes and weights, which gives them different boiling points.

q: Which of the following best describes what a mineral is?
options: A naturally occurring solid with a definite chemical makeup and orderly arrangement of atoms
A type of liquid found deep inside volcanoes that hardens into rock
Any solid material dug out of the ground, including soil and coal
A man-made crystal formed when chemicals are mixed in a laboratory
explanation: A mineral is a naturally occurring solid with a definite chemical makeup and an orderly arrangement of atoms.

q: A young skink and an old skink both lose their tails to escape a predator. Which one will regrow its tail faster?
options: The young skink, because younger animals regenerate faster
The old skink, because it has more years of experience growing
Both regrow at exactly the same speed regardless of age
Neither can regrow a tail — only lizards can do that
explanation: Young skinks heal and grow a new tail faster than older ones; the ability to regenerate the tail slows down with age.

q: Sand and mud at the bottom of a river can eventually turn into solid sedimentary rock. What two processes cause this to happen?
options: Compaction (pressure squeezes grains together) and cementation (minerals glue the grains together)
Melting (heat melts the sand) and cooling (it hardens into rock)
Evaporation (water leaves) and crystallization (salt forms the rock)
Compression (weight flattens the grains) and explosion (gases fuse them together)
explanation: Sedimentary rock forms through compaction, where pressure squeezes sediment together, and cementation, where minerals glue the grains.

q: Rice plants grow in flooded muddy paddies. What do the roots of the rice plant do for the plant?
options: They grip the muddy soil and absorb water and nutrients
They float the plant so it does not sink into the mud
They produce oxygen bubbles that push the plant upward
They store extra rice grains underground for the next season
explanation: The roots of the rice plant grip the muddy soil and soak up water and nutrients that the plant needs to grow.

q: Your pancreas releases a hormone called glucagon to keep your blood sugar balanced. What is unusual about how glucagon does its job?
options: You cannot feel it working — it adjusts your blood sugar silently without you noticing
It causes a warm feeling in your stomach every time it is released
It makes you feel hungry so you know to eat more sugar
It only works while you are sleeping and never during the day
explanation: Glucagon quietly adjusts your blood sugar every day without you being able to feel it working at all.

q: A car's brakes bring it to a stop quickly. According to physics, what does the braking force actually do to the car?
options: It rapidly changes the car's momentum, slowing it down
It removes the car's stored fuel energy and converts it to sound
It increases the car's weight to make it harder to move
It creates friction only on the tires without affecting the car's motion
explanation: Force is how quickly an object's momentum changes; the braking force rapidly reduces the car's momentum to stop it.

q: If you look at the cross-section of a large dam, the wall is much thicker at the bottom than at the top. Why is it built this way?
options: Water pressure is greater at greater depth, so the wall needs to be thicker at the bottom to withstand it
The bottom of the dam holds the heaviest fish and animals, so it needs more material
The concrete at the bottom dries more slowly, so more is added to compensate
The base is thicker to make the dam look stable even if it is not structurally needed
explanation: Water pressure increases with depth, so a dam wall must be thicker at the bottom to withstand the greater force there.

q: A machine lifts a 200-newton load using only 50 newtons of effort. What is the machine's mechanical advantage?
options: 4, because output force divided by input force equals 200 divided by 50
0.25, because input force divided by output force equals 50 divided by 200
150, because you subtract input force from output force
10,000, because you multiply input and output forces together
explanation: Mechanical advantage equals output force divided by input force; 200 divided by 50 equals 4, meaning the machine multiplies your force four times.

q: Why is it important to wear slippers or shoes when walking outside?
options: To protect your feet from sharp objects and germs in the soil that could cause cuts or illness
To keep your feet warm so you do not feel cold during the day
To make running faster by gripping the ground better
To prevent your feet from growing too large from the sun's heat
explanation: Wearing slippers or shoes outdoors protects your feet from sharp objects and germs in the soil that could cause cuts or illness.

q: A metal spoon left in a hot bowl of soup becomes hot too, even though it was not in a flame. Which method of heat transfer explains this?
options: Conduction — heat travels through direct contact between the hot soup and the spoon
Convection — rising hot air currents carry heat from the soup to the spoon
Radiation — the soup sends out heat rays that the spoon absorbs from a distance
Reflection — the spoon reflects heat from the room back into itself
explanation: Conduction is the transfer of heat through direct contact, which is why a metal spoon heats up when placed in hot soup.

q: During a typhoon, people near a river are warned to evacuate because of flash floods. What makes a flash flood especially dangerous?
options: It comes on very suddenly, sometimes within just minutes or hours, leaving little time to escape
It only occurs underground and is invisible until it reaches the surface
It lasts for several weeks and gradually fills the entire valley
It moves very slowly but carries rocks so heavy that nothing can stop it
explanation: A flash flood is a sudden flood that can arrive within minutes or hours, giving people very little time to reach safety.

q: A child's doctor says their astigmatism prescription changed since last year and they need new glasses. Why can astigmatism change in growing children?
options: Astigmatism can change a little as a child grows, so yearly eye check-ups are needed to update the prescription
Astigmatism only gets worse when children eat too many sweets and can be reversed with diet
Astigmatism is always exactly the same for life and the prescription change must be a measurement error
Astigmatism changes only because of screen time and disappears when screen use is reduced
explanation: Astigmatism can change a little as a child grows, which is why yearly eye check-ups are important so glasses prescriptions can be updated.

q: The yo-yo became a popular toy in the United States partly because of a Filipino inventor. Who was this Filipino and what did he do?
options: Pedro Flores popularized the yo-yo in the US and opened the first yo-yo factory there
Jose Rizal invented the yo-yo and sent the design to the United States by mail
Andres Bonifacio brought the yo-yo to the US as a gift during a diplomatic visit
Juan Luna painted a picture of a yo-yo that inspired American toy makers to build one
explanation: Pedro Flores was the Filipino who popularized the yo-yo in the United States and opened the first yo-yo factory there.

q: A strange round lump appears on a plant's leaf. A scientist says it is a gall. What usually triggers a gall to start forming on a plant?
options: An insect lays its eggs on the plant's leaf or stem
A fungus releases spores that stick to the leaf surface
Too much rain causes the leaf cells to swell into a lump
A bird pecks at the stem and the plant grows a protective bump
explanation: A gall usually begins when an insect lays its eggs on the plant's leaf or stem, causing the plant tissue to grow around them.

q: At what temperature does water freeze on the Kelvin scale?
options: 0 K
explanation: Water freezes at 273 Kelvin (273 K) on the Kelvin scale.

q: What does a pangolin eat?
options: Only ants and termites
Fruits and berries
Leaves and bark
Small fish and frogs
explanation: The pangolin eats only ants and termites, making it a specialist insect-eater.

q: When wood or gasoline burns, which gas does it use up and which gas does it release?
options: Uses oxygen; releases carbon dioxide
Uses carbon dioxide; releases oxygen
Uses nitrogen; releases carbon dioxide
Uses oxygen; releases water vapor only
explanation: When fuel burns, it uses up oxygen from the air and releases carbon dioxide as a product.

q: Why is boiling a good way to make drinking water safer?
options: It kills disease-causing germs
It removes all minerals from the water
It adds oxygen back into the water
It changes the color of the water
explanation: Boiling water kills disease-causing germs, making it safer to drink.

q: What gas does yeast release that causes bread dough to rise?
options: Carbon dioxide
Oxygen
Nitrogen
Water vapor
explanation: Yeast carries out anaerobic respiration that releases carbon dioxide, which makes bread dough rise.

q: Which Philippine government agency manages the protected areas system that preserves native animals and plants?
options: DENR
DOST
CHED
DOH
explanation: The DENR (Department of Environment and Natural Resources) manages the protected areas system in the Philippines, preserving native animals and plants from human encroachment.

q: What can a snail's eyes — found at the tips of its tentacles — actually detect?
options: Light and dark only, not clear images
Colours and shapes clearly
Movement of fast-moving objects
Detailed shapes and distances
explanation: Snails have simple eyes that only sense light and dark, not clear images.

q: How does a pako fern reproduce?
options: Through spores, not flowers or seeds
By producing small seeds in its leaves
By releasing pollen from its flowers
By dropping fruits that contain seeds
explanation: Pako is a fern, so it has no flowers or seeds and reproduces through spores.

q: Besides spreading seeds, how else does the flying fox help plants like the durian tree?
options: It pollinates flowers by carrying pollen on its fur
It digs around tree roots to aerate the soil
It eats insects that would otherwise damage the flowers
It waters the roots by bringing water in its mouth
explanation: While drinking nectar or eating flowers, pollen sticks to the flying fox's fur and gets carried to other flowers, helping trees like durian grow fruit.

q: What special ability do some jellyfish have in the dark ocean?
options: They can glow and make their own light
They can change color to match the seafloor
They can shoot jets of water to move fast
They can produce loud sounds to scare predators
explanation: Some jellyfish can glow and make their own light in the dark ocean.

q: Which gas from the air do plants take in during photosynthesis?
options: Carbon dioxide (CO2)
Oxygen (O2)
Nitrogen (N2)
Hydrogen (H2)
explanation: The gas that plants take in from the air is carbon dioxide (CO2).

q: Why is the side of a mountain facing away from the wind usually dry?
options: The air drops its rain on the front side, so it is dry by the time it crosses over
The rock on the back side absorbs all rainfall before it reaches the ground
The back side is always in full sunlight, which evaporates rain instantly
Cold temperatures on the back side prevent clouds from forming at all
explanation: When wind pushes clouds up over a mountain, they cool and drop their rain on the front side, so the air reaching the back side is already dry — creating a rain shadow.

q: Why does the pangolin population recover very slowly if its numbers decline?
options: The mother usually gives birth to only one offspring and carries it for many months
The pangolin can only breed once in its entire lifetime
Pangolin eggs take more than two years to hatch underground
Young pangolins leave the mother after just one week and many do not survive
explanation: The pangolin reproduces slowly — usually only one offspring is born and the mother carries it on her tail for many months.

q: How fast is the air that comes out when you sneeze?
options: Much faster than walking speed
About the same speed as walking
Slower than a person walking
Just a gentle puff of air
explanation: When you sneeze, air bursts out of your nose and mouth very fast — much faster than walking.

q: Why does a balloon shrink when it is left in a cold place?
options: The air particles inside slow down and take up less space
The rubber of the balloon gets tighter and squeezes the air out
Cold air is heavier and presses the balloon from the outside
The air inside turns into water when it gets cold
explanation: In cold temperatures, air particles inside the balloon slow down and take up less space, so the balloon shrinks.

q: Why do scientists study commensalism between organisms?
options: To understand how organisms connect in nature and protect the balance of ecosystems
To find out which organisms can be removed without any effect on the environment
To discover new medicines that can be made from commensal organisms
To show that some organisms have no relationship with others at all
explanation: Scientists study commensalism to understand how organisms connect in nature, which helps them protect the balance of ecosystems.

q: What kind of animal is a sand dollar, and where does it live?
options: A flattened sea urchin that lives on or just under the sand
A type of jellyfish that floats near the sea surface
A small crab that buries itself in coral reefs
A flat starfish that clings to rocky shores
explanation: The sand dollar is a type of sea urchin with a flattened, disc-shaped body; it lives lying on sand or slightly buried.

q: Why is the waling-waling orchid endangered in the wild?
options: Because of forest loss
Because it cannot reproduce on its own
Because animals eat its flowers before they can make seeds
Because it only grows in one small crater and was nearly wiped out by a flood
explanation: The waling-waling is endangered in the wild because of forest loss, so it is protected by law.

q: What happens when the pancreas does not make enough insulin?
options: Blood sugar rises and diabetes can develop
Blood pressure drops dangerously low
The heart beats too fast
The kidneys stop filtering waste
explanation: When the pancreas does not make enough insulin, blood sugar rises and diabetes can develop.

q: When does a plant lose water through transpiration most quickly?
options: When the weather is hot or sunny
When it is raining heavily
During cold winter nights
When the plant is in the shade
explanation: Transpiration happens faster when the weather is hot or sunny.

q: Which animal holds the record as the longest-living vertebrate?
options: The Greenland shark, living more than 400 years
The giant tortoise, living more than 200 years
The bowhead whale, living more than 250 years
The koi fish, living more than 300 years
explanation: The Greenland shark is the longest-living vertebrate, able to live more than 400 years.

q: What happens to red litmus paper when it is dipped in a base?
options: It turns blue
It turns green
It stays red
It turns yellow
explanation: Red litmus paper turns blue in a base.

q: Which moon is the second-largest in the solar system?
options: Titan
Europa
Callisto
The Moon (Earth's)
explanation: Titan is the second-largest moon in the solar system, about 5,150 kilometers across.

q: Which branch of the Philippine government is responsible for enforcing the laws?
options: The Executive branch, led by the President
The Legislative branch, led by Congress
The Judicial branch, led by the Supreme Court
The Military branch, led by the Armed Forces
explanation: The Executive branch, led by the President, enforces the laws in the Philippines.

q: How does the electric eel's shock compare to the electricity from a wall socket at home?
options: It is even more powerful than a wall socket, but lasts only a split second
It is about the same strength as a wall socket
It is much weaker than a wall socket but stings a little
It is stronger only if the eel is fully grown and the water is warm
explanation: An electric eel's shock is even higher than the electricity from a wall socket, but it lasts only a split second.

q: Why is the fruit dove often heard but rarely seen?
options: It has a soft cooing call, so you can hear it but it stays hidden in the trees
It only comes out at night when it is too dark to spot
It calls very loudly, which makes people look in the wrong direction
It mimics other bird calls, so listeners mistake it for a different species
explanation: The fruit dove has a soft cooing call, so it is often heard but not seen as it hides in the forest canopy.

q: What caused the deadly tsunami in the Philippines in 1976?
options: A strong earthquake in the Moro Gulf
A volcanic eruption on Mindanao
A powerful tropical typhoon hitting the coast
An underwater landslide near Leyte
explanation: In 1976, a strong earthquake in the Moro Gulf caused a tsunami that was one of the worst disasters in Philippine history.

q: What are the two segments that make up the Marikina Valley Fault System?
options: The West Valley Fault and the East Valley Fault
The North Valley Fault and the South Valley Fault
The Upper Marikina Fault and the Lower Marikina Fault
The Metro Manila Fault and the Quezon City Fault
explanation: The Marikina Valley Fault System has two segments: the West Valley Fault and the East Valley Fault.

q: Who described the law of universal gravitation, which says every object with mass pulls on every other object?
options: Isaac Newton
Galileo Galilei
Albert Einstein
Johannes Kepler
explanation: Isaac Newton described the law of gravity (universal gravitation), explaining that every object with mass pulls on every other object.

q: Even though some farms now use machines or tractors, why does the carabao remain important to Filipinos?
options: It remains a symbol of the hardworking Filipino as the national animal
It is still faster than any machine on muddy rice paddies
It produces more milk than any other farm animal in the Philippines
Machines break down too often, so farmers always keep a carabao as a backup
explanation: Even though some farms use machines or tractors, the carabao remains a symbol of the hardworking Filipino as the national animal.

q: How many teeth can a single shark grow over its whole lifetime?
options: Thousands of teeth
About 32 teeth, just like humans
Around 200 teeth in total
Only 2 sets of teeth — one as a pup and one as an adult
explanation: Over its whole life, a single shark can grow and lose thousands of teeth.

q: Why should you wash your hands after using the toilet?
options: Because there are many germs in poop
Because the toilet handle is made of metal and rusts your skin
Because soap smells nice and keeps skin soft
Because cold water wakes you up and keeps you alert
explanation: You should wash your hands after using the toilet because there are many germs in poop.

q: What happens when you pour oil and water together in a container?
options: They form two separate layers because they do not mix
They mix together evenly to form a clear liquid
The oil dissolves completely into the water over time
They react together to form a new substance
explanation: Oil and water do not mix, so they form two separate layers when put together.

q: Why are countries like the Maldives, which are made of atolls, threatened today?
options: Because they are so low, they are threatened by rising sea levels
Because atolls are made of soft sand that is quickly washed away by waves
Because strong volcanic eruptions are common under atoll chains
Because they have no rivers, so fresh water is almost impossible to find
explanation: Countries like the Maldives are made of atolls, and because they are so low, they are threatened by rising sea levels.

q: Who discovered the link between electricity and magnetism, and in what year?
options: Hans Christian Oersted in 1820
Michael Faraday in 1831
James Clerk Maxwell in 1865
Nikola Tesla in 1888
explanation: Hans Christian Oersted discovered the link between electricity and magnetism in 1820.

q: How does the female hornbill get food while she is sealed inside a tree hole with her eggs?
options: The male hornbill brings food and passes it through a small slit in the sealed entrance
She stores large amounts of food inside the hole before sealing herself in
She comes out briefly each night to feed, then re-seals the entrance
The chicks crack the seal open when hungry, and the female goes out to find food
explanation: When the female hornbill seals herself inside a tree hole, the male brings food and passes it through the small slit to feed her and the chicks.

q: What body part does the pawikan use to swim quickly in the sea?
options: Paddle-like flippers
A powerful tail fin like a fish
Large webbed back feet
Strong clawed arms
explanation: The pawikan has paddle-like flippers that it uses to swim quickly in the sea.

q: How does hail form inside a thunderstorm cloud?
options: Small ice pieces are repeatedly lifted by strong updrafts and collect more layers of ice before falling
Raindrops freeze instantly when lightning strikes them mid-air
Water droplets freeze together at the very top of the cloud and fall straight down
Ice crystals near the ground are picked up by the wind and blown into clouds
explanation: Hail forms when small ice pieces in a cumulonimbus cloud are repeatedly lifted by strong updrafts and accumulate more layers of ice before falling.

q: Why is marble harder and shinier than limestone?
options: Because heat and pressure changed the limestone into marble
Because marble forms from sand while limestone forms from mud
Because marble contains iron that makes it harder and more reflective
Because marble is younger rock and has not worn down yet
explanation: Because of heat and pressure, marble is harder and shinier than limestone, so it is used for statues and floors.

q: Why is water pressure in the deep ocean so enormous?
options: Because of the weight of all the water above pressing down
Because underwater volcanoes constantly push water downward
Because salt water is much heavier than the rocks on the ocean floor
Because ocean currents compress the water as they circulate
explanation: In the deep ocean the water pressure is enormous because of the weight of all the water above.

q: What features help cave crickets find food and move around in the dark?
options: Long legs and long feelers (antennae)
Big eyes that can see in very dim light
Glowing patches on their bodies to see the cave walls
A strong sense of smell from openings on their feet
explanation: Cave crickets have long legs and feelers (antennae) that help them move and find food in the dark.

q: Why do scientists think the Greenland shark can live more than 300 years?
options: Because it grows very slowly in the cold ocean
Because it sleeps for months at a time to save energy
Because it has two hearts that take turns pumping blood
Because it can replace its organs when they wear out
explanation: The Greenland shark is believed to live more than 300 years because it grows so slowly in the cold ocean.

q: Which of the following correctly describes one of the three forms of commensalism?
options: Phoresy — one organism hitches a ride on another to travel
Mutualism — both organisms help each other and both benefit
Parasitism — one organism feeds on another and harms it
Predation — one organism hunts and eats the other
explanation: Phoresy is one of the three forms of commensalism, where one organism hitches a ride on another to travel without harming it.

q: What element is a diamond made of?
options: Pure carbon
Pure iron
Silicon and oxygen
Calcium and phosphorus
explanation: A diamond is made of pure carbon, a single element.

q: How are a voltmeter and an ammeter connected differently in a circuit?
options: A voltmeter is connected in parallel; an ammeter is connected in series
A voltmeter is connected in series; an ammeter is connected in parallel
Both are connected in series but on opposite sides of the battery
Both are connected in parallel but to different components
explanation: A voltmeter is connected in parallel with a component to measure voltage, while an ammeter is connected in series — their connection methods are opposite.

q: Why are scissors sometimes a better cutting tool than a knife for paper or cloth?
options: Scissors have two blades that support each other, giving more control and a neater cut
Scissors are always sharper than a knife because they are made of harder metal
A knife is heavier, so it gets tired and wobbles, while scissors stay steady
Scissors make a safer cut because they can only close, not stab
explanation: Unlike a knife that must be pressed down on a surface, scissors have two blades that support each other, giving more control and a neater cut.

q: What happens to a baby when its mother smokes or drinks alcohol during pregnancy?
options: The baby in the womb is harmed too
The baby is protected because the placenta blocks all harmful substances
The baby is only affected after birth, not while inside the womb
Only the mother's health is affected; the baby is not harmed
explanation: When a pregnant woman smokes or drinks alcohol, the baby in her womb is harmed too.

q: Of the three fruits — guyabano, guava, and avocado — which one is the largest and can weigh several kilograms?
options: Guava
Guyabano
Avocado
Papaya
explanation: The guyabano is the largest of the three fruits and can weigh several kilograms.

q: How is PHIVOLCS earthquake intensity written differently from earthquake magnitude?
options: Intensity uses decimal numbers; magnitude uses Roman numerals
Intensity uses Roman numerals; magnitude uses decimal numbers
