options: It swallows its prey whole, usually head first
It bites off large pieces and chews them slowly
It uses venom to dissolve the prey before eating
It tears the prey apart with its claws before swallowing
explanation: A python does not chew its food; it swallows its prey whole, usually head first.

q: How does a solar water heater provide hot water without using electricity?
options: Rooftop collectors absorb sunlight and transfer the heat to a water tank
It uses mirrors to focus sunlight onto a boiler that generates electricity to heat water
Chemicals in the collector panels react with sunlight to produce heat
Solar panels charge a battery that powers an electric heating element
explanation: A solar water heater uses rooftop collectors to absorb sunlight and transfer the heat to a water tank, providing hot water without using electricity.

q: Do all plants have roots that hold them firmly in the ground?
options: Most do, but some water plants float and hold on differently
Yes, every single plant has deep roots in the ground
No, most plants float freely and do not need roots
Only trees have roots; small plants do not
explanation: Most plants have roots to hold on, but some water plants float and are not stuck deep in the ground, so they hold on differently.

q: How do some catfish move across land to find a new pool of water?
options: By wriggling with their fins
By rolling on their sides
By jumping with their tails
By crawling on their belly scales
explanation: Some catfish can move across land by wriggling with their fins to travel between water sources.

q: Why can dirty water be cleaned using physical methods like filtering instead of chemical reactions?
options: Because water and dirt form only a mixture, not a compound
Because dirt dissolves completely in water
Because water becomes a new substance when mixed with dirt
Because filtering adds chemicals that destroy the dirt
explanation: Dirty water is just a mixture of water and dirt, so physical methods like filtering can separate them without a chemical reaction.

q: Which river in the Philippines is the longest?
options: Cagayan River
Pasig River
Pampanga River
Agusan River
explanation: The Cagayan River in Luzon is the longest river in the Philippines.

q: Which strait did Manila-Acapulco galleon trade ships pass through during the Spanish period?
options: San Bernardino Strait
Surigao Strait
Sibuyan Strait
Mindoro Strait
explanation: The Manila-Acapulco galleon trade ships passed through the San Bernardino Strait during the Spanish period.

q: What actually stops a cut from bleeding instead of it just 'magically disappearing'?
options: Tiny body parts called platelets and fibrin do the work
The blood dries up because air touches it
White blood cells absorb all the leaked blood
The skin grows back instantly to seal the cut
explanation: Platelets and fibrin are the tiny body parts that actually clot blood — it is a real physical process, not magic.

q: What does a dialysis machine do for a patient whose kidneys have failed?
options: It filters waste and excess water from the blood
It pumps extra oxygen into the bloodstream
It produces hormones the kidneys can no longer make
It sends electrical signals to restart the kidneys
explanation: When kidneys fail, a dialysis machine takes over the job of filtering waste and excess water from the blood to keep the patient alive.

q: How does more CO2 in the ocean harm corals, clams, and similar sea animals?
options: It makes the ocean more acidic, slowing their ability to build shells
It removes the salt that their shells need to stay hard
It raises the water temperature until their shells melt
It reduces sunlight so they cannot get energy to grow
explanation: As the ocean absorbs more CO2 it becomes more acidic, which slows the ability of corals and clams to build their calcium carbonate shells.

q: Which nutrient from foods like fish, eggs, and beans helps a child's body grow and repair itself?
options: Protein
Carbohydrates
Vitamins
Fiber
explanation: Protein from fish, eggs, meat, and beans helps the body grow and repair itself.

q: What are the smaller earthquakes called that follow a strong earthquake and can last for several days?
options: Aftershocks
Foreshocks
Tremors
Micro-quakes
explanation: After a strong earthquake, weaker earthquakes called aftershocks usually follow and can continue for several days.

q: When an animal moves to a warmer place because the season has turned cold, what adaptation is it using?
options: Migration
Hibernation
Camouflage
Mimicry
explanation: Migration is the adaptation where animals move to another place when the season changes.

q: Where does most of the nitrous oxide greenhouse gas in the air come from?
options: Farming — microbes in fertilized soil produce it
Burning coal and gasoline in power plants
Factories that make plastic and rubber products
Natural forest fires caused by lightning
explanation: Much of the nitrous oxide in the air comes from farming, when microbes in fertilized soil produce it.

q: A gun pushes a bullet forward when fired, and the gun itself jerks backward. What is this backward jerk called?
options: Recoil
Friction
Inertia
Momentum
explanation: When a gun fires the bullet forward (action), the bullet pushes the gun backward (reaction) — this backward push is called recoil.

q: Why does sweating help cool your body down on a hot day?
options: When sweat evaporates from the skin, it takes heat away with it
Sweat contains cold water that lowers your body temperature directly
Sweat makes your skin slippery so hot air cannot stick to it
Sweat blocks your pores so the body stops producing heat
explanation: When sweat evaporates from the skin, it takes heat away from the body, which cools us down.

q: At what exact point does light change direction when it moves from air into water?
options: At the boundary or surface where air and water meet
As soon as it enters the middle of the water
Just before it exits the water back into air
At the deepest part of the water it travels through
explanation: Light changes direction right at the boundary where the two materials (like air and water) meet — that is where refraction happens.

q: How does cogon grass spread and grow into new areas?
options: Through tough underground stems called rhizomes
By scattering seeds carried by the wind
By sending runners along the surface of the soil
Through spores released from its leaves
explanation: Cogon spreads through tough underground stems called rhizomes.

q: Plants need light to make their own food. What kind of thing is light?
options: A form of energy
A type of gas
A kind of matter
A chemical substance
explanation: Light is a form of energy, and plants use it to make their own food.

q: What is one reason the Philippines is expanding the use of solar, wind, and geothermal energy?
options: To reduce greenhouse gas emissions
To lower household electricity prices immediately
To replace all rivers with power-generating dams
To stop all typhoons from forming
explanation: The Philippines is expanding renewable energy to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and achieve a cleaner future.

q: Which planet in our solar system spins almost completely on its side?
options: Uranus
Saturn
Neptune
Venus
explanation: Uranus is the planet that spins almost on its side, tilted nearly sideways.

q: Which is the largest hot desert in the world?
options: The Sahara in Africa
The Arabian Desert in Asia
The Gobi Desert in Asia
The Kalahari Desert in Africa
explanation: The Sahara in Africa is the largest hot desert in the world, covering about 9.2 million square kilometers.

q: What helps baby warty pigs stay hidden from predators?
options: Stripes on their bodies
Spots on their snouts
A very dark black coat
Large ears that blend with leaves
explanation: Baby warty pigs have stripes on their bodies that help them hide.

q: What do your eyes do when you try to focus on an object held very close to your face?
options: Both eyes turn slightly inward toward the nose
Both eyes turn slightly outward toward the ears
One eye looks forward while the other relaxes
Both eyes look straight ahead without moving
explanation: When looking at a very close object, both eyes turn slightly inward toward the nose to focus on it together.

q: Where are most of the remaining tamaraws in the Philippines protected?
options: Mounts Iglit-Baco Natural Park on Mindoro
Mount Apo Natural Park on Mindanao
Palawan Biosphere Reserve on Palawan
Northern Sierra Madre Natural Park on Luzon
explanation: Most of the remaining tamaraws are protected in the Mounts Iglit-Baco Natural Park on Mindoro.

q: You push an upside-down glass into a bucket of water and the inside stays dry. What does this show?
options: Air inside the glass takes up space so water cannot enter
Glass is waterproof so no water can get in
The water is too heavy to rise into the glass
A vacuum forms that pushes the water out
explanation: Water cannot enter the upside-down glass because air already occupies the space inside it — proving air takes up space.

q: Why is it actually safe to be inside a car during lightning — even though the tires are rubber?
options: The metal shell of the car carries electricity around you and into the ground
The rubber tires stop electricity from ever reaching the car
The plastic dashboard absorbs all of the electrical charge
The glass windows deflect lightning away from the car
explanation: You are safe because the metal body of the car carries the electricity around you and into the ground — not because of the rubber tires.

q: How are low-lying Philippine islands being threatened by climate change?
options: Rising sea levels may flood or submerge them
Warmer air is causing them to crack and sink faster
More frequent storms are breaking them into smaller pieces
Increased rainfall is washing away their soil into the sea
explanation: Some low-lying Philippine islands are threatened by sea level rise from climate change.

q: In modern science, what is the main reason two organisms are placed in the same group?
options: They share a common ancestor
They look very similar on the outside
They live in the same habitat
They eat the same kind of food
explanation: In modern classification, organisms that share a common ancestor are grouped together.

q: Instead of a true heart, what does an earthworm have to pump blood through its body?
options: Five pairs of heart-like aortic arches
One simple tube-shaped heart
Two chambers that work like a pump
A network of tiny pulsing blood vessels with no central pump
explanation: An earthworm has no true heart, but five pairs of heart-like aortic arches that pump its blood.

q: What was the nationality of the famous physicist Albert Einstein by birth?
options: German
American
Swiss
Austrian
explanation: Albert Einstein was a German-born physicist.

q: Which colorful mantis shrimp known for its vivid colors and powerful punch can be found on Philippine reefs?
options: Peacock mantis shrimp
Banded mantis shrimp
Flower mantis shrimp
Ghost mantis shrimp
explanation: The Peacock mantis shrimp (Odontodactylus scyllarus) is one of the most colorful mantis shrimp and is seen on Philippine reefs.

q: What part of a clock allows the gear train to move one tooth at a time with each swing of the pendulum?
options: The escapement mechanism
The main spring
The minute hand axle
The balance wheel
explanation: A clock's escapement mechanism allows the gear train to advance by exactly one tooth per pendulum swing, keeping accurate time.

q: Which immune cells directly destroy body cells that have been infected by a virus?
options: Cytotoxic T cells (killer T cells)
B cells that make antibodies
Red blood cells that carry oxygen
Platelets that form clots around the infection
explanation: Cytotoxic T cells directly kill virus-infected cells by seeking out cells displaying viral antigens on their surface and destroying them.

q: A pendulum with a smooth, slippery pivot swings for a longer time than one with a rough, rusty pivot. Why?
options: Less friction at the pivot means less energy is lost with each swing
A smoother pivot is lighter so gravity pulls it less strongly
A slippery surface makes the pendulum swing faster and gain energy
Rough surfaces push the pendulum forward giving it extra force
explanation: If the pivot is smooth, there is less friction, so less energy is lost and the pendulum swings for a longer time.

q: What does the fact that almost all distant galaxies are slowly moving away from us tell scientists?
options: The universe is expanding and began with the Big Bang
The Milky Way is at the exact center of the universe
Gravity between galaxies is getting weaker over time
All galaxies are moving in a single direction toward empty space
explanation: Distant galaxies moving away from us is evidence that the universe is expanding and began with the Big Bang.

q: The unit of energy called the 'joule' is named after which scientist?
options: James Prescott Joule
James Watt
Isaac Newton
Michael Faraday
explanation: The joule, the unit of energy and work, is named after James Prescott Joule, an English scientist.

q: If you have a common cold, what does medicine actually do for you?
options: It helps you feel more comfortable while your body heals itself
It kills the cold virus so you recover faster
It prevents the cold from spreading to your lungs
It replaces the immune cells lost during the infection
explanation: There is no direct cure for the common cold; medicine only helps you feel better while your body heals itself.

q: What is one useful feature of having a santol tree in a yard?
options: It grows quite tall and gives cool shade
It produces flowers that repel mosquitoes
It has roots that clean the soil of harmful chemicals
Its leaves release a fresh scent that cools the air
explanation: The santol tree can grow quite tall and gives cool shade in a yard.

q: How can the parts of a mixture be separated?
options: By physical means like filtering, without a chemical reaction
Only by heating the mixture until one part evaporates
By adding a chemical that reacts with one of the parts
By freezing the mixture solid and then breaking it apart
explanation: A mixture can be separated by physical means like filtering because no chemical bonds need to be broken.

q: Why does PAGASA give each typhoon that enters the Philippines a name?
options: So people can easily identify it and follow news about it
So pilots can avoid the typhoon's path more safely
So scientists can measure how strong each typhoon is
So the government knows how many typhoons come each year
explanation: PAGASA gives each typhoon a name so people can easily identify it and follow the news about it.

q: Why does a highlighter pen glow brightly under a UV (black) light?
options: The ink absorbs ultraviolet light and releases it as visible light
The ink reflects ultraviolet light back without changing it
The ink produces its own electricity when UV light touches it
The UV light heats the ink until it becomes bright enough to see
explanation: Fluorescence happens when a material absorbs ultraviolet light and emits visible light — which is why highlighter ink glows under UV.

q: Why does floating plastic trash collect in ocean gyres to form garbage patches?
options: Water circles within a gyre, trapping floating debris in the middle
Ocean currents push all trash toward the equator where gyres form
Wind blows plastic into the center of the ocean where gyres are
Gyres are areas of still water where everything naturally sinks and gathers
explanation: Because water circles within a gyre, floating plastic and trash collect there, forming a garbage patch.

q: In which region of the solar system is Pluto located?
options: The Kuiper Belt, beyond Neptune
The Asteroid Belt, between Mars and Jupiter
The Oort Cloud, at the very edge of the solar system
The inner solar system, between Earth and Mars
explanation: Pluto is in the Kuiper Belt, a distant region beyond the planet Neptune.

q: When water vapor changes directly into frost (solid ice) without first becoming liquid water, what is this change of state called?
options: Deposition
Sublimation
Condensation
Freezing
explanation: The change from a gas straight to a solid is called deposition — just like frost forming on a cold surface.

q: What kind of environment does the nipa palm grow in?
options: Soft mud that is regularly flooded and drained by tides
Dry rocky hillsides with very little rainfall
Dense forest floors with deep, rich soil
Sandy ocean beaches above the high-tide line
explanation: The nipa grows in soft mud that is flooded and drained by the rise and fall of the tides.

q: In which direction does the Coriolis effect curve moving air in the Northern Hemisphere?
options: To the right
To the left
Straight upward
Straight downward
explanation: In the Northern Hemisphere, moving air curves to the right due to the Coriolis effect.

q: Why is the Rafflesia flower considered a parasite?
options: It has no leaves, stem, or roots and lives inside a host vine
It steals pollen from other flowers using insect traps
It releases poison that kills surrounding plants for nutrients
It wraps its roots around another plant and blocks its sunlight
explanation: The Rafflesia has no visible leaves, stem, or roots — it is a parasite that lives inside a vine and only emerges when it blooms.

q: Why does a metal door handle feel hard and solid when you touch it at room temperature?
options: Almost all metals are solid at normal indoor warmth
Metals are always solid no matter how hot or cold they get
Door handles are made of painted wood that only looks like metal
Room temperature is too cold for any material to stay liquid
explanation: Room temperature is the normal indoor warmth, and at that temperature almost every metal is solid — which is why a door handle feels hard.

q: When you rub a balloon on your hair, the total electric charge stays the same. What happens instead?
options: Electrons move from one object to the other, making one positive and one negative
Both objects gain extra electrons from the air around them
The friction destroys some charge in each object equally
New positive charges are created inside the balloon
explanation: When two objects are rubbed together, electrons simply move from one to the other — the total charge does not change.

q: How does weather radar let forecasters detect rain even at night or far away?
options: It sends out radio waves that bounce off raindrops back to the receiver
It uses satellites to photograph clouds and measure their thickness
It measures how much the air pressure drops when rain is forming
It detects the lightning that always accompanies heavy rainfall
explanation: Weather radar sends out radio waves that bounce off raindrops, so forecasters can tell where it is raining and how hard.

q: Why do some engineers use bamboo to build bridges and structures?
options: Bamboo has a tensile strength comparable to steel per unit weight, making it very strong
Bamboo is hollow so it is lighter than any other building material
Bamboo grows faster than trees so it is always available nearby
Bamboo bends without breaking so it can absorb water pressure in floods
explanation: Bamboo has a tensile strength comparable to steel per unit weight, making it an excellent sustainable building material.

q: Under ideal conditions, how often can some bacteria double in number?
options: Every 20 minutes
Every 2 hours
Every 24 hours
Every 1 hour
explanation: Under ideal conditions, some bacteria can double in number every 20 minutes, which is why they can grow into billions within just a few hours.

q: Which two fruits are usually harvested in the Philippines during the rainy months of August to October?
options: Lanzones and rambutan
Mango and papaya
Banana and pineapple
Guava and jackfruit
explanation: In the Philippines, lanzones and rambutan are usually harvested in the rainy months from August to October.

q: When a falling object reaches terminal velocity, what happens to its speed?
options: It falls at a constant speed
It keeps speeding up
It slows down and stops
It speeds up then reverses direction
explanation: At terminal velocity, air resistance equals gravity, so the net force is zero and the object falls at a constant speed without speeding up anymore.

q: Why is a dugong NOT classified as a fish?
options: It is a mammal that must surface to breathe air
It has fins instead of flippers
It lives only in rivers and lakes
It lays eggs on land
explanation: A dugong is a mammal, not a fish, because it must come up to the surface to breathe air, unlike fish that breathe in water.

q: What did Ignaz Semmelweis discover in the 1840s about keeping new mothers safer in hospitals?
options: Having doctors wash their hands sharply reduced deaths
Giving mothers fresh vegetables prevented infection
Keeping windows open removed dangerous air
Changing bed sheets every day stopped disease
explanation: Semmelweis showed in the 1840s that deaths of new mothers dropped sharply when doctors washed their hands before treating patients.

q: What shape are lymph nodes, and roughly how many does the human body have?
options: Bean-shaped, and there are hundreds spread throughout the body
Round like marbles, and there are about 20 in the body
Flat like coins, and there are about 50 in the body
Tube-shaped, and there are about 10 in the body
explanation: The human body has hundreds of small bean-shaped lymph nodes spread all over the body.

q: In a geothermal power plant, what does the underground steam do to produce electricity?
options: It spins a turbine connected to a generator
It heats water in a boiler that melts copper wires
It pumps water uphill to turn a water wheel
It pushes air through fans that charge batteries
explanation: In a geothermal power plant, steam drawn from underground spins a turbine connected to a generator, which produces electricity.

q: How do diving beetles breathe while they are underwater hunting prey?
options: They carry an air bubble under their wing covers (elytra)
They absorb oxygen directly through their skin
They have gills like fish to breathe in water
They hold their breath and return to the surface every minute
explanation: Diving beetles carry an air bubble under their elytra, which provides oxygen for them to breathe while they hunt prey underwater.

q: How do wood-rot fungi help the environment when they break down dead trees?
options: They return nutrients to the soil for other plants to use
They make the wood harder so animals can live inside it
They produce seeds that grow into new trees
They create a layer of bark that protects the forest floor
explanation: Wood-rot fungi break down lignin and cellulose in dead trees, returning the nutrients locked in the wood back to the soil where other plants can use them.

q: What chemicals, once used in refrigerators and spray cans, damaged the ozone layer by breaking apart ozone molecules?
options: CFCs (chlorofluorocarbons)
Carbon dioxide
Methane
Nitrogen oxide
explanation: CFCs, once used in old refrigerators, air conditioners, and spray cans, rose into the sky and broke apart ozone molecules, causing the ozone layer to get thinner.

q: Why does the Philippines experience so many volcanoes and earthquakes?
options: It is part of the Pacific Ring of Fire
It sits on top of a single giant volcano
It is located at the center of the Pacific Ocean
It has more underground rivers than any other country
explanation: The Philippines is part of the Pacific Ring of Fire, a zone of intense volcanic and earthquake activity, which is why it has so many volcanoes and earthquakes.

q: What exactly is the scab that forms on a wound?
options: A dried-out blood clot that protects the skin while it heals
A layer of dead skin cells pushed up by the body
A plug of white blood cells covering the cut
A crust of bacteria that the body uses to seal the wound
explanation: A scab is a blood clot that has dried out, acting like a protective cover so new skin can heal underneath.

q: Why do many deep-sea fish, like the barreleye fish, have very large eyes?
options: To detect the tiny amounts of light available in the deep ocean
To scare away predators with their unusual appearance
To see in color because the deep ocean is very colorful
To see behind them without turning their head
explanation: Many deep-sea fish have enormous eyes adapted to detect the tiny amounts of light available in the dark deep ocean, helping them spot prey or predators.

q: Why do some birds hold their wings open and glide without flapping?
options: To save energy by riding the air
To show other birds they are not a threat
To cool down their bodies in hot weather
To spot prey more easily from high up
explanation: Birds sometimes hold their wings open and glide on the air without flapping in order to save energy.

q: What can happen to a horseshoe crab if it loses a leg?
options: A lost leg may grow back during its next molt
The crab dies because it cannot survive without all legs
The leg is replaced immediately without any molting
The leg scar seals permanently and never grows back
explanation: Horseshoe crabs are very tough, and a lost leg may grow back during the crab's next molt as it keeps growing.

q: If you suddenly notice a new, unusual smell coming from food that was left out, what does that suggest?
options: A chemical reaction is forming a new substance with its own odor
The food has simply changed temperature
Water vapor is evaporating from the food
The food is releasing stored vitamins into the air
explanation: A sudden new smell, such as from rotting food, is a sign of a chemical reaction forming a new substance with its own odor.

q: What happens to the current in a circuit when you open (turn off) the switch?
options: There is a gap so current stops flowing and the light goes off
Current flows faster because the resistance is removed
Current reverses direction and the light dims
Current continues but goes through a different path
explanation: When you open (turn off) the switch, it creates a gap in the circuit so current stops flowing and the light goes off.

q: Why is summer hotter than other seasons in a region?
options: That half of Earth is tilted toward the Sun, so rays are more direct and days are longer
The Sun is physically closer to Earth during summer
The clouds disappear completely so more sunlight reaches the ground
The Earth spins faster during summer making the days feel longer
explanation: Summer is hotter because the region is tilted toward the Sun, which makes sunlight hit more directly and days last longer.

q: What is one of the main reasons many unique animals and plants in the Philippines are threatened?
options: Habitat loss from deforestation and pollution
Too many national parks protecting the wrong species
Introduced animals competing for the same food
The rise in ocean temperature caused by nearby volcanoes
explanation: Habitat loss from deforestation and pollution is one of the main threats to many endemic animals and plants in the Philippines.

q: What was special about the large plate-like bones along Stegosaurus's back?
options: They may have helped with body heat or display
They were sharp weapons used to slice predators
They were hollow and acted as lungs for extra breathing
They were used to store fat like a camel's hump
explanation: Stegosaurus had a row of large, plate-like bones standing up along its back, which scientists think may have helped with body heat regulation or display.

q: When you send a photo over the internet, how does the data actually travel?
options: It is split into many tiny chunks called packets that may take different paths and are reassembled at the other end
It travels as one complete file through a single direct cable
It is converted into light and travels in one straight beam
It is stored on a satellite and beamed down all at once
explanation: Data sent over the internet is split into many tiny chunks called packets that may take different routes and are reassembled at the destination.

q: In what year did Henry Ford start the moving assembly line for the Model T?
explanation: Henry Ford started the moving assembly line for the Model T in 1913, revolutionizing how cars were built.

q: Around what year did Gutenberg invent the printing press?
options: Around 1440
Around 1200
Around 1600
Around 1350
explanation: Gutenberg invented the printing press around the year 1440, in the 15th century.

q: What can a strong earthquake under the sea create?
options: A tsunami — a huge wave that can strike the coast
A tornado over the ocean surface
A volcanic eruption on the sea floor only
A series of loud thunderclaps heard from shore
explanation: A strong undersea earthquake can displace huge amounts of water, creating a tsunami — a massive wave that can travel to and strike coastlines.

q: Which part of the carbon cycle moves over thousands to millions of years, involving rocks and fossil fuels?
options: The slow carbon cycle
The fast carbon cycle
The ocean carbon cycle
The photosynthesis carbon cycle
explanation: The slow carbon cycle operates over thousands to millions of years through rocks and fossil fuels, while the fast cycle operates through plants, animals, and air over days to years.

q: What is Apo Reef's ranking among coral reefs in the world?
options: It is the second largest contiguous coral reef in the world
It is the largest coral reef in Asia
It is the deepest coral reef in the Pacific Ocean
It is the third longest barrier reef in the world
explanation: Apo Reef is the second largest contiguous coral reef in the whole world, making it one of the Philippines' most important marine treasures.

q: Why do sailors regularly scrape barnacles off the bottom of their boats?
options: Barnacles make the hull rough and slow the boat down, burning more fuel
Barnacles are poisonous to the fish that sailors want to catch
Barnacles corrode the metal hull and cause it to rust faster
Barnacles make noise underwater that scares fish away
explanation: Many barnacles clinging to a boat's hull make it rough and slow the boat down, causing it to burn more fuel, so sailors scrape them off periodically.

q: Besides gold, what important metal found in the Philippines is used for carrying electricity?
options: Copper
Iron
Aluminum
Nickel
explanation: Besides gold, the Philippines is also rich in copper, a metal important for carrying electricity in wires and cables.

q: What do white blood cells do when germs get inside the body?
options: They catch and swallow germs like the body's soldiers
They carry oxygen to body cells to fight infection
They produce antibiotics that dissolve germs
They block blood vessels so germs cannot spread
explanation: White blood cells act like the body's soldiers, catching and swallowing germs that get inside.

q: What happens in a clownfish group when the largest female dies?
options: The dominant male changes sex and becomes the new female
The group splits up and each fish finds a new anemone
The youngest male takes over as the new leader
All the remaining fish die because only the female can lead
explanation: When the leading female dies, the dominant male in the group changes sex and becomes the new female — a process called protandrous hermaphroditism.

q: Why does a gun kick backward when it fires a bullet forward?
options: The total momentum must stay balanced, so the gun moves back as the bullet moves forward
Gravity pulls the gun down while the bullet flies up
The explosion pushes both the bullet and gas forward, dragging the gun along
Air pressure behind the bullet pushes back on the shooter's hand
explanation: When a gun fires, the bullet moves forward and the gun recoils backward because the total momentum must stay balanced — this is conservation of momentum.

q: Why is fresh water scarce on many small islands in the Philippines?
options: The land is small so little rain is collected, and over-pumping wells lets salty seawater seep in
The islands are surrounded by too many coral reefs that block rainfall
The soil on small islands absorbs all rain immediately so none reaches wells
Strong winds blow most rain clouds away before they can drop water
explanation: On small islands, there is little land to collect rain and no big rivers; if too much water is pumped from wells, salty seawater seeps in, making fresh water very limited.

q: What keeps a Filipino bangka from tipping over while being paddled?
options: Outriggers on both sides balance the boat
A heavy metal keel underneath the hull
Two rows of seats that spread the fishermen's weight
A flat bottom that rests on shallow water
explanation: The bangka has outriggers on both sides that keep it stable and prevent it from tipping over while paddling.

q: Which color of light causes plants to bend most strongly toward it?
options: Blue light
Red light
Yellow light
Green light
explanation: Plants bend most strongly toward blue light because it is the most effective part of sunlight at causing phototropism.

q: What is the white half-moon shape at the base of your fingernail called, and what is it?
options: The lunula — the spot where new nail is still being formed before it hardens
The matrix — a scar left behind from a past injury
The cuticle — a layer of dead skin covering the nail root
The nail bed — the pink tissue that gives the nail its color
explanation: The white half-moon at the base of a nail is called the lunula — it is where new nail is still forming and has not yet hardened.

q: How does making atchara keep the shredded papaya from spoiling?
options: The acid and salt in the vinegar and salt mixture stop spoilage microbes
The sugar ferments into alcohol that kills all bacteria in the jar
The papaya is dried in the sun until all moisture is removed
The jar is sealed airtight so no bacteria can ever enter
explanation: Atchara is preserved because the acid from vinegar and the salt stop spoilage microbes from growing, so the food lasts longer.

q: What does the nose do with the information it picks up from a smell?
options: It sends signals to the brain so it can identify the smell
It stores the smell as a chemical inside the nose lining
It filters out bad smells before they reach the lungs
It converts the smell into sound waves the brain can read
explanation: The nose sends signals to the brain so the brain can tell what the smell is.

q: How do thick mats of water hyacinth cause problems for fishermen?
options: They block boats and make it hard to fish
They poison the fish hiding underneath them
They dry up the water by absorbing too much of it
They attract crocodiles that attack the fishermen
explanation: Thick mats of water hyacinth block boats and make it hard for fishermen to work on the water.

q: Which combination of observations is a sign that a chemical change has happened?
options: A change in color, giving off heat or smoke, and bubbling
A change in shape, size, or position without any new substance
Melting, freezing, or evaporating when temperature changes
Stretching, bending, or compressing without breaking
explanation: A change in color, giving off heat or smoke, and bubbling are all signs that a chemical change has occurred, forming a new substance.

q: What does tilting a mirror show about reflected light?
options: Reflected light goes wherever you point the mirror, showing you can aim it
Reflected light always bounces straight back to its source
Tilting a mirror makes light brighter by concentrating it
A mirror changes the color of the light that bounces off it
explanation: By tilting a mirror, you can aim a patch of reflected sunlight onto any surface, showing that reflected light travels in whatever direction the mirror is pointed.

q: What number does diamond hold on the Mohs hardness scale?
explanation: Diamond is number 10 on the Mohs hardness scale, making it the hardest natural material known.

q: Why does a gecko's sticky grip look like magic to the human eye?
options: The millions of tiny hairs on its feet are too small to see without a microscope
The feet produce an invisible glue that washes off in water
The gecko uses suction cups that only work on smooth surfaces
Static electricity builds up on its feet making it cling to walls
explanation: A gecko's grip looks like magic because its foot hairs are so tiny they are invisible to the naked eye — you need a microscope to see the millions of hairs.

q: What actually causes the common cold?
options: Viruses that infect the nose and throat
Cold air entering the nose and throat
Getting wet in the rain without drying off
Breathing in dust from old books or carpets
explanation: The common cold is caused by viruses that infect the nose and throat, not by cold air, rain, or dust by itself.

q: Why doesn't a child have the exact same fingerprint as a parent?
options: DNA only sets the general pattern; the exact detail of every line forms uniquely during development
Fingerprints are completely random and have nothing to do with DNA
Children always have opposite fingerprint patterns from their parents
Fingerprints are identical at birth but change as a person grows
explanation: DNA only sets the general pattern type (like loop or whorl), but the exact detail of every ridge line is unique to each person and not inherited as a whole copy.

q: A campfire shows all three ways heat can move. Which correctly matches the method to the example?
options: Conduction when you touch the hot wood, convection in rising warm air, and radiation in the heat felt from the side
Radiation when you touch the wood, conduction in the rising smoke, and convection in the glow you see
Convection when you touch the coals, radiation in the rising air, and conduction in the light given off
Conduction in the rising smoke, radiation when you touch the ash, and convection in the heat felt from a distance
explanation: In a fire, conduction occurs when you touch hot wood, convection in the rising warm air, and radiation in the heat you feel even standing to the side.

q: What does the large central vacuole in a plant cell mainly do?
options: It stores water and helps keep the plant firm and upright
It converts sunlight into sugar for the plant to use
It controls what enters and leaves the cell like a gate
It makes proteins that the plant needs to grow
explanation: Plants have a large central vacuole that stores water and helps keep the plant firm and upright through water pressure.

q: What is an antibody?
options: A protein made by the immune system to fight off a specific germ
A white blood cell that swallows bacteria whole
A chemical released by the liver to break down toxins
A type of red blood cell that carries oxygen to fight infection
explanation: An antibody is a protein made by the body's immune system specifically to recognize and fight off a particular germ.

q: Why does red cabbage juice used as a pH indicator stop working well after it gets old?
options: The anthocyanin breaks down and microbes spoil the juice over time
The juice absorbs too much acid from the air and becomes permanently neutral
The pigment gets brighter and too strong to show color changes
The water evaporates, leaving only the dye which no longer reacts
explanation: Over time, the anthocyanin in red cabbage juice breaks down and microbes spoil it, so it is best to use fresh juice or keep it in the fridge.

q: How can a person get a tapeworm?
options: By eating raw or undercooked pork or beef
By drinking water left in an open cup overnight
By touching a dog or cat that has a tapeworm
By breathing in dust from old soil in the garden
explanation: A person can get a tapeworm by eating raw or undercooked pork or beef that contains tapeworm larvae.

q: Why is secondhand smoke especially dangerous for a child who has asthma?
options: The smoke makes the small airways in the lungs swell and tighten, triggering an attack
The nicotine in smoke destroys the antibodies that normally prevent asthma
Smoke lowers the amount of oxygen in the room making the child dizzy
The smell of smoke causes a stress response that speeds up the heart dangerously
explanation: For a child with asthma, secondhand smoke causes the small airways in the lungs to swell and tighten, which triggers a sudden attack and makes breathing very difficult.

q: Where does most of our food begin its journey before it reaches our table?
options: On a farm or fishpond
In a grocery store
Inside a factory
At the local market
explanation: Most of our food begins on a farm or fishpond, where farmers and fishers harvest it before it travels to the market and finally to our table.

q: At what temperature does water both melt and freeze?
explanation: A substance's melting point and freezing point are the same temperature; for water, both are 0°C.

q: Why does the sky look red and orange at sunset?
options: Light travels through more air and blue light is scattered away
The Sun produces red light only in the evening
Dust particles in the air add color to the sky
The Earth's surface reflects red light upward
explanation: At sunset, light travels through more air, which scatters away the blue and leaves the red and orange colors.

q: How do mangrove roots help the plant survive in salty seawater?
options: They filter salt out of the seawater
They grow above the water to avoid the salt
They store fresh water inside their bark
They absorb salt and use it to make food
explanation: Mangrove roots filter salt out of seawater, and some kinds also push extra salt out through their leaves.

q: In a series circuit with several resistors in a row, what is true about the current flowing through them?
options: The same current flows through every part
Each resistor gets a different amount of current
The current doubles each time it passes a resistor
The current is zero until it reaches the last resistor
explanation: When resistors are in series, the same current flows through every part of the circuit.

q: Which Philippine herbal plant was developed into a medicine for cough?
options: Lagundi
Ampalaya
Malunggay
Sambong
explanation: Lagundi (Vitex negundo) is a Philippine herbal plant that was studied and developed into a medicine for cough.

q: What does a hummingbird do at night to save energy?
options: It slows its heartbeat and breathing in a state called torpor
It eats as much nectar as possible before sleeping
It flies to a warmer place and rests until morning
It shares body heat with other hummingbirds in a group
explanation: At night a hummingbird slows its heartbeat and breathing (called torpor) to save energy, because its tiny body cannot store much food.

q: What is one key difference between anaerobic respiration and regular aerobic respiration?
options: Anaerobic respiration happens without oxygen and makes less energy
Anaerobic respiration requires more oxygen and makes more energy
Anaerobic respiration only happens in plants, not animals
Anaerobic respiration produces oxygen as a waste product
explanation: Anaerobic respiration happens when there is no oxygen available, but it produces less energy than aerobic respiration.

q: What is one way students can help fight invasive species in their area?
options: Report any strange plant or animal they see
Collect invasive plants and keep them as pets
Feed invasive animals so they stay in one area
Release pet animals outdoors when no longer wanted
explanation: Students can help against invasive species by reporting any strange plant or animal they see, planting native plants, and never releasing pets.

q: How many vertical columns (groups) does the periodic table have?
explanation: The periodic table has 18 groups, which are its vertical columns.

q: Why are PM2.5 particles especially harmful to health?
options: They are tiny enough to travel deep into the lungs
They dissolve in blood and poison the body quickly
They block the nose and prevent breathing entirely
They are visible to the eye and easy to inhale by accident
explanation: PM2.5 particles are so tiny they can travel deep into the lungs, which is why they are measured in the air quality index.

q: What is the correct name for a baby cat?
options: Kitten
Puppy
Cub
Foal
explanation: A baby cat is called a kitten, while a baby dog is called a puppy.

q: In the food pyramid, which part of the pyramid should you eat the most of?
options: The widest part at the bottom
The narrow part at the very top
The middle section
All parts should be eaten in equal amounts
explanation: In the food pyramid, the widest part at the bottom should be eaten the most, and portions get smaller toward the tip.

q: Why does the Philippines have so many unique species found nowhere else on Earth?
options: Its islands provided isolation that allowed many species to evolve separately
Its warm tropical weather is perfect for all animals and plants
Its many rivers and lakes provide enough fresh water for all species
Philippine scientists have discovered and named more species than any other country
explanation: The Philippines is one of the world's most biodiverse places because its islands provided isolation, allowing many unique species to evolve that exist nowhere else on Earth.

q: If the entire sky is covered with clouds, what okta reading would a weather station record?
options: 8/8 oktas
4/8 oktas
1/8 oktas
0/8 oktas
explanation: Cloud cover is measured in oktas (eighths of the sky); 8/8 oktas means the entire sky is covered by cloud.

q: Which of the following keeps a population from growing without limit?
options: Shortage of food, disease, predators, and competition
The total number of species in an ecosystem
The average temperature and rainfall of the habitat
The size and speed of each individual animal
explanation: Population size is held in check by limiting factors such as shortage of food and water, disease, competition, and predators.

q: Besides being famous for surfing, what natural feature makes Siargao important for marine life?
options: Its extensive mangroves and lagoons that shelter fish
Its deep underwater trenches that protect large whales
Its coral reef gardens that attract foreign tourists
Its underwater caves that serve as breeding grounds for sharks
explanation: Besides surfing, Siargao has extensive mangroves and lagoons that serve as natural shelters for fish and other marine creatures.

q: Why are fossil fuels called non-renewable?
options: They do not form again quickly once they are used up
They are found only in countries that do not share them
They release so much energy that they burn up completely
They are solids and cannot be made into gas or liquid
explanation: Fossil fuels are called non-renewable because they do not form again quickly once they are used up.

q: Why do people stir or turn a compost pile regularly?
options: To let air in so that decomposers can stay alive and keep rotting the material
To spread moisture evenly so that nothing dries out too fast
To mix hot and cool layers so the temperature stays the same throughout
To push the compost down and make room for new waste on top
explanation: The decomposers in compost are alive and need air; turning the pile lets air in so rotting continues.

q: Into which body of water does the Abra River empty?
options: The South China Sea
The Pacific Ocean
Lingayen Gulf
Laguna de Bay
explanation: The Abra River flows from the Cordillera through the Ilocos Region and empties into the South China Sea through Ilocos Sur.

q: Why do some farmers tie a jackfruit to the branch while it is still growing?
options: Because it is so heavy it could be dangerous if it falls
Because tying it helps the fruit grow bigger and sweeter
Because the wind can easily blow the fruit off the branch
Because insects will eat the fruit if it is not protected
explanation: A jackfruit is so heavy that it can be dangerous if it falls from the tree, so some farmers tie it to the branch to prevent that.

q: What is prohibited by law in the Philippines regarding the pawikan (sea turtle)?
options: Collecting their eggs and killing them
Feeding them at sea or touching them on the beach
Taking photographs of them without a permit
Swimming near their nesting areas during nesting season
explanation: The pawikan is an endangered animal, and collecting their eggs and killing them is prohibited in the Philippines.

q: What is the difference between magma and lava?
options: Magma is molten rock underground, and it becomes lava once it erupts from a volcano
Lava is found underground and turns into magma when it reaches the surface
Magma is the cooled solid form of lava after an eruption
They are the same material with different temperatures
explanation: Molten rock underground is called magma, and it becomes lava once it erupts out of a volcano.

q: Which SI unit is used to measure electric current?
options: Ampere (A)
Volt (V)
Ohm (Ω)
Watt (W)
explanation: The ampere (A) is the SI base unit used to measure electric current.

q: A circuit has a voltage of 12 volts and a resistance of 4 ohms. What is the current?
options: 3 amperes
48 amperes
8 amperes
0.3 amperes
explanation: To find the current, divide the voltage by the resistance: 12 volts ÷ 4 ohms = 3 amperes.

q: If you turn red cabbage juice green by adding a base, what happens when you then add an acid to it?
options: The color changes back to red
The color turns permanently green and cannot change again
The juice becomes colorless because the reaction cancels out
The juice turns purple, which is a brand-new color
explanation: The color change in red cabbage juice is reversible — adding acid after a base brings the color back to red, and this can be repeated many times.

q: How does the skin color of a jackfruit change as it ripens on the tree?
options: It starts green and slowly turns yellow or brownish
It starts yellow and slowly turns bright red
It starts white and slowly turns dark purple
It stays green the whole time until it falls off the tree
explanation: While growing on the tree, the jackfruit skin is green, and as it ripens it slowly turns more yellow or brownish.

q: What type of germ causes leptospirosis?
options: A bacterium called Leptospira
A virus that spreads through air
A fungus that lives in standing water
A parasite found in contaminated food
explanation: Leptospirosis is a disease caused by a bacterium called Leptospira.

q: Why does a large predator need a wide territory to survive?
options: It gains only a little energy from each animal it catches, so it needs a large area
It must protect its territory from smaller animals that steal its food
It requires a large space to find a mate during breeding season
It needs room to exercise and build up enough speed for hunting
explanation: A large predator needs a wide area because it gains only a little energy from each animal it catches.

q: What is molasses?
options: The dark, thick leftover syrup when sugar cane does not fully crystallize
The first clear liquid squeezed directly from sugar cane stalks
The white powder produced when raw sugar is fully refined
The sweet sap collected from the roots of the sugar cane plant
explanation: Molasses is the dark, thick leftover syrup that remains when not all the sugar turns into crystals; it is used in food and as animal feed.

q: Which vaccines help prevent some types of pneumonia in children?
options: Pneumococcal and Hib vaccines
BCG and MMR vaccines
Hepatitis B and polio vaccines
Rabies and tetanus vaccines
explanation: Vaccines such as the pneumococcal and Hib vaccines help prevent some types of pneumonia in children.

q: What is the name of the bone in the upper arm?
options: Humerus
Femur
Radius
Tibia
explanation: The bone in the upper arm is called the humerus.

q: How does winding the crown of a mechanical watch store energy?
options: It compresses a coiled steel spring called the mainspring, which unwinds slowly to drive the gears
It charges a small battery that powers an electric motor inside the watch
It tightens a rubber band connected to the hands of the clock face
It pulls a weight upward that slowly falls and keeps the gears moving
explanation: The mainspring of a mechanical watch is a coiled steel spring; winding the crown compresses it and stores energy that unwinds slowly to drive the watch gears.

q: Where does the word 'electricity' come from?
options: From 'elektron,' the Greek word for amber
From 'electra,' the name of an ancient Greek goddess of lightning
From 'elec,' a Latin word meaning spark or flame
From 'lectron,' a Roman word meaning to attract or pull
explanation: Ancient people noticed that rubbed amber could attract small objects; from the Greek word for amber, 'elektron,' we get the word electricity.

q: How tall is Mount Apo, the highest mountain in the Philippines?
options: 2,954 meters
1,954 meters
3,500 meters
2,144 meters
explanation: Mount Apo stands 2,954 meters tall, making it the highest peak in the Philippines.

q: How did the Himalayas form, and why are they still slowly rising today?
options: The plate carrying India crashed into the plate of Asia, and that collision continues to push the land upward
Ancient volcanoes erupted so many times that their lava piled up into the highest peaks on Earth
Erosion by wind and water carved the rest of Asia down, leaving the Himalayas standing tall
The Himalayas formed when a giant meteor struck Asia and pushed the crust upward millions of years ago
explanation: The Himalayas formed when the plate carrying India crashed into the plate of Asia, and they are still slowly rising today because the plates continue to press together.

q: What does the male Palawan peacock-pheasant do to court a mate?
options: It spreads its colorful feathers
It sings a long and complex song from the treetops
It builds an elaborate nest to impress the female
It performs an aerial dance high above the forest
explanation: The male Palawan peacock-pheasant spreads its colorful feathers to court a mate.

q: How does a vine's tendril respond when it touches a branch?
options: It quickly curls around the branch
It pulls away from the branch to avoid damage
It grows new roots to anchor into the bark
It sends out sticky sap to glue itself to the surface
explanation: A vine's tendril can sense touch; when it feels a branch, it quickly curls around it to climb upward.

q: How many pairs of legs does a millipede have on each body segment?
options: Two pairs
One pair
Four pairs
Three pairs
explanation: A millipede has two pairs of legs on each segment, which is why it has more legs than a centipede.

q: In the study of evolution, what does 'fitness' mean?
options: An organism's ability to survive and reproduce in its environment
How strong and muscular an organism's body is
How fast an organism can run away from predators
How healthy and disease-free an organism is throughout its life
explanation: In evolution, 'fitness' refers to an organism's ability to survive and reproduce successfully in its own environment, not physical strength.

q: Which province in the Cordillera is known as one of the best gold mining areas in the Philippines?
options: Benguet
Mountain Province
Ifugao
Apayao
explanation: Benguet in the Cordillera is known as one of the best gold mining areas in the Philippines and has a long history of gold extraction.

q: What are lianas, and what is one example of a liana?
options: Woody, rope-like vines that climb forest trees; rattan is an example
Flat-leaved plants that float on the surface of rivers; water lily is an example
Underground root networks that connect different trees; bamboo is an example
Tall straight trees that grow faster than all others in the forest; mahogany is an example
explanation: Lianas are woody, rope-like vines that climb high forest trees; rattan is one example of a forest climbing plant.

q: Which type of radiation from radioactive decay can pass through both paper and thin metal, but is stopped by thick steel or lead?
options: Gamma radiation
Alpha radiation
Beta radiation
Ultraviolet radiation
explanation: Gamma radiation is the most penetrating type — alpha is stopped by paper, beta is stopped by thin metal, but gamma needs thick steel or lead to stop it.

q: Why are mountaintops colder than lowlands, even though they are closer to the Sun?
options: The Sun is so far away that a few kilometers of height makes no difference; thin air is what makes it cold
Clouds always cover mountaintops and block the Sun's warmth from reaching them
Mountains reflect the Sun's rays back into space instead of absorbing them
The wind at the top blows away all the heat before it can warm the rocks
explanation: The Sun is millions of kilometers away, so a few kilometers of height makes no difference; it is the thin air at high altitude that makes mountaintops cold.

q: What does an electric motor do?
options: It turns electricity into motion using magnets and electric current to spin a rod
It turns motion into electricity by spinning a coil inside a magnet
It stores electrical energy in chemicals and releases it as needed
It converts heat from a burning fuel into electrical energy
explanation: An electric motor turns electricity into motion: it uses magnets and electric current to spin a rod, which then runs a fan, a blender, or a wheel.

q: What are the four stages of a beetle's life cycle?
options: Egg, larva, pupa, and adult
Egg, nymph, pupa, and adult
Egg, caterpillar, cocoon, and adult
Egg, larva, adult, and elder
explanation: A beetle goes through complete metamorphosis: egg, larva, pupa, and then adult beetle.

q: Why do scientists study how skinks regrow their tails?
options: To learn how to help the human body heal better
To find out how fast lizards can grow in warm climates
To discover new materials that are as tough as a skink's tail
To understand how diet affects the speed of growth in reptiles
explanation: Scientists study how skinks regrow their tails because they hope to learn from it how to help the human body heal better.

q: What happens to wet, sandy ground when a strong earthquake shakes it?
options: It behaves like a liquid, causing buildings to sink or tilt
It hardens into solid rock, giving buildings extra support
It dries out completely and cracks open in a straight line
It turns into mud that slowly flows downhill over several days
explanation: Liquefaction makes wet, sandy ground act like a liquid when violently shaken, so heavy structures on top can sink or lean.

q: Why do mangrove roots stick up out of the water instead of staying underground?
options: To absorb sunlight for making food
To get air, because the muddy underwater soil has very little oxygen
To trap fish and small animals for nutrients
To store rainwater above the waterline during dry seasons
explanation: Mangrove roots grow upward above the water's surface because the muddy soil underwater contains too little oxygen for the roots to breathe.

q: A crab loses one of its eyes. When does its new eye grow back?
options: Immediately, within a few hours of losing it
When it sheds its old shell in a process called molting
Only if the water is warm enough during summer
After it eats enough food to produce the eye material
explanation: Crabs can regrow a lost eye during molting — when they shed their shell — because regrowing body parts is a special ability of crustaceans.

q: Why is the coconut palm sometimes called the 'tree of life'?
options: Because it lives for hundreds of years without ever dying
Because nearly every part of it — fruit, leaves, trunk, and roots — is useful to people
Because it only grows near sacred places and temples
Because its coconut water can cure most sicknesses
explanation: The coconut palm earns the nickname 'tree of life' because almost every part of the tree — fruit, leaves, trunk, and roots — can be used by people.

q: Which blood type is called the universal recipient?
options: Type O positive
Type A negative
Type B positive
Type AB positive
explanation: A person with AB positive blood is called the universal recipient because they can safely receive blood of any type.

q: What causes the leaves of a makahiya plant to fold shut when you touch them?
options: Tiny muscles in the leaf stem quickly contract and pull the leaf closed
Water rushes out of special cells at the base of each leaf, making them go soft and limp
The leaf releases a chemical that causes it to curl away from harm
Electrical signals travel through the plant and tighten the leaf fibers
explanation: When touched, water quickly leaves the water-filled cells at the base of each makahiya leaf, causing the cells to go limp and the leaf to droop shut.

q: How long would the fastest rocket take to reach the nearest star to our Sun?
options: About one year
A few hundred years
Thousands of years
A few decades
explanation: Space is so vast that even the fastest rocket would take thousands of years to reach the nearest star after the Sun.

q: What is the name of the nearest large galaxy to the Milky Way?
options: The Triangulum Galaxy
The Large Magellanic Cloud
The Andromeda Galaxy
The Whirlpool Galaxy
explanation: The nearest large galaxy to our own Milky Way is the Andromeda Galaxy.

q: Where was Philippine independence declared?
options: At Malacanang Palace in Manila
At Emilio Aguinaldo's house in Kawit, Cavite
At the Barasoain Church in Malolos, Bulacan
At Fort Santiago in Intramuros, Manila
explanation: Philippine independence was declared at Emilio Aguinaldo's house in Kawit, Cavite.

q: What happens to makahiya leaves after no one touches them for a few minutes?
options: They stay closed until the next morning
They slowly open up again and return to their normal shape
They fall off the branch and must regrow
They turn yellow before slowly unfolding
explanation: Makahiya leaves do not stay shut forever — after a few minutes without being disturbed, they slowly open back up to their normal shape.

q: What happens to a person who has their spleen removed?
options: They cannot survive for long because the spleen pumps blood
They can still live but may catch some infections more easily
They must receive a transplant or they will die quickly
They lose the ability to digest food properly
explanation: A person can live without a spleen, but they become more vulnerable to certain infections because the spleen helps fight them.

q: What is the Philippine flag mainly made of?
options: Woven and sewn fabric with blue, red, and white cloth joined together
Painted paper that is laminated to make it weatherproof
Dyed plastic sheets stitched along the edges
Pressed dried leaves coated with waterproof wax
explanation: The flag is made of fabric — pieces of blue, red, and white cloth are sewn together, and the sun and stars are added on the white triangle.

q: How do many birds attract a mate?
options: By building the largest nest they can find material for
By combining color, sound, and movement together to impress a mate
By offering food items as a gift and waiting quietly
By chasing rivals away and then singing a single call
explanation: Many birds use color, sound, and movement together as a combined display to win the attention of a mate.

q: What is special about the pod of the sigarilyas (winged bean)?
options: It glows in the dark to attract insects for pollination
It has four wing-like ridges along its sides
It produces a red liquid that is used as a natural dye
It is covered in tiny spines that protect it from being eaten
explanation: The sigarilyas pod has four wing-like ridges, which is how it gets its name, and as a legume it also enriches the soil.

q: In which country is the Nobel Peace Prize awarded?
options: Sweden
Denmark
Norway
Finland
explanation: The Nobel Peace Prize is awarded in Norway, while all the other Nobel Prizes are given out in Sweden.

q: Why does a small amount of water freeze faster than a large amount?
options: Small amounts of water have a lower melting point than large amounts
The smaller amount loses its heat more easily, so it cools and freezes faster
Small amounts of water contain fewer minerals, which helps them freeze
Cold air sinks to the bottom of small containers but rises in large ones
explanation: A smaller amount of water loses heat more easily than a large amount, which is why a thin ice candy hardens faster than a big container of water.

q: What problem does plastic waste flowing through rivers like the Pasig River cause in the Philippines?
options: It poisons the soil along riverbanks, stopping all plants from growing
It piles up and clogs canals, which can cause flooding during heavy rain
It releases gases that turn the river water salty
It blocks sunlight from reaching the river bottom, killing all fish
explanation: Plastic flowing into rivers like the Pasig River takes hundreds of years to break down, piles up, clogs canals, and causes floods during heavy rain.

q: How is the climbing perch different from the mudskipper, even though both can leave the water?
options: The climbing perch cannot breathe air at all, but the mudskipper can
The mudskipper lives in freshwater while the climbing perch lives on coastal mudflats
The climbing perch lives in freshwater and moves using its gill covers, while the mudskipper lives on coastal mudflats and uses its fins like arms
The climbing perch can only survive on land for a few seconds, but the mudskipper can stay for hours
explanation: Both fish can leave water and breathe air, but the mudskipper lives on coastal mudflats and uses its fins like little arms, while the climbing perch lives in freshwater and moves using its gill covers.

q: What was the Pasig River used for during the colonial period?
options: As a boundary line between Spanish and local territories
As one of the main trade routes, with boats traveling from Laguna de Bay into Manila
As a source of drinking water pumped directly to Manila's churches
As a defensive moat around Intramuros to stop invaders
explanation: During the colonial period, the Pasig River served as one of the main trade routes of the Philippines, with boats sailing from Laguna de Bay into Manila.

q: Where do we get the vitamins our body needs?
options: Our body makes all the vitamins it needs on its own
We breathe them in from the air around us
We get them from the plants and animals we eat, such as vegetables, fish, and eggs
Our skin absorbs them from sunlight and rainwater
explanation: We get vitamins from the plants and animals we eat, including foods like vegetables, fish, and eggs.

q: How fast does Earth spin at the equator?
options: About 500 kilometers per hour
About 1,670 kilometers per hour
About 3,000 kilometers per hour
About 300 kilometers per hour
explanation: At the equator, Earth spins at approximately 1,670 kilometers per hour.

q: How does a clownfish use a sea anemone?
options: It eats the anemone's tentacles as its main source of food
It uses the anemone as a home that hides it from enemies, safe from the anemone's sting
It carries the anemone on its back to move it to warmer water
It cleans the anemone's tentacles in exchange for being left alone
explanation: The clownfish lives safely among the sea anemone's stinging tentacles and uses it as a home that protects it from predators.

q: Why do farmers usually plant a nitrogen-hungry crop like corn after a legume in a crop rotation plan?
options: Corn needs the same pests as legumes, so they share natural pest control
The legume adds nitrogen to the soil, which the corn crop then uses
Corn grows faster when planted in soil that has been compacted by legume roots
Legumes remove salt from the soil, and corn requires low-salt conditions
explanation: Legumes add nitrogen to the soil, so planting a nitrogen-hungry crop like corn afterward takes advantage of that stored nutrient.

q: Where in the body are many lymph nodes located?
options: Mainly inside the lungs and along the spine
In the neck, armpits, and groin — which is why we feel swelling there when sick
Clustered only around the heart and major blood vessels
Spread evenly throughout the skin all over the body
explanation: Many lymph nodes are found in the neck, armpits, and groin, so those areas often swell when we are fighting an illness.

q: At what launch angle does a thrown object travel the farthest distance (assuming no air resistance and flat ground)?
options: 30 degrees
60 degrees
45 degrees
90 degrees
explanation: Without air resistance on level ground, a projectile reaches its greatest range when launched at 45 degrees.

q: How much do chameleons vary in size?
options: They are all roughly the same size — about as long as a ruler
Some are as small as a fingernail while others grow as long as a human arm
They range from mouse-sized to roughly cat-sized
They only vary slightly, staying between 10 and 20 centimeters
explanation: Chameleons vary greatly in size — some species are as tiny as a fingernail while others can be as long as a person's arm.

q: How do most tree squirrels survive the winter?
options: They hibernate deeply underground and do not wake until spring
They stay awake all winter and eat the food they stored in autumn
They migrate to warmer forests before the cold season begins
They slow their heart rate so much that they appear to be dead
explanation: Most tree squirrels stay awake through winter and rely on the food they cached (stored) during autumn to survive.

q: Why is kakawate commonly used as a living fence on farms?
options: Its wood is so hard that animals cannot bite through it
It grows easily from a cut branch, making it cheap and simple to plant
Its flowers release a smell that keeps away pests and insects
Its roots spread underground and anchor soil so fences do not lean
explanation: Kakawate is ideal for living fences because it grows easily from a cut branch, so farmers can plant pieces directly into the ground.

q: What kinds of plants are found in Philippine grasslands, and where do these grasslands mostly appear?
options: Tall hardwood trees, mainly on flat coastal plains near the sea
Cogon and talahib grass, especially on hills that used to be forest
Dense ferns and mosses, found deep inside old-growth forest areas
Low-growing shrubs and cacti, typical of dry mountain slopes
explanation: Philippine grasslands are filled with cogon and talahib grass and are found mainly on hills that were once forested, where they are hot and sunny.

q: What do you do before eating a rambutan?
options: You boil it until the skin turns soft
You peel it first to get to the soft flesh inside
You squeeze out the juice and drink it
You dry it in the sun for several days
explanation: A rambutan must be peeled first to reach the soft, sweet flesh inside.

q: What is the unit used to measure voltage?
options: Watt, with the symbol W
Ampere, with the symbol A
Ohm, with the symbol Ω
Volt, with the symbol V
explanation: Voltage is measured in volts, written with the symbol V.

q: Why is the carabao considered a national animal of the Philippines?
options: Because it is the fastest land animal found in the Philippines
Because of its great help to farmers in the fields
Because it appears on the Philippine coat of arms and the national flag
Because it is the rarest animal found only in the Philippine islands
explanation: The carabao is regarded as the national animal of the Philippines because of the great help it provides to Filipino farmers.

q: Why does a tightrope walker stretch out their arms while crossing a high wire?
options: To signal to the audience that they are safe and in control
To balance more easily by spreading their weight to the sides
To generate forward momentum so they do not stop moving
To keep their costume from flapping in the wind
explanation: Stretching arms out to the sides helps a tightrope walker balance, just as we instinctively spread our arms when we are about to fall.

q: What do bangus and tilapia need to stay healthy in a fishpond?
options: Warm, still water with plenty of algae covering the surface
Enough oxygen and clean water in the fishpond
Saltwater mixed with fresh water in equal amounts
A sandy bottom and low water temperature
explanation: Bangus and tilapia need enough oxygen and clean water in their fishpond to stay healthy.

q: When a catfish is on land, what must stay moist so it can breathe?
options: Its skin, which absorbs oxygen directly from the air
Its gills, which must stay moist to allow it to still breathe
Its fins, which release water vapor to cool the body
Its mouth, which catches small water droplets from the ground
explanation: A catfish on land must keep its gills moist; dry gills cannot extract oxygen, so the fish would suffocate.

q: Why does a scuba diver need a regulator attached to their air tank?
options: To heat the air so it does not feel cold in deep water
To reduce the very high pressure of the tank air to a comfortable breathing pressure
To add extra oxygen to the air before the diver breathes it
To measure exactly how many breaths the diver takes underwater
explanation: Scuba tanks store air at very high pressure (200–300 bar), and the regulator reduces that pressure so the diver can breathe comfortably.

q: How does a flower attract the right pollinator?
options: It produces a single very loud buzzing sound to call insects from far away
It uses color, scent, and shape together as signals to guide the right pollinator to it
It releases a sticky liquid on its petals that traps any insect that lands
It blooms only at night so that only certain animals can see it
explanation: A flower often combines color, scent, and shape as a set of signals working together so the correct pollinator can find it.

q: What are the tiny holes on the underside of a leaf called, and what passes through them?
options: Veins; water travels through them from the roots to the leaf tips
Stomata; carbon dioxide enters through them and oxygen exits
Chloroplasts; sunlight is captured through these openings
Pores; sugars produced by photosynthesis flow out through them
explanation: The tiny holes on the underside of a leaf are called stomata — carbon dioxide goes in through them for photosynthesis, and oxygen comes out the same way.

q: What is one important job of the liver?
options: To produce insulin that controls the amount of sugar in the blood
To filter the blood and remove poisonous substances to keep it clean
To pump oxygen-rich blood to every organ in the body
To store extra red blood cells until the body needs them
explanation: The liver filters the blood and removes harmful substances, keeping the blood clean.

q: What was the first animal to orbit the Earth, and what was its name?
options: A chimpanzee named Ham, sent up by the United States
A dog named Laika, aboard the spacecraft Sputnik 2
A cat named Félicette, aboard a French rocket
A monkey named Albert, sent up by NASA
explanation: The first animal to orbit Earth was a dog named Laika, who traveled aboard Sputnik 2.

q: Where is the gallbladder located in the body?
options: Behind the stomach, on the left side of the belly
Just under the liver, on the right side of the belly
Below the kidneys, near the lower back
Inside the liver, surrounded by liver tissue
explanation: The gallbladder sits just under the liver on the right side of the belly.

q: Why do many animals migrate — travel long distances with the seasons?
options: To escape predators that only live in one region all year round
To find food, warmth, or good places to raise their young
To follow the magnetic poles as they slowly shift over time
To mark new territory and claim it for their group
explanation: Animals migrate to find food, warmth, or suitable places to raise their young, such as birds flying to warmer regions when the cold arrives.

q: Who proved that white light is actually made up of different colors?
options: Galileo Galilei, using a telescope to study sunlight
Albert Einstein, using a glass plate experiment
Isaac Newton, using a prism
Marie Curie, using radioactive materials
explanation: Isaac Newton demonstrated that white light is made of many colors by passing it through a prism.

q: Why can you hold a solid in your hand but not a liquid or a gas?
options: Solids are always heavier, so they stay in your hand while liquids and gases float away
A liquid drips away and a gas spreads out, so you need a container to hold them
Solids are always cold, which makes them easy to grip, while liquids and gases are warm
A liquid is too slippery and a gas is too hot to hold safely
explanation: A solid keeps its shape so you can hold it, but a liquid drips away and a gas spreads out in all directions, so both need a container.

q: Why is the tarictic hornbill endangered?
options: It has been over-hunted for its colorful feathers used in traditional ceremonies
Widespread forest loss in the Visayas and capture for the pet trade have greatly reduced its numbers
Rising sea levels have flooded most of its nesting areas on low-lying islands
It cannot survive the warmer temperatures caused by recent climate changes
explanation: The tarictic hornbill is endangered because large areas of forest in the Visayas have been destroyed and birds are also captured for the pet trade.

q: What is the heaviest naturally occurring element on Earth?
options: Lead, with atomic number 82
Gold, with atomic number 79
Plutonium, with atomic number 94
Uranium, with atomic number 92
explanation: Uranium, with atomic number 92, is the heaviest element that occurs naturally on Earth.

q: Why did many people think Mount Pinatubo was no longer an active volcano before 1991?
options: Scientists had officially reclassified it as an extinct volcano in the 1980s
It had been quiet for over 500 years before its 1991 eruption
Its crater had completely filled with soil and trees, hiding any sign of activity
Nearby earthquakes had sealed the volcanic vents permanently
explanation: Pinatubo had been quiet for more than 500 years before its 1991 eruption, so many people believed it was no longer active.

q: Who was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize, and in which field?
options: Rosalind Franklin, in Chemistry in 1952
Ada Lovelace, in Physics in 1895
Marie Curie, in Physics in 1903
Lise Meitner, in Chemistry in 1944
explanation: Marie Curie became the first woman to win a Nobel Prize when she received the Physics prize in 1903.

q: What is the trade-off when you use a lever to lift something heavy with less force?
options: You save time because the lever moves faster than your hand would
You must move the effort end through a longer distance
The lever wears out quickly and must be replaced after heavy use
You lose control of the direction the heavy object moves
explanation: A lever lets you use less force, but in return you must push or pull the effort end over a greater distance — there is no free gain in strength.

q: What does a pelican do with its pouch before swallowing the fish it caught?
options: It drains the water out of its pouch first
It swallows the fish and water together
It tosses the fish into the air and catches it
It squeezes the pouch to crush the fish
explanation: After scooping, a pelican drains the water out of its pouch before swallowing the trapped fish.

q: Why does a quartz watch keep such accurate time?
options: Its gears are made of very hard metal
A quartz crystal vibrates very fast when electricity passes through it
A tiny battery heats the quartz crystal to make it expand
Its hands are driven by a spinning magnet
explanation: A quartz watch keeps time because a quartz crystal vibrates very fast when electricity passes through it, giving a very steady rhythm.

q: Which part of a simple sand-and-charcoal water filter must be replaced over time, and cannot just be rinsed clean?
options: The gravel layer
The sand layer
The charcoal layer
The stone layer
