explanation: The Ring of Fire is the big system around the whole Pacific, while the Philippine Fault is just one part of it — a crack that runs through the Philippines.

q: What role do helpful bacteria in our gut play?
options: They help us digest food
They produce red blood cells to carry oxygen
They destroy all viruses that enter the stomach
They absorb water through the gut wall
explanation: Helpful bacteria live in our gut and help us digest food.

q: During the June solstice, the Sun is directly overhead at which special latitude line?
options: The Tropic of Cancer
The Tropic of Capricorn
The Equator
The Arctic Circle
explanation: On the June solstice, the Sun is directly overhead at the Tropic of Cancer, about 23.5 degrees north of the Equator.

q: Why is every organism in an ecosystem important, even a very tiny one?
options: Because every organism has a role to play, and losing even one can upset the balance
Because tiny organisms are always at the bottom of the food chain where they do the most work
Because larger animals cannot survive without eating tiny ones every single day
Because tiny organisms produce all the oxygen that larger animals breathe
explanation: In an ecosystem every organism, even a tiny one, has a role to play, so losing even one can upset the balance.

q: What makes the sperm whale the record-holder among diving mammals?
options: It can dive over 3,000 meters deep and stay under for more than 90 minutes in a single dive
It can hold its breath for over 24 hours by slowing its heart to one beat per minute
It dives deeper than any other animal on Earth, including deep-sea fish
It can dive 1,000 meters in under a minute because of its streamlined torpedo shape
explanation: The sperm whale is the deepest-diving mammal, recorded diving over 3,000 meters for more than 90 minutes in a single dive.

q: You rub a plastic comb on your hair and hold it near a thin stream of water from a faucet. What happens?
options: The water stream bends toward the comb because the static charge pulls on it
The water stream speeds up because the comb pushes air toward it
The water stream breaks into droplets and falls straight down
Nothing happens because static electricity only affects metal objects
explanation: The static charge on the comb pulls on the water even without touching it, causing the stream to bend toward the comb.

q: An earthquake measures 6 on the Richter scale. How much larger is the shaking amplitude compared to a magnitude 5 earthquake?
options: 10 times larger
2 times larger
100 times larger
5 times larger
explanation: On the Richter scale, each whole-number step up means 10 times larger shaking amplitude.

q: Why are there always far fewer lions than zebras in an ecosystem, even if lions are not hunted?
options: Because energy is lost at each level of the food chain, so there is less energy available for predators
Because lions choose to stay in small groups so they can hunt more effectively
Because zebras reproduce much faster and always outnumber predators by chance
Because predators must rest more and so they need less food than plant-eaters
explanation: The reason predators are few and plants are many is the loss of energy at each level, not just chance.

q: In what year did Lord Kelvin propose the Kelvin temperature scale?
explanation: Lord Kelvin (William Thomson) proposed the Kelvin scale in the year 1848.

q: An amoeba is made of just one cell. How does it carry out all the activities of life?
options: That single cell does everything including eating, moving, and reproducing
It shares tasks with nearby cells in the water that help it survive
It takes turns doing each activity, resting in between to save energy
It absorbs energy from sunlight the same way plants do with chlorophyll
explanation: Some organisms like the amoeba are made of just one cell, and that single cell does everything including eating, moving, and reproducing.

q: How often does Halley's Comet return close enough to be seen from Earth?
options: About every 76 years
About every 10 years
About every 365 years
About every 26 years
explanation: Halley's Comet returns to be seen from Earth about every 76 years.

q: How do bananas grow on a banana plant?
options: In a large bunch made of groups shaped like hands with many fingers
In single rows hanging straight down from one long stalk
In round clusters like grapes, each attached to a separate thin stem
In pairs attached side by side to a single thick branch
explanation: Bananas grow in a large bunch made of groups shaped like hands with many fingers.

q: A 5 GHz WiFi connection is faster than a 2.4 GHz connection but has one main drawback. What is it?
options: 5 GHz has a shorter range, so it does not reach as far
5 GHz uses more power and drains device batteries much faster
5 GHz only works indoors and is blocked completely by windows
5 GHz cannot connect to older devices because it uses a different plug
explanation: WiFi uses radio waves: 5 GHz is faster but has shorter range, while 2.4 GHz is slower but reaches farther.

q: How does dirty water cause malnutrition in children, even if they eat enough food?
options: Dirty water causes diarrhea, which drains nutrients from the child's body
Dirty water blocks the stomach so food cannot be properly swallowed
Dirty water makes food taste bad so children refuse to eat their meals
Dirty water coats the intestines with mud that stops all nutrient absorption
explanation: Dirty water causes diarrhea that drains nutrients from a child's body, making clean water and good hygiene essential for fighting malnutrition.

q: How does a calamansi compare to a dalandan in size and taste?
options: Calamansi is small and sour, while dalandan is larger and sweeter
Calamansi is large and sweet, while dalandan is small and sour
Calamansi and dalandan are the same size but dalandan is more bitter
Calamansi is medium-sized and mild, while dalandan is smaller and very spicy
explanation: Calamansi is small and sour, while dalandan is larger and sweeter than calamansi.

q: What is the source of energy used to generate hydroelectric power?
options: The force of flowing water, usually at dams
The heat from steam released by underground volcanic activity
The push of ocean tides moving in and out of bays
The weight of rainwater collected in large rooftop tanks
explanation: Hydroelectric power is electricity made from the force of flowing water, usually at dams.

q: What are the four stages of a butterfly's life cycle in the correct order?
options: Egg, caterpillar, pupa, adult butterfly
Egg, adult butterfly, pupa, caterpillar
Caterpillar, egg, adult butterfly, pupa
Pupa, egg, caterpillar, adult butterfly
explanation: A butterfly goes through complete metamorphosis in four stages: egg, caterpillar (larva), pupa (chrysalis), and finally the adult butterfly.

q: What is the difference between weather and climate?
options: Weather describes the atmosphere over a short time like one day, while climate is the average pattern over many years
Weather describes long-term patterns over decades, while climate describes today's conditions
Weather and climate both describe the same thing but are used for different countries
Weather only applies to storms and rain, while climate only applies to temperature
explanation: Weather is the state of the atmosphere over a short time such as a single day, while climate is the average pattern of weather in a place over many years or decades.

q: How many pairs of legs does a horseshoe crab have for walking on the seafloor?
options: Five pairs
Three pairs
Four pairs
Six pairs
explanation: A horseshoe crab has five pairs of legs for walking on the seafloor, with the last pair acting like a pusher to shove it forward through mud.

q: When a lymph node in your neck swells during an illness, what does the swelling actually mean?
options: The node is working hard by gathering many defense cells to fight infection
The node itself is infected and needs to be removed by a doctor
The node has grown too large and is blocking blood flow to your head
The node is filling with fluid because your kidneys are not filtering well
explanation: When a lymph node swells, usually the node itself is not the sick part — it is gathering many defense cells, so the swelling is a sign it is working hard.

q: What substance in red blood cells gives blood its red color and carries oxygen?
options: Hemoglobin, an iron-rich protein
Platelets, which stick together when you are cut
Plasma, the liquid part of the blood
White blood cells that absorb oxygen from the lungs
explanation: Red cells contain hemoglobin, an iron-rich protein that binds oxygen and gives blood its red color.

q: At about what age does a baby's first tooth usually appear?
options: About six months
About two years
About three months
About one year
explanation: A baby's first tooth usually appears at about six months of age.

q: Why is a coral reef important to many fish and sea animals?
options: It provides a home and shelter for many fish and other sea animals
It produces the oxygen that all sea creatures breathe underwater
It warms the surrounding water to the temperature sea animals need
It filters salt out of the water so fish can drink it
explanation: A coral reef is a home and shelter for many fish and other sea animals.

q: How do trees planted in reforestation help the area around them?
options: They give shade and make the surroundings cooler
They produce electricity by harnessing wind through their branches
They release chemicals that repel insects from nearby crops
They pump extra groundwater to the surface for farming
explanation: Trees planted in reforestation give shade and make the surroundings cooler.

q: How do octopuses and squid breathe underwater?
options: With gills that take oxygen from the water
With lungs that let them hold large amounts of air
Through their skin, which absorbs oxygen directly from the water
Through a blowhole on top of their head
explanation: The octopus and squid breathe with gills that take oxygen from the water.

q: Which group of things are all examples of materials that melt when they get hot?
options: Ice cream, chocolate, and candle wax
Wood, stone, and plastic bottles
Glass jars, metal spoons, and paper bags
Sand, soil, and gravel
explanation: Many things melt when it is hot, such as ice cream, chocolate, and candle wax.

q: A mudskipper and a frog both have eyes on top of their heads. How does this help them?
options: They can hide their body in water or mud while only their eyes poke out to watch for enemies
They can see in two directions at once because one eye faces forward and one faces backward
Eyes on top allow them to see better in the dark when hunting at night
It keeps their eyes dry even when they swim rapidly through fast-moving water
explanation: Like a frog, a mudskipper has eyes on top of its head, so both can hide their body in the water or mud while only their eyes poke out to watch for enemies.

q: How does the atmospheric pressure on Venus's surface compare to Earth's?
options: It is 90 times greater than at Earth's sea level
It is about the same as on Earth because both planets are similar in size
It is 10 times lower because Venus has almost no atmosphere
It is 2 times greater, just enough to make breathing difficult
explanation: The atmospheric pressure at Venus's surface is 90 times greater than at Earth's sea level — so extreme that Soviet spacecraft that landed there survived only a few hours before being crushed.

q: How many bones are found in one human hand?
explanation: There are 27 bones in one human hand.

q: Why is the tarsier threatened with losing its habitat?
options: Because the forests it lives in slowly disappear when trees are cut down
Because other larger animals hunt tarsiers and drive them away from their territory
Because tarsiers only live on one small island and cannot migrate elsewhere
Because climate change makes Philippine forests too warm for tarsiers to survive
explanation: The tarsier is threatened because the forests it lives in slowly disappear when trees are cut down.

q: How long ago did the Mesozoic era begin and end?
options: From 252 million to 66 million years ago
From 541 million to 252 million years ago
From 66 million to 2.6 million years ago
From 4,500 million to 541 million years ago
explanation: The Mesozoic era lasted from 252 million to 66 million years ago.

q: What makes Candida yeast harmful to a person, even though it normally lives in the body without causing problems?
options: It can cause infections when the immune system is weakened or the balance of microbes is disrupted
It multiplies rapidly whenever a person eats too much sugar and attacks the stomach lining
It produces a toxin that destroys red blood cells only when the body temperature rises
It becomes dangerous only when it escapes the gut and enters the lungs during a cold
explanation: Candida is a yeast that normally lives harmlessly in the body but can cause infections when the immune system is weakened or the balance of microbes is disrupted.

q: How do true sea snakes reproduce differently from most other snakes?
options: They give birth to live young right in the water and never come onto land
They lay eggs in nests built on the seafloor out of sand and shells
They lay eggs on beaches at night and then return to the water immediately
They carry their eggs in a special pouch on their belly until the eggs hatch
explanation: True sea snakes give birth to live young right in the water and do not come onto land at all.

q: How does the tuna's special circulatory system help it hunt even in cold ocean water?
options: It warms the tuna's muscles and brain slightly above the surrounding water temperature, keeping the tuna fast
It pumps extra blood to the gills so the tuna can extract more oxygen in cold water
It stores warm blood in a special organ that the tuna releases to heat the water around it
It slows blood flow to the tail so more energy stays in the fins for quick bursts of speed
explanation: Unlike most fish, tuna can warm their muscles and brain slightly above surrounding water temperature using a special circulatory system, letting them stay fast even in cold water.

q: How do land snails breathe?
options: With a simple lung that takes in air
With gills that absorb oxygen from moisture in the soil
Through their skin, which pulls oxygen from the surrounding air
Through a tiny tube under their shell that pumps air in and out
explanation: Land snails breathe air using a simple lung, not gills.

q: How do the fruit dove's green feathers help it survive?
options: They help it hide among the leaves of trees
They attract mates during the breeding season by reflecting sunlight
They absorb heat from the sun to keep the bird warm at night
They startle predators because the bright color looks like a poisonous frog
explanation: The fruit dove's green feathers help it hide among the leaves of trees, serving as camouflage.

q: Why are hydrogen fuel cells considered a clean energy technology?
options: They produce only water as a byproduct and emit no carbon dioxide
They reuse the same hydrogen over and over so no fuel is ever used up
They collect energy from sunlight to split water into hydrogen and oxygen
They store electricity in the hydrogen gas so no chemical reaction occurs
explanation: Hydrogen fuel cells convert the chemical energy of hydrogen and oxygen into electricity with water as the only byproduct, emitting no carbon dioxide.

q: According to PHIVOLCS, how many active volcanoes does the Philippines have?
explanation: According to PHIVOLCS, the Philippines has 24 active volcanoes, the most well-known being Mayon, Taal, and Kanlaon.

q: What is one important role of the spleen in fighting disease?
options: It holds many white blood cells that help fight germs that get into the blood
It produces the red blood cells that carry oxygen to all parts of the body
It filters urine and removes harmful chemicals before they reach the kidneys
It stores extra platelets that are released to seal wounds when you are injured
explanation: The spleen holds many white blood cells that help fight germs that get into the blood.

q: What does the tinikling dance show a bird doing in the rice fields?
options: Dodging the traps and sticks that farmers set
Building a nest between the bamboo poles
Searching for insects along the rice stalks
Flying away from a swooping eagle
explanation: The tinikling dance shows how the tikling bird dodges the traps and sticks that farmers set in rice fields.

q: Which scientist has the unit of pressure named after him?
options: Blaise Pascal
Isaac Newton
Robert Boyle
Evangelista Torricelli
explanation: The unit of pressure called the pascal (Pa) is named after the scientist Blaise Pascal.

q: Why is the carabao mango named after the carabao?
options: Its long, slightly curved shape resembles the horn of the carabao
Its yellow color matches the carabao's hide in the dry season
It was first grown on farms that also raised carabaos
Carabaos were known to eat this mango more than other animals
explanation: The carabao mango is named after the carabao because its long, slightly curved shape is said to resemble the horn of the carabao, our national animal.

q: Why are seagrass meadows considered one of the richest habitats in the sea?
options: They are home to a great variety of fish and animals
They produce more oxygen than coral reefs
They trap sediment and build new islands over time
They are the only place where sea turtles can lay eggs
explanation: Seagrass meadows are home to a great variety of fish and animals, making them one of the richest living habitats in the sea.

q: How are Rafflesia seeds spread from one place to another?
options: Small animals eat its fruit and carry the seeds
The wind blows the seeds to new locations
The seeds float on rivers to reach new hosts
Insects carry pollen that turns into seeds
explanation: Rafflesia seeds are spread when small animals eat its fruit, carrying the seeds to new locations.

q: Why can a person drool while sleeping?
options: The mouth keeps making saliva even during sleep, which drips out when the mouth is open
The body produces extra water at night to keep the throat from drying out
Sleeping on your side causes water from the stomach to leak into the mouth
The tongue relaxes and pushes saliva out between the lips
explanation: The mouth keeps making saliva even while you sleep, so it can drool out when your mouth is open.

q: What type of rock mostly makes up the Moon's highlands, and roughly how old is it?
options: Anorthosite, about 4.4 billion years old
Basalt, about 3.5 billion years old
Granite, about 2 billion years old
Obsidian, about 1 billion years old
explanation: The Moon's highlands are mainly anorthosite — the Moon's oldest crust, formed about 4.4 billion years ago as its magma ocean cooled.

q: A thermometer reads 27°C. What is this temperature in Kelvin?
explanation: To convert Celsius to Kelvin, you add 273, so 27°C equals 300 K.

q: Why is the sense of smell so closely tied to memory and emotion?
options: The olfactory nerve connects directly to brain regions that control feelings and memory
Smell signals pass through the spinal cord before reaching the brain
The nose sends chemicals directly into the bloodstream to trigger emotions
Smell and sight share the same nerve pathway to the brain
explanation: Smell is strongly linked to memory and emotion because the olfactory nerve directly connects to brain regions that control feelings and memory.

q: What happens when an acid touches chalk or marble?
options: It bubbles and slowly dissolves the material
It hardens the surface and makes it shine
It turns the material a bright red color
It makes the material absorb water faster
explanation: Acids react with calcium carbonate materials like chalk and marble, causing them to bubble and slowly dissolve.

q: What makes active transport different from simple diffusion in cells?
options: Active transport uses energy from ATP to move molecules against the concentration gradient
Active transport only works with water molecules through the cell membrane
Active transport moves molecules from low to high concentration without any energy
Active transport happens only in plant cells, not animal cells
explanation: Active transport uses energy from ATP to move molecules against their concentration gradient, as seen in the sodium-potassium pump in nerve cells.

q: What is the eyewall of a typhoon actually made of?
options: A thick ring of swirling clouds, rain, and wind
Solid sheets of ice formed at very high altitude
A layer of still, warm air surrounding the eye
Dense sea foam pushed upward by the spinning storm
explanation: Despite its name, the eyewall is not a solid wall — it is a thick ring of swirling clouds, rain, and wind that looks like a wall from inside the eye.

q: Why are railroad tracks for trains like the LRT and MRT made of steel?
options: Steel is strong and tough enough to handle the huge weight of full trains without bending or breaking
Steel is the cheapest material available in large enough quantities for long track lines
Steel expands less than other metals in hot weather, keeping the tracks perfectly straight
Steel is magnetic, which helps the train's motor grip the track safely
explanation: Railroad tracks must handle the huge weight of full trains daily, and no other ordinary material is strong and tough enough for this except steel.

q: What is the chemical symbol for the metal copper?
options: Cu
Co
Cp
Cr
explanation: The chemical symbol for copper is Cu, taken from the Latin word 'cuprum'.

q: What covers the feet of cattle to protect them as they walk?
options: Hard hooves
Soft paw pads
Thick scales
Claws
explanation: Cattle walk on four legs that have hard hooves, which protect their feet.

q: What is the main job of the larva stage, like a caterpillar, in an insect's life cycle?
options: Eating and growing to store energy for the pupa stage
Finding a mate and laying eggs for the next generation
Spinning silk to build a protective cocoon immediately
Flying to new plants and spreading pollen
explanation: The larva focuses on eating and growing, storing the energy it will need for transformation in the pupa stage.

q: Why do river stones become smooth and rounded over time?
options: Constant abrasion as they are carried by the current scratches and wears down their rough edges
The river water slowly dissolves the outer layer of the rocks, making them round
Pressure from the weight of water above flattens the stones into smooth shapes
Minerals inside the rocks react with water and fill in the rough spots
explanation: River stones become smooth and rounded because of constant abrasion — they are scratched and worn down as they are carried along by the river current.

q: Where is the cuttlebone located inside a cuttlefish's body?
options: Inside the back, just under the skin along the top of its body
In the centre of the body near its stomach
At the front, behind the head just above the eyes
Along the bottom of the body underneath the fins
explanation: The cuttlebone sits inside the back of the cuttlefish, just under the skin along the top of its body, hidden by soft flesh.

q: What kind of sound does a maya bird usually make?
options: Short, repeated chirping sounds
Long, melodious whistling songs
Deep hooting calls repeated slowly
Loud screeching cries to warn others
explanation: The maya makes short, repeated chirping sounds that we often hear in the morning.

q: What main ingredient is used to make nilupak, and what nutrient does it give the body?
options: Pounded cassava, which stores starch and gives the body energy
Pounded sweet potato, which is rich in vitamin A for good eyesight
Mashed banana, which provides potassium and prevents muscle cramps
Ground rice, which contains protein needed for muscle growth
explanation: Nilupak is made from pounded cassava, a root crop that stores starch, giving the body energy.

q: Which material is known as one of the lightest solids because it is made up mostly of air?
options: Aerogel
Styrofoam
Pumice
Balsa wood
explanation: Aerogel is one of the lightest solid materials because it is made up mostly of air.

q: What happens during nuclear fission?
options: A heavy atomic nucleus splits into lighter pieces, releasing energy
Two light atomic nuclei combine to form a heavier nucleus
An atom loses electrons and becomes a positively charged ion
A radioactive atom gives off a particle and turns into a different element
explanation: Nuclear fission is the splitting of a heavy atomic nucleus into lighter pieces, which releases energy.

q: In what year was the first quartz wristwatch, the Seiko Astron, released?
explanation: The Seiko Astron, the first quartz wristwatch, was released in the year 1969.

q: Which body of water lies to the WEST of the Philippines?
options: South China Sea
Philippine Sea
Sulu Sea
Celebes Sea
explanation: The Philippines is surrounded by three major bodies of water: the Philippine Sea to the east, the South China Sea to the west, and the Sulu Sea to the southwest.

q: Why is the animal called balintong given that name?
options: It rolls over or tumbles when it is scared
It balances on its tail when resting on tree branches
It spins in circles to confuse predators before running
It leaps and flips in the air when chasing prey
explanation: The name balintong means one who rolls over or tumbles, because that is what the animal does when it is scared.

q: What makes the water hyacinth a problem in lakes and rivers?
options: It can double its numbers in just a few days and quickly cover the whole water surface
It produces a toxin that poisons fish and drives them away from the area
Its roots grow so deep that they block water from flowing through riverbeds
It uses up all the nutrients in the soil along riverbanks, killing other plants
explanation: The water hyacinth is one of the fastest-growing water plants and can double its numbers in just a few days, quickly covering the whole surface of a lake or river.

q: At what temperature in Celsius does water freeze and ice melt?
options: 0 degrees Celsius
4 degrees Celsius
10 degrees Celsius
-10 degrees Celsius
explanation: Water freezes, and ice melts, at 0 degrees Celsius.

q: What gives eggplant skin its purple color?
options: A natural pigment inside it
A special mineral absorbed from the soil
Sunlight reacting with the outer layer of the skin
The same substance that makes leaves green
explanation: Eggplant skin is purple because of a natural pigment inside it, the same kind of coloring that makes ube and other purple fruits their color.

q: Why can't a garbage patch in the ocean be seen from a satellite in space?
options: The plastics are too small and spread out to show up on satellites
The ocean's blue color covers the plastic and makes it invisible from above
Garbage sinks below the surface before it drifts far enough to form a patch
The patches are only found in very deep water where satellites cannot detect them
explanation: The plastics in a garbage patch are too small and spread out, so they do not show up even on satellites — you have to get close by boat to see them.

q: Besides restoring forests, why do some reforestation programs also plant mango trees?
options: So that people have food from the fruit-bearing trees
So that the trees grow faster because mango roots fix nitrogen
So that the shade keeps smaller seedlings from drying out
So that the sweet smell of the flowers attracts birds to spread seeds
explanation: Some reforestation programs plant fruit-bearing trees like mango so that people also have a source of food.

q: How does citizen science help scientists monitor wildlife?
options: Ordinary people including students record animals they see and report the data to scientists
Scientists send untrained volunteers to set camera traps in the forest
Students analyze lab samples collected by professional researchers
Citizens donate money to fund wildlife tracking devices
explanation: Citizen science allows ordinary people, including students, to help monitor biodiversity by recording animals they see and reporting to scientists.

q: Why do people who exercise often usually have a slower resting heartbeat?
options: Regular exercise makes the heart stronger, so it needs fewer beats to pump blood
Fit people have thicker blood that flows more slowly through the body
Exercise shrinks the blood vessels, so the heart does not need to pump as hard
Regular exercise lowers body temperature, which slows the heart down
explanation: People who exercise often usually have a slower resting heartbeat because their heart becomes stronger and more efficient.

q: How many moons does the planet Mercury have?
options: Zero
One
Two
Three
explanation: Mercury has no moons at all; it has zero.

q: How do scientists show the direction that light travels when using the ray model?
options: By drawing straight arrows pointing in the direction light travels
By drawing wavy lines to show the up-and-down movement of light
By drawing circles spreading outward from the light source
By shading the area that light illuminates with a bright color
explanation: Scientists use the ray model of light, drawing straight arrows to show the direction light travels.

q: How many wings do insects like butterflies and bees typically have?
options: Four wings
Two wings
Six wings
Eight wings
explanation: Many insects, like butterflies and bees, have four wings.

q: What does the electromagnet do inside a doorbell to produce a sound?
options: It pulls a small hammer to strike a bell
It vibrates a metal plate that hums loudly
It spins a motor that moves an air horn
It heats a coil that causes a buzzer to ring
explanation: In a doorbell, an electromagnet pulls a small hammer to strike a bell and make a sound.

q: Where inside a sugarcane plant is the sweet juice stored?
options: Inside the stalk
Inside the roots
Inside the leaves
Inside the seeds
explanation: Sugarcane leaves make food from sunlight, and the sweet juice is stored inside the stalk; when the stalk is pressed, the sweet liquid used to make sugar comes out.

q: Where can the tabon scrubfowl be found besides the Philippines?
options: On other islands of Southeast Asia
Only on the island of Palawan
In the forests of Australia and New Zealand
On small coral atolls in the Pacific Ocean
explanation: The tabon scrubfowl is found not only in the Philippines but also on other islands of Southeast Asia.

q: What purpose does the sampaguita flower's strong night scent serve?
options: It attracts insects that help the plant reproduce
It keeps away animals that might eat its petals
It signals to other sampaguita plants that night has fallen
It traps insects inside the flower to absorb nutrients
explanation: The sampaguita's strong night scent attracts insects that help it reproduce through pollination.

q: Why is a spider NOT classified as an insect?
options: A spider has eight legs and only two body parts, while an insect has six legs and three body parts
A spider has wings at some stage of its life, but insects never develop wings
A spider is too big to be an insect, which must be smaller than a fingernail
A spider lives on land, while true insects must spend part of their life in water
explanation: A spider is not an insect because it has eight legs and only two body parts, whereas an insect has six legs and three body parts: head, thorax, and abdomen.

q: Why do mangroves grow best where a river meets the sea?
options: The tide mixes fresh water from the river with salty sea water, creating the brackish water mangroves prefer
The deep mud at river mouths contains nutrients that only mangroves can absorb
River mouths get more sunlight than inland areas because the canopy is cleared by flooding
The current at river mouths carries seeds faster, helping mangroves spread quickly
explanation: Mangroves thrive where a river meets the sea because the tide mixes fresh water with salty sea water, creating the brackish conditions they prefer.

q: Which of the following is listed as a cheap, nutritious local food good for nourishing a baby in the first 1,000 days?
options: Malunggay
White rice alone
Instant noodles
Soft drinks with sugar
explanation: Cheap local foods like malunggay, mung beans, eggs, galunggong, and sweet potato are full of the nutrients a baby needs during the first 1,000 days.

q: What type of glass is used to make most everyday drinking glasses, bottles, and house windows?
options: Soda-lime glass
Borosilicate glass
Lead crystal glass
Tempered glass
explanation: Most glass we see every day — drinking glasses, soda bottles, jars, and house windows — is soda-lime glass, the most common type because it is cheap and easy to make.

q: Where does a dragonfly lay its eggs?
options: In water such as a pond, stream, or rice field
On the underside of dry leaves on the forest floor
Inside cracks in tree bark away from sunlight
In soft soil near the roots of tall grasses
explanation: A dragonfly lays its eggs in water such as a pond, stream, or rice field.

q: How do hollow bones help birds fly?
options: They make birds lighter, so their wings need less force to lift them into the air
They act as air tanks that store oxygen for long flights over the ocean
They bend slightly under the wing to increase the surface area during flapping
They reduce the bird's body temperature, which makes muscles work more efficiently
explanation: Birds have hollow bones full of air spaces, making their bodies light so their wings need less force to lift them into the air.

q: How does secondhand smoke affect a person who does not smoke?
options: Breathing in another person's smoke also harms their heart
It only affects the lungs, leaving the heart completely safe
The harmful chemicals are diluted enough in open air to cause no damage
It raises blood pressure briefly but causes no lasting harm
explanation: Even if you do not smoke, breathing in another person's smoke (secondhand smoke or passive smoking) also harms your heart.

q: Why are many mountains in the Philippines actually volcanoes?
options: The country lies along the Pacific Ring of Fire
The islands were formed by ancient meteor impacts that left volcanic craters
Heavy rainfall erodes the land and forces magma to the surface
The Philippine plate has no subduction zones, so magma builds up under mountains
explanation: Many mountains in the Philippines are volcanoes because the country lies along the Pacific Ring of Fire, a zone of intense volcanic and earthquake activity.

q: How long can the katala (Philippine cockatoo) survive in the wild if not threatened?
options: Thirty years or more
About five years
Around ten to fifteen years
Up to twenty years at most
explanation: The katala is long-lived, capable of surviving thirty years or more in the wild if not threatened.

q: What is the difference between narrow-spectrum and broad-spectrum antibiotics?
options: Narrow-spectrum antibiotics work against only one type of bacteria, while broad-spectrum ones fight many types at once
Narrow-spectrum antibiotics are stronger and used only in hospitals, while broad-spectrum ones are milder
Narrow-spectrum antibiotics kill bacteria by breaking cell walls, while broad-spectrum ones stop bacteria from reproducing
Narrow-spectrum antibiotics are given by injection, while broad-spectrum ones are taken as pills
explanation: Some antibiotics work against only one type of bacteria (narrow-spectrum), while others fight many types at once (broad-spectrum).

q: Why does stainless steel not rust even in a humid, often-wet kitchen?
options: It has a special metal mixed in that forms a protective shield against air and water
It is coated with a thin layer of oil during manufacturing that seals out moisture
Its smooth surface prevents water droplets from sticking long enough to cause rust
It contains carbon that reacts with oxygen before the iron underneath can rust
explanation: Stainless steel has a special metal mixed in that forms a shield against air and water, preventing rust even in humid conditions.

q: Why is Gregor Mendel called the 'father of genetics'?
options: He discovered how traits are passed from parents to offspring by studying pea plants.
He invented the microscope that scientists use to study cells.
He was the first person to grow pea plants in a laboratory greenhouse.
He discovered that all plants reproduce by making seeds.
explanation: Mendel earned the title by studying pea plants and figuring out the rules by which traits are inherited.

q: What did Pacific Island navigators use the Southern Cross (Crux) constellation for?
options: To find which direction is south.
To predict when a storm was coming.
To count how many days were left in the year.
To tell what time of day it was.
explanation: Pacific Island navigators used the Southern Cross to find south, just as sailors in the north use the North Star.

q: What causes sunburn that makes skin red and sore?
options: Ultraviolet (UV) rays from the sun damage the skin.
Heat from the sun dries out the surface of the skin.
Visible light from the sun bleaches the top layer of skin.
Infrared rays from the sun burn the skin like a hot object.
explanation: Sunburn is caused by UV rays, which are invisible and damage skin cells even on a cloudy day.

q: When you use a block-and-tackle system of many pulleys, what trade-off do you have to accept?
options: You must pull a much longer length of rope to lift the load.
The load rises much faster than when using a single pulley.
The direction you pull stays the same as with a single pulley.
The weight limit is lower than when using a single pulley.
explanation: A block and tackle reduces the force needed but requires pulling a longer rope — a classic machine trade-off.

q: What happens inside a rechargeable phone battery when you plug it in to recharge?
options: Charged particles (ions) move back to their original side.
New chemicals are added to replace ones that were used up.
The battery heats up and creates fresh electrical energy.
Electricity from the charger fills up empty spaces in the battery.
explanation: During recharging, ions move back to their starting side, restoring the battery so it can be used again.

q: How does sweating help cool your body down?
options: When sweat evaporates from your skin, it absorbs heat and carries it away.
Sweat forms a cold layer of water that blocks heat from entering your skin.
Sweating uses up extra energy, which lowers your body temperature.
Sweat reflects sunlight away from your skin, so you absorb less heat.
explanation: Evaporation of sweat absorbs heat from the skin, which is why you feel cooler after sweating.

q: Why is Puerto Galera in Oriental Mindoro considered a UNESCO Man and Biosphere Reserve?
options: It has rich marine biodiversity with beautiful coral reefs and popular diving spots.
It is home to the Philippines' largest national forest park open to the public.
It is a protected site because of its ancient pre-colonial temple ruins.
It contains one of the deepest marine trenches found in Philippine waters.
explanation: Puerto Galera was designated a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve because of its exceptional marine biodiversity and coral reefs.

q: How does a kite (bati) manage to stay up in the air?
options: Wind pushes up on its tilted face while the string holds it back so air can lift it.
The kite is lighter than air, so it naturally floats upward when released.
The string pulls the kite upward by creating tension against gravity.
Heat from the sun warms the kite and makes the air around it rise.
explanation: Wind striking the kite's tilted surface creates an upward push, and the string keeps it angled so the air continues to lift it.

q: What gave engineers the idea for the shape of an aircraft wing?
options: The curved wings of birds, which have allowed them to fly naturally.
The flat fins of fish, which help them move through water efficiently.
The wide ears of elephants, which they use to fan and cool themselves.
The spinning seeds of maple trees, which spin as they fall.
explanation: Aircraft wings are modeled on birds' curved wings, copying a design that nature perfected over millions of years.

q: How many meters are equal to one kilometer?
options: 1,000 meters
100 meters
10,000 meters
500 meters
explanation: The prefix 'kilo' means one thousand, so one kilometer equals exactly 1,000 meters.

q: Which organ in your body produces insulin?
options: The pancreas
The liver
The kidneys
The stomach
explanation: The pancreas, located behind the stomach, is the organ that makes insulin to help control blood sugar.

q: How can brand-new islands form in the middle of the ocean?
options: Underwater volcanoes erupt repeatedly and build up enough rock to rise above the sea surface.
Earthquakes push large sections of the seafloor upward until they break the surface.
Strong ocean currents pile sand and sediment into mounds that grow into islands.
Coral reefs grow tall enough over thousands of years to appear above the water.
explanation: When underwater volcanoes erupt again and again, the built-up lava and rock can eventually rise above the ocean surface to form new islands.

q: What dangerous substance can grow on stored maize and is linked to liver cancer?
options: Aflatoxin produced by the fungus Aspergillus flavus
Mycotoxin released by mold growing on wet soil
A pesticide residue absorbed from fertilized farmland
A bacteria released from improperly washed grain
explanation: Aspergillus flavus produces aflatoxin on stored maize; long-term exposure to aflatoxin is linked to liver cancer.

q: What is the difference between permeable and impermeable rock?
options: Permeable rock has holes that let water pass through, while dense impermeable rock blocks water.
Permeable rock is harder than impermeable rock and does not break under pressure.
Permeable rock can hold heat much longer than impermeable rock.
Permeable rock is found only near volcanoes, while impermeable rock forms on ocean floors.
explanation: Permeable rocks have pores or cracks that allow water to soak through, while dense impermeable rocks stop water from passing.

q: Why does an octopus have blue blood instead of red blood?
options: It uses copper instead of iron to carry oxygen through its body.
It lives in cold, deep water where blood naturally turns blue.
Its blood is mixed with blue ink from its ink sac.
It absorbs blue pigment from the algae and plants it eats.
explanation: Octopus blood is blue because it uses a copper-based protein to carry oxygen, unlike the iron-based protein in red blood.

q: What do animals use as energy while they hibernate through winter?
options: Body fat stored before hibernation begins
Food they collect and hide inside their den or burrow
Sugar produced slowly by their muscles while they rest
Water stored in special tissues in their body
explanation: Animals eat heavily before hibernating to build up body fat, which their bodies slowly burn as fuel throughout the winter.

q: How is a frog's life cycle different from a butterfly's?
options: A frog has no pupa stage; it goes only from egg to tadpole to frog.
A frog lays eggs on land, while a butterfly lays its eggs in water.
A frog goes through more stages than a butterfly does.
A frog's tadpole stage is the same as a butterfly's larva stage in every way.
explanation: Unlike a butterfly, a frog skips the pupa stage and transforms directly from tadpole to adult frog.

q: Why do many desert animals have light-colored fur or skin?
options: Light colors reflect sunlight and help them blend in with the sand.
Light colors absorb more heat to help them stay warm at night.
Light colors are easier for predators to see, which warns them away.
Light colors help them find each other more easily across the open desert.
explanation: Light coloring in desert animals serves two purposes: reflecting the harsh sun and providing camouflage in sandy surroundings.

q: Why do dogs pant when they are hot?
options: Panting evaporates water from their tongue and mouth, which carries heat away.
Panting pumps cool air into their stomach to chill the blood.
Panting makes their heart beat faster so blood moves to cooler body parts.
Panting releases extra water from their body to make them lighter.
explanation: Dogs cannot sweat through their skin, so they pant to evaporate moisture from their mouth and tongue, which cools them down.

q: How do scientists know about Earth's deep layers even though no drill has reached the core?
options: They study seismic waves from earthquakes, which change speed and direction as they pass through different layers.
They send heat-resistant robots down the deepest volcanic vents to measure the layers.
They use powerful X-rays aimed at the ground to see through solid rock.
They study the pressure and temperature of lava from erupting volcanoes.
explanation: Seismic waves bend and speed up or slow down when they pass through different materials inside Earth, allowing scientists to map the layers.

q: Why is it NOT safe to assume a small open window makes it okay to run a vehicle engine indoors?
options: One small window is not enough to clear out all the carbon monoxide, which can still build up to dangerous levels.
Carbon monoxide is heavier than air and sinks to the floor where windows cannot reach it.
Windows only let out water vapor, not invisible gases like carbon monoxide.
A running engine produces so much heat that a window would need to be fully open to help.
explanation: A cracked window provides insufficient ventilation; carbon monoxide can still reach deadly concentrations indoors even with some airflow.

q: What is the main difference between a decomposer and a scavenger?
options: A scavenger is a visible animal that eats chunks of dead matter, while a decomposer like bacteria is tiny and fully breaks down what remains into the soil.
A scavenger lives underground and eats roots, while a decomposer lives above ground and eats dead leaves.
A scavenger only eats plants, while a decomposer only breaks down dead animals.
A scavenger produces compost, while a decomposer produces seeds for new plants.
explanation: Scavengers are visible animals eating large pieces of dead matter, while decomposers are microscopic organisms that completely break down what is left.

q: According to Pinggang Pinoy, what should take up half of your plate at each meal?
options: Vegetables and fruit together
Rice and vegetables together
Protein-rich food and rice together
Fruit juice and protein-rich food together
explanation: Pinggang Pinoy guidelines say half the plate should be vegetables and fruit, with the remaining half split between rice and protein.

q: Whose X-ray image was important in helping Watson and Crick discover the shape of DNA in 1953?
options: Rosalind Franklin
Marie Curie
Barbara McClintock
Dorothy Hodgkin
explanation: Watson and Crick used an X-ray image of DNA taken by Rosalind Franklin as crucial evidence when working out the structure of DNA.

q: Who invented the World Wide Web (WWW)?
options: Tim Berners-Lee
Bill Gates
Steve Jobs
Alan Turing
explanation: The World Wide Web was invented by Tim Berners-Lee, not the internet itself but the system of web pages and links we use today.

q: Where does the Brahminy kite build its nest?
options: High in trees near water, using sticks and leaves.
On rocky cliff ledges above the sea using mud and grass.
On the ground near rivers, hidden under dense bushes.
In hollow tree trunks near water, lined with soft feathers.
explanation: The Brahminy kite builds its stick-and-leaf nest high in trees close to water, where it hunts for food.

q: What happens to sea cucumbers (balatan) after they are harvested in the Philippines?
options: They are dried and sold to Chinese markets as a valuable seafood called trepang.
They are ground into medicine and used in local herbal clinics.
They are released into fish ponds to clean algae from the water.
They are preserved in vinegar and sold as a local condiment called bagoong.
explanation: Philippine sea cucumbers are harvested, dried, and exported to Chinese markets as trepang, which has driven population declines on many reefs.

q: What is the difference between how objects behave in elastic versus inelastic collisions?
options: In some collisions objects bounce apart, while in others they stick together and move as one.
In elastic collisions both objects stop moving, while in inelastic collisions they continue moving.
In elastic collisions one object absorbs all the energy, while in inelastic collisions energy is shared equally.
In elastic collisions objects slow down gradually, while in inelastic collisions they stop all at once.
explanation: Elastic collisions result in objects bouncing apart, while inelastic collisions result in objects sticking together and moving as a single combined mass.

q: Why are small lumps you can feel in your neck not always a sign of something dangerous?
options: They are likely lymph nodes, which are always in your body and only swell when they are fighting an illness.
They are fat deposits that build up during childhood and disappear in adulthood.
They are muscle knots caused by carrying heavy school bags every day.
They are glands that swell after eating salty food and shrink once you drink water.
explanation: Small neck lumps are usually lymph nodes — a normal part of the immune system — that become noticeable only when enlarged while fighting infection.

q: What is the purpose of the three soft 'eyes' or holes found on one end of a coconut?
options: The new sprout pushes out through one of these holes when the coconut germinates.
They allow the coconut to absorb water from the soil while it is still on the tree.
They release a sweet gas that attracts animals to eat and spread the coconut.
They are air holes that keep the coconut from bursting in hot weather.
explanation: One of the three germination pores (eyes) is softer than the others, and the seedling sprout pushes through it when the coconut begins to grow.

q: What does a higher coefficient of friction tell you about two surfaces?
options: The surfaces are rougher and there is more friction between them.
The surfaces are smoother and objects slide more easily over them.
The surfaces have more mass and are therefore harder to lift.
The surfaces conduct electricity better than surfaces with lower coefficients.
explanation: The coefficient of friction is higher for rougher surfaces, meaning there is more resistance to sliding between them.

q: What is a common misconception about mangrove trees and saltwater?
options: People wrongly think mangroves love salt, but they actually just tolerate it and can grow fine in fresh water.
People wrongly think mangroves die in salt water, but they actually need salt to survive and grow.
People wrongly think mangroves absorb salt from seawater to use as fertilizer.
People wrongly think mangroves only grow in fresh water and cannot survive any salt at all.
explanation: Mangroves do not prefer salt — they simply tolerate it better than other plants and can actually grow well in fresh water.

q: Why are ceramic (porcelain) materials used on high-voltage power line insulators?
options: Because ceramics are good electrical insulators and do not conduct electricity.
Because ceramics are lightweight and make it easier to hang cables from poles.
Because ceramics reflect lightning away from the wires during storms.
Because ceramics are magnetic and keep the electrical current flowing along the wire.
explanation: Ceramics do not conduct electricity, making them ideal insulators to prevent electricity from escaping into the poles or towers.

q: How does a snail build its shell?
options: A thin layer of its body called the mantle releases calcium that hardens into shell.
It collects small pebbles and sticks them together with a sticky liquid from its foot.
It sheds an outer layer of skin that dries and hardens in the sun over time.
It absorbs minerals from the soil through its foot and pushes them outward.
explanation: The mantle, a thin layer of the snail's body, secretes calcium that gradually hardens into the spiral shell.

q: Why are flowers that bloom at night often white or pale instead of brightly colored?
options: Because color cannot be seen in the dark, so they rely on strong scent to attract bats and moths.
Because pale flowers absorb more moonlight, which they need for extra energy at night.
Because bright colors would scare away the insects that pollinate them at night.
Because night temperatures are too cold for plants to produce colorful pigments.
explanation: At night, color is invisible, so night-blooming flowers skip bright colors and instead use scent to attract nocturnal pollinators like bats and moths.

q: What makes the cassowary stand out as a bird?
options: It is a large flightless bird from New Guinea and Australia with sharp claws.
It is a large flying bird from South America known for its colorful feathers.
It is a small water bird from Australia that runs across the surface of ponds.
It is a flightless bird from Africa that is the tallest bird in the world.
explanation: The cassowary is a large, flightless bird found in New Guinea and Australia, recognized for its powerful legs and sharp claws.

q: What is the main job of the lymphatic system?
options: It carries lymph fluid through vessels and nodes, filtering out germs before the fluid returns to the blood.
It pumps oxygenated blood from the heart to all the organs of the body.
It produces the hormones that control growth and body temperature.
It absorbs digested food from the intestines and delivers it to the liver.
explanation: The lymphatic system filters germs from lymph fluid in nodes throughout the body before returning the clean fluid to the bloodstream.

q: What is a sloth's typical resting position in a tree?
options: It hangs upside down with its head pointing down.
It sits upright on a branch gripping it with both feet.
It curls into a ball on a wide branch to sleep.
It hangs sideways with its body parallel to the branch.
explanation: Sloths are famous for hanging upside down from branches, spending most of their lives in this head-down position.

q: According to Newton's law of cooling, when does a hot object cool the fastest?
options: When the temperature difference between the object and its surroundings is greatest.
When the object is placed in a vacuum where no air can carry heat away.
When the object is the same temperature as the room it is placed in.
When the object is wrapped in a material that prevents heat from escaping quickly.
explanation: Newton's law of cooling states that the greater the temperature difference between an object and its surroundings, the faster heat is lost.

q: Why do some animals produce venom?
options: Either to hunt for food or to defend themselves against enemies.
Only to mark their territory and warn off competing animals.
Only to paralyze prey; they never use it for self-defense.
To digest food externally before swallowing it whole.
explanation: Animals use venom for two main reasons: to capture and kill prey, or to protect themselves from predators.

q: How did the Emden Deep get its name?
options: It was named after the German ship Emden, which discovered it in 1927.
It was named after a Filipino fisherman named Emden who first reported it.
It was named for the German word for 'deep,' which is 'emden.'
It was named after a German scientist who studied deep-sea trenches.
explanation: The Emden Deep was discovered in 1927 by the German ship Emden and was named after that vessel.

q: How does sweating prevent your body from overheating?
options: As sweat dries on your skin, it carries heat away from your body.
Sweat creates a cool liquid layer that blocks more heat from reaching your skin.
Sweating speeds up your heartbeat so blood reaches your skin faster.
Sweat absorbs oxygen from the air, which cools the surface of the skin.
explanation: When sweat evaporates from the skin, it takes heat along with it, lowering your body temperature.

q: Why was molave wood used to build historic churches in the Philippines?
options: It is one of the most durable Philippine hardwoods and resists decay even without chemical treatment.
It is the lightest Philippine wood, making it easy to transport to build sites.
It absorbs water easily, which makes it ideal for structures near the sea.
It produces a natural resin that hardens into a protective coating on buildings.
explanation: Molave is prized because its natural durability allows it to resist rot and insects for centuries without chemical preservatives.

q: What is the key difference between a homogeneous and a heterogeneous mixture?
options: A homogeneous mixture looks uniform throughout, while a heterogeneous mixture has clearly visible different parts.
A homogeneous mixture can be separated easily, while a heterogeneous mixture cannot be separated at all.
A homogeneous mixture contains only solids, while a heterogeneous mixture contains liquids and solids.
A homogeneous mixture is always a liquid, while a heterogeneous mixture is always a solid.
explanation: Homogeneous mixtures (like sugar water) look the same throughout, while heterogeneous mixtures (like salad) show clearly distinct ingredients.

q: What makes Philippine shrews like the Mindanao shrew and Palawan moss shrew special?
options: They are found nowhere else in the world — they are endemic to the Philippines.
They are the smallest mammals in Southeast Asia and can fit in a teaspoon.
They are the only mammals in the Philippines that can breathe underwater.
They were brought to the Philippines by Spanish colonizers in the 1500s.
explanation: Several Philippine shrews are endemic species, meaning they exist only in the Philippines and are found on specific islands.

q: When is the Ati-Atihan festival held every year?
options: On the third Sunday of January
On the first Saturday of February
On the last Sunday of December
On the second Friday of March
explanation: The Ati-Atihan festival is celebrated on the third Sunday of January each year in Kalibo, Aklan.

q: Who is credited with coining the word 'radioactivity'?
options: Marie Curie
Albert Einstein
Isaac Newton
Louis Pasteur
explanation: The word 'radioactivity' was coined by Marie Curie.

q: What made it possible for living things to begin surviving on land millions of years ago?
options: The ozone layer formed as oxygen built up in the atmosphere
Large amounts of carbon dioxide dissolved into the oceans
The continents spread apart creating more land area
Volcanic eruptions cooled the planet enough for life
explanation: Millions of years ago the ozone layer formed as oxygen built up, helping make it safe for living things to survive on land.

q: Even though carbon monoxide is poisonous, it has a useful role in industry. What is one example of that use?
options: Removing oxygen from iron ore to make iron and steel
Adding color to plastics in a factory
Cooling machines that get too hot during manufacturing
Purifying drinking water at treatment plants
explanation: Carbon monoxide is used in making iron and steel to remove oxygen from iron ore, showing that even a dangerous gas can be useful when handled carefully.

q: How does a stick insect protect itself from birds and other predators?
options: Its body looks almost exactly like a twig, hiding it from view
It sprays a foul-smelling liquid when attacked
It makes a loud buzzing sound to scare enemies away
Its bright colors warn predators that it is poisonous
explanation: A stick insect has a body that looks almost exactly like a twig, and this camouflage hides it from birds and other predators.

q: Besides producing rubber, how does the rubber tree help the environment?
options: It takes in carbon dioxide and releases oxygen, helping clean the air
It filters harmful chemicals out of the soil with its deep roots
It produces a sap that repels insects and keeps pests away
It absorbs salt from the ground, making farmland more fertile
explanation: Like other trees, the rubber tree takes in carbon dioxide and releases oxygen, which helps clean the air.

q: In a termite colony, which group is responsible for finding food and building the nest?
options: The workers
The soldiers
The queen
The drones
explanation: In a termite colony the workers find food and build the nest, while the queen lays eggs and the soldiers defend the colony.

q: What is the highest value that longitude can reach on Earth?
options: 180 degrees
360 degrees
90 degrees
270 degrees
explanation: Longitude ranges from 0 degrees at the prime meridian to 180 degrees.

q: What is the Benham Plateau (Philippine Rise)?
options: A large underwater plateau in the Pacific Ocean within the Philippines' Exclusive Economic Zone
A mountain range in the northern Philippines rich in gold and copper
A deep ocean trench along the eastern coast of Mindanao
A coral reef system located inside the Sulu Sea
explanation: The Benham Plateau (Philippine Rise) is a large submarine plateau in the Pacific Ocean within the Philippines' Exclusive Economic Zone, recognized as a potential source of minerals.

q: What is the job of the tonsils in your body?
options: They help trap germs that enter through the mouth and nose
They produce digestive juices that break down food
They filter waste products out of the blood
They send electrical signals from the brain to the muscles
explanation: The tonsils help trap germs that enter through the mouth and nose.

q: What is nectar, and why do pollinators visit flowers to get it?
options: A sweet liquid inside a flower that pollinators use as food
A sticky powder that clings to insects and helps them fly
A scent released by flowers to attract butterflies at night
A colorful pigment in petals that signals the flower is ripe
explanation: Nectar is a sweet liquid inside a flower that pollinators use as food.

q: What energy transformation happens inside a generator?
options: Kinetic (motion) energy becomes electrical energy
Chemical energy becomes light energy
Heat energy becomes sound energy
Electrical energy becomes mechanical energy
explanation: In a generator, kinetic or motion energy becomes electrical energy.

q: How can lightning actually help plants grow?
options: Its intense heat combines nitrogen in the air into a form plants can absorb through rain
It heats the soil so roots grow deeper toward moisture
It breaks apart rock, releasing minerals that wash into the soil
It produces ozone that protects leaves from harmful ultraviolet rays
explanation: Lightning's intense heat can combine nitrogen in the air into a form plants can use, and rain carries it into the soil.

q: Who became President of the Philippines after Manuel Roxas died in 1948?
options: Elpidio Quirino
Ramon Magsaysay
Carlos P. Garcia
Diosdado Macapagal
explanation: Elpidio Quirino became President after Roxas died in 1948, and he was the sixth President of the Philippines.

q: Why does a convex lens sometimes produce an upside-down image?
options: When the object is far away, light rays cross after the focal point, flipping the image
The glass curves inward, bending all light beams downward
The coating on the lens reflects some light back, reversing the image
Light travels slower through thick glass, causing the image to rotate
explanation: When the object is far from the lens, the light rays cross after the focal point, so the image flips upside down — this is how projectors and cameras work.

q: How do elephants help plants spread to new areas?
options: They carry plant seeds in their droppings and deposit them far away
They dig up roots with their tusks and plant them elsewhere
They spray water from their trunks onto dry seeds to help them sprout
They knock down old trees so sunlight reaches new seedlings
explanation: Elephants help nature by spreading plant seeds through their droppings.

q: What happens to the weather in the Philippines when the habagat arrives?
options: It rains frequently, so children carry umbrellas more often on the way to school
Strong dry winds blow dust across the streets every afternoon
The temperature drops sharply and mornings become very cold and foggy
Typhoons stop forming and the skies stay clear for weeks
explanation: When the habagat arrives, it rains frequently, so children carry umbrellas more often on the way to school.

q: What is special about many of the freshwater fish found in the rivers and lakes of the Philippines?
options: They are endemic, meaning they are found only in specific parts of the Philippines
They can survive equally well in both fresh water and salt water
They migrate every year to rivers in other Asian countries to breed
They are the largest freshwater fish species found anywhere in Southeast Asia
explanation: The rivers and lakes of the Philippines are home to hundreds of freshwater fish species that are endemic, or found only in specific parts of the country.

q: In which region of the Philippines is the province of Pampanga located?
options: Central Luzon (Region III)
Ilocos Region (Region I)
Calabarzon (Region IV-A)
Cagayan Valley (Region II)
explanation: Pampanga is a province in the Central Luzon region (Region III) of the Philippines, and its capital is San Fernando.

q: How do large Philippine fruit bats like flying foxes find their food?
options: They use their vision to locate fruit
They use echolocation like smaller insect-eating bats
They follow scent trails left by other animals
They use sensitive hearing to detect fruit falling from trees
explanation: Large Philippine fruit bats like flying foxes are megabats that use vision to find food, not echolocation like the smaller insect-eating microbats.

q: What are the three main layers of the Earth, from outermost to innermost?
options: Crust, mantle, and core
Crust, magma, and inner core
Atmosphere, lithosphere, and asthenosphere
Outer shell, middle ring, and lava center
explanation: The Earth has three main layers: the crust (the outer skin), the mantle (the thick middle layer), and the core (the center).

q: Why does adrenaline make you breathe faster when you are scared or in danger?
options: So more oxygen enters your lungs to power your muscles to move quickly
So your body temperature drops to keep your brain cool under stress
So carbon dioxide builds up in your blood and makes you more alert
So your heart slows down and your body conserves energy for later
explanation: Adrenaline makes you breathe faster so more oxygen can enter your lungs, giving your muscles the oxygen they need to move quickly and strongly.

q: What are the names of the two moons of Mars?
options: Phobos and Deimos
Titan and Ganymede
Europa and Callisto
Triton and Charon
explanation: Mars has two small moons called Phobos and Deimos; they are shaped like potatoes and are probably captured asteroids.

q: Why can corn be planted in most parts of the Philippines?
options: Corn grows well in the warm climate that the Philippines has
Corn needs very little water, and the Philippines has very dry soil
Corn thrives in cold highlands, which cover most of the Philippines
Corn grows best in salty coastal soil found throughout the country
explanation: Corn grows well in the warm climate of the Philippines, so it can be planted in most parts of the country.

q: Why is boiling a safe way to make unsafe water fit to drink?
options: Boiling kills the germs that can cause diarrhea and other illnesses
Boiling removes salt and minerals that are bad for the body
Boiling adds oxygen to the water, making it taste fresher
Boiling causes dirt particles to sink to the bottom of the container
explanation: Boiling water kills germs that can cause diarrhea and other illnesses, making dirty water safe to drink.

q: Which is the largest muscle in the human body, and what does it help you do?
options: The muscle in the buttocks; it helps us stand up and climb
The muscle in the thigh; it helps us run fast and jump high
The muscle in the upper arm; it helps us lift and carry heavy things
The muscle in the back; it helps us bend forward and straighten up
explanation: The largest muscle in the body is in the buttocks, and it helps us stand up and climb.

q: What does finding lots of earthworms in the ground tell you about the soil?
options: The soil is healthy and rich
The soil is too dry and needs water
The soil contains harmful chemicals from pollution
The soil is too sandy and cannot support plant roots
explanation: Lots of earthworms in the ground is a sign that the soil is healthy and rich.

q: Why do most children end up with DNA that is almost identical to their parents'?
options: Mutations in any one gene are very rare because the body guards and repairs DNA so well
Genes are locked inside bones, which protect them from any changes
Children copy their parents' genes exactly through a process that never makes any errors
Only one parent passes genes to the child, so only half the DNA can change
explanation: Mutations are rare for any one particular gene because the body guards and repairs DNA so well, which is why most of us have DNA almost identical to our parents'.

q: What happens if a young stick insect loses one of its legs?
options: It can grow a new leg back when it sheds its skin
The leg is permanently lost and the insect learns to walk with five legs
The wound heals over and leaves a hard stump that protects the insect
Other insects in the group carry the injured stick insect until it recovers
explanation: If a young stick insect loses a leg, it can grow a new one back when it sheds its skin.

q: What can a strong habagat cause in parts of the Philippines?
options: Many days of rain that lead to flooding
A long dry spell that dries up rivers and farms
Powerful earthquakes along coastal areas
Extremely cold temperatures that freeze mountain lakes
explanation: A strong habagat can bring many days of rain that cause flooding in parts of the Philippines.

q: What comes out when you cut a jackfruit, and how do people protect themselves from it?
options: Sticky sap; people rub oil on their hands and knife so it does not stick
Sweet juice; people wear gloves so the juice does not stain their skin
Tiny seeds; people cover the fruit with cloth to catch the seeds
A strong smell; people hold their breath and cut quickly to avoid it
explanation: When you cut a jackfruit, sticky sap comes out, so people rub oil on their hands and knife so the sap does not stick.

q: How does the lifespan of a queen ant compare to that of a worker ant?
options: The queen can live for many years, while workers live only a few months
The worker and the queen live the same length of time, about one year
Worker ants outlive the queen because they stay safe underground
The queen lives only a few weeks because laying eggs wears her out quickly
explanation: A queen ant can live for many years, while worker ants live only a few months.

q: Where did Emilio Aguinaldo first officially wave the Philippine flag?
options: At Kawit, Cavite on June 12, 1898
At Malolos, Bulacan on July 4, 1896
At Intramuros, Manila on June 12, 1896
At Batangas City on August 23, 1896
explanation: Emilio Aguinaldo first officially waved the flag at Kawit, Cavite on June 12, 1898 during the declaration of independence.

q: Where in the Philippines is the Puerto Princesa Underground River located?
options: Palawan
Cebu
Mindanao
Batangas
explanation: The Puerto Princesa Underground River is in Palawan, Philippines.

q: What happens when two particles that have the same type of electric charge are placed near each other?
options: They push each other away
They attract and stick together
They cancel each other out and become neutral
They spin around each other like tiny planets
explanation: Particles with the same charge, like two protons, push each other away.

q: What device is officially used to define the exact length of one second worldwide?
options: An atomic clock
A pendulum clock
A digital stopwatch
A quartz wristwatch
explanation: The atomic clock is officially used to define the exact length of one second worldwide.

q: Why won't an ordinary electric fan turn itself off when the room becomes cool?
options: A fan has no thermostat, so it cannot measure the room's temperature and must be switched off by hand
A fan's motor breaks down when the air is too cold, so it stops on its own
A fan always runs at the same speed regardless of what button you press
A fan is connected to the same switch as the lights, so turning off the lights stops it
explanation: An ordinary electric fan has no thermostat — it doesn't measure the room's heat, so it won't stop by itself when it's cool; you must switch it off by hand.

q: Which statement best shows how ecologically significant termites are on Earth?
options: The combined weight of all termites on Earth exceeds the combined weight of all humans
Termites are found on every continent, including Antarctica
A single termite queen can lay more than one million eggs per day
Termites build mounds that are taller than any building made by humans
explanation: The combined weight (biomass) of all termites on Earth exceeds the combined weight of all humans, showing how ecologically significant these insects are.

q: What was the nationality of the astronomer Nicolaus Copernicus?
options: Polish
German
Italian
Czech
explanation: Nicolaus Copernicus was a Polish astronomer from Poland.

q: What does the climbing perch eat?
options: Small animals like insects, worms, shrimp, and tiny fish, as well as water plants
Only algae and underwater plants attached to rocks
Mainly large fish and frogs that live near the riverbank
Exclusively insects that land on the surface of the water
explanation: The climbing perch eats small animals like insects, worms, shrimp, and tiny fish, and also eats water plants, so it is not picky about food.

q: Which element appears first in the periodic table with atomic number 1?
options: Hydrogen
Helium
Carbon
Oxygen
explanation: Hydrogen is the first element in the periodic table, with atomic number 1.

q: Which layer of Earth's atmosphere is the outermost, where the air slowly fades into space?
options: The exosphere
The thermosphere
The mesosphere
The stratosphere
explanation: The exosphere is the outermost layer of the atmosphere, where the air slowly fades away into space.

q: In a pot of boiling water, what is the circular movement called where hot water rises and cooler water sinks?
options: Convection
Conduction
Radiation
Evaporation
explanation: In a pot of boiling water, hot water at the bottom rises while cooler water at the top sinks — this circular motion is called convection, and it heats all the water.

q: Why do planets that are closer to the Sun orbit faster than planets farther away?
options: Closer planets feel stronger gravity from the Sun, which pulls them along faster
Closer planets are smaller and lighter, so they naturally move more quickly
Closer planets have thinner atmospheres, which create less drag to slow them down
Closer planets formed more recently and still have leftover speed from their formation
explanation: Planets closer to the Sun feel stronger gravity, so they orbit faster than the planets farther away.

q: Why can't you scoop up or hold steam in your hand?
options: Steam is a gas, so it slips through your fingers and spreads into the air
Steam is too hot and immediately turns into ice when it touches cool skin
Steam is a liquid, so it pours off your hands like water
Steam is very heavy, so it sinks to the floor before you can grab it
explanation: Steam is a gas, so it just slips through your fingers and spreads into the air — you can't catch it.

q: Why does sound or light get weaker the farther you are from its source?
options: As a wave travels farther, its energy spreads over a wider area, making it weaker
Waves slow down over distance and lose energy through friction with the air
The air absorbs the wave completely after it travels a certain distance
Waves reflect off the ground repeatedly, and each bounce removes some energy
explanation: As a wave travels farther from its source, its energy spreads over a wider area, so sound or light grows weaker the farther away you are.

q: Why is washing your hands important for people other than just yourself?
options: It stops germs from spreading to other people, especially babies and the elderly who have weaker defenses
It removes vitamins from your skin that could make others allergic if they touch you
It prevents your own fingerprints from leaving marks that carry viruses on surfaces
It keeps your hands warm, which makes you less likely to sneeze on others
explanation: Handwashing stops germs from spreading to other people, especially babies and the elderly who have weaker defenses, so the whole family is better protected.

q: What does a sailfin lizard do when it feels threatened by a predator?
options: It dives into water and can swim and hide underwater for several minutes
It puffs up its body to look bigger and hisses loudly at the attacker
It drops its tail, which wriggles on the ground to distract the predator
It changes color to match the ground and stays completely still
explanation: When threatened, the sailfin lizard dives into water and can swim and hide underwater for several minutes.

q: How does the coloring of a shark's body help it hide in the ocean?
options: Its dark back and pale belly (countershading) make it hard to spot from above or below
Its silver stripes reflect sunlight and blend in with the sparkling surface of the water
Its bright blue color matches the deep ocean where most sharks live
Its spotted pattern looks like the sandy ocean floor where it rests
explanation: A shark's dark back and pale belly is a trick called countershading that makes the shark hard to spot from above or below in the water.

q: What is the most important job of fuses and circuit breakers in a home?
options: To cut the power before overheated wires can start a fire
To store extra electricity when the main supply is turned off
To increase the voltage so appliances run more efficiently
To measure how much electricity each appliance uses every month
explanation: The most important job of fuses and breakers is to prevent fires by cutting the power before overheated wires can burn the insulation and start a flame.

q: How is resting for a fever different from resting a sprained ankle?
options: With a fever the whole body rests to fight germs, while with a sprain only the injured part rests to repair
With a fever you keep moving to sweat out the germs, while a sprain means complete bed rest
Both require the same kind of rest: stay in bed and do not move any part of the body
A fever requires exercise to raise your temperature, while a sprain requires keeping the limb elevated
explanation: Resting for a fever means the whole body rests to gather strength to fight germs, while with a sprain or broken bone just one part rests so it can repair.

q: What keeps a cuttlebone both strong and very light?
options: Tiny pillars between its many thin stacked layers
A solid hard shell with no air spaces inside
A spongy foam material soaked in seawater
Long thick ribs running through its center
explanation: A cuttlebone is made of many thin layers with tiny pillars between them that keep it strong while staying very light.

q: Which island group is Palawan usually counted as part of?
options: Luzon
Visayas
Mindanao
Palawan is its own separate island group
explanation: Palawan, found in the western part of the Philippines, is usually counted as part of the Luzon island group.

q: What happens when overfishing occurs?
options: Fish are caught faster than they can reproduce, so their numbers keep falling
