Fish populations grow too large and overflow into shallow waters
Fishermen use nets that accidentally catch too many different species
Fish reproduce faster than they can be caught, causing overpopulation
explanation: Overfishing means catching fish faster than they can reproduce, which causes their numbers in the sea to keep falling.

q: Which of these useful products can be made from tree bark?
options: Rope and paper
Glass and plastic
Metal wire and cloth
Rubber and concrete
explanation: Bark can be used to make rope, paper, and other useful things.

q: How small a gap can an octopus squeeze through?
options: A gap as small as its eye
A gap as small as its head
A gap as small as its arm
A gap as small as its whole body length
explanation: Because an octopus has no bones, it can squeeze through a gap as small as its eye.

q: How does a solar still clean dirty water?
options: The sun's heat evaporates the dirty water and clean drops collect under a plastic cover
Sunlight kills the bacteria in the water by shining directly on it
A plastic cover filters out dirt particles as water passes through it
The sun heats a special chemical that reacts with the dirt and removes it
explanation: A solar still uses the sun's heat to evaporate dirty water, and the clean drops collect under a plastic cover.

q: Why is it better for Philippine island communities to protect reef sharks instead of catching them?
options: Tourists pay to dive and see reef sharks alive, bringing income and jobs to the community
Reef sharks eat other fish that would otherwise destroy coral reefs
Catching reef sharks is against Philippine law and carries heavy fines
Reef shark meat is poisonous, so catching them puts fishermen in danger
explanation: Many tourists come to the Philippines to dive and see reef sharks alive, bringing income and jobs to island communities.

q: What happens to your muscles when you move and exercise often?
options: They grow stronger
They grow longer and thinner
They become more flexible but weaker
They store more fat to give you energy
explanation: When we move and exercise often, our muscles grow stronger.

q: How do a bird's feathers help keep it warm?
options: They trap the bird's body heat close to its skin
They reflect sunlight so the bird does not overheat
They absorb heat from the sun and store it inside
They block cold wind by lying flat against the body
explanation: A bird's thick feathers trap its body heat, keeping the bird warm.

q: If you push a wall with a force of 10 newtons, how large is the wall's reaction force on you?
options: 10 newtons, pointing back at you
More than 10 newtons, because the wall is heavier
Less than 10 newtons, because the wall does not move
0 newtons, because the wall is not alive and cannot push
explanation: The reaction force is always the same size as the action force, but points in the opposite direction.

q: How does a heron usually catch a fish?
options: It grabs and clamps the fish with its beak
It skewers the fish like a barbecue stick, piercing all the way through
It scoops the fish up in a pouch under its beak
It stuns the fish by slapping the water with its wing
explanation: Despite the common belief that herons skewer fish, they usually just grab and clamp the fish with their beak rather than piercing through it.

q: In which liquid would an object feel a stronger buoyant force?
options: A denser liquid, like salt water
A less dense liquid, like fresh water
The buoyant force is the same in all liquids
A warmer liquid, because heat increases the push
explanation: A liquid pushes up with a buoyant force, and this force is stronger in a denser liquid.

q: What does PAGASA's Signal No. 1 mean?
options: Light winds are coming and it is time to start preparing early
Very strong winds are expected within 12 hours
The typhoon is currently passing over the area
All schools and offices must close immediately
explanation: Signal No. 1 is PAGASA's lowest warning, meaning light winds are coming and it is time to start preparing early.

q: What makes Coron Bay in northern Palawan famous among divers?
options: Sunken Japanese ships from World War II beneath its waters
The world's largest living coral reef system
Underground rivers that flow into the sea
Schools of whale sharks that gather there every year
explanation: Coron Bay in northern Palawan is famous for sunken Japanese ships from World War II beneath its waters, popular among snorkelers and scuba divers.

q: Why do many stingrays have a sharp, venomous spine on their tail?
options: To defend themselves against threats, not to hunt
To steer while swimming through strong currents
To dig into the sand when resting on the seafloor
To attract prey by waving the tail like a lure
explanation: Many stingrays have a sharp, venomous spine on the tail that they use to defend themselves against threats, not to hunt.

q: Why don't we get badly burned the moment we step outside on a sunny day?
options: The ozone layer blocks most of the most dangerous UV rays from the sun
Our skin produces a natural sunscreen when exposed to sunlight
Clouds always reflect enough sunlight to keep UV levels safe
The atmosphere is too thick for UV rays to pass through at all
explanation: The ozone layer blocks most of the most dangerous UV rays, preventing us from burning right away when we go outside.

q: What happens to a solution when you add more water to it?
options: It becomes more dilute
It becomes more concentrated
It turns from a liquid into a solid
The solute stops dissolving and sinks to the bottom
explanation: Adding water to a solution means there is less solute in more water, making the solution more dilute.

q: What is the standard household voltage in the Philippines?
options: 220 volts AC at 60 Hz
110 volts AC at 60 Hz
220 volts AC at 50 Hz
110 volts DC at 60 Hz
explanation: Standard household electricity in the Philippines is 220 volts AC at 60 Hz, which is higher than the 110 volts used in the United States.

q: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
options: Au
Go
Gd
Ag
explanation: The chemical symbol for gold is Au, from the Latin word 'aurum'.

q: When does a growing baby's heart start to beat?
options: Only a few weeks after life begins
At about six months, when the baby can be felt moving
Right at birth, when the baby takes its first breath
After the brain and nervous system fully form
explanation: The growing baby's heart starts to beat only a few weeks after life begins.

q: What does a stick insect do when it senses danger?
options: It stays perfectly still so it will not be noticed
It sprays a foul-smelling liquid at the threat
It drops to the ground and plays dead
It quickly flies away using its hidden wings
explanation: When there is danger, a stick insect stays perfectly still so that it will not be noticed.

q: Why is geothermal power considered cleaner than coal power?
options: Geothermal burns nothing and uses the Earth's heat, so it does not produce smoke or run out
Geothermal produces less electricity, so there is less waste energy released
Geothermal plants are built underground, so their emissions stay below the surface
Geothermal uses water to cool the steam, which washes away the pollutants
explanation: Unlike coal plants that burn fuel and produce lots of smoke, geothermal just uses the Earth's heat, so it is cleaner and does not run out.

q: What is the minimum wind speed for a Category 5 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson scale?
options: 252 km/h (157 mph)
185 km/h (115 mph)
220 km/h (137 mph)
300 km/h (186 mph)
explanation: A Category 5 hurricane, the strongest on the Saffir-Simpson scale, has winds of 252 km/h (157 mph) or higher.

q: How far away can you hear a lion's roar?
options: Up to 8 kilometers away
Up to 1 kilometer away
Up to 3 kilometers away
Up to 15 kilometers away
explanation: A lion's roar is very loud and can be heard from as far as 8 kilometers away.

q: Who proposed the theory of evolution by natural selection?
options: Charles Darwin
Gregor Mendel
Louis Pasteur
Isaac Newton
explanation: Charles Darwin, an English naturalist, proposed the theory of evolution by natural selection.

q: What do you find inside a guava fruit?
options: Soft flesh and many tiny seeds
A hard pit surrounded by thin juice
One large seed with no flesh
Thick dry pulp with no seeds at all
explanation: Inside a guava is soft flesh and many tiny seeds.

q: What does the tabon bird eat?
options: Seeds, fruit, worms, and small insects it finds on the ground
Only fish it catches by diving into the sea
Small mammals and lizards it hunts in the forest
Nectar from flowers and small flying insects it catches in the air
explanation: The tabon eats seeds, fruit, worms, and small insects it finds on the ground.

q: What gives kutsinta its chewy, jelly-like texture?
options: A little lye mixed into the rice-flour batter before steaming
Sugar syrup poured over the cake after it is cooked
Coconut milk stirred into the batter to make it thick
Extra water added to the rice flour to soften the dough
explanation: Kutsinta is a rice-flour cake mixed with a little lye, which makes the batter set into a chewy, jelly-like texture when steamed.

q: Who was the first person to break the sound barrier by flying faster than sound?
options: Chuck Yeager
Neil Armstrong
Yuri Gagarin
Amelia Earhart
explanation: Chuck Yeager was the first person to break the sound barrier, flying faster than sound.

q: What does the hormone insulin do in the body?
options: It helps glucose enter cells, which lowers the sugar level in the blood
It stores extra sugar as fat in the liver and muscles
It signals the stomach to stop producing acid after a meal
It carries oxygen from the lungs to all parts of the body
explanation: Insulin is a hormone from the pancreas that helps glucose enter the cells, which lowers the sugar level in the blood.

q: Why are fungi called decomposers?
options: They break down dead leaves, wood, and animals and return nutrients to the soil
They produce oxygen that other living things need to breathe
They absorb sunlight and convert it into food for the forest
They protect trees from insects by releasing chemicals into the soil
explanation: Fungi digest food outside their bodies, breaking down dead matter, which is why they are called decomposers that clean nature and return nutrients to the soil.

q: Why do craters on the Moon last for a very long time?
options: The Moon has no wind or rain to wear them away
The Moon's rocky surface is harder than any rock on Earth
New craters fill in the old ones and make them deeper
The Moon's gravity is too weak to let rocks slide into the craters
explanation: Craters on the Moon last for a very long time because the Moon has no wind or rain to wear them away.

q: Where was Lupang Hinirang first played?
options: Kawit, Cavite
Manila
Malolos, Bulacan
Cebu City
explanation: Lupang Hinirang was first played in Kawit, Cavite on June 12, 1898, during the declaration of independence.

q: What kind of substance is baking soda?
options: A base
An acid
A neutral salt
A solvent
explanation: Baking soda is a base, and when mixed with vinegar (an acid) it fizzes because of a chemical reaction.

q: Why does a neutral atom have no overall electrical charge?
options: The number of protons equals the number of electrons, so the charges cancel out
It has no protons and no electrons, only neutrons inside
Its electrons move so fast that their charge becomes zero
The protons and neutrons bond together and cancel each other's charge
explanation: In a neutral atom, the number of protons equals the number of electrons, so it has no overall electrical charge.

q: Which fish is known as one of the fastest in the ocean?
options: The sailfish, reaching about 110 km/h
The swordfish, reaching about 80 km/h
The tuna, reaching about 90 km/h
The mako shark, reaching about 70 km/h
explanation: One of the fastest fish is the sailfish, reaching up to about 110 kilometers per hour.

q: When did the BSP first release the polymer (plastic) 1,000-peso banknote?
options: April 2022
January 2020
June 2019
December 2023
explanation: The BSP first released the polymer (plastic) 1,000-peso banknote in April 2022.

q: Who created HTML, the language used to build web pages?
options: Tim Berners-Lee
Bill Gates
Steve Jobs
Alan Turing
explanation: Tim Berners-Lee created HTML, the language used to build web pages.

q: On a spinning object, which part moves the fastest?
options: The outer edge, because it travels a longer distance each turn
The center, because it spins the most times per second
All parts move at the same speed because they turn together
The middle, because it receives the most force from the motor
explanation: On a spinning object, the outer edge moves faster than the center because it has to travel a longer distance each turn.

q: Why does drinking enough water help your blood flow easily through your body?
options: Your blood is mostly water, so staying hydrated keeps it flowing smoothly
Water cools the blood so it moves faster through narrower vessels
Water dissolves the red blood cells so they fit through tiny capillaries
Water adds oxygen to the blood, making the heart pump more strongly
explanation: Your blood is mostly water, so drinking water helps it flow easily through your whole body, making it easier for blood to carry oxygen and nutrients.

q: Which of these can slow down or stop radioactive decay?
options: Nothing — heat, cold, pressure, and chemicals do not change the rate of decay
Extreme cold temperatures, which slow down all atomic movement
High pressure, which squeezes the atoms and prevents them from breaking apart
Strong acids, which react with the radioactive atoms and neutralize them
explanation: Radioactive decay cannot be turned off or sped up — it is not changed by heat, cold, pressure, or chemicals, and keeps going at its own steady rate.

q: What kinds of plants do goats eat?
options: Many kinds, including leaves and bushes, not just grass
Only short grass that grows close to the ground
Mostly grain and seeds, not leafy plants
Only soft plants like flowers and vegetables
explanation: Goats eat many kinds of plants, including leaves and bushes, not just grass.

q: Why does the Sun have a weaker effect on ocean tides than the Moon, even though the Sun is much bigger?
options: The Sun is much farther away, so its pull on the oceans is weaker than the closer Moon
The Sun's gravity pulls equally on all sides of Earth, so the effects cancel out
The Sun's gravity pulls on land but not on water because water can flow away
The Moon moves faster, which creates a stronger pulling force on the oceans
explanation: Even though the sun is bigger, it is much farther away from Earth than the moon, so its effect on tides is weaker than the moon's.

q: How long can a pangolin's tongue be?
options: Longer than its whole body when fully stretched out
About the same length as its front leg
About half the length of its body
Just long enough to reach inside a termite tunnel
explanation: The pangolin's tongue is so long that it can be longer than its whole body when stretched out.

q: In what year did the Philippine-American War officially end?
explanation: The Philippine-American War officially ended in the year 1902.

q: What color does methyl orange indicator turn in a base?
options: Yellow
Red
Orange
Purple
explanation: Methyl orange turns yellow in a base.

q: Why do caretakers hold a platypus by the tail and keep it away from its legs?
options: The sharp spur on its legs can deliver venom and must not reach the handler
Its legs are very fragile and can break easily if touched
The platypus uses its legs to spray a defensive liquid
Its claws carry bacteria that cause dangerous infections
explanation: Caretakers hold the platypus carefully by the tail and away from its legs so the sharp venomous spur cannot reach them.

q: Why is the deepest part of a cave always completely dark?
options: Sunlight cannot reach that far into the cave
The cave walls absorb all the light before it gets deep
Bats block any light from entering the inner cave
Water on the cave walls bends light so it turns back before going deep
explanation: The deepest part of a cave is always completely dark because sunlight cannot reach there.

q: How do the parts of a feather work together to make a smooth, strong surface?
options: Tiny branches with hooks lock together along a central shaft
The feather is made of one solid flat piece with no moving parts
Overlapping scales fold together like fish scales on skin
The branches are glued together by a sticky oil from the bird
explanation: A feather has a central shaft, and tiny branches with hooks lock together to make a smooth, strong surface.

q: In which island group of the Philippines is the province of Sorsogon located?
options: Luzon
Visayas
Mindanao
Palawan
explanation: Sorsogon is a province in the Bicol Region (Region V), which is part of Luzon.

q: What happened to the town of Cagsawa during Mayon Volcano's 1814 eruption?
options: It was completely buried, leaving only the bell tower visible
It was destroyed by an earthquake that struck the same day
Its church was spared but all houses were burned by lava
Heavy floods from the eruption washed the town into the sea
explanation: The 1814 eruption of Mayon buried the town of Cagsawa, and today only the bell tower can still be seen.

q: How do shipworms help the mangrove ecosystem?
options: They break down dead wood and return nutrients to the water and soil
They eat small fish that would otherwise overcrowd the mangroves
They filter salt from the water so mangrove roots can absorb fresh water
They build tunnels in mud that help mangrove roots get more oxygen
explanation: Shipworms help break down dead wood in mangroves, returning nutrients back to the water and soil.

q: Where is the Kuiper Belt located in our solar system?
options: Beyond Neptune's orbit
Between Mars and Jupiter
Just inside Earth's orbit around the Sun
Around Saturn's rings
explanation: The Kuiper Belt is a wide region of icy-rocky objects found beyond Neptune's orbit, where Pluto and other dwarf planets are located.

q: Why is the colugo a better glider than the sugar glider?
options: The colugo's membrane is larger and also covers the neck, fingers, and tail
The colugo has stronger leg muscles for leaping from trees
The colugo's skin flap is made of a thicker, more waterproof material
The colugo can flap its membrane like wings to gain extra height
explanation: The colugo's patagium is bigger and more complete than the sugar glider's, extending to the neck, fingers, and tail — not just from elbow to knee.

q: Which indigenous people are known as the homeland group of the Cordillera Central mountain range in northern Luzon?
options: Igorot
Lumad
Badjaos
Mangyan
explanation: The Cordillera Central is the homeland of the Igorot indigenous peoples and contains scenic highlands and famous rice terraces.

q: Which animal holds the record as the largest reptile on Earth today?
options: The saltwater crocodile
The Komodo dragon
The leatherback sea turtle
The anaconda snake
explanation: The saltwater crocodile is both the largest crocodile and the largest reptile on Earth today.

q: How does the schistosomiasis parasite most commonly enter a person's body?
options: The larva burrows through the skin when a person wades in contaminated water
A person swallows the larva by drinking dirty water
A mosquito injects the larva when it bites a person
The larva floats into the nose when a person breathes near dirty water
explanation: The cercaria larva swims in contaminated water and burrows through a person's skin when they wade or swim in it, often without the person feeling it.

q: A leech is in the same animal family as which of these creatures?
options: Earthworm
Centipede
Flatworm
Snail
explanation: A leech is a segmented worm, in the same family as the earthworm.

q: Why do the white or yellow patches on variegated leaves not make food for the plant?
options: Those patches have no chlorophyll, so they cannot do photosynthesis
Those patches face away from sunlight, so they stay cooler than the green parts
Those patches are too thick for sunlight to pass through to the leaf cells
Those patches store water instead of making food
explanation: The white or yellow patches on variegated leaves have no chlorophyll, so only the green parts can carry out photosynthesis and make food.

q: Why does a rotting piece of fruit slowly seem to disappear over time?
options: Fungi and other living things digest and absorb the nutrients in the fruit
The water inside the fruit evaporates and takes the solid parts with it
Sunlight breaks down the fruit's cells until nothing is left
Insects eat the fruit from the inside and carry it away piece by piece
explanation: Fungi and other decomposers digest rotting fruit and soak up the nutrients, making the food seem to vanish back into nature.

q: Which feature makes oregano leaves easy to recognize by touch and smell?
options: They are thick, juicy, and fragrant with a soft fuzzy surface
They are thin and waxy with a bitter taste and a smooth texture
They are flat and leathery with tiny thorns along the edges
They are long and needle-like with a sharp minty scent
explanation: Oregano leaves are thick, juicy, and fragrant with a soft fuzzy surface, making the plant easy to recognize.

q: What is a gangsa?
options: A flat gong from the Cordillera region used in Igorot rituals and celebrations
A large drum from Mindanao played during Maguindanao festivals
A wind instrument made from bamboo used in Visayan folk dances
A stringed instrument played by the Lumad peoples of Mindanao
explanation: The gangsa is a flat gong from the Cordillera region of the Philippines, used in Igorot rituals and celebrations, with each gangsa having its own pitch.

q: Why was President Ramon Magsaysay called the 'Man of the Masses'?
options: Because he helped ordinary citizens
Because he was born into a very poor farming family
Because he won the most popular votes of any Philippine president
Because he spoke only the local dialects and refused to use English
explanation: Ramon Magsaysay earned the nickname 'Man of the Masses' because he helped ordinary citizens.

q: In which country was paper first invented?
options: China
Egypt
India
Greece
explanation: Paper was first made in China.

q: Air is mainly a mixture of which two gases?
options: Nitrogen and oxygen
Oxygen and carbon dioxide
Carbon dioxide and hydrogen
Hydrogen and helium
explanation: Air is not a single gas but a mixture of several gases, mainly nitrogen and oxygen blended together.

q: Why is grass sometimes wet in the morning even when it did not rain the night before?
options: Water vapor in the air condensed into droplets on the cool grass during the night
Dew falls from clouds that pass quietly overhead before sunrise
Underground water seeps up through the soil and wets the grass from below
The wind blows moisture from nearby rivers and lakes onto the grass
explanation: At night the ground and leaves cool down, and water vapor in the air condenses into droplets called dew on these cold surfaces.

q: What happens when hot water vapor touches a cool surface?
options: It cools and forms tiny droplets of liquid water that can be collected
It reflects off the surface and rises back up as steam
It freezes instantly into tiny ice crystals on the surface
It passes through the surface and warms the object from the inside
explanation: When hot vapor touches a cool surface, it cools and condenses, forming tiny droplets of clean water that can be collected.

q: Is a bleached coral reef already dead?
options: No — bleached coral is still alive and can recover if the water cools down
Yes — bleaching always means the coral has died and cannot come back
No — bleached coral grows faster than normal coral during warm periods
Yes — once coral turns white it releases poison that kills nearby fish
explanation: A bleached coral is not dead yet; it is still alive and can recover if the water cools down again.

q: Approximately how long can the Philippine Eagle grow from head to tail?
options: About 100 centimeters (almost 1 meter)
About 50 centimeters (about half a meter)
About 150 centimeters (one and a half meters)
About 30 centimeters (about the length of a ruler)
explanation: The Philippine Eagle can reach almost 1 meter (about 100 centimeters) in length from head to tail.

q: When is it hardest to read the time on a sundial?
options: On hazy or partly cloudy days when the shadow becomes faint
On very cold mornings when the gnomon is covered in frost
At exactly noon when the shadow is the shortest it can be
In summer when the sun is so bright the shadow becomes blurry
explanation: On hazy or partly cloudy days the shadow on a sundial becomes faint and hard to read accurately; it is clearest under bright, strong sunshine.

q: How do rats affect rice farmers in the Philippines?
options: They damage rice crops and reduce the farmers' harvest
They eat insects that would otherwise destroy the rice plants
They loosen the soil in rice fields, helping roots grow deeper
They carry water from canals to dry areas of the rice fields
explanation: In the Philippines, rats damage rice crops and reduce farmers' harvest, making them a serious agricultural pest.

q: What is a group of meerkats called?
options: A mob
A pack
A colony
A herd
explanation: Meerkats live in large family groups called a mob.

q: What do glucagon and insulin work together to keep balanced in the body?
options: Blood sugar levels
Body temperature
Blood pressure
Oxygen levels in the blood
explanation: Like pulling on opposite ends of a rope, glucagon and insulin work together to keep blood sugar balanced — neither too high nor too low.

q: A pig is called an omnivore. What does this mean about what it eats?
options: It eats both plants and small animals
It eats only plants and grains
It eats only meat from other animals
It eats only insects and worms
explanation: A pig is an omnivore, meaning it eats both plants and small animals.

q: What is the main problem with monocropping — planting the same crop in the same soil every year?
options: It uses up nutrients faster and lets pests build up in the soil
It makes the soil too wet for most plants to grow the following year
It causes the roots to grow too deep and damage underground water pipes
It makes the crops grow taller than normal and easier for storms to knock down
explanation: Monocropping uses up nutrients faster and lets pests build up, which is why crop rotation is the healthier farming method.

q: How does the mudskipper help keep the mangrove mudflats healthy?
options: By eating algae and small animals, it keeps the mudflats clean and balanced
By digging burrows that allow fresh rainwater to mix with salt water
By spreading mangrove seeds across the mudflat as it moves around
By eating the roots of competing plants so mangroves can grow more easily
explanation: By eating algae and small animals, the mudskipper helps keep the mangrove mudflats clean and balanced.

q: Why can a saw cut through wood even when you push with moderate force?
options: Its sharp teeth focus the force onto tiny points, creating very high pressure
Its wide blade spreads the force evenly so friction is reduced across the surface
Its metal teeth vibrate at high speed and melt the wood fibres apart
Its teeth are harder than wood so they simply push the wood fibres aside
explanation: The sharp teeth of a saw focus force on tiny points, making very high pressure that goes into wood easily.

q: Which word best describes the leaves of the balete tree throughout the year?
options: Broad, green, and always present on the tree
Narrow, pale, and shed completely each dry season
Small and waxy, falling off whenever temperatures drop
Wide and red-tipped, replaced by new leaves every month
explanation: The balete has broad green leaves that stay all year, so it always looks fresh and leafy.

q: According to PAGASA, what is the wind speed range of a typhoon?
options: 118 to 184 km/h
60 to 90 km/h
185 to 215 km/h
30 to 60 km/h
explanation: PAGASA classifies a typhoon as having winds of 118 to 184 km/h.

q: How do you calculate the average speed of a whole trip?
options: Divide the total distance by the total time
Divide the fastest speed by the slowest speed
Add the starting speed and ending speed, then divide by two
Multiply the total time by the number of stops made
explanation: Average speed is the total distance divided by the total time for the whole trip.

q: What is the name of the hard central part that corn kernels grow on?
options: The cob
The stalk
The husk
The tassel
explanation: Corn kernels grow packed tightly together on a hard central core called the cob.

q: What color does potassium produce in a flame test?
options: Violet (lilac)
Bright orange
Blue-green
Crimson red
explanation: In a flame test, potassium (K) produces a violet (lilac) flame color.

q: How does a coral reef grow larger over time?
options: New polyps build on top of the skeletons of dead polyps
Live coral slowly absorbs minerals from seawater and expands outward
Coral eggs settle on the ocean floor and hatch into new reef sections
Waves push loose coral fragments together and they fuse into a larger reef
explanation: A reef grows as new polyps build on top of the old skeletons of polyps that have died.

q: How do mangroves help reduce global warming?
options: They store carbon for a long time, lowering the amount of carbon dioxide in the air
They release large amounts of oxygen that neutralize carbon dioxide directly
They shade the ocean surface, preventing sunlight from warming the water
They absorb heat from the air and transfer it underground where it cannot warm the planet
explanation: By storing carbon for a long time, mangroves help lower the carbon dioxide in the air that contributes to warming the planet.

q: Where do mangrove trees grow in relation to the tides?
options: In a zone covered by seawater at high tide and exposed to air at low tide
In deep, permanently underwater areas away from the shore
On dry land just above the highest tide mark where salt spray cannot reach
In freshwater rivers far inland, far from any salt water
explanation: Mangroves live in a tidal zone where seawater covers their roots at high tide and uncovers them at low tide, so the roots are sometimes in water and sometimes in air.

q: Where does mucus from the nose drain, and what usually happens to it?
options: It drains down the throat and we often swallow it without noticing
It drains into the sinuses and is reabsorbed by the body overnight
It drains out through the tear ducts and is washed away by tears
It drains into the lungs where it is broken down by stomach acid
explanation: Mucus drains from the nose down the throat, and we often swallow it without noticing.

q: Which type of car was invented first — a steam-powered car or a gasoline-powered car?
options: The steam-powered car (1769) came before the gasoline car (1886)
The gasoline car (1886) came before the steam-powered car (1899)
Both were invented in the same decade, in the 1880s
The electric car was invented first, before both steam and gasoline cars
explanation: The steam-powered car built by Cugnot in 1769 came well before Karl Benz's first gasoline car in 1886.

q: Why are organisms placed in the same classification group?
options: Because they share similar features
Because they live in the same habitat
Because they are the same size and color
Because they eat the same type of food
explanation: Organisms are placed in the same group when they share similar features, which is the basis of biological classification.

q: If you add phenolphthalein indicator to a basic (alkaline) solution, what color will you see?
options: Pink
Yellow
Blue
Colorless
explanation: Phenolphthalein turns pink when it is added to a base.

q: What type of organism is usually the FIRST to grow on bare volcanic rock where there is no soil?
options: Lichens
Ferns
Grasses
Mosses
explanation: Primary succession on bare volcanic rock begins with pioneer species like lichens, which grow first and help prepare the ground for other plants.

q: Why do areas far from a typhoon's center sometimes experience heavy flooding?
options: Typhoon rain bands bring heavy rain even hundreds of kilometres from the storm's center
Typhoons push large ocean waves inland that can travel far from the storm's path
Strong winds from the typhoon carry rainwater from the storm's center to distant areas
The typhoon's low pressure pulls moisture from distant rivers causing them to overflow
explanation: Typhoon rain bands bring heavy rain even hundreds of kilometres from the storm's centre, causing widespread flooding in areas not directly hit.

q: What does a bacteriophage do to a bacterium?
options: It injects its DNA into the bacterium and takes over the cell to produce new phages
It releases a chemical that dissolves the outer wall of the bacterium
It wraps around the bacterium and prevents it from absorbing nutrients
It tricks the bacterium into producing antibodies that destroy itself
explanation: A bacteriophage is a virus that attacks bacteria by injecting its DNA into the bacterium and taking over the cell to produce new phages.

q: How do molds help the environment?
options: They break down dead plants and animals and return nutrients to the soil
They filter toxins out of polluted water by absorbing them into their cells
They produce oxygen that replaces what plants cannot make during the night
They eat insect larvae that would otherwise destroy living plants
explanation: Molds are decomposers that break down dead plants and animals to return nutrients to the soil.

q: What is the chemical formula of carbon dioxide?
options: CO2
CO
C2O
CO3
explanation: The chemical formula of carbon dioxide is CO2 — one carbon atom bonded to two oxygen atoms.

q: How does mold spread from one piece of food to another?
options: Tiny spores float in the air and land on food
Mold grows underground and pushes up through food that touches the ground
Mold travels through water droplets that splash from one surface to another
Insects carry mold cells on their bodies and deposit them on new food
explanation: Mold spreads through tiny spores that float in the air and land on food, where they begin to grow.

q: Why does it not hurt when we trim our fingernails?
options: Nails have no nerves, so they cannot feel pain
Nails are made of dead skin cells that have already fallen off the finger
Nails are so hard that scissors cannot actually cut through living tissue
Our brain ignores nail pain because trimming is a familiar activity
explanation: Nails have no nerves, so there is no pain when we trim them.

q: Which minerals are most important to the Philippine mining industry?
options: Gold, copper, and nickel
Iron, coal, and silver
Diamond, zinc, and platinum
Limestone, marble, and quartz
explanation: Mining minerals such as gold, copper, and nickel is an important part of the Philippine economy, providing jobs and income for the government.

q: Which group of animals includes spiders, ticks, mites, AND scorpions?
options: Arachnids
Insects
Crustaceans
Myriapods
explanation: The arachnid group includes scorpions along with spiders, ticks, and mites.

q: What fills the air around us even though we cannot see it?
options: Tiny atoms like oxygen and nitrogen
Invisible droplets of water vapor only
Small particles of dust and smoke
Empty space with no particles at all
explanation: Air looks empty but is actually full of tiny atoms — mainly oxygen and nitrogen — that we breathe in to stay alive.

q: When isaw is cooked over hot coals and turns brown, what kind of change is happening?
options: A chemical change caused by heat
A physical change because it gets hotter
A reversible change because it can cool down
A freezing change that makes it solid
explanation: Heat causes a chemical change that browns or chars the meat and gives it a smoky flavor and smell.

q: How long does the measles vaccine usually protect you after getting two doses?
options: Almost lifelong protection
Only for one year
About five years
Until you turn 18
explanation: Unlike vaccines that must be repeated yearly, two doses of the measles vaccine usually give long-lasting, almost lifelong protection.

q: Why are many fruit bats in danger today?
options: Hunting and loss of forests threaten them
They cannot find enough fruit to eat in cities
Cold weather kills them during the dry season
They are outcompeted by larger bats
explanation: Many fruit bats are endangered because of hunting and the destruction of forests where they live.

q: How does a firefly make its glow?
options: A chemical reaction between luciferin and oxygen inside its belly
By rubbing its wings together very fast to create heat
By absorbing sunlight during the day and releasing it at night
By producing electricity in special organs in its legs
explanation: A firefly's light comes from a chemical reaction where luciferin mixes with oxygen inside its belly.

q: What body part lets a colugo glide through the air?
options: A wide skin flap called a patagium connecting its neck, legs, and tail
Long feathered wings similar to a bird's
A bushy tail it uses like a parachute
Webbed feet that catch the wind
explanation: The colugo has a wide skin flap called a patagium that connects its neck, legs, and tail, allowing it to glide.

q: Why do auroras mostly appear near the north and south poles?
options: Earth's magnetic field funnels Sun particles toward the poles
The poles are closest to the Sun so they receive more solar wind
The sky is darker at the poles so the lights are easier to see
Ice and snow at the poles reflect sunlight and create the colors
explanation: Earth's magnetic field lines funnel particles from the Sun into the atmosphere near the poles, creating auroras.

q: Why does the liquid in a thermometer rise when the temperature goes up?
options: The liquid expands as it gets warmer and moves up the tube
The liquid turns into gas and pushes the column upward
Heat makes the glass tube shrink, squeezing the liquid up
The liquid becomes heavier when warm and sinks to fill more space
explanation: A thermometer works because the liquid inside expands when it gets warmer, causing it to rise up the tube.

q: What is the main purpose of TESDA in the Philippines?
options: Providing technical and vocational training so Filipinos can work without a four-year degree
Giving college scholarships to top high school graduates
Regulating the prices of goods in public markets
Building public roads and bridges across the country
explanation: TESDA provides technical and vocational training to Filipinos, allowing them to work in various fields without needing a four-year college degree.

q: How does a hydropower dam like Magat or Ambuklao produce electricity?
options: Flowing or falling water spins a turbine to generate electricity
Burning coal heats water that pushes a turbine
Solar panels on the dam convert sunlight into electricity
Wind blowing across the reservoir powers generators
explanation: In hydropower, the force of flowing or falling water spins a turbine to make electricity at dams like Magat and Ambuklao.

q: Why are aluminum alloys used to build aircraft instead of steel?
options: They are lighter than steel yet still strong enough to handle flight
They are cheaper to buy and easier to find than steel
They can stretch without breaking, which steel cannot do
They do not rust at all, while steel rusts quickly
explanation: Aluminum alloys are used in aircraft because they are lighter than steel yet strong enough to handle the stresses of flight.

q: What is one important advantage of having two eyes instead of one?
options: We can judge how far away objects are more accurately
We can see more colors than animals with one eye
We can see clearly in complete darkness
We have a wider range of vision behind our heads
explanation: Having two eyes helps us better judge how far away an object is.

q: What do tears do for your eyes every day, not just when you cry?
options: They keep the eye wet and clean by washing away dust and germs
They make the eye see more clearly by adjusting the lens shape
They change the color of the iris to protect against bright light
They produce the fluid that the eye uses to grow and repair itself
explanation: Tears keep the eye wet and clean by washing away dust and germs and preventing the eye from drying out.

q: What are the sharp spines on a cactus actually made from?
options: Leaves that changed shape to help the plant save water
Hardened roots that grew out through the stem
Small branches that shrank and became pointy over time
Crystals of salt that formed on the outside of the plant
explanation: A cactus's spines are modified leaves whose changed shape helps the plant lose only a little water.

q: Why does a sloth sometimes sit in sunlight?
options: To warm up its body because its body temperature is naturally low
To dry off its wet fur after sleeping in the rain
To attract insects that it then eats for food
To signal other sloths that this tree is its territory
explanation: A sloth's body temperature is naturally lower than most animals, so it basks in sunlight to keep its body warm enough.

q: How does sedimentary rock form?
options: Layers of sand, mud, and sediment pile up and press together over time
Melted rock from a volcano cools and hardens underground
Extreme heat and pressure deep in the Earth change one rock type into another
Minerals dissolved in water crystallize when the water evaporates
explanation: Sedimentary rock forms when layers of sand, mud, and other sediment pile up and press together over long periods of time.

q: What makes dry ice look like it is producing smoke or fog?
options: It turns directly from solid into gas without melting first
It melts so quickly that steam rises from the warm liquid
It reacts with oxygen in the air to produce white smoke
It absorbs heat and makes the nearby air freeze into ice crystals
explanation: Dry ice is solid carbon dioxide that turns directly into gas (sublimation), which is why it appears to be smoking.

q: What chemical did Ramon Barba spray on mango trees to make them flower?
options: Potassium nitrate (KNO₃)
Calcium phosphate (Ca₃(PO₄)₂)
Sodium chloride (NaCl)
Magnesium sulfate (MgSO₄)
explanation: Ramon Barba used a potassium nitrate (KNO₃) spray to make mango trees flower, revolutionizing mango farming.

q: What is the name of the North Star?
options: Polaris
Sirius
Betelgeuse
Vega
explanation: The North Star is named Polaris, and it sits almost directly above Earth's North Pole.

q: Which situation requires the most centripetal force to keep an object moving in a circle?
options: A heavy object spinning very fast in a small, tight circle
A light object spinning slowly in a large, wide circle
A heavy object spinning slowly in a large, wide circle
A light object spinning fast in a large, wide circle
explanation: More centripetal force is needed when the spin is faster, the circle is tighter (smaller), and the spinning object is heavier — all three factors together require the most force.

q: When is it safe to eat taro (gabi) leaves?
options: Only after they are fully cooked, such as in the dish laing
Anytime, since raw taro leaves taste sweet and mild
Only the young leaves can be eaten, but they must stay raw
Only when dried and ground into powder
explanation: Taro leaves can be eaten when fully cooked, as in the popular dish laing; eating them raw can be harmful.

q: What is the Philippine Fault Zone?
options: A major line of earth fracture running through the Philippines that frequently causes powerful earthquakes
A deep underwater trench east of the Philippines where the ocean floor cracks open
A chain of volcanoes stretching from Luzon to Mindanao
A series of valleys carved by rivers over millions of years
explanation: The Philippine Fault Zone is a major line of earth fracture running along the Philippines and is a frequent source of powerful earthquakes.

q: What happens to your pupil when a bright light suddenly shines in your eye?
options: The pupil shrinks automatically to protect the inside of the eye
The pupil widens to let in more light so you can see better
The pupil stays the same size but the eyelid closes instead
The pupil moves to the side of the eye away from the light
explanation: The pupil shrinks on its own as a reflex when bright light hits the eye, preventing too much light from dazzling and harming the inside of the eye.

q: How is filariasis spread, and what does it cause?
options: It is spread by mosquitoes and causes legs to swell greatly because tiny worms block fluid channels
It is spread by contaminated water and causes high fever and rash
It is spread by touching infected animals and causes skin blisters
It is spread through the air and causes lung damage and coughing
explanation: Filariasis is spread by mosquitoes and is caused by tiny worms that block the body's fluid channels, making the legs swell greatly.

q: How does a microwave oven heat your food?
options: It makes the water molecules inside the food move, which creates heat
It produces infrared light that warms the outer surface of food
It passes electric current through the food to heat it up
It uses hot air blown by a fan inside the oven to cook the food
explanation: Microwave ovens heat food by making its water molecules move, generating heat throughout the food.

q: What happens to the airways when cigarette smoke damages the tiny hairs (cilia) inside them?
options: Mucus builds up in the airways because the cilia can no longer clean them
The airways shrink in size and make breathing faster
The lungs produce more cilia to replace the damaged ones quickly
The damaged cilia become harder and block the flow of air completely
explanation: Smoke damages the cilia that normally clean the airways, so mucus builds up and cannot be cleared properly.

q: Why is a forested watershed better protected than bare land?
options: Tree roots and forest soil soak up rainwater, reducing floods and keeping water clean
Forests block wind so less rain falls on the watershed in the first place
The shade from trees keeps the water cool so it does not evaporate
Trees absorb pollutants from the air before they can reach the water
explanation: A forest protects a watershed because its roots and soil soak up and store rainwater, reducing floods and landslides and keeping the water clean.

q: What causes the loud booming sound of thunder?
options: Lightning rapidly heats the air along its path, causing it to suddenly expand and boom
Clouds collide with each other and release stored energy as a loud sound
Rain droplets fall so fast they create a shockwave when they hit the ground
Thunder is the sound of electricity building up inside a storm cloud
explanation: Thunder is caused by lightning — a huge static spark — that heats the air so fast it suddenly expands, creating the loud booming sound.

q: Who was the Supremo, or leader, of the Katipunan?
options: Andres Bonifacio
Jose Rizal
Emilio Aguinaldo
Apolinario Mabini
explanation: Andres Bonifacio was the Supremo, or leader, of the Katipunan, the revolutionary society that fought against Spanish colonial rule.

q: What useful effect does a volcanic eruption have on the surrounding farmland?
options: Volcanic ash makes the soil rich and fertile, helping crops grow well
The heat from lava permanently warms the soil, lengthening the growing season
Eruptions flatten the land, making it easier to plow and plant
Ash blocks sunlight for years, keeping temperatures cool for certain crops
explanation: Although dangerous, volcanic eruptions deposit ash that makes soil rich and fertile, so farms around Philippine volcanoes are very productive.

q: Why does bread dough puff up and become soft when yeast is added?
options: Yeast releases carbon-dioxide gas as it feeds on sugar, and the bubbles make the dough rise
Yeast absorbs water from the dough and swells, pushing the dough outward
Yeast produces heat that expands the dough like a balloon
Yeast makes the flour stick together more tightly, trapping air that was already there
explanation: Yeast releases carbon-dioxide gas as it feeds on sugar; the gas bubbles make the bread soft and puffed up.

q: At what height is the commonly accepted boundary where outer space begins?
options: About 100 kilometers above Earth, called the Karman line
About 10 kilometers above Earth, where commercial planes fly
About 1,000 kilometers above Earth, where satellites orbit
About 50 kilometers above Earth, at the top of the stratosphere
explanation: The Karman line, about 100 kilometers high, is commonly used as the boundary where space begins.

q: What color does a universal indicator turn when a liquid has a neutral pH of 7?
options: Green
Red
Blue
Yellow
explanation: Universal indicator turns green at a neutral pH of 7, which is neither acidic nor basic.

q: Which type of worm is best for composting rotting material quickly?
options: The red wiggler (Eisenia fetida), which lives near the soil surface
The common deep-burrowing earthworm found in garden soil
Any large earthworm because bigger worms eat more material
Mealworms, because they are the fastest eaters of all worm species
explanation: The red wiggler (Eisenia fetida) lives near the soil surface and eats rotting material quickly, making it ideal for composting.

q: When should you take antibiotics?
options: Only when a doctor says they are needed, not for every fever or cough
Whenever you have a fever to help your body fight the infection faster
Every time you feel a cold coming on to prevent it from getting worse
Twice a day for one week whenever you feel any kind of body pain
explanation: You should only take antibiotics when a doctor says they are needed, not for every fever or cough, to avoid misuse.

q: How do some electric fish communicate with each other underwater?
options: They send weak electric pulses to find mates and signal others in their group
They make vibrations with their swim bladder that travel through the water
They release chemicals into the water that other fish can taste and smell
They flash patterns of bioluminescent light from organs on their sides
explanation: Some electric fish use weak electric signals with different pulses to talk to one another, find mates, and communicate within their group.

q: Which metal salt is responsible for the blue color in fireworks?
options: Copper salts
Iron salts
Magnesium salts
Sodium salts
explanation: The blue color in fireworks comes from copper salts burning at high temperatures.

q: Why does the sea breeze become weak or disappear on a cloudy day?
options: Without sunshine the land does not heat up, so there is little temperature difference between land and sea to drive the breeze
Clouds block the wind from blowing in from the ocean toward the land
Rain from the clouds cools the sea water, stopping it from evaporating
Cloudy skies create high air pressure over the sea that pushes air back out
explanation: The sea breeze needs sunshine to heat the land and create a temperature difference with the sea; without it, the convection that drives the breeze does not occur.

q: How can a tick make a person or animal sick?
options: It carries germs and passes them into the body when it sucks blood
It bites and injects a venom that slowly damages the nervous system
It lays eggs under the skin that hatch and cause an allergic reaction
It spreads bacteria through its droppings left on skin after feeding
explanation: A tick can carry germs that cause disease and pass them on when it sucks blood from a host.

q: How does a chameleon change its color?
options: It adjusts tiny crystals in its skin that reflect light differently
It pumps colored liquid from special glands into its transparent skin
It absorbs pigment from the food it eats and releases it through its skin
It contracts muscles that stretch or compress colored skin patches
explanation: A chameleon changes color by adjusting tiny crystals in its skin, which reflects light differently to produce different colors.

q: How does the spin cycle of a washing machine remove water from clothes?

The drum heats up during spinning, evaporating the water from the fabric
A built-in fan blows hot air through the drum while it spins
The spinning motion wrings the clothes like a twisted towel
explanation: The fast-spinning drum flings water out through tiny holes due to the speed of rotation, leaving the clothes partly dry.

They are the highest rice terraces in Asia, located on a volcano's peak
They are flooded year-round and harvested by boats instead of by foot
They are the oldest terraces in the Philippines, built over 5,000 years ago

q: Why is it silent in outer space even when stars explode?
options: Sound cannot travel through space because there is no air or material to carry it
Space is too cold for sound waves to form, so they freeze and disappear
The distances are so great that sound slows down to zero before it arrives
Light travels faster than sound in space so it cancels out the sound waves
explanation: Sound cannot travel through a vacuum or space because there is no air or medium for it to move through.

q: Why do tomato and eggplant plants stay in one spot even when watered every day?
options: Their roots hold them firmly in the soil
Their thick stems are too heavy to be moved by water
They attach themselves to nearby plants for support
Their leaves catch the water and weigh the plant down
explanation: In a vegetable garden, roots hold plants like tomatoes and eggplants firmly in place so they do not move even when watered daily.

q: How can you grow a new pineapple plant without using seeds?
options: Plant the crown cut from the top of the fruit; this is vegetative propagation
Bury a ripe pineapple slice in the soil and water it until it sprouts
Split the pineapple root in half and plant each half separately
Dry the pineapple skin, grind it into powder, and mix it into the soil
explanation: The pineapple crown cut from the top of the fruit can be planted to grow a new plant, which is an example of vegetative propagation.

q: How many babies can a father seahorse carry at the same time?
options: Hundreds to thousands of babies
Only one or two at a time
About ten to twenty babies
Up to fifty babies at most

12 constellations
48 constellations
100 constellations
